You clearly tell yourself there's no need to expect anything anymore, but at this moment, you still feel a bit of anticipation. But that hope comes with a sense of desolation. You warn yourself not to re-enter the marriage you once had, to be influenced by it, to warn yourself...... Don't dwell on the past, because all that's left is pain, and all you can face is the future.
The only thing you want to hold onto is the future...... So you walk into the jewelry store on your own, fiddling with the bracelets on the counter and the necklaces hanging there. After following you into the store, Tenna suddenly realizes that the things he had given you before were far too few; he hadn't even bothered to understand your preferences...... He only knew you liked flowers, but what about anything else? He knew nothing about it.
You casually picked up a string of amethysts and slipped them onto your wrist. The beads were a bit large, making your wrist look very slender and small. It seemed like you had eaten less lately—you had lost weight. Tenna thought absentmindedly, but in the end, he only took a bracelet of lapis lazuli beside him. The color resembled his, and then he casually handed it to you. You glanced at it casually but didn't take the bracelet. Instead, you picked up a small pink crystal bead and put it on your wrist. You took the bracelet to pay, and Tenna glanced at the bracelet and also took it to pay. He planned to take it home, since maybe he could give it to you later so you could wear it—even though you two hadn't yet started, he was already thinking about the future. Maybe it's just that, no matter what, he'll definitely bring you back, and you'll definitely become his wife again. No matter what, this is the fact Tenna is certain of.
He quietly followed behind you, and you ignored Tenna. He simply followed you into a nearby accessory shop, which seemed to sell all sorts of ornaments and all sorts of miscellaneous items. You casually picked two paper sculptures and bought them because you planned to decorate your current home. After all, you'd definitely be living there for a long time, so you needed to decorate it properly.
The item in his hand was a bit heavy, and you handed it to Tenna again. He always comes to see you on weekends, and if he does nothing, just staring at you annoys you...... But in short, he just happens to be a tool or something, so you don't hesitate to hand him the thing. Anyway, what he wants to do now is probably just to please himself...... But no matter what, you wouldn't be willing to go back and be a useful tool.
This has basically been the way I've been through this period...... About a month has passed, even though ...... Indeed, your attitude is much better than at the beginning, at least you won't always act like Tenna doesn't exist, but aside from that, there's nothing more, besides that...... Tenna still wants to be like before, to be able to touch you all the time, see you, and embrace you...... To be able to hear your voice, not to be so cold and indifferent. But it seems impossible to do that, it seems you will never be able and never show him the tenderness you once had. But...... But the longer the time passed, the more he longed for those moments and missed them more. He was almost impatient to hope you—his wife—or rather, his ex-wife—could return to his side. He could no longer endure it, so Tenna only took some excessive actions.
He instructed his staff not to hire Y/N, then formally visited the queen, expressing his dissatisfaction with the previous marriage partner and asking if he could require all companies in the cyber world to forbid hiring her and punish her. Perhaps the queen sensed something, but in any case, she agreed to Tenna's request.
…… And you, on Monday, were mysteriously fired by your current company. You went to other companies to submit resumes, but no one was willing to pay attention to you, as if avoiding you like a snake. When you finally visited the Queen, you learned some unfortunate news: due to the failed marriage alliance, cooperation between the two worlds was now suspended. The cyber world blacklisted you, and now no company will hire you. What will you do for your food and living expenses? You went to the TV world, but not a single Dark Clan dared to hire you. You don't know what Tenna would think...... Probably, he really was unhappy about this marriage, but for now, you could only go find Tenna. You don't understand...... But you can only try. After all, after the divorce, he keeps coming to you, and he probably ...... He wouldn't completely abandon you, right?
So you finally knock on Tenna's office door and hear a lukewarm invitation to enter. Once again, you see Tenna with a cold expression, or rather a curled smile, busy handling the pile of documents in front of you.
He saw you too—he knew his plan would definitely work. At that moment, the corners of his mouth wanted to lift, but he restrained his movements and simply said coldly, "What brings you here now?" ”
Your heart sank. With this...... Maybe Tenna won't help you either, but you still mustered your courage and said, "...... In the cyber world, I can't survive anymore, because the Queen has already blacklisted me...... I... I hope you can give me a place to live, or just give me a job...... Please, Mr. Tenna, it doesn't matter how low the salary is, I...... I can do anything. "As you spoke, you lowered your head slightly. Tenna's mood brightened again—he liked seeing you like this, having no one to rely on, and in the end, only relying on him, and he just spoke casually.
"Ah, then show me your sincerity." He said this, casually shifting the chair back a bit, legs spread and lying back on the chair's backrest. Instinctively, he pulled a cigarette from his pants pocket, because ever since you left, he'd been used to it—but seeing your frown instinctively, Tenna instinctively stubbed out the cigarette.
Your body trembled, and you quietly glanced up at Tenna, watching his current movements...... Think about it, isn't it already obvious what he wants you to do? So you slowly kneel on the floor, set aside your things, and then your hands tremble as you touch his pants. Tenna is a bit surprised...... But he doesn't mind you doing that, just resting his chin on his hand and watching you with interest.
You took a deep breath, unzipped his pants, then unfastened his belt, releasing that large member. Your hand stroked it a couple of times, making it hard again. Although your movements weren't very practiced, Tenna just let out a muffled groan, clearly enjoying it too. You took another deep breath, gently licking the tip with your tongue, feeling a bit of sticky fluid flow into your mouth. Then you slowly opened your mouth and softly took it into your mouth, trying hard to wrap it around and suck it, but unfortunately, only half of it was buried in your mouth. Tenna looked down at you, swallowing hard—oh my god, he really wanted to hold you right now, to bury that penis deep inside your body...... For a long time, he had been longing for all of this—missing your soft body, missing your voice, and remembering the feeling of you in his arms back then...... But he also saw your reddened eyes at that moment, and for some reason, he just felt panicked—probably because that mechanical heart hurt so much now, as if telling him that none of this should have happened.
He ...... His body is feeling happy now, but you don't seem happy just looking at him. He doesn't want to go through the same things as those days again. In the end, he just presses your head down to make you lift your head again, and that member pulls out of your mouth. You look at him with a hazy gaze, looking a bit pitiful. Tenna thinks, at this moment, to be able to have you completely...... Maybe your voice would sound very nice, right? But he doesn't want to hear your cries; that sound only makes him restless, and he doesn't even know why he is so agitated.

Second, be my secretary, and I'll offer you a job." He spoke concisely, though he was indeed lying—he just wanted to continue that marriage with you, which is why he made such a request. He ...... Yes, although he wouldn't say it out loud, he had to admit that during the days you were gone, he missed you very much, missed you very much.

Although you weren't willing, this was your only way out right now, and of course, you could only agree.
“…… Alright, I agree, Tenna. "Your voice carried a hint of obscurity, while Tenna just propped up her chin and smiled in satisfaction. Honestly, things have gone smoothly so far, and it's not in vain that he deliberately made this choice to force you to stand before him again—he's very satisfied.
And now, he just waved his hand and said casually, "You may leave now. Since you agreed, come home with me today, and then start working as a secretary tomorrow." He was already eager to go home with you. You let out a gloomy 'oh', clearly in a bad mood. Then you walked out of the office with a lowered head and obedient eyes, while Tenna didn't notice it; he was just thinking...... He hadn't been to that house without you for a long time. Now, today, he can finally take you home. Of course, before that, he also needs to make some preparations.
So he returned to that house. He usually hired people to clean it, so the room was very tidy, but...... It was too quiet, and it was obvious at a glance that no one had lived here for a long time.
Tenna hesitated for a moment, then went out to a nearby florist to buy a bouquet of white roses. Then he opened the wrapper and carefully placed the flowers into a vase. He then went to a nearby dessert shop to pack several kinds of desserts: matcha pudding, mango mille crepe, tiramisu, chocolate cake—it was almost everything. Although he somewhat remembered your preferences...... But he didn't know if you would like other things, so he simply bought them all.
Next, he solemnly placed the lapis lazuli bracelet he had bought earlier on your dressing table, then headed toward the nearby jewelry store. Driven by selfishness, he bought a pile of blue and purple gemstones as the centerpiece, surrounded by silver accessories as accents, and placed them on the dressing table as well. Finally, he went to the nearby clothing store. Last time he saw you buy clothes, Tenna remembered your size and didn't have time to prepare a new ...... today. He just bought some clothes that he thought would look great on you...... If you're willing to change them for him to see, that would be great.
Finally, he bought some new books on the empty bookshelf that he thought you'd like, and placed them one by one...... He was anxious, wondering if, as soon as you stepped through the door, seeing these small yet warm decorations would make you happy...... He just bought a few more ornaments from the jewelry store and casually placed them in his room, then pretended nothing had happened and rushed back to the office. By the time work was almost over, Tenna kept thinking he could come find you soon, but before that, there was a knock at the door, and then he saw you timidly walking in holding the documents in your hands.
You keep your head down, afraid to look at him, oh my god...... You don't know what this marriage will look like if it continues. After all, he clearly doesn't love you, after all...... He doesn't care about you at all, and you're still learning, trying your best, trying not to love Tenna anymore...... But you still can't do it.
Tenna stood up and took your hand. His voice was as cold as ever: "Alright, now let's go home." Actually, he was very happy, because the place where you were was truly home to him...... He was glad to have you again. Of course, he also knew you probably couldn't keep up with his pace, so he deliberately slowed down and walked with you slowly onto the street...... You don't know why his pace was so slow, but it was still a bit fast for you, and you weren't used to holding his hand. You instinctively tried to pull your hand away, but Tenna just held your hand tightly—he gave you no room to escape, and you couldn't pull your hand away. In the end, you could only silently stare at the ground, letting Tenna lead you forward.
Until you stopped at a large door, then you heard the door open. You had arrived at your destination. Tenna opened the door. This was still a familiar place, but ...... There were still fresh roses on the table—probably bought today, probably...... Because you remarried, some habits were the same as before. Your heart stirred, but you couldn't believe your judgment. You only dared to walk in hand and foot, restless as you sat on the sofa, your feet still unable to touch the ground, just hanging in the air. You didn't dare do anything, just sat on the sofa, staring blankly at the empty bottle. Then you felt the sofa collapse beside you, and out of the corner of your eye, you saw Tenna sitting beside you...... Oh my god, why on earth did this? You don't understand either, but out of the corner of your eye, you see Tenna seems to have turned off the screen...... His antenna also droops, and he looks like he's in a bad mood.
And at this moment, he was just maintaining the same posture. You might think he was just daydreaming. You carefully looked around the room and naturally noticed the books on the bookshelf next to the sofa...... Ah, those were limited editions! There were several books you hadn't even managed to get at the bookstore before, but several books you had always wanted to read but were very expensive to buy together, so you hadn't made up your mind to buy them...... Your eyes lit up, and you took the books down from the shelf. Because of this, your seat was a bit farther away from Tenna, but seeing the books put you in a good mood...... You eagerly started turning the pages, and Tenna saw that your mood seemed to improve a bit before letting out a sigh of relief and sitting down beside you again. You didn't pay much attention to these things, just read with great interest, while Tenna quietly turned her head to look at you, almost greedily—he hadn't seen you so close in ages.
You didn't notice his gaze, just immersed in the novel before you. Then Tenna quietly moved closer to you until his arm rested on your shoulder...... He longed so much to have you completely right now, because you must be his possession.
But Tenna just swallowed hard, her voice a bit dry as she said, "...... My antenna isn't comfortable." "Just like before...... He hopes you can straddle him, so he can see you clearly and see everything about you. He ...... He wants you to be with him forever.
But when you hear this, you feel as if you've fallen into an ice cave; you thought everything might be different...... But in fact, you also know what Tenna wants right now. And you...... You remarried Tenna according to his request, so there's no reason not to fulfill his demands.
You weakly replied with a "yes." Tenna was still puzzled by how your voice suddenly changed like this, but soon he had no energy left to think further...... Or rather, he simply didn't have the patience anymore, because you had already turned over and straddled his legs. You were just a small one; as long as Tenna tightened his arms, you could only obediently stay in his arms. Of course, he didn't do that. You just took a deep breath, your hands trembling slightly as you gently stroked the tips of those two antennas. You heard Tenna let out a muffled groan, and his tense body relaxed. It was clear he really enjoyed all this, and you could only continue.

Only in that moment, all it takes is a lasting embrace, and just a moment when our hearts are close is enough.
Although often this hug lasts all night.
You think, when you see his death, even if it's just a possibility, your heart breaks. You will absolutely stop that possibility from happening. You absolutely do not want to see him die.
…… Even if it means exchanging your own death for his survival, such a thing is possible. Of course, all of this now is just a vague thought in your mind. You are just lost in thought, thinking about this as you walk toward your room.
…… Then, you forget the threshold at your room's door, tripping over it, instinctively leaning forward, your eyes wide as you stare at the ground within reach.
Tenna saw this too. Without even bothering to gather his scattered emotions, he got up and ran toward you, instinctively wanting to hug you, at least to keep you from falling to the ground.
Maybe at that moment, a miracle happened, or maybe it was just a simple illusion. In any case, who knows what it was? All you felt was a dazed sensation in front of you, followed by a twisted sensation—a blank space. When you came to, you were at the door, lifting your foot, not yet stepping down, nor stepping on the doorframe.
You dazedly put down your foot, instinctively turning your head to meet Tenna's gaze, who was about to run toward you.
Tenna also understood that you seemed to have noticed something. Her anxious steps slowed down, just stammering her lips as she stood in front of you, facing your eczema without speaking.
You looked up at Tenna, took a deep breath, and asked, "Just now, was it the kind of time reversal you mentioned?" ”
Tenna nodded. There was no need to hesitate about this kind of thing. In fact, he was actually desperately hoping you would realize its importance.
You let out a soft moan. In fact, you still felt it was a bit absurd. Just moments ago, you were seriously thinking about how to experiment and verify it, but in such an absurd situation, you experienced the feeling of time rewinding, easily avoiding possible danger.
In the end, you still scratched your hair. To be honest, your thoughts were a bit messy now, just like your hair was still a bit messy. You simply took Tenna's hand and sat down together on the sofa, and Tenna followed your movements and sat down beside you.
“…… Ah, so now I can also experience the feeling of time rewinding. "You were still a bit dazed. After sitting down and looking at your hands, you didn't know what you were thinking.
Tenna nodded and added, "Besides, you never kept those memories during the previous backward period, but now you do......"
He was clearly still a bit worried, since Tenna wasn't sure if this should be considered a good thing. And why did he retain memories? What exactly was the principle behind it? Could it be that because you knew about the existence of time reversal, you could sense it all?
This way of thinking doesn't seem unreasonable, but Tenna always finds this matter a bit unbelievable. You just turn your head to look at Tenna, place your hand on his, and pat him with a hint of reassurance: "Alright, preserving memories isn't a bad thing. Maybe it's my eagerness to experiment and the truth that made me remember all of this myself. So it's understandable, and if you can't figure something out, don't dwell on it anymore. Maybe after some time, these problems will be solved, and you won't even need to think much more." You nodded as you spoke, confirming your own idea.
“…… Maybe that's what you mean, but dear, I'm just afraid you'll leave me because of it. "Tenna placed her other hand on yours, then tightly held yours, or rather, wrapped in his palm.
You didn't really mind that, just shrugged and gently patted his back with your other free hand: "It's okay, I've told you, even if I really die, I'll always love you. Even if I become a ghost, I'll come back to find you." So, there's no need to be afraid of this. However...... Actually, preserving memories does have its benefits. ”
You smiled and spoke, but then your screen turned pitch black again, tears streaming down your face. If you tried to catch it by speaking now, you'd surely catch many droplets, like the sadness spreading beside him, like the spreading silence and cold water, enough to make you drown.
You take a deep breath, lift your upper body, stand on tiptoe and kiss the tears on the screen, and softly say, "Alright, I won't say the word 'death' anymore. I will absolutely do my best to avoid the possibility of death, okay?" ”
You see Tenna suddenly nod.
So you chuckled softly and rested your head on his chest. Alright, you wanted to give him a hug, but your current posture was a bit awkward, making the hug feel strange. In short, you just buried yourself in his chest and muffled as you said, "Mm...... Look, it's good that I remember these memories from the time of rewinding. That way, I know I might encounter danger, and I can avoid future dangers that might be risky. So the existence of these memories is also very good. ”
"And actually, you know very well, right? It's just that those things won't let me die so easily! I'm not some fragile porcelain vase that needs your constant protection and care. I'm a person, perfectly intact, staying in your arms. See, I really exist. There's no way I could suddenly die or disappear, unless something happened that I couldn't avoid—ah, I hope the memories of time rewind at that time can help me escape this accident." You smiled, climbed onto Tenna's back, and then hugged him again. After all, at some point he let go of his hand—probably while you were whispering those words against his chest.
In fact, he can feel the breath you blow on his chest when you speak, and the slight tremor in your chest as you utter every word. In short, he couldn't help but let go. He was indeed listening attentively to your words, wanting to argue something, but he just stammered, waiting for you to finish.
Then he felt your hands wrapped around his neck, pressing your head against his TV. He couldn't see your expression clearly, just instinctively wrapped his arms around you and hugged you. Of course, Tenna was already trying hard to suppress his emotions, but some tears still fell and soaked your clothes.
You didn't really mind, just softly said, "So, you see, this is actually quite good. Don't worry so much anymore. Trust me, isn't it great to know in advance and avoid danger and such?" ”
He was still sobbing, his voice broken and broken: "But if you do this, you inevitably feel the panic and fear before time rewinds, those unavoidable moments of pain and fear, the despair at that moment......" He was somewhat incoherent.
And you just pat his head again: "Well, because of fear, you can further avoid the possibility of danger. Feeling panic and fear leaves a mark in your memory, so I remember it and pay attention next time. For example, in what happened just now, I will definitely pay attention to that threshold next time." ”
Tenna was silent for a moment, then muttered a complaint: "But your memory is terrible. Have you forgotten how many times you almost hit your head on the shelf?" ”
You coughed awkwardly and lightly: "Ahem! That's exactly why I need you to stay by my side all the time. Look, you've taken good care of me, and only you know what. That fear and despair must have built up in your heart, right? But for now, I'll help you share all of this." ”
“…… Anyway, trust me? ”
Tenna was silent, then you felt his head move and nodded.

Somehow, you always have a bad feeling. Of course, even in this situation, Tenna hasn't forgotten to call your name, so you still follow him in the end. You just keep quiet, wanting to know what exactly that ominous feeling in your heart is all about.
You followed Tenna past the front stage, seeing the stage fall into darkness and silence after it closed—you were very familiar with this silence, because it had been like this for a long time. Tenna kept glancing back at you from time to time to check if you were following, to confirm he could see you all along.
Although you're curious how he'd react if he suddenly disappeared at this moment and couldn't see him, you didn't intend to do so.
You don't want to proactively cause him to feel anxious, as that would only lead to guilt and guilt, so just maintain the status quo.
Until you pass through door after door and enter the snowy field where the cold wind howls and snowflakes drift. You wrap yourself tightly and stand beside the tree, looking up at the sky—it's just pitch black. Then you look toward that similarly dark, unknown doorway. Out of the corner of your eye, you notice Tenna is also uneasy—or rather, he actually wants to escape from here. He may not want to face what comes next, but he knows he has to do it, that he has no choice.
So you quietly took two steps toward Tenna's direction, then slipped your hand into his tightly held palm as comfort. You saw that although he was bowing his head, he still held your hand tightly, wrapping it tightly in his palm.
…… Then, you saw the figures of those three people appear at the doorway, so you quietly pulled your hand out and just hid behind the tree. Because you felt that maybe you shouldn't be standing here. To be honest, you don't have any other abilities, so it's better not to get in the way here.
But maybe it's only natural...... Tenna still failed, maybe he had his own sense of self-awareness—this was a doomed failure, so before it all began, he wanted to escape. And you saw it all in full, and belatedly realized that maybe leaving with him back then would have been a better choice? No, maybe he didn't want to leave either.
Because you see him so happy now to hand out the ultimate prize that was supposed to be on the treetop—then you widen your eyes, unable to believe what you've just seen. You see a pitch-black shadow appear behind Tenna at some point, raising its blade and pointing it at him.
You have to do something. Whatever it is, but maybe everything will be too late in a flash. Suddenly, something comes to mind. You pull out the knife you've hidden on yourself when you've been feeling uneasy, and don't dare hesitate for a moment, slashing straight toward your neck. As you raise the blade, you run toward the distance, still too close to it.
Because only death brings rebirth, and at this moment, you overcome the fear and pain brought by death, so you know none of this will happen again, only rebirth. You even do all this with a smile and relief. You remember the pain of dying and the feeling of near suffocation, then your vision goes black and blank. When you come to your senses, you are standing not far away, still holding the knife to your neck, blood dripping from the scraped skin, wetting the blade.
You look up in a daze, still unsure if you've truly succeeded. If not, you'll have to try again—then you see Tenna's screen go black again, with tears falling continuously. He kneels in the snow, hugs you tightly, and knocks the knife from your hand.
Tenna, in fact, from that moment of blurred before his eyes and the moment he felt the familiar distortion of time and space, suddenly understood that you had encountered danger again—no, more like choosing death, because in that instant, in the pitch-black reverse, he truly saw your fate, smiling as blood flowed, soaking every inch beneath you, staining the pure white snowflakes red, while you lay there peacefully, your body gradually turning cold. Then, in the very next second after rewinding in time, he noticed the knife you were holding against your neck. He couldn't care about anything else; his only thought now was to run over, hold you tight, and stop your movements.
He was even a bit annoyed that he had prepared this dagger for you earlier, since he was afraid you might be in danger and gave it to you. But now, it was you who brought danger upon yourself.
The falling blade missed, and then the trio shouted something and rushed forward. You weren't interested, and you didn't listen anymore. You just looked at Tenna, who was hugging you tightly, gently wiped the tears from his face, and then smiled with pure joy: "So I succeeded on the first try? That's great." Don't cry, look, we're all standing here perfectly fine now, nothing happened at all. ”
"But what if that time-space rewind function just fails? What if it happens to ...... What if all of this fails? I can't bear losing your future......" His voice was still choked with tears, confused, and even gasping for breath—clearly, he was crying even harder.
You could only pat his head: "It's okay, didn't I succeed?" Besides, I can't bear to lose your future. If I hadn't done anything just now, maybe I would have just watched you die—just thinking about it scares me. That's why I thought of doing this. Maybe my sudden death alone could actually bring us a future where we both survive together. ”
"But if you do that, nothing happens, and you die for no reason—" Tenna was still shaken, emphasizing the possibility.
But you just interrupted him slowly: "Is that so?" Alright then, let's both step into death together. Maybe a shared death is another kind of rebirth. I don't care about that; I just want to always be with you. "As you spoke, you cupped Tenna's head, pressed your forehead against his screen, and looked at him intently. Even though you didn't know if you were looking into his eyes, it didn't matter.
Tenna seemed stunned, or maybe just silent. In any case, he didn't speak for a while, leaving only silence surrounding you. Of course, there was also the distant sounds of battle as background music.
After a long silence, he finally tugged at your collar: "No matter what, let me see your wound first......"
You let him do as he pleased, though honestly, you still feel a bit guilty.
Tenna was stunned once again. He saw the uneven colors of skin beneath the newly formed bloodstains. Some of the skin tones were already very close to the original, but near the scar, there were still quite a few that were clearly recognizable—they were newly formed skin. Or rather, the wounds had already endured countless times, the cuts had been cut countless times, leaving deep wounds. Only this time the wounds were shallow, and they would probably heal in a little while.
He began to blame himself, wondering why he had never noticed before—yet he never had such a close look at your neck before, nor noticed skin color, so naturally he wouldn't notice the patchwork of skin marked by death and rebirth.
Maybe, without his knowledge, you would have died countless times already, yet now you still stand in front of him, even looking at him with a puzzled gaze.
So he starts to feel afraid. Tenna hugs you tightly again, but you don't understand and just hug him back.
You ask softly, "What's going on?" ”
He hesitated for a moment, then hesitated deeply, then asked in a trembling voice, "Without my knowledge...... Have you died many times? ”
You cleared your throat twice, feeling a bit guilty, and replied uncertainly, "Didn't I say before? Trading my own death for a new life for us is a very worthwhile thing......
So what you said about experimenting before was just a disguise; you can't suddenly show that you already knew about it. But you do fear the pain that death brings. You really didn't have memories before; you just guessed through subtle shifts in the position of things and started trying on your own. So every death feels like an adventure to you. And now, you don't know why Tenna entered this cycle with you, still retaining memories.
But all these adventures are the sacrifices that should be made to protect this family, to maintain perfection.
“…… Th-is it worth it? "You heard Tenna's voice. Although he probably didn't want to accept it, he still trembled as he asked, perhaps confirming something.
So you nod without hesitation: "Of course it's worth it. Because I love you, I can't bear a future where we can't coexist, I can't bear to see our current family destroyed. If it's just a possible adventure, and there won't be any other danger besides that, why not give it a try? I don't think there's anything wrong with that. Of course, maybe it's just that I've been working hard for the future where we coexist, even if it's just a risky death. ”
Maybe you just piled up countless deaths just for this one success? Honestly, you don't even remember. You can't even remember why you died, only barely remembering it was probably for Tenna. But now it's best to succeed on one try; otherwise, you'd have to pile up new wounds on top of the same ones.
In short, you are now holding each other tightly in this snowy field, leaning on each other's warmth, and then celebrating the birth of a perfect family.
End.

The room was still somewhat dim. You groggily opened your eyes, and the first thing rushing into your nose was a fragrance with a hint of sweetness. You thought it might be jam and bread, maybe other desserts, some oil aroma, or maybe it was freshly fried eggs. After all, you could even hear the faint sound of oil splashing and dancing.
Next came the crisp sound of a porcelain plate clashing against a glass tabletop. But the sound was very soft, clearly meant not to disturb you, who was dozing off in bed. Still, this meaningless yet subtle noise actually made you feel more at ease, or rather, you could immerse yourself in these sounds and fall back asleep. The fresh aroma enveloped you, and the occasional crisp sounds sounded more like a lullaby. You groggily closed your eyes, turned over, and decided to continue sleeping.
But while you lay in bed with your eyes closed, you felt a warm hand covering your eyes. Earlier, you were startled by the faint light shining through the curtains, but now it was pitch dark.
Then you hear Tenna's voice—gentle, and of course, with a touch of everyday uplift and joy: "Darling, it's time, time to get up...... I'll open the curtains. ”
You muttered softly from your throat, "But I still want to lie down a little longer......"
"You've been lying down long enough. If you don't eat soon, lunch will be postponed again." Tenna's voice sounded a bit troubled. In fact, you don't even know how he actually judges time; it's just that at some point, a set of rules was established here. At least when you follow these rules, you don't feel there's any problem.
"Hmm...... Then get up! "You tried to raise your voice to sober up, opened your eyes, and your eyelashes were still brushing in Tenna's palm, but what you saw was still a dull white, after all, your eyes were still covered."
It wasn't until you heard the curtains rustle and a faint light peeking through your fingers that you were truly sure it was time to get up.
…… After all, it seems that the brightness outside also symbolizes different times.
His hand was still on your eye, and after a while he carefully let go. You blinked a few times to get used to the light before putting on your clothes and stepping outside, heading to the dining table to eat.
The temperature of the food on the table was just right—clearly having calculated your wake-up time precisely. You picked up two slices of slightly crispy bread, spread blueberry jam, and slowly began to savor it. You squinted, savoring this simple yet warm breakfast, then saw Tenna sitting across from you, resting his chin on his hand, seemingly looking at you, though you couldn't catch his gaze.
His apron hadn't been taken off yet. Imagine whether you could still smell a bit of oil smoke on it, or maybe the sweet aroma of dessert. You picked up a scone with your fork, but instead of rushing to eat it, you hesitated for a moment before handing it to Tenna.
"Thanks for your hard work. You should have a bite too. You always have to watch me eat, and I feel a bit embarrassed." You stuck out your tongue a little embarrassedly.
Tenna's tone sounded as if she were flattered: "Oh? Me? Actually, it's okay if you don't have to consider me. This was originally prepared for you—" He even waved his hand to refuse, basically explaining everything.
You tilted your head slightly and looked at him: "I can't eat it anyway...... Besides, breakfast and such—shouldn't we all enjoy it together? ”
"Alright, alright, I'll have a bite." He sighed, followed your fork down, and bit into the scone. Still, that small piece was somewhat trivial to him, but he still chewed hard twice before swallowing.
"But it really does taste great." He coughed twice as he spoke, probably not wanting to praise himself. Sorry, maybe it was possible.
"Of course, I really trust Tenna's cooking. It's definitely delicious." You raised your eyebrows proudly.
Then the dining table fell silent again, with only the sound of knives and forks clashing on plates. Chewing on roasted bacon, you glanced at the black tea placed on the table, your eyes darting around. Then you picked up the teapot and poured a cup for Tenna, then a cup of black tea for yourself, along with two sugar cubes.
You stand up and push the cup of tea toward Tenna.
"Alright, stop staring at me while I eat! Have some tea!" You pursed your lips, a bit slurred, since you were still chewing on bacon.
Tenna picked up the cup of black tea and took a sip. He seemed a bit hesitant, but still chose to speak: "Your tea brewing skills are quite good." Of course, this sentence sounded sincere, though it sounded a bit forced.
"I didn't brew the tea, I just poured it. So judging by this, Tenna's cooking is the best!" As you spoke, you took a small sip of black tea. Honestly, this kind of daily routine played out in this room every day.
After dinner, you listen to the sparse sound of water and the clinking of bowls and plates coming from the kitchen. You know Tenna is probably cleaning, while you sit on the sofa, leaning your back against it, deciding to enjoy your own time—you casually pull a book from the nearby shelf, not even paying attention to its name, and just open it to look at it, since there are bookmarks inside.
But just then, Tenna suddenly poked her head out from the kitchen, mixed with the sound of running water. The emotion in his words was hard to discern, but you could still hear the sentence clearly: "Honey, don't sit down and read right after dinner!" You can start with something else! ”
You sigh, "Alright, you've actually heard this many times before. You can't sneak a book for a while."
Alright, alright, you know he's thinking of you. Reading directly would definitely be bad for your health—so you closed the book and placed it on the coffee table in front of you, tapped your waist, stood up, and chose to stroll around the room first...... Well, although there's nothing much to look at, you still find it especially interesting to look at the potted plants on the floor every day. Even though the changes aren't significant, you still look at them seriously, and at least you can spot some clues—this leaf has lifted by one millimeter compared to yesterday's waist, and new leaves are about to sprout on the branch over there.
You squatted down with interest to watch for a while, and only when you got tired did you knock your legs and stand up, choosing to take a casual walk in the room. At this moment, the sound of running water in the kitchen stopped. Tenna came out carrying a rag and wearing an apron. Although the dining table wasn't dirty, he insisted on wiping it down.
Seeing you, he instinctively asked, "Are you going out for a walk later?" Anywhere is fine. ”
You hesitated for a second, then shook your head: "No way, I still want to read a little first......
"Oh...... Then in the afternoon? Maybe you could watch some TV shows too? Some of the book's plots have already been made into movies. Can I help you search for them? ”
In this regard, you still insist: "No, some things can't be captured in movies!" Reading paper books is better, but if we go for a walk together in the afternoon, that's fine, right? Then come back and watch some TV shows, just treat it as a way to relax. ”
You think for a moment, then naturally plan the time ahead.
Tenna's voice was filled with joy: "I knew it...... You really won't give up watching my show! Don't worry, today will definitely be your favorite TV show too! ”
You smiled helplessly, estimating that time was about right, you jumped back onto the sofa, letting the soft sofa collapse wrap around your body. Then you leaned back against the sofa backrest: "Ah, of course, I believe in your choice!" "After all, we've lived together for so long, how could I not know each other?"
And you really like this kind of life. Even though you say nothing, you know deep down that this is your "perfect family."
Tenna felt that this kind of life was so wonderful—so good it even felt dreamlike and not real. Sometimes he wondered if this was some kind of fairyland or fairy tale that would wake up after the bell tolled. If that were the case, he would rather remain immersed in this dream forever.
He still did his usual routine, preparing meals at fixed times for three meals a day, calling you up to eat at fixed times, resting his chin on his chin with joy and happiness as he watched you eat. Of course, occasionally he enjoyed your feeding service—though all of it was made by his own hands, for some reason, the food you personally fed him always felt a bit sweeter. Even the bacon sprinkled with salt and pepper had a hint of sweetness in that moment.
Meals at fixed times, occasional schedule changes, and day-after-day sharing a bed, quietly getting up in the morning, carefully tucking you in, looking back every few steps to watch you lying peacefully, then wearing an unconscious smile as she prepares breakfast.
Then, when you're quietly reading or doing other things, he'll keep staring at you in a similar posture—since you can't notice his gaze, that's why he's so confident and bold.
Perhaps this is his "perfect family." After all, Tenna never dared to dream of such a life before, until you entered his life and felt that his former irritability and irritability could be easily soothed. As long as you were still by his side.
As long as you are still by his side.
—So actually, he was still a bit troubled. This feeling of distress had only recently emerged. The reason he felt distressed was actually because he realized your lifestyle habits weren't very good, which made him anxious.
But if that's all there is, he just needs to give appropriate reminders—when you instinctively sit down to read or go straight to sleep after eating, or when you sit in the same spot all day without leaving anything, or when you've stared at his screen for too long on a TV show.
All this requires just some appropriate reminders. After all, although it's not very healthy, it's okay to do this once or twice occasionally, and he is happy to indulge your behavior.
But what if—and that's not all?
Tenna knew your sleep wasn't very good, so she prepared medicine and capsules for you. He knew you liked reading and put all the things you loved first, knowing you weren't very fond of exercise, so his usual workout routes were quite short.
He noticed that your movements were always a bit unsteady, like accidentally bumping into the wall next to you, getting bumped by the table in front, or simply not noticing there was another layer on the bookshelf—or maybe you just didn't remember at all, but you always bumped your head up when picking up the book.
He would subtly grab your arm, pull you away from the wall, or let you stand steadily in the chaos. He would place his hand on the shelf so your forehead would only bump into his hand instead of hitting it directly. Later, he would simply place all the books you read on the upper shelf, clearing the bottom shelf so you wouldn't bump into it again.
But beyond that, it was far more than that. Although he was so careful and cared for this "perfect family" every day to keep it going, he could only watch helplessly as you swallowed that capsule, took a sip of water, and then probably choked—in short, he kept coughing, clutching his chest, bending over, showing no sign of stopping. All he could do was anxiously pat your back, watching your persistent coughing, and only feel anxious about it.
—Then, when your vision blurs and you still don't know what happened, the scene shifts to Tenna watching you pick up the capsule, ready to swallow it.
He was startled, snatched the capsule from your hand, and forced a couple of laughs: "Darling, I just remembered the capsule's efficacy might be a bit lacking. Let's start with another one today." ”
You glanced at him in confusion, but still nodded obediently, since you thought there was nothing wrong with his explanation.
Seeing that you showed no sign of doubt, Tenna finally let out a careful breath in his heart. Although he didn't know if switching to something else would lead to the same outcome, nor was he sure what had just happened—no matter what, he had to give you another one.
So this time, he brought you a steaming, freshly brewed potion, which even smelled a bit sweet.
You carefully swallowed the medicine, and this time there were no other problems. Tenna finally breathed a sigh of relief. After finishing the medicine, she lit the bedside lamp and read for a while before falling asleep. He stared at your quiet expression, watching your eyelashes flutter unconsciously, and looking at your face, gradually falling asleep as well.
At least, today was a perfect pass, right?
But the next day, as usual, he was preparing breakfast and was about to call you, when he saw you rubbing your eyes and walking out of the room. Maybe you hadn't seen the way clearly, or maybe you had misjudged the distance. In any case, you didn't see the threshold at the bedroom door. When you walked over, you didn't think to cross over and your body tilted forward and nearly collapsed, leaving you stunned as you stared at the ground so close to you.
Tenna fumbled over to catch you, but with a second left before you hit the ground, he was still a few steps away.
—Then, as the feeling blurred again, Tenna realized she was standing at the dining table again, still holding a plate. This time, she didn't hesitate again, put down the tray, and walked to the bedroom door to catch you, who was about to leave but was about to fall.
You looked up shyly and smiled at Tenna: "Sorry...... I didn't react ......"
As you spoke, your voice quieted.
"Of course it's okay, darling. No matter what, whenever it happens, I'll catch you." Tenna looked at the hair swirling on top of your head, gently stroked your head, and said this very softly.
No matter what, he breathed a sigh of relief in his heart. It seemed that this kind of time-reversal-like feature was indeed very helpful to him—at least he could confirm your status. And if he didn't make it in time, he would have other chances.
But he also felt a lingering fear—what if one day this ability suddenly disappeared? What if one day he wouldn't have time to hold you? What if, one day, relying on this ability, he could only watch you stop breathing in front of him? These were things he dared not even imagine.
But now, he could roughly tell that this regression would only trigger when you encountered danger, or even death. Either way, he was relieved, even joyful, because this way, you wouldn't have to experience pain—this kind of anxiety and fear would be better if only he could experience it.
The reason is that he confirms you actually remember nothing.
After all, if you remembered, you wouldn't look at him with that admiration, a bit of confusion, and a wet gaze. But he really enjoyed that look in your eyes.
Everything in the "Perfect Family" can still go on as usual, except for the tenna that silently relies on time rewinds to save you a lot of pain when you are completely unaware.
At least you know nothing, yet still think everything is as perfect as before, and that's enough for Tenna.
However, he still needs to think about what to do next; relying on time rewinding all the time is unrealistic...... He can't become dependent on this, and besides, there's always a sense of fear that he might lose you because of it.
After hesitating for a moment, he took out paper and pen, wrote something on the blank sheet, and then looked at the paper and nodded in satisfaction.
Tbc.

title: "Perfect Family" 2
content:
Immersed in reading, the morning quickly slipped by. After lunch, I took a short nap, nestled in the arms of the giant TV person and rested on the bed for a while. Drowsy and drowsy, time passed unnoticed, and soon it was afternoon.
You rubbed your eyes and saw Tenna still had a pitch-black screen. You couldn't tell if she was staring at you or something else, but you gently tapped the screen with your knuckles: "Oh...... Get up! We promised to go out for a walk this afternoon! After saying that, you actually sat up energetically, threw on your coat, and got ready to go out for a walk.
Tenna seemed to mutter a few words, but you didn't really hear what he was saying. You just tilted your head in confusion and looked at him: "Huh, what are you talking about?" ”
You really didn't hear clearly, and of course, you were genuinely curious about it.
But Tenna quickly shook her head: "Oh no, no, nothing—darling, just pretend I didn't say anything, it's nothing important." He clasped his hands behind his back, then gave you a smile. For some reason, you always felt like he seemed a bit nervous, but when you turned your head to look at him, you couldn't see anything. In any case, you just shrugged, then took his hand and gave a sincere smile.
Of course, his palm is huge, so you can't hold it. You just slip your palm into his palm, and then he naturally grips it tightly. It's warm and cozy, and not too light, not too heavy. In short, you've used this handshake posture countless times and are used to it.
Turn off the lights in the room and step outside. Outside is a bright lounge, where some employees are sitting on the sofa playing games, including the weather couple leaning together. When they see you, they smile and nod. You nod happily too, then pull Tenna out. He slows down a little with your pace, otherwise you won't be able to keep up with him.
However...... Out of curiosity, you still asked, "Tenna, are you not working today?" I remember you usually don't see you in the mornings and afternoons. "Although it's not very useful, probably, at these times you'll see Tenna active on stage, the spotlight shining on him, as if he never gets tired. Only the events of lunch and dinner mysteriously appear at your table. Sometimes it's steaming hot seafood baked rice, sometimes fennel paired with grilled lamb chops and a serving of pasta, and sometimes a chocolate brownie or caramel pudding on the side......
Well, you're actually curious about what time he actually cooks...... But that's his secret, and you won't ask too much! Some things just stay under the beautiful lie of the past, after all, things always seem this perfect on the surface.
Tenna seemed to stiffen for a moment, then you heard him give a couple of awkward laughs, but it was very fast, as if he didn't want you to notice: "Oh...... Oh! Honey, why are you asking that? Of course, I'm about to give my employees a break recently, so I took some time off myself. Plus, I get to have some free time to be with you. Don't you like this kind of thing?" As he spoke, he lowered his head, the pitch-black TV screen facing you, looking a bit aggrieved. The antenna drooped, and you felt as if he was staring straight at you.
—Of course, he knows he's just lying, and of course, he also knows that no matter what he says, you'll believe his words.
So you couldn't help but stand on tiptoe and pat his machine's shell: "Ah, of course I wouldn't like it! Actually, I really like these days...... As long as Tenna is always by my side, I feel great. I really like it, really enjoy being with you." Then you gently hugged him, lightly kissed the food on the dark TV screen, let go of him, and then slipped your hand into his palm: "Alright, let's not talk about that! Let's take a walk first. Standing still isn't really a walk......"
As you spoke, you quickened your pace and walked out, taking longer steps. Tenna followed right behind you, probably with a long gaze fixed on you. Although you were a bit puzzled why he wasn't sitting side by side with you, you know, he used to squeeze into a row with you, and sometimes even shrank down because holding his hand would be inconvenient.
Although you were a bit uneasy inside, it worked. In any case, you didn't say much. As usual, you walked around the corridor twice. Up ahead, it seemed like a concert was underway. Although you couldn't hear the singing, you did hear instrumental music—probably saxophone? You didn't know much about music or similar things, just curiously glanced over there and prepared to walk back.
"Let's head back now. Does it feel like it's about time?" You suggested, glancing back at him while you were at it.
Tenna nodded at you. Of course, the screen was no longer pitch black; she even showed the signature smile of a host. Maybe thinking about watching TV soon made him excited. In any case, you couldn't help but chuckle, probably unable to help yourself.
You shake your gripping hand: "Alright, we still have a lot to do anyway. It's okay to walk back slowly, right?" Oh...... Let's hurry up, I want to sit down and rest. "You mumble, grabbed his hand and walked back, then threw yourself hard onto the sofa, blinking as Tenna sat in front. In short—probably to protect your eyes, he was even known for his serious reputation, insisting on keeping some distance before watching TV. Although you wanted to say your eyesight wasn't a problem, he insisted on doing it. Well, you have to accept that.
The TV screen starts to change, you hug your knees, watching a movie play — "The Bridges of Madison Dream"? It's a romance film that's been around for years, you feel that way, but I have to say it's still quite good, though it struggles between family and true self love...... Forget it, anyway, this kind of feeling is beautiful, isn't it?
After watching this film, it's almost time for dinner. You all enjoy a red wine stew with beef together, then share a fruit tart on display. After dinner, you relax a bit, and it's time to sleep.
You lie on the bed, and the slightly smaller Tenna hugs you. You say goodnight to each other, turn off the desk lamp, and the room falls into darkness, and you both fall asleep.
—That's how it should be. When you wake up the next day, it's supposed to be the same routine. But after finishing breakfast and admiring the potted plants as usual, sitting on the sofa, you instinctively pull out the book you've been reading recently to continue, but a piece of paper falls out from the open page.
You picked up the paper in confusion and looked at what was written on it.
[1. Do not leave your room after 10 p.m
You cannot leave your room before 7 a.m
Medication must be taken at least half an hour before going to sleep
You must drink water first, then take the medication with the water
You must maintain a seated posture to drink liquids and take small sips
Posture must be maintained properly
Avoid the following ingredients: pepper, Sichuan peppercorns, mustard......
Do not touch objects with sharp properties
You can only leave the bedroom to eat at nine, twelve, or eighteen
Without anyone following, dangerous movements cannot be performed
No one follows strenuous exercise that cannot be done: sprinting, swimming, ......
A five-minute stand-up relaxation activity must be used at every hour of reading
Exercise should not be less than half an hour each day
You can't watch electronic devices for an hour before bed (not even TV!) (By the way, after this sentence, there's a little TV emoji showing tears)]
…… You pause for a moment, flipping through the paper to make sure there's nothing written on the back. Uh, obviously this looks like some kind of rule-based horror tale? But some of the words and sentences are a bit rambling, almost like some kind of reminder, making you want to laugh. And for no reason, the handwriting is a bit like Tenna.
Anyway, pick up this piece of paper and stand up, ready to ask Tenna.
Although he had written the paper based on his mental impression, he hesitated and hadn't decided where to put it, nor did he know if he needed to add more. After all, no matter what, the rules written on this note couldn't help you avoid all dangers, nor could they be all the instructions he could remember. He wished you wouldn't encounter any danger at all. If you got even a little hurt, Tenna would get nervous, even though those wounds might heal in the next second.
In any case, this tension was unlikely to dissipate, and Tenna decided not to take out the note for now—maybe he needed to add something to it. He just carefully hid the note, as long as it wasn't seen by you.
But...... What other way could he avoid danger from you? After all, Tenna wanted you to avoid these possible injuries without knowing anything, or maybe his protective instincts were just too strong. In any case, he did seriously think about what to do with the props he had placed in the background.
…… Oh, he just thought of it! Tenna picked up an empty capsule ball and happily raised it, even thinking he was a genius! To think of such a great method!
Isn't it enough that you can never get hurt? Isn't it enough to never let you leave his sight and to ensure you're always in a safe place? As long as you stay locked here, you'll never leave, and of course, you'll never encounter danger.
So he enthusiastically took advantage of your sleep to carefully put you into the capsule ball. He even lined it with soft plush so you wouldn't hurt yourself when you woke up or struggled. Then he went to prepare breakfast, humming off-key songs, imagining what would happen next. In short, he thought everything he had done was the best choice.
…… However, when he came back carrying the tray, he saw you sitting there holding the blanket, looking at him with a hint of disappointment and a cold gaze. Although he had long prepared himself for this, even though he had warned himself about possible reactions, seeing your look still felt like falling into an ice cave. It felt like a hole had broken through his heart, with only the cold wind rushing in, and his body stiffened in place. After a while, he forced a smile no different from usual: "Oh, darling, you're awake." ”
You nodded, "Yes, I'm awake." After that, you didn't say anything more. It seemed you had no intention of saying anything more.
…… He silently put down the plate, even set a table in front of the capsule toy, and then placed the steaming hot breakfast on it.
"Darling, I think you should understand what I'm doing...... I'm just, just afraid you'll walk into death somewhere I can't see, or encounter some other danger. I'm just afraid you'll be outside my protection. I don't want to lose you......" Tenna explained nervously. He knew this excuse sounded a bit forceful, but in such a short time, he couldn't come up with any good words.
You just nodded absentmindedly, probably not paying attention to what Tenna said, so Tenna quieted down, but the antenna hung down, and the dark screen pointed in your direction.
You picked up your knife and fork and ate a simple breakfast—still fried eggs with bread, with freshly fried bacon on top. Of course, there was a glass of milk nearby, but you didn't touch a bite, instead gnawing on the bread and fried egg as if venting frustration.
Tenna watched all this in a panic, of course he was uneasy, having no idea what the outcome would be.
Then, you collapsed headfirst onto the table. The scene shifted, and this time the time rewind was still very long, roughly ...... It was when he was about to pull you out and put you into the capsule capsule shell.
He stood by the bed, and even in the darkness, he could see your face clearly, your slightly fluttering eyelashes, because he had long since adapted to the darkness.
After hesitating for a moment, Tenna decided to try again, so he carefully picked you up, led you back to the capsule toy shell he had prepared, and then placed you inside.
This time he changed his story. When you woke up inside the capsule toy, Tenna squatted in front of the capsule and looked at you, saying seriously and persistently, "Darling, I think maybe if you step out of my sight, you'll somehow run into danger, so maybe this place is more suitable for you?" I promise, I'll do anything for you, and I'll make your life here as comfortable as possible. ”
Naturally, he still failed, the same ending, the same look. But this time, you gulped down two mouthfuls of milk before preparing breakfast. Then, for some reason, you suddenly started coughing, leaning on the table and coughing repeatedly. Tenna patted your back, trying to make you feel better, but it was useless. The scene blurred again, then reversed, and he stood by your bed once more.
Honestly, he knew that if he tried again, the result would be the same...... Tenna was troubled by this, but honestly, he no longer wanted to see those cold, disappointed eyes. Two times was enough; he no longer could handle a blow.
He still hopes you'll always smile, looking at him with warm eyes, and saying childish words like hugs and kisses. Tenna still feels that these ordinary yet somewhat childish moments of life are actually your whole life.
After some hesitation, he gently slipped into a corner of the blanket, hugged you, and smelled your faint scent—maybe the scent of shampoo. Tenna wasn't quite sure what those you occasionally used were, but in any case, he drifted off to sleep. But this time, he was at ease, in a sweet sleep, without those cold gazes or terrifying, possibly revived memories.
Naturally, you don't remember everything inside the capsule toy shell, and you still get up, eat, and laugh with Tenna as usual, deciding the day's schedule. That's the best thing you can do—you remember nothing, and Tenna hopes you remember nothing. But he also feels a subtle sense of disappointment, because you remember nothing, which means you have no idea what might happen, and he tries hard to hide it all—anyway, well, Tenna still hopes you know nothing, and he'll find a way to solve it properly.
All you need to do is keep that smile forever, gaze at him, and when he looks over, hold your face and look back happily.
So he hesitated for a moment, but still slipped that note into the book you've been reading recently. Of course, last night he had added a few more on the spot.
Then, with a hint of nervousness and unease, he started scrubbing the dishes. Fortunately, the sound of running water drowned out the noise outside, easing some of his inner anxiety. But waiting was the hardest time to endure, because Tenna knew you would definitely come over with that piece of paper to ask him. He didn't even hide much—he had written all those words himself, and you had definitely seen his handwriting.
But Tenna would never admit that she wrote it herself.
Oh my, he'd rather you think those are rules you really have to follow and enforce than think it's just a joke. Tenna was already trying her best to figure out how to avoid the dangers you encountered.
Then, he turned off the faucet, because he heard footsteps behind him. He knew you were coming, so he took off his gloves, took a deep breath, and turned to look at you.
You raise the paper and ask, "Tenna, this handwriting looks just like yours. You must have written it, right?" ”

title: "Perfect Family" 3
content:
Tennax you, split into dual perspectives, dividing lines, and from Tenna's perspective, there's more psychological depiction. In short, it might not be very useful (yeah, right).
…… By the way, I mixed in Bai Ye's personal touches, but this book is really good (. ）
——
You watch Tenna turn off the faucet, take off her gloves, then turn around and flash a bright smile at you, while you just tilt your head in confusion.
"What's wrong? I was just asking casually, why do you look so nervous? I'm not angry at you because it might be just a prank, and of course, I won't be sad because of a possible lie. After all, I believe you, so whatever you say, I will believe you." After saying this, you nodded. This is indeed your true thought, because you love him purely and sincerely, and naturally trust him sincerely.
Tenna, on the other hand, only appeared a bit inexplicably nervous and uneasy, but that state quickly disappeared, as if everything had just been her imagination.
"Oh no...... Darling, I'm just a little nervous! And of course, I have to take the question you raised seriously. After all, I can guarantee that this note never exists in my memory. So I was just thinking about this issue too! "As he spoke, he began waving his hands.
"Hmm...... Is that all? "You hesitated for a moment, looked at the note again, then confronted Tenna: "Are you sure you have absolutely no memory of this note?" But is this clearly your handwriting? ”
After all, you won't forget what Tenna's handwriting looks like—you've seen it many times.
"No—I have absolutely no memory of it! Maybe someone just copied what I wrote and then secretly tucked it into your book?" This time, Tenna just glanced at the note briefly, waved her hand, and began to deny it.
You blinked at him, determined not to expose his clumsy lie. Oh my god, you know, no one else could come to your house except the two of you, and besides—you never said you saw this note in a book, so how would he know that? And there's even a little emoji drawn on the back of the last note. You can tell the note was from Tenna, probably handed to him specially and stuffed into the book so he wouldn't accidentally notice.
But since he's trying hard to deny it, it proves he doesn't want you to expose him—at least right now—so you just chose to stay silent and then tolerate his lie. After all, some of the words on this note may seem strange, but...... It's still beneficial for you, so you don't think there's anything wrong with following them.
But you're still curious why Tenna wrote these rules, and why she strongly denies that he wrote them all himself. It seems his intention was to make you follow them. So...... Why is that?
With such doubts in mind, you decide to break the harmless rules above and try to see what might happen.
Now, you just nod to show you understand: "Alright! I understand...... I believe you wouldn't lie to me. You probably really don't know this paper, hmm...... I don't even know who wrote it......
You can clearly see Tenna's wild, guilty smile, so you can't help but want to laugh out loud. But the corners of your mouth lift twice, and in the end, you hold back. You don't want to be caught laughing by Tenna, or else this so-called rules and strange pretend game would have failed from the start, right?
In short, after putting away this paper, you leave the kitchen and sit back down on the sofa to continue reading. Then comes your usual lunchtime, walk, TV program, and finally dinner.
After dinner, you even glanced at the time. You know, there are several rules related to time: you can't leave your room after ten o'clock, which means you can't watch TV after about nine. No matter what, you decide to give it a try.
So you just sit on the sofa hugging your knees, watching Tenna pick out the film for you. It's very old, even in black and white, called 'Twelve Angry Men.' But it's actually pretty well made—it has both moral and reasoning and a detective plot. You watch it so intently, and as the ending approaches, Tenna suddenly stammers, "Darling, I think you probably can't keep watching." ”
You were interrupted, and the screen thoughtfully showed a pause button, so you glanced at it and saw it was already nine o'clock. Hmm, it was indeed this time—but you still looked at Tenna, tilted your head slightly, and asked, "Hmm, why?" ”
"Ah...... Huh? Why? There's no reason, I just think, uh, you should—no, you definitely need to rest! And the note you brought over this morning also said it, I saw it! You can't leave your room at ten o'clock, and you can't look at electronics an hour in advance, so...... It should be nine o'clock, yes, that's exactly the time you need to go to your room to rest. In short, you can't watch TV anymore! "He was gesturing with both hands to explain everything, while you just tilted your head and watched his actions. Honestly, this kind of thing really troubles you......
So you hesitantly said, "But there's still a short part left to finish. How about I finish the ending first?" It's only about ten minutes, please......" As you spoke, you put your palms together and bowed to Tenna, giving him a pitiful look full of pleading.
Tenna froze in place, and of course, his movements froze, since he rarely saw you like this. Usually, whenever you say something or make a request, he'll definitely do it and do his best to fulfill it. So this was actually the first time he'd seen you act like a request.
He suddenly coughed several times, as if he had choked. In fact, you and he both knew he wouldn't have choked: "Uh...... Ahem, okay, alright! Then let's finish watching this film! But after you're done, you have to rest! Darling, you can't do it if you don't get some rest. "He started rambling again, but the chatter stopped. He paused again and resumed playing the film that was about to end, while you sat on the sofa watching with great interest. After all, you were genuinely curious about what verdict these juries would ultimately deliver for the defendant, this boy—sure enough, it was a not guilty verdict.
As the cast list began to play, you stood up, still wanting more: "Alright, that's it! I should go back and rest now!" As you spoke, you stretched lazily and even yawned.
"Of course, of course, I can read to you for a while. What would you like to hear today?" Tenna now stands beside you again, carefully taking your hand. You glance at him sideways: "Ah, what are you listening to...... I don't really mind! Could you just read a little to me?" ”
Anyway, it's time before bed, so there's no need to read anything too seriously. If you want to appreciate it seriously, you'll place it on your bookshelf and read it word by word.
After washing up, lying on the bed, pulling up the blanket, you see Tenna pulling a book from the nearby shelf. The bedroom's bookshelf is full of books you've read before...... So it's okay to listen to him read; you might even be daydreaming.
This time, he randomly picked a copy of "White Nights." You still have a deep impression of this book, and you even like it very much—although the female lead parts from the male lead after the White Nights end and returns to her once promised fiancé, under those four White Nights, it was a clash of hearts, true love and unparalleled joy.
So, heart-to-heart collisions and genuine emotions will bring endless emotion, even though after the white night ends, it all seems like a vivid fantasy.
Listening to Tenna's slowing voice, you felt your eyelids grow heavy. Gradually, you closed your eyes and drifted off to sleep. But before you fully fell into darkness, you muttered to yourself: rules aren't necessarily unbreakable, after all, you clearly haven't touched any electronic devices for an hour before bed...... Hmm, I'll try something else tomorrow.
Tenna felt a small relief when she saw you didn't doubt you, just followed his guess. After all, he was still a bit scared and knew just how clumsy his lie was. So he was worried you'd keep pressing, but luckily you didn't do that, but instead trusted him.
Of course, he actually knows, even a bit arrogantly, that he knows you'll always choose to believe his words.
However, he was still a bit nervous and uneasy. If you really tried to explore these rules and ended up turning back time and forgetting everything, how would he stop you?
Fortunately, you didn't try anything else; the day looked just like any other day, which made him breathe a sigh of relief.
But when he plays a movie for you at night, he always feels heavy-hearted, because on one hand, Tenna knows to stick to the schedule, so even though he's watching you intently, he also gets distracted to check the time. On the other hand, he actually can't bear to spend that time with you, but since he's supposed to follow that rule and keep you away from danger—he has to be willing to, let go of unrealistic hopes.
Time ticked by, almost nine o'clock. His heart, which might not have existed before, beat faster with every passing second. At least he could hear it clearly. As for whether machines or TVs could truly have hearts, he didn't really know.
But when the hands hit nine, a clock automatically rings in his mind, and the time starts ticking. He frantically pauses the film and then starts urging you to rest and sleep.
But when asked why, Tenna was really stuck—uh, well, what should he say now? Forgive him, he's never lied, and of course, he couldn't have thought up words in advance. In fact, he doesn't want to deceive you, but to protect you, to let you spend this time in peace, without even knowing, he decided to keep it from you.
So, he just said he had read what was written on that note in the morning, and did it to help you follow the rules. He absolutely wouldn't dare admit that those rules were written by himself—in fact, even the time of nine o'clock was determined by him, since at ten o'clock you should be huddled and sleeping.
But because of your request, he still played the TV a little longer for you. Guilt and the pleasure brought by your prayers surfaced in his heart, and Tenna could only pray that you couldn't see anything. So after the movie ended, she turned off the screen, left it pitch black, pulled you back to her room, then sat down with her back to you, grabbed a book from the shelf, and began reading it to you.
Maybe it's to make amends, maybe for other reasons, or maybe it's just a little guilty. Or perhaps, at this moment, forcing yourself to read something to clear your mind is actually a good thing.
At least Tenna did this: he lowered his volume, slowed down his reading, and read aloud to you bit by bit. As he read, his emotions drifted, and the more he read, the heavier his mood became.
…… He doesn't like this story. Why, after pouring out their feelings to each other, does the girl still leave with her fiancé, whom she had been waiting for for a fulfillment during the day? Why is it that, in the end, the so-called dreamer remains empty, clinging to the air and continuing to sink into fantasy? Only those few days of love are real, so why does the boy choose to give up instead of pursuing this kind of love?
If it were him, he would never choose to give up. Since love had arisen, since it was an unforgettable affection, he should fight for it no matter what. As for what the outcome would be—as long as he worked hard to change the ending, that would be enough. Sweet and fulfilling—this is the ending it should have.
He doesn't know why you like this book. It's precisely because you like it so much that Tenna specially organized your bookshelf and placed it in a prominent spot, selecting it to read aloud to you.
But when he stopped speaking, he heard your shallow breathing. When he turned to look, you had already closed your eyes and drifted into a peaceful sleep, apparently asleep for quite some time.
So Tenna stopped reading, carefully softened her movements, stuffed the book back onto the shelf, tidied it up a bit, then crawled under the covers, turned off the dim desk lamp, then turned around and gently hugged you as you fell asleep—if you used too much force, it might wake you up.
It wasn't until the next morning that he woke up on time, and Tenna was almost jolted awake—he had a dream, and honestly, even after waking up, he had already forgotten what the dream was about. But when he woke up, seeing you still sound asleep, he couldn't help but let out a sigh.
…… He couldn't remember exactly what he had seen, only vaguely remembering that it was probably blood, blood, and endless blood. He was terrified, as if waking up with a fear of losing everything. But the moment he saw you, all that fear vanished, leaving behind only a faint sense of comfort and warmth.
Sure enough, only by constantly watching you and being with you can you truly feel that warmth and comfort. He carefully opened the blanket to prevent the chilly morning air from disturbing your sleep, then Tenna changed clothes, put on an apron, and went to prepare breakfast for you.
The bread was baked in a bread maker, buttered with butter and eggs crackling in a small frying pan. The golden, slightly jiggling soft-boiled egg was placed on a plate, slightly tarred on the outside. Several sausages and bacon baked in the oven were brought out, along with freshly washed lettuce that was still dripping with water as garnishes. Besides that, the sweet aroma of flour flavor also filled the air. Scones and waffles were baked separately on a plate, topped with a bit of cream and condensed milk, served with freshly brewed black tea, and breakfast was ready.
Tenna glanced at the time; it was usually the time he prepared breakfast, still a while before you fully woke up and reached the dining table. He timed the time and said he would wake you right at seven o'clock, so that by the time you changed and washed, everything would be just right.
But before Tenna could wait for the clock to reach seven, he saw you rubbing your eyes as you walked out of the room. He widened his eyes and walked toward you—but before he could get there, Tenna realized you probably hadn't seen the way well or something, kicked straight into the doorframe, and then staggered forward.
…… If only he had changed the rules so that if he didn't call out, you couldn't leave the bedroom in the morning. Tenna was frustrated, but he still hurried forward, feeling a lingering fear. If he couldn't catch you now and had to set back at this moment, everything would be terrible.
Fortunately, this time he caught you smoothly, and the time rewind effect didn't trigger anymore. Maybe he ran fast enough to do all this. Luckily, this time he didn't just watch you fall, nor did he accomplish anything while you were in danger.
Tenna exhaled, steadying her heavier breathing. He couldn't help but tighten his grip on you, as if clutching a lost treasure tightly.
Only you blinked, confused. From this angle, you couldn't see Tenna's expression, but you could feel his anxiety and unease. Although doing this move from this angle would be a bit difficult, you still awkwardly reached out and patted his back. Hmm, it really was a bit hard too.
"Alright, I'm still here perfectly fine. What's wrong? It's like I'm dead." You said with a smile.
Tbc.

title: "Perfect Family" 4
content:
Although you were a bit puzzled about how Tenna's face turned so ugly in that instant, you had no interest in pressing further. Of course—probably out of respect, you knew Tenna was definitely hiding something from you, and you were waiting for him to take the initiative to confess everything to you.
"Oh...... Darling, it's nothing, I'm just too nervous. "Because you're being held by Tenna, you can't see his expression clearly, only hear his voice as if forcing a smile.
In short, even though you wanted to pull away from this embrace, he still held you tightly, and you could feel his body trembling. In short, it was as if he was afraid of losing you because of it—at least that's how you felt. But why did he react this way? You were a little confused, but in this position, you could only pat his shoulder.
"Alright, anyway, you've confirmed that I'm still here perfectly fine! You can see me, hear my voice, and touch me—doesn't all of this prove that I'm real? In short, I won't suddenly disappear. I've carefully planned what we'll do in the days ahead." "Your voice is lively. At least you can feel his body no longer trembling. Maybe his emotions have calmed down and he's let go of you.
But when you look at him, he's still a pitch-black screen, and you can't see anything.
