Gradually, the TV also quieted down, no longer making any noise.
In fact, you don't really understand why you live. You are just living, just learning, just moving forward. You don't understand the meaning of this until you get into university and on the day you receive your admission letter, curiously stepping into your bedroom, which is somehow filled with black smoke.
—Then, you came into this world, and from the moment you saw him, you fell irresistibly in love with Tenna. But you never had the courage to say this somewhat bittersweet feeling.
He always mocks you, and you always forgive him even though you cry, and then you repeat the same process over and over. Perhaps it's time to break this cycle.
After all, now that you've stepped out of the exit, you're standing again in your room, looking at that TV that was once abandoned, with its antenna wrapped in bandages after your careful repairs, and through the reflection on the screen, you see yourself.
Then you slightly bent down and hugged the TV.
“…… Tenna, long time no see." Your voice choked with emotion. You sniffled, wanting to cry, but mostly guilt. So you had ignored Tenna for so long, missed so many words from him in the past, but you felt his antenna gently touch you, then you lowered your hand and looked at his screen.
“…… Just a minute ago, we parted ways. Did your memory have trouble again? ”
You break into a smile through your tears, wipe your own tears, and even though he's become like this because of neglect in previous years—it's okay, Tenna is Tenna.
"I didn't, I just ...... Talking about myself at fifteen, and with you, long time no see. ”
After saying this, the TV screen went pitch black again, and then he slowly typed a few words.
“…… Long time no see. So, are you here to fulfill your promise back then? ”
You know what he's talking about—he's talking about the promise you made to always be together, the promise you made to make TV the bride.
And you nod vigorously, wiping away your tears: "Yes, I've come to fulfill my promise, I love you...... tenna。 As you spoke, your voice quieted and your face turned red, but you awkwardly lowered your head and scratched your own face.
You touch the outer shell of the Tenna, and it seems a bit hot too.
"Alright." This time, he quickly agreed to your request.
You rummage through your closets and find a poorly fitting black suit in the house. Put it on, then find a white tulle dress and veil, and cover Tenna with a wedding dress. This is a mismatched bride TV, a wedding that is also out of place. After all—this isn't a proper marriage, nor a serious audience, only you two take it seriously.
You cleared your throat and simply went ahead to deliver a piece of completely made-up wedding vows: "Whether in health or in sickness, whether in wealth or in poverty, whether in happiness or in sorrow, I will always be by Tenna's side. I vow to present all the beauty and joy to you and me. I vow to cherish this relationship, whether it be friendship, love, or family affection. I vow... to always be with Tenna, because this is a unique, special television on which I have invested infinite feelings. Because this will be my only friend, family, and lover."
After saying this, you hurriedly hung a relatively large, crude plain ring on Tenna's antenna. Forgive yourself—you had been searching for these items for a long time.
Then you kissed Tenna.
He seemed to be stunned for a moment, and then text quickly flashed across the screen in various combinations: "Whether in health or in sickness, whether in aging or in poverty, Anton Tenna will always be by Y/N's side. Anton Tenna is and will only be Y/N's family, friend, and lover."
You waited until the characters finished flashing, then put a ring on your own left ring finger as well. Then, feeling a bit embarrassed, you scratched your cheek and leaned in to kiss Tenna again. You could feel his screen and casing heating up, while you just smiled sincerely, removed the mismatched veil, and then put it on your own head.
After a while, you saw another line of text appear on the TV screen: "...I love you. I love you with all my heart."
And you just nodded, because you had known this truth for a long time, and you smiled as you said: "I love you too."
Then you touched the TV's antenna, finally reconciling all your inner knots, and walked briskly toward the entrance of the dark world. It was time to go back—it was time to see the true other side of your lover.
With this thought, you quickened your pace and ran through the gate of the dark world, then fell into an embrace.
You looked up to see it was Anton Tenna, still with a tense, expressionless face, and you noticed that his left ring finger was wearing that somewhat large ring. You thought these plain rings were probably bought by your fifteen-year-old self during a youthful crush—ah, indeed they were, because back then you were nervously planning how exactly you would marry the television.
You just smiled and tiptoed. Tenna still looked unhappy, but he obediently lowered his head. You put the veil on his head, looking a bit mismatched.
You just smiled, lifting your eyebrows: "Tenna... how about we have another wedding?" This time there would be an audience: all the employees of the TV world would be spectators at this wedding.
Tenna just silently nodded, staring down at you, then coughed twice. He lowered his head to bite your lips, lightly sucking twice before letting go, and hugged you tightly, as if you might run away in the blink of an eye.
You, on tiptoe, held the TV's head in both hands and kissed the screen, smiling: "Mm, I love you too."
END.

title: Game Time 1 (dntx you)
content:
Maybe there's OOC, dntx you. By the way, I was really so angry I cried while writing......
——
"Oh dear...... So boring...... You lie on the sofa complaining, swinging your legs casually, then bury your head in the sofa.
Of course—no one cares about you, or rather, the Dark People don't care about you. After all, you know what kind of person Anton Tenna is in this world. If she allowed you to stay here and cause trouble, that's more or less. Although you don't even know why he allowed you to stay here, it's probably because the Dark Folk are naturally caring for the Light Ones.
You didn't care about any of that—since no one answered you, you simply looked up, turned over, and sat back down on the sofa. Then you immediately saw Tenna sitting on the leather chair on the other side, the screen pitch black, as if she hadn't noticed what you were doing at all.
You couldn't help but feel speechless, walking over with your hands on your hips and looking down at him—well, that's not possible, since he's only about as tall as you when he's sitting down. In fact, you need to lift your head slightly to see him clearly.
You stand on tiptoe, a bit annoyed, trying to grab his antenna, but the next second his screen lights up, and the two antennas shake and slip away from your hand.
He looks at you expressionlessly: "What do you want to do?" ”
You saw his expression shrink slightly. Whether you said it or not, you were still a little afraid of him—after all, you knew he wasn't easy to talk to, but you still straightened your back and stared straight at his screen—after all, you couldn't see his eyes.
"Hmm, ahem, because it's too boring, I've decided to requisition your TV screen for gaming! After all, besides your TV, there's no other TV in your lounge that can be used." You put your hands on your hips and announced, even though you didn't know why, despite the room being meant for rest and entertainment, there was nothing else except the sofa—oh, and there's this one you instinctively found a bit annoying.
"What game?" His voice was cold and indifferent, and you couldn't help but take two steps back—after all, you started to regret coming to him directly. If you'd known, you should have looked for a TV somewhere else first. Anyway, there must be other TVs with big screens in this world, so why face such a ...... A guy you can't even quite put your finger on.
You pull out those few game CDs on you, hmm...... A fighting game, a two-player game, no need for this, you can't find anyone to play with you. A two-player survival game...... It's probably a drifting adventure on the sea, kind of like Life of Pi...... No, single-player is a bit too difficult, you can't play it. Two-player cooperative puzzle game...... Actually, you're quite tempted, but you sneak a glance at the guy in front of you and finally snort coldly in your heart, not asking if he wants to play games with you! He's really annoying; who knows what he'd say if we played together......
In the end, you chose a single-player adventure game—a simple Japanese RPG, a classic Dragon Quest story. After searching for a long time, you finally found a game disc you thought was quite interesting, then raised it high, your eyes sparkling: "This one!" "I want to play this!" Here, here you go. "You hand it to Tenna, looking at him expectantly.
Actually, Tenna had already noticed your sneaky glance earlier—he really wanted to say something more, but held back. After all, he knew that what he said was probably something you didn't want to hear, and for now, he didn't want you to leave here angry.
Tenna took the disc. I don't know exactly how he operated it, but he handed you a game console, then sat down opposite you on the sofa. He held the TV head and started projecting the game screen to you, while you happily sat cross-legged on the sofa and pressed buttons to start your adventure story.
Although there is a lot of textual storyline, this game still tests puzzle-solving thinking and skill, since it's somewhat of a 2D platforming puzzle-solving adventure game, and there are quite a few small monsters to clear along the way.
You seriously solve the puzzles along the way; those levels are a piece of cake for you—but in terms of combat controls, it's unclear whether your reflexes are slow or ...... The combat system in this game isn't very well designed. After all, you don't feel any impact at all, and the controls feel a bit sluggish. You even suspect it's a bit of a transmission issue, since pressing a button usually delays a little before the character actually acts.
Once again, the character dies. After the familiar GameOver CG, you purse your lips but don't lose heart. Instead, you regroup and decide to do it again. After so many times, you have to remember the boss's move moves and what you should do next.
But—while you were focused on attacking the boss, you heard Tenna's voice, casual and tinged with mockery: "...... Looks like you're bad at fighting games, no real skill. ”
He just watched you die several times, and even he knows how to get through it.
You choked for a moment, distracted by what he said, your hand instinctively trembled. The character who could have perfectly dodged the boss's finishing blow and landed the final blow shifted, landing in an inaccurate spot, and was killed by the boss's strafing fire. The gameover CG reappeared on the screen.
You angrily slammed the controller onto the sofa: "Yeah, I know I'm terrible. I've never been good at combat—but, but I was about to clear it just now, and it was you who suddenly said something that distracted me!" You started to blame him. After all, you were very self-aware, and you knew you were bad at playing. But as long as you enjoyed the game, that was enough. You didn't mind trying a few more times to clear it.
But you were originally quite interested, but after hearing that one sentence, your enthusiasm suddenly faded. Tenna just snorted coldly: "I've been watching all along, and your gaming skills really aren't great." ”
You glared at Tenna with red eyes—well, you don't even know if he actually saw it. You just raised your voice and said, "Bad at it, that's bad! If I try a few more times, I'll clear it. If you keep talking......"
After saying that, you still press the confirm button and decide to restart and challenge the boss again. But for some reason, after this restart, the screen actually starts to garbage, black-and-white noise appears on the TV screen, and even—intermittently and suddenly goes black. You try to control your character forward, triggering the boss again, but this time, because of the garbled screen and black screen, the character dies quickly.
Accompanied by the sound effect of death, Tenna's slightly mocking voice said, "I thought after so many times, you would remember it completely." ”
“…… The boss's jumping and moving positions are different! Even if I remember his attack order, I can't always guess where he moves! "You said angrily, feeling like your rage was almost full, but you still held back and started another round. This time, the screen was completely guttered. You didn't know if he was deliberately going against you. If he hadn't finished this boss and cleared the game, your intuition would have been that he wouldn't hand over the game disc so easily. You'd have already run the entire dark world looking for other TVs."
You puff out your cheeks, holding your breath as you control your character forward. Indeed, you've fought many times, so you have memorized the controls and map—you cleared that boss with a garbled screen and no visible scenario.
Tenna also raised her voice, speaking in a slightly surprised tone: "Oh? Isn't this something you can do?" ”
“…… Yeah, but if I hadn't died so many times before, how could I have done it! "You dropped the game console. Anyway, you've cleared this game, and you don't plan to play anymore. Besides, you just wanted to pass the time, but now you've been holding in all your anger, so you're completely fed up and not bored at all.
You feel like you're about to cry from anger—but in the end, you just step forward and pound the TV's head hard to vent your anger, your eyes red. You don't want to cry in front of him anymore, but you still have some shame: "Broken TV!! I'm not playing with you anymore, I'll go find another TV to use. I refuse to believe there are no other televisions in this TV world!" ”
You looked at the decorative screen in front of you, seemingly getting even more imposing, and you didn't care what else he would say—in short, it was probably something unpleasant. Anyway, you rushed out the door—yes, you pulled down the lounge door too, and you wanted Tenna to sit there and enjoy the cold wind!
But after running a short distance, you stop, panting, sniff twice, wipe the tears streaming down your eyes, and sob twice. You feel wronged, but you also know that if you really tell Tenna, at most he'll just apologize stiffly. But—but you don't want that. If things end up unpleasant, why not just do it well from the start? If you end up going our separate ways, then not meeting at first is probably the best choice—at least that's what you think.
You don't want a rigid apology, you don't expect that kind of apology—but if he comes after you to apologize, it's not that you can't forgive him for now.
You just ...... You just want to give him another chance. Even though you always tell yourself that this is the last time, there's nothing you can do—who told you not to really be ruthless with him? Who told you to ...... to like this guy? You don't even know why you like him; maybe this is just the origin of unpredictable love.
So your steps slowed down more and more, curling up in a corner and quietly crying. You felt a bit awkward, hoping Tenna would catch up and find you, but also wishing he never came back, so you could tell yourself that it really was time to give up.
Until you sneak around this corner, sneaking around and spotting a deep blue figure.
TBC.

title: Game Time 2 (dntx you)
content:
You sniffled, feeling even more wronged, wanting to cry your heart out without caring why you were acting recklessly—fine, fine, you don't even know if crying would help, but your eyes rolled around, then you sobbed loudly, wiped the corners of your eyes, and sobbed loudly, choking and sobbing, crying until you could barely breathe. Just like every time before.
And just like every other time, the TV head turned around and walked toward you after hearing the sound. His screen was pitch black, and no one understood what he was really feeling about. And you didn't care, since he made you cry because of it, why care about all that?
Tenna squatted down in front of you, your face covered in tears and cheeks flushed from crying. His screen was still pitch black, but you knew very well that this was probably the biggest concession he could make right now. You sniffed, quieted down a bit, but still sobbing, then reached out and grabbed his antenna—avoiding the spot where the wound had been before, then shaking it wildly.
"I hate you...... I hate you the most, I hate you the most! Big villain! "You let out your emotions recklessly, uttering completely sarcastic remarks. Yes, you have tried to stop liking him...... But you can't do it. Maybe, in love, the first person to fall in love is always the one who gives in? You don't know.
Tenna just lowered the TV head a little, letting you hold the antenna and shake it. He felt his mind shaken, and as the antenna shook, the sea inside also wavered. He saw your sadness and your affection. He knows...... You love him.
So he wants to keep you, probably just because of a simple, simple wish. He doesn't know if he loves you; he just can't bear to give up, but he's unwilling to face these things—he's always been aware. He just feels he can't do that—he can't love you. After all, if you're just deceiving him, and leaving after everything is over, then what will Anton Tenna do?
So at this moment, he just lowered his head, letting you hold the antenna, casually, a bit coldly, and a bit stiffly saying, "Mm." ”
Then he tugged your hips and picked you up. You curled up in his arms, and he turned to walk back toward the lounge.
The pitch-black screen finally lit up again, but the corners of his mouth were still curved. He touched the tip of his nose, not knowing why.
You were stunned for two seconds, then naturally let go. Then you snapped back to reality, blushing, slapping Tenna's screen and shouting, "You...... What are you doing! Put me down!" You slapped your palm until it was red, but he showed no particular reaction. You spoke with a sobbing voice, while he kept his eyes straight ahead, speaking in a hoarse, somewhat cold tone: "Why should I listen to you?" ”
You're stuck. Indeed, he doesn't need to listen to you—after all, you have nothing to do with him. Still, your face flushed: "But...... But you can't do that! I don't like it this way! "Actually, you're feeling guilty. You don't even know if what you say will actually work—it hasn't been like this before. Most of the time, it's only after you faint from crying that he comes to find you. By the time you wake up, you'll already be lying in the lounge under a blanket. If you ask him, he'll say it was pippins who covered you up.
But he didn't answer you because he walked quickly. By now, he was back in the lounge, decisively sat down on the sofa, then sat across from you holding the TV's head. His screen went pitch black again, and then another scene flashed before appearing. It was a puzzle game you bought some time ago but never had time to play. You've always loved this series of puzzle games, and now that the sequel came out, you naturally bought it.
You glare at the unresponsive Tenna, suspecting he's doing it on purpose, but you still pick up the controller and start controlling the detective character on the screen—better not to go against the game.
Emotions come and go quickly. You quickly become fully immersed in the game. However, this sequel is actually a combination of open world exploration and puzzles. You're a directionally challenged person who searched for a long time in the game before finally finding your way. Anton Tenna kept watching your movements, and finally, unable to resist, the TV started playing again: "You don't look very smart, just spinning in place. Aren't you afraid of getting dizzy?" ”
“…… None of your business! How well I play the game has nothing to do with you. "You grumbled and took a detour for more than ten minutes before finally finding the right direction.
"It matters. I can't stand seeing such a dumb detective on my TV screen." He said. Alright, even though how you want to play the game has nothing to do with him, he's happy to watch you sit here a little longer—just a little longer, to focus intently on him. But since you've been lost all along, you open your phone to start looking up guides, figuring out the right route, while Tenna suddenly feels bored.
It took a lot of effort to calm down—or rather, you know that's just how he is. What just happened was a silent reconciliation between you two. But now you threw the controller aside, stood up angrily, and shouted, "You can't stand it! That other TV always works! I need to find a TV that won't disturb me while I'm gaming!" Saying that, you walked past him and tried to walk outside. Yes, I don't know why he threw you on the sofa opposite the lounge door, and you sat at the doorway. The next second, Tenna's big hand grabbed the back of your neck and easily lifted you up.
You frown, swinging your arms and legs back and forth, trying to shake yourself off, but Tenna's hand holds you firmly, and no matter what, you can't reach the ground.
"What do you want! I already said I hate you...... You want me to stay here—don't you feel bad yourself?" You felt like crying again, sniffled, but tried to stay calm as you spoke.
Tenna's screen went black again, he turned his head, and you felt he was watching you.
His voice was a bit stiff: "In the world of television, besides me, there's no other television." ”
Then he put you down.
You were incredulous, turned your head to look at him: "Why? Isn't this the TV world?" ”
"This is a dark world built from your home." His voice was flat, without any ups and downs. You paused, then thought about it and realized it was true—you had bought this somewhat damaged TV when collecting scrap before. Although you didn't watch much shows, you still had many game discs left unfinished. Later on, inexplicably, a dark world appeared.
"Oh...... Then I'll go back to the Light World to play games. At least you won't be able to talk." You muttered a few words, then prepared to find the exit from the Dark World. Honestly, playing games in the Light World is more fun. In the Dark World, you feel like you're just being the puncher every day.
Tenna didn't react, just moved a bit and blocked the lounge door: "You can't go back to the world of light." "If you return to the world of light—then what does he even think he is?" And he didn't want you to find out that he'd already had his staff lock the doors to the dark fountain and the main entrance. For now, you can't go back.
"You said if you won't let me go back, I can't leave...... Step aside!" As you spoke, you tried to pull Tenna's heavy mechanical body away, but unfortunately, you couldn't. You didn't even shake him in the slightest. You're so angry you want to kick him twice, but you're afraid you'll hurt your own foot.
His screen lit up. After a brief channel switch, the TV screen froze back on the game screen. This time, the game map opened without receiving your instructions and marked the correct destination markers. He had just checked the game channels that were still available. Fortunately, there were indeed some guides for this game, so he marked the guide as provided.
Your movements pause for a moment, then you look up hesitantly at the TV screen. To be honest, you don't understand why Tenna is doing this, but he just grabs the controller you just dropped and puts it back into your hand. Instinctively, you press the joystick as the detective character runs forward, gradually approaching the destination.
You pouted. If that's the case, then you could keep playing...... But you felt a bit awkward: "...... Fine, I want yogurt, but you're blocking the door, I can't get out." You started awkwardly changing the subject. Although you did pull the door away, Tenna was big enough to sit here and blocked the entrance, not letting you out.
Tenna didn't move, just pointed to the small door beside her: "There's a small door in the lounge. You can go get it yourself." ”
“…… Is it good? ”
"I don't know, I haven't tried it before."
"How long have you been sitting there?" You walked through that small door, and as soon as you opened it, you sneezed a few times. You never expected that the kitchen was covered in dust.
This question made Tenna hesitate for a moment: "...... About three or four years ago?" "Never replaced them...... Ah, a few years ago, they did replace a batch when he first arrived at this house. Back then, you would still excitedly hold the TV and say you liked it the most.
But later, you never said those things again.
You stuck out your tongue and closed the small door: "I don't want ...... It's been spoiled for ages, hasn't it? I want you to get me fresh yogurt! Preferably with a lower viscosity, I'm thirsty!" You started pointing around fiercely.
Then Tenna took out a cup of warm water and handed it to you: "Then you should drink more hot water." "After all, you feel thirsty.
You choked, then glared at him again: "No, I want yogurt, go get it!" "Actually, you just wanted to sneak out of the lounge while telling him to do something...... Somehow, ever since he took you back to the lounge, your sixth sense has been alerting you.
TBC.

title: Game Time 3 (dntx you)
content:
You glared angrily at Tenna sitting there, then banged his TV screen twice.
“…… Let me out!" "You don't want to make any more excuses, so just be honest. Anyway, you're not in the mood to play games right now...... Even if he's already marked the path for you, you still don't want to keep playing.
Tenna really did turn back into a pitch-black screen. He stood up, looking down at you, and you instinctively took two steps back, thinking you really didn't need to be afraid—after all, control of this TV was still in your hands! So you pouted and looked at him with your head held high.
"Then I'll go with you." His voice was hoarse, a bit cold, and deliberate.
You can't help but feel a bit scared, since such a big TV is following behind you, but soon, you can't care about those things anymore. You run to the kitchen not far away and grab a box of fresh yogurt, while Tenna follows behind you at a leisurely pace. His footsteps are especially clear, making it impossible for you to run quickly or shake him off, because he always manages to keep up with you.
You slurped your yogurt and tried several twists and turns, finally reaching the entrance where you once came from the world of light. Although the door was tightly shut, you still happily stepped forward and pulled the doorknob—the door was locked and wouldn't open.
You pause for a moment, and Tenna steps forward, standing in front of you to block the door.
“…… No, you can't go back." He thought for a moment, but finally spoke so firmly. To be honest, Tenna had thought about quite a lot. At this moment, he should have begged the Lightfolk to keep watching him, to beg the Lightfolk to stay here and immerse themselves in the fun of the game. He could no longer tolerate losing—but he didn't want to do it either, so all he could do now was look down at you and say those cold, cold words.
You glared at him angrily: "Why should I! Why do you make decisions for me on your own...... I—when I get back, I'm going to replace your broken TV!" This statement sounded a bit uncertain, since you didn't know when you'd finally return to the world of light, to go home—even though you were the only one at home, that was a place where all your sense of security existed, a place where you could feel at ease. As for family...... You no longer had that kind of thing, ever since they wanted to abandon you for your brother.
Tenna stepped forward, closing in on you two steps. You instinctively swallowed a couple of mouthfuls, feeling a bit guilty, and stepped back two paces, but still looked at him with a stubborn attitude.
His voice seemed a bit urgent—maybe it was just your imagination, your fantasy, since you were nervous right now.
“…… Change the TV? Do other TVs really know your preferences so well? He finished speaking rapidly, then fell silent again. You don't know why the screen stayed black, or why those two antennas seemed to have just dropped for a moment before quickly rising again.
"Anyway, you can gradually learn about your preferences. I usually play those games often, so I'll know if I switch to another TV." You muttered softly, your voice growing quieter and quieter, because for some reason, he was bent over. The pitch-black screen leaned close to you, and you couldn't help but feel scared.
"Do other TV shows understand your hand fetish?" For some reason, you find his voice a bit eerie, eeri.
"So what...... If you lose, you'll just start over again. At least you won't be like you, saying a few words to me just because you can't beat me!" You glared at him twice, then covered your mouth. You know you've been speaking quite boldly lately—after all, this scary-looking TV wasn't trying to stop you.
"You only want a silent TV?" For some reason, after saying this, he fell silent as well.
"Right...... That's right! I want to play the game properly, I don't want to be disturbed—oh, even if it's a TV person! "You muster up the courage and shout loudly, closing your eyes.
“…… You don't need to return to the world of light. "After the unsettling silence, you only hear these words, then you feel yourself being lifted up, and when you open your eyes to look, you find yourself sitting on Tenna's arm.
"Put me down! It's not like I can't walk on my own!" You tried hard to kick your legs twice, but it didn't help, while Tenna just talked to herself.
"If you go back, you'll be alone too. Why not stay here...... Don't you think that's great?" It sounded like a question, but he just spoke in Chen Dataset's tone, very certain. Probably because he's certain you'll stay here.
"So what...... I'm doing fine on my own. "You muttered quietly, not knowing why he was walking so fast, but once again returned to the lounge and put you down on the sofa. He handed you the game controller, then sat at the door again, propping up his head on the TV and reopening the game screen.
You threw that box of yogurt on the ground during your struggle. You felt a bit regretful you hadn't finished it, so you smacked your lips, propped your chin up and boredly controlled your game character to reach your destination. After pondering for a while, you finally deduced the truth behind the incident and successfully solved the case.
You set the next side quest as a tracking item, and immediately a navigation path appeared before your eyes. Only then did you realize that Tenna had already marked the destination markers on the map. You cleared your throat twice, wanting to thank him, but...... He was so quiet it was almost eerie, making you hesitant to speak.
Although it was a bit bumpy, you eventually reached your destination. This case was relatively simple, you solved it quickly, and then it seemed to trigger the main quest—well, the marked points still appeared on the map.
I have to say, even though you're bored and playing games, time still flies by—it's just that you're not used to it. After all, Tenna has been quiet for so long that you can't help but ask, "Why did you suddenly stop talking?" ”
"This is your request." For some reason, you somehow sensed a hint of sarcasm in that sentence.
“…… Anyway, thank you." You cleared your throat twice and touched your nose. Although it was indeed your request, suddenly losing your voice made you feel a bit lonely.
After all, in this dark world, no one plays with you. Except for this TV—only this one. The other Dark People somehow run away as soon as they see you.
"Oh." He answered you very quickly in a short voice.
You tapped your controller; the game screen was still loading. Next up was a cutscene CG, but you didn't want to watch. You hesitated for a moment and asked, "But in the dark world, I'm also alone......"
Just being honest, or maybe you're just making things up.
You hear Tenna snort coldly, half mocking: "Are you ignoring something that exists?" ”
“…… Yes, yes, you are here, but days like this are no different from when I am in the Light World. "Because there's nothing to do, you play games every day in the Light World. Anyway...... Let's talk about the future later. When you were in the Light World, you were clearly facing this TV every day too.
Oh, you just said in a fit of anger that you want to replace this TV when you get back.
"Oh, so what are you talking to me now?" His voice returned to a cold, rigid tone, and you started to doubt yourself, because you strangely felt he seemed angry.
“…… Didn't say anything. I just found it a bit strange that you hadn't spoken for a long time. "You whispered, watching as the main storyline animation finally finished, you began to control the character to move.
But Tenna suddenly closed the game screen, and what appeared immediately was that face that had never been happy, with a downward curve at the corner of her mouth.
"Because it's bedtime now." He said as he stepped forward, took the game console from your hand, and then pushed you into a room. This room had been your residence recently—very simple, with no decorations, except for a poster of Anton Tenna stuck on the wall.
But today, when you lay down on the bed, for some reason you found a TV plushie on the bed—just a black screen, with a bent wire wrapped in tape, exactly like the TV in your Light World. Looking around, you realized the room had become exactly the same as your bedroom in the Light World.
…… When did he do it? He's been with you all along...... Could it be when you ran out of anger earlier? You don't know, you just hugged the stuffed animal in your arms tightly—by the way, if you sleep holding the TV at night, would it be radiated? But originally, it was just a furry stuffed animal, how could that be? Unless you have a plush allergy.
Thinking this, you can't help but yawn, rub your nose, and quickly crawl under the covers. Alright then...... Better get a good sleep first.
You closed your eyes, but couldn't help but smile. Indeed, perhaps the world of the dark would be warmer, since it felt more like home, much better than the empty houses in the world of light.
But you can't give up! After all, staying in the dark world all the time is nothing!
In a daze, you drift off to sleep—in your dream, you're sitting on the sofa playing a game, seemingly in the dark world. You must be playing some game that requires skill. Tenna is still holding his head on the TV, seemingly mocking you a bit. You start arguing with him, get so angry you try to run out through the lounge door.
He wrapped his arms around the waist and lifted you up, the screen pitch black, and said slowly, "I know you love me." ”
"But you know—"
Before you could finish the last half sentence, you woke up from the dream, gasping for breath, thinking how he could possibly know what you were thinking. Uneasy, you turned over and fell back asleep again.
TBC.

title: Game Time 4 (dntx you)
content:
When you fully wake up, you rub your eyes and stared blankly at the TV plush toy tightly hugged in your arms. You don't even know what you're thinking, anyway...... You're probably just daydreaming. Are you wondering if Tenna specially arranged this room? After all...... Other than him, the other Dark People in this TV world probably aren't so familiar with your room's layout.
…… After all, you only occasionally feel a bit weak and empty because the house is empty and empty, then drag the TV into your room, then sit on the bed hugging your knees, just watching the show absentmindedly, or rather, you just need a little sound to dispel your fear and loneliness when you're alone.
You get dressed and eat the steaming hot breakfast on the table, then walk out of the room. For some reason, Tenna is already sitting on a chair in the lounge. His screen is still pitch black, looking like he's resting with his eyes closed.
You hesitated for a moment. To be honest, you hadn't figured out what you should do today, nor had you figured it out...... What kind of attitude should you have when facing this guy? After all, although what he said was really harsh, the room was decorated and there were other aspects...... You still felt a bit grateful.
But you don't know if he'll actually agree to your invitation. After all...... What if you're just delusional? What if you just assume he likes you? That's a huge misunderstanding that absolutely must not happen—
So you sat on the sofa opposite him, hesitated for a moment, then cleared your throat twice and said, "You...... Want to play games with me? ”
His screen lit up. He seemed to be looking up at you, or maybe just looking down at you with a half-smile: "Oh?" Didn't you think my words were disturbing you? ”
You always feel like Tenna is being sarcastic...... Hmm, maybe this isn't just your imagination.
When he brings up this topic, you feel a bit awkward too, lowering your head and not daring to look at that TV again. You just think about it and feel that giving him a chance to play with him is a win—others might not even get the chance to be your playmate! Of course, that's just because you don't have friends.
So you put your hands on your hips, lifted your head, and deliberately spoke with a high vantage point: "Hmph...... This is an opportunity that others can't even dream of. Why don't you cherish it?" After saying that, you swallowed hard; you really couldn't get used to this way of speaking.
So you sneak a glance at Tenna out of the corner of your eye, only to see his screen go completely black again. He just coldly responds with an 'oh' and then ignores you.
"What do you want to do today?" He just casually switched to the next topic.
You thought he agreed, and excitedly ordered a two-player cooperative puzzle game. Instead, you watched Tenna hold his TV head, projecting the game's image onto the screen.
“…… This is a two-player game. You can't just let me play with two controllers by myself, can I?" You pointed at yourself in disbelief.
"Didn't you say playing with you was a chance that no one could even dream of? Just find someone else to play with." Tenna lowered her voice. For some reason, you always felt he was a bit sarcastic...... But you couldn't see anything from this screen right now.
If they go out to find other Dark People...... Most of them probably wouldn't dare come over, since most are still afraid of Tenna, the big boss.
So your remaining choice is either to pick the lock and go to the Light World to find someone to play games with you. But that's too difficult, since the town's Light Folk are all in small groups with their own companions, and you...... still have nowhere to gather together.
Or have Tenna play games with you...... No, you're still a bit unwilling, so you got up, holding back a breath, cheeks puffed up, and ran toward the lounge: "Alright, I'll go find the other Dark People right now!" ”
But for some reason, when you walked out the corridor, you didn't see any other Dark People along the way. Either they saw you and then hurried away, looking flustered, as if they saw someone they shouldn't have. It took a lot of effort to finally catch a Zapper. Before he could jump away, he had to hurriedly salute you.
You kindly and smilingly asked Zapper if he could play games with you, and Zapper was so startled he gave you a big bow—almost to the point of kneeling on the ground, though you weren't sure if he could do it. Then he dashed off in a flash.
Helpless, you could only storm back to the lounge, only to find Tenna sitting leisurely on the sofa with his legs crossed. You rolled your eyes inwardly, then walked over to Tenna and reached out a hand: "...... I—I invite you to play games with me......" Your voice softened a bit, just quietly finishing the sentence. You can't be sure if he did it on purpose, but right now, he's the only gaming partner you can choose from.
Only then did he leisurely take your hand and then stand up. Of course, he's much taller and more impressive than you. Then Tenna took your hand and sat back down. He snapped his fingers, and the wall opposite was a large projector—game screens displayed on it. You stared at everything in shock, then looked up at Tenna sitting next to you and couldn't help but raise your voice: "So why does it seem like you're the only TV in the TV world with other audio-visual devices?" ”
"After all, what you want is a TV. In this world, I am the only television." He answers your question calmly, and you just feel he's being sophistry—although the pristine white wall in front of you is just a projection device, it can display images, so in a broad sense, it's still a television!
For some reason, you always have some suspicions about this—you feel a bit uneasy, a bit doubtful that you're mistaken. After all, suspecting Tenna is deliberately doing this just to make you look at him or something, maybe it's just your own imagination. Better not think about these things and just enjoy it first.
You had just started the game for a short while before you yawned, hurriedly ran out to find other Dark People, and while passing the gate to the world of light, you tried to force it open. It really drained your strength. Last night, because of that dream, you didn't sleep very well...... Now you're feeling a bit sleepy.
Tenna lowered her head to glance at you, her lips straightened: "What, are you so bored?" ”
Maybe it's just ...... Maybe it's an illusion that arises when you're half-asleep. You always feel that his words are rarely taken lightly, and of course, you still seem a bit dissatisfied.
You yawned again, forced yourself to perk up, and waved your hand: "No, no...... I heard this game is really fun! I just didn't sleep well, it doesn't affect my gameplay! "After saying that, you sat up straight and stared intently at the screen.
Tenna didn't say anything more. Each of you controlled a character into the game scene. It was a cooperative escape room game—because two people were locked in different rooms. Some puzzles could be solved by themselves, while others required cooperation from each other.
You control the character, quickly piecing together the ship model in front of you, and then you feel a bit troubled—after all, even though you've done it, the ship's route is still unclear. It seems you have to wait until the ship reaches the destination before you can get the sealed key.
You fiddled with the boat for a long time without starting it, so you urgently urged Tenna: "Do you have any directions or something?" I need this over here. "For the fun of the puzzle game, you tacitly avoided looking at each other's screens. Tenna glanced at your screen and started mocking you.
"Are you blind? If you don't need your eyes, you can donate them." As he spoke, he took your game controller and pressed a button. The sails on the boat were lowered, and finally, they could be moved.
You paused, pouted, and looked a bit aggrieved: "I was just too impatient...... What right do you have to scold me! Besides, I was probably just a little sleepy...... A little groggy...... Your voice gradually faded, just weakly making excuses for yourself, and Tenna didn't refute you.
He just put the game controller back into your hand: "Mm, next time I suggest you play games with a clear mind." ”
"Then do you want me to catch up on sleep here? I'll just sleep on the sofa for a while. I promise I'll wake up soon." You couldn't help but choke at him, feeling a bit unconvinced, thinking you'd have to get back at it later.
Then Tenna nodded. You looked him up and down in disbelief, and he grew a bit impatient: "If you want to rest, just do it quickly. Don't stare here with your eyes wide open. I don't have a blanket on me." ”
You glanced at him skeptically, then closed your eyes and leaned back on the sofa. You have to say, the lounge sofa is really perfect for lying down...... It's soft and perfect for sleeping—at least you fall asleep after a while. Then, unknowingly, because Tenna sat on the sofa next to you, the sofa sank in one spot, and you also leaned in that direction, landing on top of Tenna.
His body stiffened for a moment, and the screen went dark, lowering his head. Maybe seeing you were sound asleep, he carefully picked you up and leaned against his chest. He held you, and you were sleeping soundly against his chest. Tenna just gently rested the TV's head on yours, not sure what he was thinking. The controller tossed nearby had long since disconnected and automatically cut off power, and now they were leaning against each other.
TBC.

title: Game Time 5 (dntx you)
content:
Maybe you held him a bit too tightly, but you restlessly moved a couple of times in his arms, your head resting against his hard chest, feeling a bit uncomfortable. You unconsciously twisted your body, while Tenna loosened up a little. But the screen was still pitch black, and no one could tell what he was thinking.
And when he notices you're about to wake up, he puts you down and sets you aside, and because of the crooked sofa, you end up leaning against him.
When you finally came to your senses, you noticed what your head was leaning on...... The fabric was generally uncomfortable. You hurriedly looked up, and when you looked up, it was Tenna's pitch-black screen. You suspected that leaning against him made him a bit angry and guilty, but you couldn't bring yourself to apologize.
So you just coughed twice and got up, pretending nothing had happened. Then you noticed two controllers placed together at your side—when did Tenna's controllers come here? You weren't really sure, just picked up his controller and handed it to him, pretending nothing had happened.
Then you hear him sneer: "I thought you were asleep." ”
You rolled your eyes. After these few days, you'd gotten a bit used to his way of speaking, but you still couldn't help feeling annoyed and just said angrily, "Didn't you sleep well?" That proves my sleep quality is good—otherwise, let's compare and see whose sleep is better. ”
"It seems that even if you die in a dream, you'll only think the darkness before you is just asleep." He said softly, tapping on the projector screen. Your characters were still standing there, motionless.
“…… So what? If I die painlessly in my sleep, I'd actually be happy about it...... After all, dying while awake would hurt too much. "You muttered, and following the direction of the ship recorded on the paper Tenna spat out, you finally managed to steer the ship to the destination and got a key—it looked like the key to a treasure chest, but looking around, there was no treasure chest or anything like that.
“…… Then I'd rather die sober." "You don't know why, but Tenna's tone suddenly turned sinister. You don't know what he's thinking of, but with the clicking of mechanisms, you see a treasure chest appear in the corner of the room."
You jumped up and said cheerfully, "But thank you anyway, Mr. Tenna." Then you controlled the character to open the treasure chest. Honestly, this level wasn't difficult—so after opening the chest, you got the access card to get out. At the same time, you saw a treasure map inside with a code. You read it to Tenna, listening to the sound of the mechanism turning, and then he said, "Alright." ”
He controls the character to leave the room, and you hurry to finish the game. The two characters who successfully solve the puzzle dance on the screen. Tenna loses patience to watch, drops her controller, and is about to leave.
You quickly tugged at his sleeve. His screen was still pitch black, and he didn't look very happy. You swallowed, a little scared, but still raised your voice: "There are still many levels in this game!" Just play with me! ”
You didn't realize that your voice sounded a bit like she was being spoiled. Tenna's heart did move. Looking at your pitiful expression, he felt a bit sorry for you at that moment. But he still looked up, glanced at the screen, and made a move to walk outside: "I'm not in the mood to play house here with you." ”
You get a bit anxious, drop the handle, run in front of him, and spread your arms to block him. Of course, it's like trying to stop a chariot—the difference in size between you and him is just too great.
"Then who can play with me if you leave?" You can't leave. "You started making a fuss too. Of course, you still felt a bit guilty—even though you guessed he might like you a little, you couldn't be sure if your guess was true.
If ...... If he really listened to me and stayed, then the chances would increase by about 20%......
Tenna stopped, bent down, and the screen lit up. He just glanced at you with a flat smile, and you noticed the tip of his nose...... It seemed like something like Venus flytrap or something like that popped up? You felt like he wasn't in a good mood, and just as you were wondering whether to say it or forget it, you heard him say in a flat tone, "Are you sincere?" ”
You paused for a moment, then nodded instinctively and raised your voice: "Yes, of course it's sincere!" ”
—Well, it's not entirely sincere either...... But playing games with someone you like is definitely fun. It's precisely because playing with them is so fun that you hope they stay. You hope that happiness lasts longer.
He just bent over silently, saying nothing, as if trying to see if you had lied. You swallowed nervously, feeling a bit uneasy. He kept watching you, making you feel a bit uneasy, and you were thinking about not slinking back to sit down first—after all, waiting so long for his answer, you went from initial anxiety and excitement to disappointment.
Just as you lower your head, trying to find a gap in the ground to squeeze in and avoid this awkward situation, you finally hear him speak.
“…… Then I'll reluctantly play with you a little longer. I have other things to do." Hearing him reply, your voice unhurried, you excitedly lift your head and tug at the corner of his shirt toward the sofa. But he turns around and tightens your hand, pulling you onto the sofa. He sits next to you, still in the same spot as before.
Ever since he held your hand, your cheeks turned bright red. To be honest...... You don't understand why he did this. If he truly liked you, he should have told you directly. But if not, why would he do it, giving you hope for no reason? You don't understand.
Well, though you don't dare say it out loud, and you don't dare tell him...... You just sneak a glance at him, and Tenna notices your gaze. Meanwhile, because you're distracted, your game character on the screen dies—yes, at Tenna's request, you switch to a different game, this time an online fighting game.
"What...... Is fighting me not worth your effort?" He asked in a questioning tone, and you quickly shifted your attention back.
"No, no, no...... I was just daydreaming, looking around! "You emphasized this, hurriedly pulling out a combo to try to defeat Tenna's controlled character, but he just held that character in the air, then kept firing downward shots, interrupting your combo attacks and chasing after you.
"Looking around isn't a good habit during battle." He commented, "It's still chasing after your game character. You might not think you're strong, but you can finish it normally without any problem!" I don't even know why they're constantly chasing you to kill...... Is Tenna's gaming skill really that high?
After playing five or six rounds in a row, it was always your game over. Annoyed, you slammed your controller onto the sofa: "I'm done playing! Why are you always the one winning...... Am I really that weak?" You started to doubt yourself, and Tenna heard that last sentence so low it was almost negligible.
And he just said softly, "Your attack is too weak, or rather, you're too weak." He mercilessly belittles you, and you widen your eyes at Tenna beside you, but of course, he can't see it.
“…… So what, so what! I just look weaker when fighting you...... I'm going to find someone else to play with—I don't believe I'm that weak! "You stomped your foot, stood up, and tried to run out of the lounge.
Just before you left the lounge, Tenna spoke up behind you, "You can't find anyone else." ”
So, you can only play with him.
Your steps paused: "...... I knew it, you told the other Dark People to do it, didn't you?" "That's why earlier when you went out, you couldn't catch a single Dark Citizen."
All you respond to is silence. Tenna doesn't speak, and knowing you can't find anyone else and running out again would be unwise. You want to save energy, so in the end, you turn around and reluctantly sit next to Tenna.
"Can't we play a different game then?" You try to struggle pointlessly.
"No." Of course, all he got in return was a cold reply.
With no other choice, you switch to another character to play this fighting game, but every time you lose completely. You sniff, because you've been losing all the time, and tears welled up in your eyes. You really felt wronged—why? This wasn't a game, it was clearly playing you.
“…… I don't want to play anymore. Why are you always the one winning? W-bad TV!" You tossed the game controller aside and sobbed as you said this. You had originally planned to repay Tenna when you left this morning, but now—you just want to get back at him. Why does he keep winning? Isn't this really unfair to you? Even though you know your skills aren't great—why is he always crushing you? You barely have a chance to fight back!
You sobbed, wiping tears from the corners of your eyes, wanting to go back to your own room, at least your stuffed toy wouldn't bully you. But just a second before you got up, you felt something cold, glass-like pressed against your cheek, followed by a warm touch—you opened your eyes and realized it was Anton Tenna pressing close to your face, kissing the tear stains on your cheek.
You stared at him in shock, while he slightly lifted his body, his arms resting on either side of your body. The shadow pressed down, and you couldn't help but lie back on the sofa, staring blankly at Tenna.
“…… I know you love me. "He spoke softly, yet in a voice you could hear clearly.
You instinctively want to reach out to cover his mouth, but he just presses your arm again: "But you know...... Do I love you? ”

title: Game Time 6 (dntx you)
content:
You paused, not understanding why he would say this at this moment—this was completely out of place! Honestly, you don't understand.
So you were silent for a while, but just tapped the dark screen twice with your hand, then asked, "Why do you like me?" "Even though you know you love him or something...... It's completely for no reason.
"Then why do you love me?" He didn't answer your question, but simply asked in return.
You're a bit stuck. To be honest...... You really can't give a specific reason. After all, you can't tolerate his words either, can't tolerate his occasional behavior, or rather...... You can't fully tolerate him.
But if you want to find a reason, it seems you can find some. You think hard and honestly answer: "Hmm...... Because you've always been with me? Because you quietly help me decorate the room? Because...... Well, I don't know why, I just like you. ”
You scratch your head irritably, and it's precisely because of this affection that you subconsciously treat him a little better.
Tenna slightly lifted her posture. You could finally sit up a little straighter.
"No reason. That's the answer I'm giving you." He snorted coldly. If he had to give a reason...... There should indeed be some of them, but he didn't want to tell you. Some things, he just needs to know himself.
You blinked, pointed at yourself, then at Tenna: "...... So you chose to tell me now...... I—can I pretend nothing ever happened? "That way, everything will develop exactly as before.
Habit is a scary thing. At least, now you seem to be somewhat used to what Tenna says, and a bit used to losing your temper when dissatisfied—because you find Tenna doesn't do anything about it, so you've become bolder.
Tenna just shook his head, then pressed down on your face and bent down to bite your lips. His large tongue scraped along your lips, wet, entering your mouth, filling your entire mouth, making only some stammering sounds as he pushed you, tears welling up involuntarily.
You think—you didn't agree either! How did you suddenly start doing intimate things that only men and women can do? You propped up your arms, trying hard to push him away, but unfortunately, for Tenna, your strength was still a bit too soft.
Fortunately, he finally let go of your mouth, but the screen was still pitch black, and he didn't look very happy.
You swallowed twice and didn't dare say anything more, just stared at Tenna in fear.
But he spoke slowly: "...... Of course not, I want you to agree." At this moment, his words carried a hint of assertiveness.
"What if I don't agree?" Maybe you wanted to try it out, and you couldn't help but ask.
Tenna watched you in silence for a moment, then let out a cold laugh and leaned in close again. His voice suddenly became soft, so soft it was almost eerie.
"You'll agree, okay?" Even the words entering your ears carried a haze and dizziness, making it hard to read. Your mind seemed a bit dazed, and in a daze, you seemed to see some dizzying pattern appearing on the TV screen in front of you—you quickly shook your head to clear your head, hoping not to lose your mind at this moment.
“…… But I don't want to agree. After all, you—you're a broken TV! "As you spoke, you reached out and tapped Tenna's TV casing again.
Although you may forgive him, that doesn't mean you can forget them after hearing those words.
So you start counting on your fingers: "For example...... I remember you've already said 36 bad things to me! You've blocked or rejected my requests 9 times, and then, ...... You crushed me 12 games in the game! That one I don't know but felt uncomfortable about was 1 ......."
He listened quietly. In fact, he knows your characteristics...... That's why he wanted to hypnotize you just now, because after that, you'll probably completely forgive him.
But at this moment, he simply sat back down beside him and spoke casually: "If I don't say something, you won't remember at all." ”
Because...... When he praises you or treats you kindly, you can hardly remember them; instead, when you're hurt, you always remember them. So he hopes you can remember him forever, even if in this unpleasant way.
You choke up, thinking he really is telling the truth, after all...... Happiness is a fleeting thing; only pain will make you remember it forever.
You lower your head a little dejectedly: "But I don't want to think of you anymore, and all I think about is pain." Even if ...... Even if the impression of happiness isn't deep, you still vaguely remember what has happened.
"Hmm, then tell me, how many happy things did you remember before?"
You opened your mouth, then closed it again. Yes, you really don't have any happy memories...... But that clearly doesn't matter.
"Then let's work backwards...... The most recent thing was that I found you helped me tidy up my room, and the layout was exactly the same as my old bedroom. "You took a deep breath and said.
Tenna nodded, "And then?" ”
Then...... Then you can't remember. Only then do you realize—or rather, you have to admit—that in your life up to now, you don't have many happy memories.
Going further back, probably...... You happily sit at home, playing games in front of this TV. But you quickly become unhappy, because your parents, who promised to come home, have broken their promises just like countless times before and haven't come back, just letting you stay here. You know, after all, the sister who has always stayed by their side to raise is the most important thing to them.
So you fell silent, then weakly spoke: "...... I... I don't want to say it anymore." "Happiness always comes with pain, and you don't want to open your own wounds."
“…… If you can promise that the memories you'll bring me from now on will be joyful memories, and that I'll never suffer anymore, then I'll agree to your request." You took a deep breath, finally looked up at him, and said your request. Maybe this was the first time you'd ever spoken your request so seriously.
This time, Tenna was silent. He couldn't guarantee you'd always have only happy memories—he knew very well what he might and was destined to bring you.
So he just said stiffly, "I can't guarantee it. Some happiness is mixed with pain. ”
“…… Hmm, I understand. Then when can you promise me? I'll promise you then." You gave a bitter smile, after all, you knew this would be the ending. My heart seemed a bit sour, but it made me beat violently, probably because of it.
You don't know...... Is love always like this—sweet yet mixed with pain? If so, what is the so-called love you seek from him?
Tenna looked down at you, probably pondering the same thing. His screen lit up, as if ready to say something he promised, but before he could speak, you covered his mouth with both hands: "Don't tell me right now, please." Otherwise, you won't believe it.
Then...... You felt your wet, slightly cool tongue lick across your palm, your eyes widened, and you quickly withdrew your hand.
"You, you...... Rogue TV! "You don't even know what to say. Good manners make you mentally unable to curse, so you just bangbang the TV's casing a couple of times."
He didn't answer you, just said, "I'm tired." ”
His screen was off, and the entire TV crew looked completely drained. His heavy body suddenly leaned against you, nearly pinning you down on the sofa.
You glared at this baffling guy, not knowing why he suddenly acted like this, so you just muttered, "If you're tired, go back to your room and rest...... What's the point of falling here? I'm not your bed......"
He didn't seem to have been woken up by your voice, or maybe even if he did, there was no response, because you can't tell if he's awake or not, and you don't even know if the Dark People actually need to sleep.
But leaving it alone isn't a good idea. After all, you feel your shoulders are being pressed down and sore. In the end, you still carefully hold his head, move your body to the side, then rest the head of the TV on your own lap so he can lie down and rest.
At least, he probably didn't disturb him...... That's what you think.
But Tenna actually hasn't fallen asleep at all. With outsiders around, it's hard for him to fall asleep. He naturally senses your movements, knows he's resting on your lap, and he silently enjoys the moment.
You puff out your cheeks, hesitate for a moment, and finally carefully reach out to touch the TV's head—oh my god, he's forcing himself not to let his screen light up suddenly, he's going to pull back every flower that would have appeared at his nose.
You pick up the remote and switch the TV in front of you to a movie channel. You turn off the sound and watch silent movies, yawning—probably to get used to Tenna's state, but before you know it, the lights in the lounge have also been turned off, leaving only the flickering screen.
You leaned back on the sofa watching the movie and couldn't help but yawn again. This time, you fell asleep too.
TBC.

title: Game Time 7 (dntx you)
content:
You seem to have had a nightmare—bizarre and bizarre, as if a fire had broken out, and your parents were so focused on escaping with your sister, leaving behind you, the sister who never had their concern, leaving everything at home. Little you could only helplessly lean against the counter, against that TV—the one that had suffered a mouth injury, was damaged, had tape wrapped around its antenna, and its screen was slightly cracked, until its once cold mechanical casing and glass were now tinged with warmth.
Further on...... What comes after that? You can't remember clearly...... Whether this really happened, you can't recall either. You only remember that when you were about fifteen, you had a serious illness, and after that, you basically forgot everything from before. Even your own parents—when you saw them again, you didn't feel much.
They anxiously call out to you, call your name, and embrace you with tears in their eyes, but you don't know why they hold you. Finally...... Perhaps because they never got the response they wanted, they left disappointed, settled elsewhere with your sister, leaving you alone when you were only sixteen.
It's okay, you can already earn money to support yourself, and being alone won't be boring because they find it useless. Leaving that old TV behind, you can still have a short moment of entertainment.
…… Was it really a dream, or did it really happen back then? You can't say clearly, or rather, memories before eighteen are shrouded in a fog, and you can't recall clearly. You seem ...... Only clearly remember what happened after you arrived in the TV world.
And you woke up from that dream, startled again when you woke up, because you found everything pitch black before you—and when you looked closely, it was Tenna's pitch-black screen. He didn't turn on the light, just propped up his arms, probably watching you.
You swallowed nervously: "So...... Why didn't you turn on the lights? ”
"Because you've been sleeping all along, Lord Sleep God. How could I dare wake you up?" He said sarcastically.
You puffed out your cheeks and tapped his screen. For some reason, you felt like you weren't as afraid of him anymore—you didn't know why, but you said ruthlessly, "What a harsh way to talk—alright, turn on the lights!" The pitch-black room was terrifying! ”
Tenna said nothing, just snapped her fingers, and then the lights in the room came on. Suddenly touching the light, you instinctively squinted, tears streaming down your face, followed by darkness before your eyes, with only a faint light filtering through the gap.
You realize it was Tenna's hand. And he just said with contempt, "If you can't accept it, you'll blame me again. Your Majesty, what will it take for you to be satisfied?" ”
You coughed dryly twice, your face instinctively turning red: "...... I—I wouldn't do that...... "You're not some arrogant person. If anyone is self-centered, Tenna would be that kind of person."
"Mm." He replied briefly, then let go. You blinked twice, and you had to admit, you really were used to it now. You tugged at the hem of your skirt, a little embarrassed, but in the end, you spoke softly.
“…… Thank you. ”
"I can't hear clearly." He said lazily, leaning back on the sofa.
Your face flushed red as you glared at him fiercely—hmm, he probably didn't see it.
"I said, thank you!" You raised your voice and shouted—hmm, but it seems the TV doesn't have ears, so what exactly does it use to listen? It can't be a mechanical shell conduction, right? You suddenly start thinking about it.
"Mm-hmm, I heard it clearly, you don't have to shout so loudly." Tenna started to irritably pull her antenna, pulling it down, as if it were the structure for receiving audio.
You quieted down, touched your belly, hesitated for a moment: "...... I'm hungry, I want to go back to the Light World to eat. ”
Spending all day in the TV world eating TV meals is pretty boring—you're getting tired of them.
"Is it that the TV food isn't good? Or you can try something else—" His speech inexplicably sped up as he began to introduce it, while Tenna stood up, clearly preparing to bring out something.
"No, I'm tired of the Dark World's food. I want to go back and eat." You persisted—well, even though you were the only one cooking and the food you cooked wasn't very tasty. But you wanted to go back. No matter what, you missed home, you wanted to go back there, even if no one was waiting for you. The only thing waiting for you was the bulky TV form of the TV person in the world of light.
"Your cooking skills are indeed a decent dish." He seemed to be sarcastically teasing you, or maybe you just misheard...... Just pretend you didn't hear it, just keep pretending to be strong.
"So what? I just think the food I cook is really good, so I have to go back and make it myself. Some ingredients aren't ...... from the underworld." You checked the kitchen a couple of days ago, and sure enough, there aren't any ingredients you'll need.
Tenna's voice was still cold: "What do you want to eat?" ”
You paused, almost unable to believe your ears: "...... What? ”
And he patiently repeated, "What do you want to eat?" ”
You blinked, unsure if it would happen, but since you were so, you started listing dishes: "Then I want garlic pork with clear pork knuckle sauce pig's trotters sweet and sour pork ribs, Farewell My Concubine braised pork with quail eggs, roasted pigeon, jade jade soup—"
You listed the names of the dishes one after another, then Tenna covered your mouth. You blinked innocently and looked up at him. His screen was still dark. You couldn't tell what he was feeling, nor did you dare to cause trouble, so you simply reached out and removed the hand covering your mouth.
"If none of these works...... Then stir-fried pork with chives—that should be possible, right? "You tilted your head, and this request was probably reasonable.
He walked out without saying a word. When you saw him walk out of the lounge door, you quietly followed him, slowing your pace so he wouldn't notice you following behind him.
But in fact, Tenna had already noticed this; he just hadn't exposed it. He knew maybe you were just ...... for fun, that kind of thing. He also knew you probably wouldn't be at ease, but he couldn't just let you leave here.
Not just because of him, but also because of your request—of course, he knows that even for himself, he won't let you leave the TV world. Anton Tenna won't let the prey he sets his sights on run away.
So...... Even though he hadn't tried it much, Tenna still made a detour and walked into the kitchen. And as you watched him walk into the kitchen, you instinctively widened your eyes and tried to close your gaping mouth. Oh my god—Tenna actually cooks himself! You don't even know if he can cook, but...... You remember several TV channels are cooking shows, so Tenna is probably very skilled in the kitchen.
Obviously, you were too relieved too soon. Because you sat in the corner sneaking around, staring toward the kitchen, and after about ten or twenty minutes, you saw wisps of black smoke rising from the kitchen doorway, and you heard the clattering of bells and a violent explosion. It felt as if the entire TV world was shaking, and you felt your body shake off the floor and fall back to the floor.
You swallowed nervously, quietly peeked your head out from behind the wall toward the kitchen door, and then saw a figure walking out of a TV covered in black and gray on both his head and clothes. Unexpectedly, his screen was lit, which made the black gray look so out of place.
…… You might as well take this chance to find a way to return to the world of light—after all, Tenna had already left. So you quietly and steadily walked to the locked front door. You hesitated for a moment, took off the hairpin from your head, stuck it inside the lock, and studied it for a long time. It turned out your lockpicking skills were still insufficient...... The door wouldn't open. Although you couldn't quite remember why you actually picked the lock.
You try again to see if you can brute-force pull open the lock or break the door, but obviously, it won't work...... Your hands and legs hurt, and you feel like the door and lock are very solid.
You looked gloomily, then glanced over the room—ah, there really were other rooms, but one of them was sealed off for some reason, sealed with countless strips. You tried to tear open those seals to see if you could get in, but those seals were very secure.
And in another room...... Unexpectedly, a door sign was hung that read Anton Tenna.
It's Tenna's room...... You hesitate for a moment, then press the doorknob. The good news is, the door isn't locked. Feeling guilty, you glance to the sides. It's clear that no Dark People usually come to this place, so you breathe a sigh of relief, press the doorknob, and enter the room.
You turn on the light, blink to adjust to the light—otherwise, you wouldn't be able to see anything in the pitch-black room.
Well, actually, you just want to see if you can walk into the rooms on either side of the tightly locked door...... Is there a connecting passage or something?
Tenna seemed to live in this place most of the time, since it was cleaned very thoroughly, with no dust left behind.
You casually scanned his room, and if there was no passage, you turned off the lights and left—after all, suddenly coming to someone's room always made you feel a bit guilty, as if you were inspecting.
Then your gaze froze, you froze in place, eyes wide as you stared at a wall—the wall was covered with photos of you, from childhood to adulthood, and ...... even, even photos of you bathing and getting out of the bath?!
TBC.

title: Game Time 8 (dntx you)
content:
Although...... Why are these photos of you growing up? You clearly feel like you've settled here in the house just a couple of years ago...... But no, I can't recall the memories from before, only a layer of fog shrouded me. It's really strange. But why......
Forget it, you think it's better not to think about this for now. Is this guy a voyeur! He saved all your photos! And...... And there are photos of you just out of the bath—that's just too perverted!
You casually glanced at these photos, and finally your gaze froze on the spot. On it was a picture of little you, smiling, standing beside you...... It looked like a photo of your very old grandmother taking a group photo. You stood in front of a TV covered with a white dust cover, smiling brightly. For some reason, you suddenly felt sad...... But you remembered nothing.
Most of the photos seem to be from the past two years—you cry, laugh, get angry, rejoice, but without exception, the same TV casually appears in the corners of the photos.
You were silent for a moment, then tried to turn and sneak away—just pretend you didn't see it, since peeking into someone's room is never something to say out loud.
But when you turn around, you bump into a sturdy figure. Tears instinctively welled up in the corner of your eye from the pain. Just as you looked up to accuse him, you realized it was the real person in the room.
He sits with the screen going dark, fiddling at the doorframe, looking down at you, looking down. You can't help but feel a bit scared, take two steps back, and he steps back two more steps toward you.
And at this very moment, you stand firm—what's the need to be afraid? He was the one who made the mistake! You overlooked that you had a guilty conscience and barged into his room.
"Damn...... What are you doing? Is the meal ready? "You put your hands on your hips and chose to press him directly.
"It's ready. I thought you'd be waiting." Tenna said. But when he came out carrying the food, he couldn't see you. So...... That's why he thought, I have to go find you. He felt panicked, because Tenna understood that if you were gone, you must have gone to find the passage back to the world of light. Fortunately, he locked the door firmly, and luckily, he found that only his own door was open.
If it were another room...... He probably wouldn't be able to stop your resolve then. He wouldn't want you to see those things anymore. Some things are best known only to him, for example...... These photos.
“…… Isn't it boring to just wait there the whole time? I was just wandering around casually, and when I saw your room, I got a bit curious and came in to take a look. You didn't lock the door, so isn't that just letting me look around! "You raised your voice and kept shouting. You know you might be a bit in the wrong, but even if it's unreasonable...... You still have to look like you're not at a disadvantage!
"Well, but peeking into my room—don't you find it boring?" He bent down, adding even more pressure. You instinctively took two steps back, then sat down on his soft bed, with Tenna's arms resting on either side of you. Even if you didn't want to look at him, you were forced to stare at him.
Your gaze darted around: "Yes, I'm really bored, I admit it—but you've kept all the photos from childhood, and—and even photos of me after a bath, even a photo of me in my underwear right after waking up in the morning—you, how did you even take those pictures, you pervert!" As you spoke, you became even more justified, starting to type on his screen to vent your anger.
And ...... He could keep such highly private photos—who knows if this perverted TV had already seen everything! No, no, he shouldn't have imagined it like that...... And even if he saw everything, what did it matter! Anyway, everything he shouldn't have done was his fault!
"Yes, it was your guardian who made the album. I just moved those photos to my room." He admitted it straightforwardly—of course, in reality, only those ordinary photos recording beautiful memories and the past were taken before, only a dozen or so photos. The other photos...... Were all taken by him out of selfish motives.
"Guardians? Not mine...... Parents? "You always feel ...... It seems like some answer is about to come out. You feel a bit of a headache, as if a flash of inspiration strikes you in an instant, but you can't catch that spark of inspiration, nor do you know what is shrouded behind the fog—it's just a subconscious sadness, an instinctively feeling ...... Empty.
"Of course not. You still treat those two conscientious guys as your guardians." Tenna sneered.
You instinctively want to say not to let him speak about your parents like that—but you hesitate, and in your heart you stop him from saying so. So, deep down, you think the same way?
Tenna had no intention of continuing the conversation, just changed the subject: "Aren't you going to eat yet? How much longer are you going to keep pestering me here? Or...... Can I understand it as you just like to keep pestering me? ”
That sentence seemed to carry a hint of ambiguity...... You instinctively widened your eyes and patted his TV head: "What kind of talk is that? I don't like it! I-I'd rather be alone forever...... I wouldn't choose you! "You're a bit careless."
Well, actually, you're just saying the opposite. You really like it, really like it...... But it also feels a bit sour and swollen, and your heart feels a little sore. You don't know, is it that tangled love always ends like this? What exactly do you want? You don't understand.
He snorted coldly, "Oh, then who said as a kid that when they grew up, they wanted to treat TV as their bride?" ”
Unconsciously, his tone ...... actually carried a hint of grievance. You were a bit shocked to recognize this. You realized it too...... The TV in that photo was Anton Tenna.
If you think this way, you might indeed say the same. After all, at that time, the whole family was ...... probably just you, your grandmother, and this TV.
“…… Anyway, there's no way I said it!" You said in a sulk. Even though you know it was definitely something you said as a child—what kind of scene was it then? What story did it actually happen? You couldn't remember anything at all.
“…… It's exactly what you said. "His tone suddenly turned a bit sinister, and his words sounded so dazed that you couldn't help but shiver.
