"It can't be me who said it!" You lifted your neck, sticking to your own story. At this point, of course, you refused to admit it either.
"You said it." His voice remained calm, but now tinged with anger, and his speech sped up considerably.
"Impossible!" You're still holding on. Anyway, he wouldn't do anything to you...... You know, you've always known.
Tenna stopped talking. You thought it was all over. You looked up to ask him to let you go, but he just bit your lip, his sharp teeth cutting your lip. You cried out in pain, frowned, whimpered twice, and pushed his screen with your hand.
But it didn't work. He just held you tightly, your head resting on the soft bed, and his large tongue rubbed against your cracked lips, gently licking the bitten spot. A faint bloody smell spread, and the sticky saliva wet your lips. You stammered, feeling a bit uncomfortable, and couldn't help but bite your tongue tip.
His tongue took over your mouth, blocking it completely, and his tongue was recklessly teasing the depths of your mouth. Tears welled up in your eyes, your eyes red. You knew Tenna could definitely see your expression—he was just deliberately going on! Was this revenge for your earlier denial?
An even stronger smell of blood spread out. He was still licking your mouth, making you a bit dizzy—probably not very good at breathing. You pitifully stammered twice, and only then did he mercifully let go of your mouth. The sticky silver threads hung by your mouths, connected together. You coughed twice, feeling a bit uncomfortable deep in your throat.
"Alright...... Alright, I said it! Alright! Ugh...... You shouted loudly, unable to hold back two more sobs. Along with that discomfort, you actually felt a bit wronged...... What exactly are you feeling wronged about? You don't know, but at least you don't want to talk to Tenna right now. You mean what you say!
So after saying this, you fell silent again and firmly said nothing.
Tenna just responded with a satisfied "Mm." So now, it's your mealtime. ”
He waited for a while, and you didn't answer him.
Tenna laughed bitterly in anger. He really did laugh a few times, and you couldn't help but shrink back a few times. You kept worrying that this guy might do something again, so you couldn't help but press your bitten lips, only to feel more and more wronged.
"Ha, you're not saying anything now? Who knows what you really mean? Who would guess what you're really thinking?" He couldn't help but complain, but bent down, picked you up, dragged you out of the room, locked the door, and headed toward the lounge.
You pursed your lips and swung your legs, signaling you to come down and walk on your own, but Tenna just held your leg with her other hand and said coldly, "Don't move." ”
You feel a bit guilty, your body a bit stiff, and you really can't do anything else.
Tenna carried you quickly to the lounge, where you ordered the food you just ordered...... Not all of them, but at least a few dishes were brought out and placed on the table, looking quite delicious.
TBC.

title: Game Time 9 (dntx you)
content:
You are placed at the end of the table by Tenna, just looking at him in frustration.
“…… Why don't you just ignore me? Who told you to mind me, who told you to care about my thoughts, who told you to ...... "Who told you to love me?" You wanted to say this, but when you opened your mouth, you couldn't get it out. You just awkwardly closed your mouth, lowered your head, and stared blankly at the steaming hot food in front of you.
Tenna sat across from you, handed you the bowl and chopsticks, and said coldly, a bit annoyed, "Yeah, who told me to love you?" ”
He could say that out loud...... Because you probably wouldn't care, but after hearing his words, your body just shrank back, and you still showed no other reaction.
…… See, you really don't care. Even if he says it so confidently, he doesn't know if you truly feel that way, if you truly love him, or if you ...... You still care? He sneered inwardly, as if mocking, but deep down, there was still a bit of grievance he couldn't put into words.
“…… Why do you love me?" You whispered, unconsciously poking the plate with your chopsticks—this was your habit when daydreaming. Tenna just used her other pair of chopsticks to serve you food, and soon, your bowl was piled high with food, as big as a small mountain, full and full.
Looking at this bowl of food, you can't help but get a little distracted, feeling ...... It seems that a long, long time ago, someone would have done this for you, but who exactly was it? No matter what, you just can't remember.
And Tenna just said, "I don't know. Are you satisfied with this answer?" ”
His voice was still icy cold, like dark clouds hanging over you. You didn't dare look up at him and just mumbled, "...... That's not really a reason, right? So do you have a reason?" ”
Maybe...... Maybe love doesn't need a reason, just as you love Tenna, it seems you don't need a reason either. Even though you never directly admitted it, nor agreed to it. You just...... Still staying here.
Because it seems you have nowhere else to go besides this.
"So if you love me, is there a reason for that?" he said.
You thought for a moment, put down your chopsticks, and started counting on your fingers: "I think there is. You'll always be with me. Even if it makes me angry, it's reluctant, and I can forgive you. Also...... Hmm, the food you make looks really delicious...... But aside from that, you couldn't find any other reason, so you timidly looked up at Tenna.
But—but why did he subconsciously say that Tenna would always be with him? You clearly felt that you only saw Anton Tenna after entering the Dark World, clearly ...... He remembered that there really was such a TV in the Light World, but it seemed only in the past two years.
"Is that a reason?" Tenna asked.
You were silent for a moment: "...... Maybe that's not really a reason." "Love seems to be something that doesn't need a reason, and the so-called reason is just evidence you find to convince you that you love him, or that you discover he loves you."
Maybe, in fact...... That's not really that important.
You pick up a slice of garlic pork, dip it in sauce, and put it in your mouth. It's a familiar taste...... You seem to have tasted this sauce for a long time. Why do you feel like crying the moment you taste it? That flavor makes you nostalgic, as if recalling the taste that was once beautiful and warm, as if ...... Being able to let go of all pretenses and throw yourself into this warm embrace, letting go of all sadness and sensitivity.
You bit your lip, tears uncontrollably streaming down your cheeks. You sniffed, staring at the screen that was lit up, but still wearing a sour face waiting for your evaluation. Tenna cautiously said, "This smell...... Could it be that you're my mom? ”
As soon as you say it, you regret it. How could a TV person be a human mother? What are you thinking! You even want to punch yourself so you can lose your memory from earlier.
Tenna couldn't help but sneer, "What do you mean I'm your mom?" ”
He just made the whole table of dishes the way you used to love, and didn't expect any kind of comment—even though he was indeed looking forward to it. But he never expected to hear you say that!
"No, it's just, this smell is very familiar......" It's as if, long, long ago, this was the very scent that had accompanied you...... As you spoke, you picked up another bite of eggplant and put it in your mouth. Indeed, it tasted exactly like the one you remembered, but no matter how you thought about it, you couldn't retrieve even a tiny bit from that foggy deep sea of memories.
"I can't possibly be your mother." He said, unusually calm, his tone still fairly calm—uh, of course, you can't ignore the suppressed anger beneath his words, seemingly ...... And a bit aggrieved.
You fell silent. But no matter how much you searched your memories, there was nothing more to say. You only remembered that in these years, the TV was still with you at home.
So...... "Did we know each other before?" "You think about this question, but memories can't give you the answer."
"Does it matter whether you know him or not?" Tenna just asked you back.
Maybe it's important, maybe not. In fact, one of the reasons you want to return to the world of light is that you believe that once you go back, you can recover those memories from the past. In some way, you always have this feeling.
You slowly gnaw on the vegetables piled up like a small mountain, pondering for a moment, then nodding and shaking your head: "Yes, memories of the past...... will be important. But the present and future matters are also very important. ”
If you are someone with no past, could you just be a hollow person?
"I... I want to recover my past memories. No, I absolutely must recover my past memories, so I must return to the Luminal World once more." After quickly finishing your meal, you put down your chopsticks, looked directly at Tenna, and mustered the courage to speak. This time, you have truly made up your mind; you want to reclaim your memories.
Whether painful or beautiful, that is your past. If forgetting them is just a temporary escape... then now you should remember, you should face them.
Tenna stared at you, and even if you couldn't see his eyes, you could feel his burning gaze fixed on you.
His tone was heavy, tinged with some disdain: "Even if the memories you recover include things that caused you unbearable pain, things you would rather forget?"
You hesitated for a moment, but ultimately nodded firmly: "Yes. If it truly is very painful... then I cannot forgive the perpetrators. But I must put these things down and move forward." At the end, you let out a soft laugh.
Choosing not to forgive is okay too.
"Even if... you’ve once experienced happiness, only to eventually lose it?" He said these abrupt words, and you nodded and shook your head at the same time.
"Yes... joyous memories cannot last forever; a brief moment of happiness is enough to savor for a lifetime," you said softly with your head lowered and a smile.
But Tenna only stared at the top of your head. He wanted to question you: what about him? What about the old TV you once left behind in your memories if you move forward? What about the old TV that has always been with you if you forgive those past events? If... you are willing to accept your current family, were his words about being the only family left to you a complete lie?
He wanted to question you, to stop you at any cost, to stand between you and the truth. But... perhaps deep down, he was still unwilling to do so.
So in the end, he only took a deep breath: "...If you really want to know the truth, then come with me. Of course, I don't think relying on your fragile psychological endurance, you can fully accept that truth." He couldn’t resist mocking you again. Perhaps, with this sentence, it could make you hesitate for a moment, delaying your pursuit of the truth.
You just puffed up your cheeks and, pouting, poked him on the back: "No way, I'm not as fragile as you say — and, and! Even if I can’t accept it right away, maybe after some time, I will."
After all, time always washes away sorrow and grievances, even though there will still be sadness and grievances, more and more memories will eventually fill in the old pain.
"You really are fragile," Tenna repeated, saying little else. He walked ahead quickly, and you hurried to catch up, nearly unable to keep up with him. But in the end, he suddenly stopped. You, rushing forward, collided into his back with a thump, and physiological tears welled up in your eyes. You covered your forehead and looked at Tenna turning around with grievance: "It hurts..."
He let out a cold snort: "Endure the pain. Are you blind? Don’t you realize we’ve arrived?"
"How would I know? You didn’t say anything. Should I just guess what you’re thinking?" You glared at him angrily.
Tenna said nothing, turning away, and dryly said: "Next time I’ll tell you."
Then he pushed the door open and walked inside. You recognized it as the room you had come out of not long ago. You took a deep breath and followed. Tenna was standing in front of the photo wall, his back to you.
TBC.

title: Game time 10 (dntx you)
content:
For some reason, you suddenly feel a bit uneasy, along with a sense of unease rising along with it—it seems to be a subconscious emotion, as if instinct is preventing you from understanding the truth. Perhaps all of that has become a past you don't want to explore.
But...... You can't just be someone who only has the present and the future; you want to know, urgently want to know what kind of past you have.
Tenna lowered his head and looked at you, expressionless: "Do you want to look in order from front to back, or from back to front?" Although either way, the meaning to him is the same, and he might ...... He just hopes he can leave more impressions in your heart. He doesn't want you to forget him; he's afraid that once your memories are overwhelmed by past memories, all that remains is ...... Those past that belong only to you.
“…… Let's go from the back to the front. After all, when I was younger, I probably wouldn't remember clearly." You murmured, after all, recent memories are the freshest and most memorable. You want to first understand your current situation.
Tenna said no more, just led you to the right, then pointed to a photo—your sleeping face lying in bed: "This is a photo of the crime I left behind." ”
You hesitated for a moment, then nodded: "So...... I just need to put my hand on it, right? Is this some kind of photo recording the movie? ”
Tenna nodded as well: "Yes, all these photos are on video. You can just watch them directly." His voice was suppressed, unusually calm, making you feel a bit uncomfortable.
But you still felt timid and didn't dare touch the photo directly. In the end, after hesitating for a moment, you still grabbed Tenna's hand and whispered, "Then...... Can you come with me to see it? ”
Tenna's screen turned pitch black, and he lowered his head to look at you. Actually, he was surprised; he hadn't expected you to make such a request. After all, he was already prepared. Maybe after looking at this photo, you would abandon him, completely abandon him, forget him. That's why he kept you here all the time, because...... He didn't want to. He didn't want to be forgotten by you, he didn't want to be left where you were, nor did he want to watch you stubbornly stay there. You two clearly only have each other left.
"Why?" In the end, he just tried to speak in an incredibly calm voice, and you couldn't detect the slight, almost immeasurable tremors hidden beneath that voice.
"There's no reason. If you really want to find a reason...... That's probably my intuition. My intuition tells me...... It seems that if you stay with me, I'll feel at ease." You whispered, afraid Tenna would hear. After all, you're so restless, you don't want to admit you love Tenna, and you've never confirmed what he said. Even though your actions are almost certain, if you don't say it directly, nothing counts!
“…… Do whatever you want." He finally turned his head in a hurry, after all, he didn't want you to see the screen suddenly lighting up and the handful of flowers uncontrollably appearing at his nose. To be honest, he was indeed overjoyed.
You put your hand into Tenna's hand, then took a deep breath and reached out to touch the photo. In an instant, your thoughts seemed to be drawn far away, to a place you could never measure. That was just a moment, but the next second, you landed in reality, back into the familiar world of light. You seemed like just an observer, or perhaps the girl lying in bed. Now you could calmly and objectively observe all of this. Probably...... It was because no extra emotions flowed in your heart. You only felt a strange, heavy sadness in China, as if silent underwater.
The girl slowly got up, changed her clothes slowly, and opened the door, ready to leave. Her sister was sitting on the sofa, giggling and watching the LCD TV, and your parents were also sitting on the sofa keeping her company.
When they saw you come out, they just glanced up and greeted you briefly. Your mother said indifferently, "Get up and prepare your own breakfast. Your sister is greedy this morning and ate half of your portion. There's nothing you can do about the remaining half. Your dad and I will take care of it." ”
But your father just instinctively frowned and muttered, "You're up so late again. Can you get up earlier next time? You need to develop good living habits...... Otherwise, what will you do about your future work? And many of your classmates went out to work part-time jobs right after the college entrance exam. Can't you learn from them? Why are you just lazing around at home all day? ”
"Count on us to give her money. When you went to college, we only gave you fifteen hundred a month. If it's not enough, don't ask us—we don't have any more money for you." Your mother frowned and glared at her with disgust.
You feel that the girl from back then tries to say something to refute them, but in the end remains silent, just keeps her mouth shut and walks alone to the kitchen to prepare breakfast. After breakfast, she just sits there in a daze.
You look at it all, clutching your chest, feeling that indescribable sadness: "...... Is this my past? Why do you ...... See so much? ”
Tenna pointed to the only appliance in your room that could be considered entertainment—an old TV: "That TV is me. I heard everything." "As for those scenes...... They were just his imagination, added later to the footage.
"I see...... Actually, I think it's okay if they just say that. "If you lower your head, if it were just like this, it might just be simple complaints and nagging, but you would genuinely feel a bit sad.
"But what if you say it every day, and it's like this every day? I told you long ago, they're heartless and treacherous, and you insist on verifying it yourself." Tenna snorted coldly. Actually, he was a bit uneasy too, after all...... He wasn't sure what kind of attitude you would have toward his old TV after you got those memories.
"Seeing is believing, hearing is false." You gave an awkward smile.
The girl from before hugged her knees, silently shedding tears, then turned on the TV. She pressed the remote, turning the volume down to a very low level, probably not wanting to disturb anyone outside. She locked the door, blocking out the laughter and joy outside. The TV was very old and had almost no channels left. No matter how hard I pressed the switch button, I couldn't find a channel I liked, so in the end, I switched to a black-and-white sound movie broadcast.
This movie...... You always feel like you've watched it many times because the plot is very familiar, but no matter how you search, you can't find any memories related to it. It just feels like you can immediately tell how the story will develop next.
You murmured, "Next...... It should be the story where the male lead confesses to the female lead, then the male lead rushes to the battlefield, and the female lead waits in desperation. ”
And what happens next in the film is exactly what you expected. The only difference is that the female lead receives news of the male lead's death and decides to remarry, but unexpectedly, he returns afterward—the plot seems a bit melodramatic.
Tenna also complained, "I don't even know why you liked watching these melodramatic TV shows back then." ”
“…… Maybe it's precisely because these melodramatic dramas are so fake that I can laugh or cry without restraint." That's how you guessed your own thoughts back then. Tenna lowered her head and glanced at you. You were indeed watching the show intently, but the next second, shouting came from outside the door.
"It's lunchtime! Y/N, come out here!" ”
She shouted as she understood as a response, then turned off the TV, opened the door, and walked out.
My mother complained, "You know roughly when we eat. Next time, can't you come out early and wait?" "Every time, we have to call you." ”
Your father glances at you sideways: "Alright, hurry up and wash your hands and get ready to eat. Seriously, every time I have to wait for you for five or ten minutes. The food is about to get cold." ”
There wasn't a single dish on the table that you liked, nor any dish that tasted familiar. You finished the meal in a bland, hurried out, said 'I'm done,' then closed the door and went back to your room, shutting out your parents' scolding from outside.
You rubbed your chin, looked at them in disappointment, and shook your head: "Ah...... So you're not my mom. ”
If only he had. Or...... If only this TV were your family. Although his words can be harsh and his actions sometimes hurt...... But at least, there are many more things that are less heartbreaking.
You were startled by your own thoughts. How could a TV possibly be your own family? You laughed at yourself for being too ridiculous, expecting too much to the point that in the end, you got nothing.
"Of course I can't, it's your mom." Tenna emphasized every word. He was probably annoyed by being called that by you, and you couldn't help but shrink your neck.
After returning to her room, the girl hugged her knees tightly and sat on the bed again, turned on the TV, and continued from where she had paused. This was probably one of the few entertainment activities she had.
Then, the scene ends here. You blink in a daze, stand in front of the photo wall, and reach out. Sika's consciousness tries to touch the other photo beside you, but Tenna grabs her hand.
"It's this one. Are you out of your mind? You can't even figure out the order." Following the red line posted on the photo wall, there really is another photo below, and the one you just touched...... Coincidentally, it doesn't connect to any photo, not with any red thread at all.
You awkwardly said, "I thought the closest was ......."
But you still follow Tenna's words and move on to the next photo.
TBC.

title: Game Time 11 (dntx you)
content:
You closed your eyes, and after that wave of dizziness passed, you ...... again. You stood on that familiar ground. This time, you clearly realized that this seemed to be the house you were living in now.
But why are the walls pitch black? Why does furniture decoration always feel a bit out of place? You never thought about these issues before, but now—you know the truth.
Because even if it was just a shadow, you could feel the scorching heat; the rising flames were like surging waves threatening to swallow you whole. Standing in this sea of fire, you just kept floating and sinking, watching the fire with some stiffness. Instinctively, you wanted to run away, but couldn't move at all. You could only instinctively lean toward Tenna beside you, because for some reason—he seemed very cold.
And you could only barely regain some consciousness by him, and naturally saw your parents anxiously running out the door with your sister, but they didn't pay attention to the tightly shut room, as if no one cared about you.
You fell silent, lowering your gaze, your other hand grabbing Tenna's sleeve, your voice trembling: "Can you ...... Can you leave this memory? I... I don't want to keep watching...... "You don't want to keep dwelling on painful memories, nor torment yourself with past pain and sorrow. Besides, you already understand what happens next."
The girl leaned against the only still-cold television, not touched by the scorching heat, crying helplessly until the metal casing was also stained by the flames. With nowhere to go, wrapped in flames and choking smoke, she fainted, until firefighters arrived, extinguished the house's flames, and rescued you. The TV was also scarred by the flames. But from then on...... You could no longer care about anything else; most of the time, you just sat there blankly, unresponsive.
And what comes next? You can't remember the specifics clearly, but you don't want to keep watching.
Tenna silently glanced at you, then irritably covered your eyes with his hand: "Alright, if you don't want to watch, then don't. But we can't leave until this memory is finished playing." ”
You shook your head and nodded, burying your head in his huge hand, letting tears silently slide down before wetting Tenna's gloves. He was silent for a while, the screen pitch black, and he had no idea what he was thinking. In the end, he just looked up at the tightly closed door, and then at you inside the room.
…… At least now, he can stand beside you, and he can do what he used to do but just stand by blankly and do nothing. He doesn't care—he doesn't care how you see it, or how others see it. After all, it's just an unimportant thing, and Tenna knows he'...... To you, maybe it's just a TV.
So does he really feel indifferent? No, he's unwilling to accept it. Anton Tenna won't let all this happen, so he gently rubs your face with his palm, then softly holds your hand with his other hand, pulling you into his arms. Tall and broad, the embrace a bit cold, but you can almost hear the heart beating within the machine, as if ...... You can feel just how warm his heart is.
You don't mind this embrace; in fact, you're a bit flattered. You might think Tenna wouldn't do that.
But you just reached out and carefully hugged him as well. You could hear the girl's suppressed crying in the room, and uncontrollably, more and more tears welled up in your eyes. At first, you just sobbed softly, Anton Tenna awkwardly reached out to pat your head, then gently patted your back. Then you couldn't help but start crying out loud, as if you wanted to vent all your past emotions, helplessness, and grievances together, because you know, now...... At least one TV is truly listening to you cry. You know you're no longer alone, no longer having to endure all this alone.
If ...... If only he could always be by your side. Even though you were startled by your thought, because you knew that if he returned to the world of light, he'd just be an ordinary TV and wouldn't be able to interact with you. But if you want him to stay in the dark world forever, you still feel a bit unwilling, always feeling...... It's as if some obsession isn't yet fulfilled.
You burst into tears, then start wailing loudly. Tenna didn't stop you; he just tacitly accepted your crying. You don't know if he would feel annoyed, and you couldn't help but feel a bit guilty. In the end, you held back your tears, sniffed, looked up at the expressionless Tenna, and cautiously said, "...... I'm sorry, I cried too loudly just now, it seems like I got your suit dirty." ”
Unconsciously, the air around quieted down, the scorching heat disappeared, replaced by a cold sensation. You returned to Tenna's room.
His voice was calm but almost sarcastic as he said, "Then you're too hindsight. You got it dirty long ago. But this outfit will be changed soon. I have to go host the show later." ”
You blinked at him, and honestly, you found it hard to believe he hadn't scolded you? And his subtext was roughly ...... Let you cry as much as you want.
You sniffled, unable to laugh, and just muffled in a heavy nasal voice: "...... If only you were my family." "Your parents...... Obviously, they don't love you, their child, and obviously, they don't care about you.
Tenna seemed amused by you. He reached out and pinched your face, tugging at you: "Am I not your family?" ”
You could barely speak clearly, so you could only blink and look at him with a hint of grievance: "Mud ...... Vegetarian? ”
He didn't answer your question, but suddenly blurted out, "I love you—but, do you love me?" He lowered his head to look down at you. The pitch-black screen and the drooping antenna all felt especially oppressive, not to mention his screen suddenly lit up, then he grinned and gave you a smile—even though those teeth were so sharp it looked like a single bite could bite through your neck.
You take a deep breath and hold your breath. Of course you like him! But is there a difference between liking and loving...... Is there a difference?
"Of course there's a difference." His voice seemed to show a hint of annoyance. Now his other hand was pinching your face. It didn't hurt much, but you stammered as you spoke, and you realized you had unconsciously spoken the sentence you were thinking about.
"Ju ...... What is Jubiesu...... "You struggled to say this, and then you saw his widened mouth curve even more. You couldn't tell if he was feeling pleasure or if he was feeling something else.
You only hear him say, abruptly saying, "Do you want me to stay by your side forever?" ”
For some reason, you always feel a bit dizzy before your eyes. Instinctively, you want to shake your head to shake off the feeling, but his hand pinchs your face, and you can't make the gesture of shaking your head or nodding when you get the food...... It seems you can do it with complete smoothness.
You could only blink, trying to keep your mind clear. Honestly, you hadn't thought about this issue, since you assumed the TV at home would always be with you. But now, he's become a TV person and is still asking you this question...... Whether it's genuine or other factors at play, you still nod in the end.
You seemed to hear a low laugh...... You—well, you don't really understand what Tenna was laughing at; he just let go of your face. You rubbed your slightly reddened face from the pinch, glanced at Tenna with a hint of frustration, and obviously had no intention of explaining to you.
Tenna just looked at the photo wall again, and for some reason, his voice seemed much softer.
He asked, "...... Next, let's go to this photo." Although it was a question, he spoke in a tone of affirmation, confident that you couldn't argue with him. And the photo he pointed at happened to be the one you had chosen before.
You nodded, reached out to touch that photo, and felt a familiar dizziness, another elusive feeling that seemed to be inside your former self, yet also as if you were just an observer.
You opened your eyes. It was a strange, old house, looking like it was in some remote suburbs. You were holding a small box in your arms, and tears had just dried on your cheeks. In front of her stood a fairly young couple. You recognized them, and they ...... your parents. At that time, you looked only about ten years old.
That woman, who looked like your mother, slightly raised her head and spoke with a hint of disdain and arrogance: "...... We just found you. You are our child. Come back with us." ”
Your body shrank back, trembled slightly, cautiously lifted your head to look at her, then shook it firmly.
"No."
"Why not? Why are you staying here?" That father spoke up, as if ...... Willing to take you back to live is itself a kind of charity.
The little girl hesitated for a moment, then finally spoke, still firmly saying, "Because ...... Because my family is here. I don't want to leave here...... But she was still very young, and in the end, she sobbed softly.
"Your relatives? Who are you? Didn't your grandmother already pass away?" Mother was clearly getting impatient and spoke quickly.
You spread your arms, hugged the TV beside you, and sniffed: "This is my only family." ”
TBC.

title: Game time 12 (dntx you)
content:
You widened your eyes and looked at Tenna, who was expressionless beside you, then at the scene before you. For some reason, Tenna always felt like she was watching a show...... And somehow, he pulled out a voice recorder. At this point, this memory ended. For a moment, you didn't know whether to cover your ears or your eyes, because Tenna pressed the recorder and started playing the same sentence.
"This is my only family." And after finishing that sentence, he pressed the recorder to play it again. Your face flushed red as you tried to jump up to snatch the recorder, but unfortunately, compared to Tenna, you were just too short, so no matter how you tried to reach out, you couldn't get the recorder and were forced to listen to this embarrassing remark several times.
In the end, you have no choice but to cover your ears, grab Tenna's hand with your other hand, and quickly move into the next photo—you definitely don't want to hear that sentence again.
Indeed, once he entered a new memory, he stopped playing that recorder. It was just a randomly chosen photo, and you weren't sure what period it was. You just looked very young, probably from before that fire.
You stared blankly at the elderly lady with a head full of white hair but a gentle and kind smile, sitting in a rocking chair knitting a sweater. For some reason, you couldn't help but feel wronged and missed—a deep longing. Tears unknowingly streamed down your face, but you remained unaware. Tenna silently wiped the tears from your cheeks and said nothing.
Then you see yourself. As a child, you sit seriously in front of a TV, holding cheap diamonds and a curtain you don't know where you bought them, trying hard to decorate the TV, even though it looks a bit out of place.
The old lady smiled, "Nannan, yesterday a few kids came to play with you. Do you want to go out and play?" ”
The little girl said without turning her head, "I don't want to! It's not fun to be with them either. I'd rather dress up my TV here......
"The TV can't talk, and it can't play with you."
"That doesn't matter! I want this TV to be my bride! ”
“…… You can't get married yet. ”
"Hmm...... Then from now on, I want the TV to be my bride! The little girl raised her arm and shouted, radiant and excited.
"Alright, sweetie, let's eat." Until the grandmother called the little girl to go eat together, and the little girl happily took her hand, and they walked together in a certain direction. You smelled the familiar aroma of food, just like the dishes Tenna prepared for you at noon.
By the time you come to your senses, you've already left that memory, and before you know it, tears are streaming down your face. You instinctively grab Tenna's hand, choking up for a long time but unable to say a word.
He also rarely mocked you, just quietly glanced at you and asked lightly, "Do you want to keep watching?" ”
You shook your head, instinctively refusing the offer, just sniffling: "I...... No need to look anymore. ”
"So have you remembered everything now?" He continued to ask, but for some reason, you sensed a hint of nervousness in his voice.
You honestly shook your head: "I don't remember." But maybe...... The things you can't remember probably aren't that important either. "After all, the memories from the past fifteen years mostly come back after seeing that photo. You remember buying Tenna all kinds of decorations, like veils and headbands, and you even hung necklaces and bracelets on his antenna. You also recalled those familiar but gone-of-a-kind scents from memory, and remembered the time when your home was full plus a TV, and you only had two family members.
And after the fire...... The memories that continued up to entering the Dark World remained blurry, but just from those few fragments just now, you could sense that these were probably not the memories you wanted to recover.
Besides, it probably doesn't really matter.
"So, what are you going to do next?" Tenna's voice was a bit tense. He knew that if you insisted on returning to the Light World, no matter how much he tried to stop you, it wouldn't work—you wouldn't listen. So, if you wanted to return to the Light World, he could only follow your wishes.
“…… Can you play games with me?" You just tugged at Tenna's shirt and gave him a pitiful look. He clearly couldn't stand you like this, and his screen suddenly went pitch black again. Then he turned his head around, unable to see his face clearly.
You blink, your eyes darting around in your sockets. Somehow, you feel like you've suddenly found a way to handle him.
But you just tugged at the hem of his shirt again, your voice a bit pitiful: "...... I'm not in a good mood. Can you play with me for a while?" ”
Tenna finally turned her head. Her screen was lit, but she still showed no other expression, and her voice was tense, a bit stiff: "Fine." So, what are you going to play? ”
You kept blinking at him: "Hmm...... I bought an RPG game disc before. I couldn't get past one myself...... Your skills must be much better than mine, right? "You said that on purpose. Since he mocked you like that before, it means he's really good at gaming—so playing games with you and helping you clear levels is something he has to do!" You thought this with confidence.
Tenna glanced down at you. Of course, he could tell there was a hint of provocation in his words—but it didn't matter, he didn't care that much. Besides, that provocation had indeed stirred his fighting spirit.
So he simply said in a cold and resolute voice, "Of course, I'm good at any game." ”
Your eyes darted around as you asked, "Then...... Can you play horror games with me? I'm afraid of the dark." ”
This is true. Because of your fear of blacks, many of the games you buy end up unfinished, but you also like to buy puzzle games. Because many of these games are puzzle-themed but have a terrifying nature, you don't keep playing.
Then Tenna fell silent. He didn't answer you. You just gently tugged at his shirt with your hand, softened your voice, and whispered, "Please, I really think that game is probably fun, but I don't dare to keep playing......
“…… Of course, no problem. His voice was still icy, and you couldn't hear any extra emotion. Then he scooped you up and hurried toward the lounge.
From initially feeling uncomfortable to now somewhat enjoying his embrace, after all, he has treated you this way these days.
So at this moment, you just put your hand on his shoulder to keep your balance, then leaned in to look back. From a distance, you could see some pippins whispering as they walked by, and when they noticed your gaze, they sped up and ran away, making you puff out your cheeks in frustration. You never knew why those pippins were so afraid to get close to you...... Including the other employees of the TV world—could it be because of Tenna's orders? Thinking that way isn't entirely impossible.
In a moment of distraction, Tenna had already taken you to the lounge. He put you on the sofa, sat down next to you, and then handed you the game controller.
You walked over and stuffed another CD into the TV in front, then went back and sat next to Tenna, unconsciously leaning a little closer to him—almost sitting right next to him.
Tenna turned his head again. You couldn't see what expression he had, but only Tenna knew. He lowered his head and covered his nose, unable to hold back the flowers sprouting from his nose. If you saw it, you might think he picked some flowers and planted them there, since you used to do this often as a child, under the guise of dressing up for TV.
It's just a pity you didn't see it, and he absolutely could never let you see it. Since that fire, you haven't dressed him up again, so...... He could never be shown to you.
But you just stared intently at the screen, tapped the keys, opened the game, then poked Tenna, your eyes sparkling: "Time to pick a character! I'm going to pick the assassin, it looks really cool." "You've always liked the assassin class.
Tenna didn't argue with you; he just glanced around and chose a defensive tank character.
“…… Then I'll have to hide behind you and deal damage, so you have to protect me!" You swayed your legs and shook your head as you spoke.
…… Actually, you only chose to come back to play games to ease the confusion, anxiety, and sadness you felt after learning about your memories. Because you know that playing games here, at least someone will accompany you, and at least you won't have to return to the world of light and sit alone in front of that TV.
"What, you can't possibly be this weak, can't you not dodge at all?" Tenna couldn't help but mock you, then you looked at him, tears naturally welling up in your eyes, but you gazed at him with tear-filled eyes.
Tenna's antenna was hanging down, and you just shook it slightly, almost like a rogue as you said, "I don't care, you have to protect me! If I die mysteriously, it will definitely be your fault!" ”
After saying that, you start to feel a bit guilty. After all, you know what you're saying is completely nonsense, completely pointless. If you're prepared, Tenna might still be able to mock you again.
But to your surprise, Tenna was silent for a moment, then softly said, "Alright." ”
You widened your eyes in shock.
TBC.

title: Game Time 13 (dntx you)
content:
It was simply unbelievable—Tenna could actually say something like that? You glanced at him carefully twice, but from his expressionless face, you couldn't see anything either. You could only sigh softly, turn away, and cough lightly, pretending to be arrogant: "Then let's settle it then. You have to keep your word!" ”
You've all chosen your character and entered the game. The squishy ones naturally follow behind the tank, sneaking in and stabbing down monsters that suddenly appear. Unfortunately—jungle monsters always spawn from behind you, and Tenna usually controls the character to block you by a second. You can't help but start complaining: "Why are you always like this? Look, my character's health bar is almost gone!" ”
After all, you're just fragile and can die easily, and now it's just the two of you—without a healer, you're easy to die!
You still want to finish the game seriously, so when you encounter sudden attacks, you do try hard to dodge. But no matter how much you dodge, you keep losing health until you're down to just a little.
Tenna responded calmly, but you didn't know what he meant, so you couldn't help but raise your voice: "You have to protect me well!" ”
"I know, I'm working hard to protect you." You always feel there's a hint of sarcasm in his words, so you can't help but glare at him fiercely, while Tenna just looks at you innocently on the screen. Then, you watch helplessly as his character falls right in front of yours, and the character you control can't dodge the sudden onslaught—it's game over together.
You angrily slam the handle onto the sofa and poke Tenna's nose: "Say it. Are you doing it on purpose? That character isn't that easy to kill!" ”
Although Anton Tenna acted like he wouldn't mistake someone else, and he really did say that, he nodded decisively: "Yes, it's not that easy to die, but I've been taking attacks for you. It's only natural that I'll die in the end, right?" ”
…… Although he spoke with certainty and sounded very innocent, you couldn't help but feel like he was just making excuses. You couldn't really say anything to him, so you just glared at him bitterly: "I know...... Then here's the deal: this time, you become the healer, I don't believe you can! "As you spoke, you directed Tenna to choose the only healer role in the game.
You seem to hear a snicker, but when you turn your head in confusion, all you see is Tenna's pitch-black screen. Then, he looks at you and asks calmly, "What's wrong?" ”
You quickly shook your head and, unusually a bit stammering, said, "No, nothing's wrong." ”
But in the end, you're full of doubts. You always feel Tenna is scheming, even though it probably has nothing to do with the game you're playing...... Probably?
But after that, you glared angrily at the screen, unable to say a word. The reason is simple: Tenna is indeed casting healing on you, and you are diligently fighting monsters. This time, the challenge has higher stacks than last time, so the monsters' attack power is also higher. Tenna continues to cast healing at fixed intervals, but the fragile assassin dies after just a few hits, so the healer character starts reviving you.
Unfortunately, the resurrection cooldown is long, and you barely hit a few times before being killed by monsters again. Tenna stopped moving forward and just kept healing herself, waiting for cooldowns to get you back up. You were killed by monsters within two seconds, and the cycle repeated.
You stared blankly, but couldn't really say anything wrong to Tenna. Because he was indeed dutifully protecting you. In that sense, it seemed you were the one who wasn't very cooperative, after all...... You would be killed within two seconds of resurrection.
And after finally grinding down this monster, the next wave arrives quickly. This time, you die quickly again, so all you can do is watch Tenna cast healing spells while struggling to dodge attacks, but unfortunately, he is ultimately killed. You guys are still game over.
You can't help but complain, "You said your gaming skills are really high, but now you seem still pretty bad. You can't protect me at all!" ”
Tenna just reached out and tugged at your face, her tone a bit sinister: "Just because you say something like that's pretty good, huh?" ”
You were pinched in the face, your speech was a bit slurred, and you just tried hard to retort: "That's another steaming look! As long as I'm having fun, that's enough!" "You don't care about all that!
"So, are you having fun with me?" His tone was still sinister, but he just asked you this question out of nowhere.
You hesitated for a moment, then nodded: "Kaisen." ”
At this moment, Tenna turned his head and coughed twice. You have no idea what he was doing, but his screen seemed to light up for a moment, and the pollen was inexplicably drifting out.
You tilted your head, but before you could ask anything more, Tenna turned her head and said, "As long as you're happy, that's enough. Why don't we just keep playing like this?" His voice was light and a bit faint, and for some reason, you had a bad feeling and couldn't help but shiver.
"No, I want to clear this game! I can't get stuck!" You protested strongly, seriously expressing your wish.
Tenna was silent for a moment. His screen was pitch black, staring at you. Even though his screen was pitch black, you could feel that he was watching you all along. You didn't know why he was doing this, and couldn't help but shiver again, protesting, "Let go of the nest! Since two people aren't enough, call your employees to play games with us!" ”
"You're right." Tenna snorted coldly. For some reason, you felt like those words were about to freeze your teeth, and you couldn't help but shiver again.
tenna just stood up, opened the door, and casually waved outside. Then a pippins happily hopped in. He probably wanted to say something, but upon seeing you and tenna, he suddenly went silent. He just picked up a game controller, connected it to the TV, and then sat on tenna's side, far away from you.
This round, you still chose the assassin, Tenna was the healer, and Pippins picked the tank. You thought this kind of team would be fine, but you still don't believe the second and first protection can't clear the stage. But—every time you encounter a monster, the healer is the first to block the assassin, while the tank, acting like the main damage dealer, senses something is wrong and waits a few seconds before blocking the healer.
You feel a bit frustrated. You used to be full of confidence, but now you're unsure. You doubt that this time the number of layers won't even be as high as the first time.
Sure enough—even though there was a tank in the team, the healer didn't care about him at all. She didn't throw a single healer at him, just throwing all kinds of buffs at you. And seeing the tank's positioning wasn't that good either, and after all, he was killed by a monster. You couldn't help but get anxious and quickly nudged Tenna with your elbow.
"Hurry up and save him! No one can take the damage, and we'll be wiped out again!" "No sooner had he finished speaking than you were also lying dead on the ground due to the monster's sneak attack.
Tenna just cast a resurrection skill to pull you back up, calmly saying, "Why should I?" ”
You were stunned for a moment, not expecting Tenna to ask that question. While you were still dazed, the monster attacked again, striking you, and you collapsed once more.
You couldn't care about all that, just hurriedly shouted, "Because I want to finish this game! I've died so many times already, wasting so much time, I was planning to play another game!" ”
"So, do you want to clear this game more, or do you want to play with me?" As soon as she finished speaking, the healer revived the assassin once again, but after being attacked by monsters, the healer was knocked down. You tried hard to control the assassin to move, but unfortunately, you still couldn't withstand the monsters' assault. Soon, you died tragically again, and the game was game over.
You ignored the trembling pippins who were itching to escape from the lounge, just seriously thinking about the issue. Alright...... Maybe the obsession with beating the game is strong, but what do you really want?
In the end, you still hesitantly spoke up: "I...... I want to play games with you. ”
But right after, you hurriedly add, "But I really want to finish this game!" It's just ...... I want to finish this game with you, that's all. ”
Tenna stared at you with the screen pitch black. You swallowed, thinking you hadn't said anything wrong, then just waved his hand, and the pippins left the lounge as if pardoned.
Then, Tenna said calmly, "Then it's just the two of us. Let's do it again." ”
“…… Really? "You're a bit suspicious, after all...... You've fought three times just now and still haven't cleared the level.
Tenna just nodded affirmatively, so you could only open the game again with some suspicion. Well, after the three rounds just now, your skill at dodging monster attacks has really improved. At least up until now, you haven't died even once on the floor where you and Tenna first fought each other!
Of course...... This might also be thanks to the healer, since now she not only heals you but also shields you from damage at the front, while you only need to fight monsters simply. Of course, fighting monsters requires a lot of consideration!
Maybe because he changed his role, this time you have surpassed the number of floors from the second time and keep climbing higher. Your eyes light up, and as you get higher, monsters become harder and harder. You have a feeling you're about to face the boss.
Sure enough—on the next level, turning around in front of you, is the ultimate big boss of this game.
TBC.

title: Game Time 14 (dntx you)
content:
You can't help but get excited: "Finally, we've reached the final level—once we clear it, this game is completely over!" ”
The healer's character stands in front of you, taking a massive damage attack from the boss, leaving only a health skin hanging there. Tenna seems to be casually asking this question: "So after this game is over, what are we supposed to play?" ”
You focus your attention on attacking the boss while casually replying, "What are you playing?" Hmm...... For duo, I have some action or puzzle games, but I still prefer to play horror games! "After all, you're curious how Tenna would perform in a horror game.
"Alright, I understand." He didn't say much, just answered you concisely. Although you were a bit puzzled, in this situation, you didn't have the right to ask questions, because BOOS's attacks were coming at you in full swing. You fled in a panic, your health bar dropping but only to be pulled back up, all while trying every possible way to attack. Unfortunately, BOOS was really tough, and you spent a long time in this level.
Finally, BOOS takes the final blow, wailing and roaring as he collapses. You wipe the unwarranted sweat from your forehead and excitedly raise your hand to high-five Tenna: "Yay, we finally cleared the level!" ”
After saying that, you raised your hand, and Tenna did the same, but his hand covered yours and didn't high-five you. You stared at him in shock, pouted, and said a bit aggrievedly, "Why didn't you high-five...... We went through so much trouble to clear it! ”
"Yes, but most of it is thanks to me, right?" After this sentence, the damage and other damage settlement panels were displayed for you. Indeed, because you really like assassins, and Tenna didn't deal a single bit of damage, your damage share on the panel shows 100%. In contrast, both damage absorption and healing are 100% for Tenna—well, some of the damage absorbed also hits you. You know that without Tenna, you might not even get past the first two stages.
You can only clear your throat and cough twice, then look up: "So what! Anyway, I'm the one dealing damage, I'm really strong!" ”
Tenna just nodded perfunctorily: "Mm-hmm, you're amazing, you're strong, you're the best." ”
Even though you could tell he was just brushing you off, you were still happy. Your eyes curved as you grabbed his hand and shook it side to side. Your small hand tried hard to hold his: "Mm, I'm the best, so Tenna is the second best!" "You speak with such confidence, as if the whole world is made up only of you." Tenna's screen was still pitch black. You felt him turn his head to glance at you, then turn his head back. His screen lit up again, his voice a bit teasing: "Alright, then the world's number one, the strongest Y/N, will surely protect me, the fragile second place, right?" ”
You're stuck. Honestly, of course you can't guarantee it! But soon, you cleared your throat and put your hands on your hips, saying, "How can I protect you? The second place should be protecting the first place!" After all, the second place is strong too, but the reason the first place is the first place is simply because she doesn't want to work hard! ”
For some reason, you always feel Tenna giving you a half-smile. You touch your nose, feeling a bit guilty. After all, these things are just your nonsense. You never intended to convince Tenna; these are just twisted logic.
For some reason, you always felt his expression was a bit smiling, half-smirk, and rather creepy. Anyway, you couldn't help but shiver, but you still stubbornly refused, patting your chest with your other hand: "But if the second place is that weak, then I, the first place, can protect you either!" "From now on, just follow behind me and watch me show off my skills!" Saying that, you happily opened the next game, which was a horror game.
Tenna simply said softly, "Mm, you must protect me. I'll be watching closely." ”
Honestly, you're still afraid of the dark, so after buying this game, you never played it once. Today, thanks to Tenna here, you finally reopened the game. Soon, you chose the simplest level and entered together with Tenna's controlled character. The car had various dashboards that let you see data from another character entering different rooms and check their safety. You immediately decided, "Go down and check that haunted house. I'll watch the data here for you." ”
"Why aren't you the one going?" You all know that cars with their lights on are absolutely safe zones; as long as you stay here, you won't encounter any danger.
And you just say seriously, "Because I'm first, I have to stay here and see how things go. I'm working hard too!" I need to analyze based on data, and you just need to risk going into the haunted house. Besides, isn't it only natural for second place to work for first? ”
"Then the first place should be taking the risk, right?" His voice carried a hint of sarcasm.
You shook your head seriously, waving your fingers and said, "No, no, no. First, if we go on a risky trip and something goes wrong, what then? I'll stay here and see how things develop. You go downstairs!" ”
Of course, this was just an excuse because you were number one and didn't have to work. You didn't believe it anyway. You just didn't want to go down and encounter ghosts; you're very afraid of the dark.
Tenna turns to look at you, then finally gets out of the car with the camera and flashlight, entering the haunted house. You carefully look at the dashboard, confirm the data, and dutifully start announcing: "The temperature and humidity here are normal, no ghosts. You can explore this room with the lights on as usual." ”
For some reason, you seem to hear the sound of your teeth chattering, but when you turn your head and look around, you can't find the source of the sound, and the strange sound has disappeared. You have no choice but to give up and continue directing Tenna: "Keep moving forward. There is no abnormal data on the dashboard yet. You can explore normally, just turn on the lights." ”
When the room was brightly lit, the eerie grinding of teeth stopped. You suspected Tenna was making that sound, but since you had no proof, you could only turn around in confusion and glance at him again. You wouldn't know until you looked, but when you did, you were shocked. You guessed that somehow, or at some point, Tenna's body had actually shrunk! Just now, you had to tilt your head up to see him, but now you only need to tilt your head slightly to see him clearly. You blinked, a bit stunned, your mouth agape, and then Tenna's cold voice came through: "What are you looking at?" "Look at your game screen carefully. I don't want to be inexplicably dead just after entering." ”
You let out a couple of 'ohs', scolding yourself in your heart, determined never to look at Tenna in a daze again. Then you shifted your attention back and stared intently at the screen. The dashboard had been normal before, but now it started fluctuating wildly, with the temperature fluctuating wildly. You shouted urgently, "Ah, the ghost has passed by!" The data on the dashboard has moved! "Just as you finished speaking, a sudden click came from the house. The game screen went dark, and the entire room where Tenna was was lost power. After a brief adjustment, you could barely see your surroundings, and the dashboard returned to normal."
Although you haven't played this game before, you still have a rough idea of the process: "That ghost should have already left, and the power in the room should have tripped. You can go to the basement and push the switch back up." ”
But when you finished speaking, Tenna didn't move for a long time. You turned to look at Tenna in confusion, only to find his screen was still pitch black. The difference was that his figure seemed to be slowly shrinking. Gradually, you could see Tenna clearly just by turning your head. You nudged him with your elbow: "Why aren't you moving? If you stand here and don't move, that ghost might come looking for you soon." ”
Unfortunately, he still stood there, not moving. And his body kept shrinking, not saying a word. You figured he was definitely afraid of horror games, but you couldn't just leave him there, so you gritted your teeth, casually guessed the type of ghost in the house, then grabbed a candle and flashlight and rushed into the dark room.
Your teeth were chattering uncontrollably. Now you could be sure that the grinding sound you heard earlier was coming from Tenna. You lit the candle and burned out the only piece of clothing you had just found in the wardrobe with the candlelight. Then, following the notes in your notebook, you drew a formation, placing the candle in the center. You prepared to perform a ritual for the ghost, though you didn't know if your approach was right or wrong, and you were very nervous.
But just as you set up the formation, a cold wind blew by and extinguished the candle. You had no choice but to try every possible way to relight the candle with matches, but no matter what, there was no flame. Not only that, another cold wind howled by, your screen turned pitch black, followed by a loud crash. It looked like your character had died under the ghost's interference.
Although I still felt shyness and lingering fear, when I turned around and saw Tenna had already tossed the handle aside, now only about the size of a pet dog, I couldn't help but laugh a little.
You couldn't help but tease, "I didn't expect you to be so afraid of the dark. Didn't you say before that you're good at any game?" ”
Unfortunately, before he could answer and you hadn't said anything more, Tenna's game screen went black. With another bang, he fell to the ground, followed by the payment screen.
You can't help but let out a sharp crackling sound: "No—I was almost clearing the level—it's clearly the kind of ghost I guessed!" ”
TBC.

title: Game time 15 (dntx you)
content:
Tenna didn't respond. You glanced at him again and found he was still the same size as before. He clearly claimed to be good at any game, yet he was still so afraid of horror games...... You pursed your lips and had no choice but to lower your voice: "Alright, how about we redo this level?" ”
Tenna still didn't make a sound, but you noticed out of the corner of your eye. He quietly nodded, so you took a deep breath, chose the same level, and then entered. Well, this time you learned from last time and knew exactly what kind of ghost was inside this house. So you grabbed your flashlight and the items needed to seal the ghosts and rushed in.
At the end, you reminded Tenna, "Just stay in the car, protect yourself, and don't go down." With that, you rushed out of the car, arrived at the pitch-black house, pushed open the front door, gritted your teeth, turned on the front hall light, then placed the candle on the table, manipulated the character to draw a formation, and rushed to the bedroom to grab a random piece of clothing to burn. But just as you rushed out, the front hall light went out again, leaving only the candlelight faintly burning.
Tenna had reverted to his original size. He controlled the character, looking at the dashboard and said with a hint of schadenfreude, "Ah, the ghost just passed by you. Your HP dropped by 20%." ”
You pursed your lips, and now he was as mean as he always was. I really didn't know what was going on with this guy, but...... After all, he was the one you liked. Even though you were a bit annoyed by hearing that now, you just controlled the character to burn that piece of clothing, then recited the spell as needed to seal the ghost.
You won this round. You excitedly grabbed Tenna, who was about to drop the controller, and started the next round: "Don't leave yet, let's clear this round too!" ”
Tenna was almost forced to start this round of the game with you. Once again, he kept his mouth tightly shut and said nothing, so quiet that it felt strange to you. And this time, you couldn't just leave Tenna alone to run into ghosts. As for going alone or something—that was even more impossible!
So you nudged Tenna with your elbow: "Let's go into the room together this round. We'll walk together, so we won't be so scared, right?" As you spoke, your character picked up the camera and flashlight, while Tenna's character picked up another flashlight.
You took a deep breath and got out of the car. After a few steps, you realized Tenna hadn't followed, so you turned back: "What are you standing here for? Come down together." ”
"I think you can clear the level alone, so why bring me along?" His tone was half mocking. Of course, if you think he did it on purpose, he was just...... He just didn't want to run into ghosts. This is the first time you've noticed Tenna is so afraid of ghosts. Next time, just pretend to be one and scare him!
Your character pushes and pushes back and forth, and finally manages to fill his role. You just say as if it's only natural: "Of course the second place should go with the first. Otherwise, if the second place gets left out, what if they can't catch up to the first place?" ”
You hear Tenna seem to sneer, then simply say, "Alright." ”
He finally manages to control the character to move forward, but the speed is very slow. Your character circles around his character, and in the end, with no other choice, you still stand behind him, pushing the character forward: "You should be in second place, you should be standing at the front!" ”
"Why should I?" He was extremely stingy with words, but you actually felt he was just scared, because it seemed like his body had shrunk a little more.
"Because you're in second place! If the second place doesn't steal the credit, they'll never beat the first!" You still said with confidence.
But his character still moves forward slowly. You try hard to use your modeling to push him forward, and it took a long time to get him to the door. You're so patient, since you don't know how much time you've wasted on this trip. Honestly, you're a bit tired and don't really want to play games anymore.
"Alright, open the door. Last round, you successfully entered the room and searched the room, didn't you? This round won't be a problem either!" You encouraged Tenna, and he finally reluctantly controlled the character to open the door, though he still refused to go inside.
Honestly, you're a bit angry at this point. You were supposed to play games with you, but he ended up like this. You might as well call another Dark Civilian to be your playmate.
So you dropped the controller, got up angrily, and tried to leave: "Looks like you don't want to play games with me anymore. Then I'll call other Dark People to join me." "Anyway, you can't just refuse to cooperate like this."
But you had barely taken two steps before Tenna grabbed your sleeve and dragged you into her arms, her voice cold: "Don't look for other Dark People." ”
"Then why don't you just play your game properly? You even said you wanted to play with me? Look at how much you've gotten into it!" You turned around and poked Tenna with your fingers, but Tenna just lowered her head, staring at you in the darkest light.
His voice was still emotionless: "...... Alright, I'll finish this round seriously." He finally started running around with his game character, quickly turning on the lights in the room. At some point, he even brought a portable thermometer to measure the temperature in each room. Finally, he controlled the character to run to a small bedroom and said dryly, "The ghost is in this room, the thermometer is malfunctioning." Then he placed you on the sofa next to him.
Only then did you notice he had turned into a tiny ball, about the size of a pet dog, and the trembling in his voice became even more obvious. Helpless, you had no choice but to hold the little tenna in your arms, then tightly shut the room with ghosts, hanging a cross at the door to prevent this type of ghost from escaping. Then you lit a candle at the door, drew a formation, and chanted incantations as you sent the ghost away.
The screen showed you had won. You tossed down the game controller and stretched: "Hmm—finally cleared it!" I'm tired. I'll keep playing later. "You said matter-of-factly, since you can't do anything else right now except play games. You also disdainfully tossed Tenna, who had just finished playing and was slowly growing bigger and heavier.
"Hmm, then what do you plan to do next?" His voice was quite calm, so unfamiliar that it didn't even feel like Tenna, and when you looked up, all you could see was ...... His face still wore that cold, indifferent expression, as if nothing had happened.
You were silent for a moment. Even though you knew you shouldn't make this proposal, you wanted to ...... You couldn't just stay ignorant like this. You couldn't just stay in this state, constantly avoiding past realities. Escaping is shameful but useful, but...... Just a little while, just a little while. You know that only when you stop running away can you truly grow up.
So you take a deep breath and calmly say, "I want to return to the World of Light." ”
Then, you hear the machine rattling, and you wonder if you're mistaken, but then you realize it's Tenna making the sound. You watch the TV as your head slowly turns around, then lowers your head to face you.
“…… Isn't it better to stay here forever? Only by staying here will you truly stay happy forever." he said. His screen was pitch black, and you can confidently hear a faint tremor in his voice.
"Of course it's good, but...... I can't deny or abandon my past self, nor can I abandon the old you. I want to go back...... Find the traces you once left behind, I want to reclaim all the memories. I shouldn't get lost in this. So...... Tenna, trust me, okay? Because I love you, and I want to love you even more, that's why I want to do this. "As you spoke, you lowered your eyebrows, your voice trembling a little.
You really think so, but this is also the first time you've admitted that this matter really exists. Before that, you never dared to admit it, because you were afraid that Tenna wasn't as you wished, because you felt timid, uneasy, and uneasy about this relationship. You couldn't confirm whether this twisted, anxious, and sometimes aggrieved emotion was still love.
But you also feel joy and excitement about this, and feel peace and happiness beside him, so you think, perhaps that's how things are. After all...... Before that, there were no more people in your household.
Tenna remained silent. He knew you probably wanted to find some evidence to prove that you two truly loved each other, but...... In the current house, there probably isn't much more evidence left. The original house...... Has long since gathered dust in my memory.
But in the end, he still chose to give in, and he also felt hopeful for it. If ...... Even this house now bears traces of love, it means you have always loved each other. He was moved because he could never be sure if you still loved him after that fire.
So he relented: "...... Alright, you can go back, but only for one day." His voice was icy cold. Even though you knew what he said was completely useless, since Tenna couldn't come to the Light World to catch you—he was just a TV. Still, you smiled and gave him an OK gesture. You wouldn't break your promise.
"Yeah, I know. I'll definitely be back within a day." Saying this, you still feel a bit nervous, since you don't know what will happen after you get back.
And Tenna watches you step through the gateway to the world of light.

title: Game Time 16 (dntx you)
content:
You seem to be walking through the corridors of memory.
"Today, it's just me at home again...... You sat cross-legged on the wooden floor, mumbling as you fiddled with the game console in your hands. Grandma left early in the morning, saying she was going to the market and wanted to sell more eggs from the hen she laid yesterday to earn some money. Your family doesn't have much money; the little money is mostly spent on buying things for you. Grandma always thinks about earning more money to help you live a better life. To avoid disappointing her, you always work hard to get better grades. You want to move to a big city, live with Grandma, and bring this second-hand old TV and that second-hand game console over, because they've always been with you.
Muttering to yourself, you turn on the TV. There aren't many games—most are game discs that grandma picked up from trash, unwanted ones, or you rented from the county town. But even with these few games, you're already having a great time.
You open a game you haven't played before, this game...... Playing alone isn't very fun, so you guess you haven't opened it until you have no one to play with you. In the end, you have no choice but to open the game alone.
This game basically involves entering an abandoned factory to collect items that can be exchanged for money and other resources, while also avoiding the monsters inside. Honestly, entering such factories is indeed quite scary, and you heard in the county town that some of the ghosts there are quite scary.
But you still took a deep breath, mustered up your courage, controlled your character, and started the game, stepping into the factory alone. Honestly, pitch black is pretty scary, but luckily you found a flashlight that made it easier to see what's ahead. After some picking, you managed to find some things, like surprise boxes thrown around or old batteries...... You didn't know how such things could be here, but you still huffed and took them back and put them on the spaceship.
You looked at the value of these items and hesitated—should you escape now while there's no danger, or seek fortune by risk—go again? Seeing that it was already afternoon, you hesitated for a moment, but in the end, you grabbed the shovel you had just bought for self-defense and then got off the spaceship.
Trembling, you enter the abandoned factory again. At first, there was nothing, or rather, it was empty—after all, you had already taken out something valuable. Then you continued deeper until the character's movements noticeably slowed. Your flashlight shone down and saw a ...... Transparent, or rather green, writhing thing, seemingly called a slime. Instinctively, you opened your mouth wide, wanting to shout out but lost your voice. You instinctively stepped into the Slime King's interior. But beyond that was a dead end. You tried to circle back the way you came, but only to find it was a vicious loop. No matter what you did, you couldn't get out; it seemed you were lost.
You puff out your cheeks, tears quickly welling up in your eyes. You just sniff, not giving up completely, still trying to get out, but...... It's all in vain. The flashlight is out of battery, and even a shovel can't kill the slime. You're trapped in this place and can't get out. In the end, you can only put down the game controller and watch in vain as the slime wraps around your character, while your character collapses to the ground, dead.
No one restarts the ship, and no one brings back your corpse, so...... You can only restart the game, and this game counts as your loss.
You sniff, trying to comfort yourself that it was all okay—after all, this was only the first round, and you just needed to start one more round. But the next second, you noticed your perspective changed to another character, who pressed a button, transported your corpse back to the ship, and started the ship, which meant you could proceed to the second level.
But...... Wait, where did this person come from? You widened your eyes, your body trembling uncontrollably. Could it be haunted? You couldn't help but ask, "Who... who are you?" Your voice was still trembling.
Maybe it's just your imagination. You seem to see the TV's antenna slightly shake, and when you rub your eyes and look again, the antenna remains the same. Instead, the TV screen goes black, then a mosaic flashes, and then the screen lights up with characters of varying sizes, like characters taken from various news reports and other programs. You barely piece together the words the TV shows you: "anton...... tenna？ ”
You seem to see the TV's antenna trembling slightly. If it's a ghost, then you're really quite scared. After all, you've heard plenty of stories, and you definitely don't want to be involved with ghosts. Otherwise, what would Grandma do if she was left here all alone? But if it were just this TV...... Although the phenomenon was a bit strange, you could still accept it, since the TV had been with you for a long time—at least that's what you think.
"So...... Are you the TV you have? "But to be safe, you still asked a bit more. What if it's just a haunted trick trying to trick you? Even though if the potion is sincere about tricking you, you probably have no way to do it......
The TV screen was black-and-white mosaic again, and then a big hook pattern flashed on the screen. Anyway, you breathed a sigh of relief and were quite excited—your TV was conscious! Of course, you knew this couldn't be told to others, but since it was a little secret between you and your family—you had to admit, you still felt a bit nervous.
So you ask again, "Can you play games with me?" This time, the TV just redraws the matching hook. You excitedly shout 'yes,' and then the TV screen switches back—it's the same game as before. The difference is you have a teammate, but they probably won't talk to you.
You still chose the factory from earlier. You still have some resentment toward the slime that trapped you. This time, Tenna was the one who got off the ship with you, but you entered the factory directly from the entrance, while he detoured outside the factory and entered through another secure entrance.
You excitedly start licking the room—no, it's just collecting supplies. This time, you find the same surprise box as last time, an abandoned TV, and a countdown that starts counting down as soon as you pick it up...... It shows something called a bomb.
Then, before you even realize it, there was a loud boom—your character was blown to death.
You widened your eyes, staring blankly at your fallen body and the changing camera angles, quickly shouting, "Tenna!" Tenna！ "Hurry back to the spaceship, I'm already dead. You can't die anymore......"
He also carried a few things down and returned to the spaceship. It looked like a toy dog and a battery box. Then he finally started the ship and flew away. His corpse was summoned back by him, and it was time to choose the next location.
After a glance, you still feel a lingering fear, and decide not to choose a factory again. Instead, you choose another place with a higher mortality rate and resource rates—an abandoned villa.
When you arrive, you excitedly rush down: "Alright, I don't believe there's anything in this room that can stop me!" You grab the shovel and run off excitedly. Tenna's character follows you calmly into the villa.
Hmm...... Gift boxes, discarded cards, battery boxes, and even an abandoned TV here...... You muttered, but in the end, you struggled to carry the valuable abandoned TV outside. Then, you heard a clicking sound from the first floor of the villa, like some kind of wood twisting. You went out to take a look and saw it was a soldier patrolling there—apparently called the Nutcracker. You were startled and instinctively stood there, but the Nutcracker aimed its gun at you. Before you could react, you saw Tenna already behind the Nutcracker, swung a shovel a few times, stunned him, and knocked him to the ground, ending your crisis.
You exhale, beaming with joy: "Thank you, tenna! I thought I was going to die there...... Good thing you're here! ”
The screen didn't switch, only showing lines of character by word after a long time. I don't know if it was some kind of good word pieced together from some news report: "It's okay." This is what I should do. ”
“…… Then you have to keep protecting me all the time. I really don't want to die for no reason anymore." You said coquettishly. While you were there, you ran out with Tenna and threw the things back on the spaceship. You don't want to die and still have nothing to retrieve, making a wasted trip.
The TV was quiet, with only the hum of the heat. You might think it wouldn't answer you, but in the end, a line of text slowly popped up on the screen: "Mm, I will always protect you, forever." ”
Forever.
You don't know, you just gave a silly smile to this TV: "Yeah, it's a deal!" Pinky swear, hanging for a hundred years, no change—wait, you can't pinky that. "You stuck out your tongue, a little embarrassed.
At that moment, your ship started up again, and the TV screen went pitch black again. Then, a grin flashed across the screen, leaving you a bit stunned. Instinctively, you leaned over and gently patted Tenna's shell: "Stop laughing, it's so scary!" ”
So the TV put away that smile, leaving only the game screen, and the antenna seemed to bend down a bit...... Maybe it felt a bit wronged?
Either way, you remember that was the first real conversation between you and your home TV.
TBC.

title: Game Time 17 (dntx you)
content:
Since then...... You always take advantage of grandma being away to talk to the TV by yourself. After all, you don't dare talk when someone else is around—what if they think you're crazy?
