But when you're bored, you still turn on the TV and play games with Tenna. He becomes your silent companion, and all of this feels like a secret between you two.
However...... It still happens occasionally
After all, even though you're a bit weak, you love playing and really enjoy puzzle games. Many single-player puzzle games are played by just one person. You struggle to control the console and spin the screen, but no matter how hard you try, you can't find a real way to clear the level. At this point, Tenna seems to be unable to take it anymore. Somehow, he picked out a red circle and placed it in the spot where you couldn't find the right spot after searching for ages.
You were a bit unhappy, and grandma wasn't home either, so you pouted and spoke up: "Why do you need to hint me!" I just wanted to think it over myself, and only when I figured out the answer would I be the happiest...... If you hint me now, wouldn't that ruin everything! ”
The TV screen went black, then turned bright white, struggling to type one character after another: "But...... I think you should need help? If you can't see it all along...... I think I should have hinted you instead. ”
At this moment, Tenna spoke in a polite tone, but you pouted, threw away the game controller, and started rolling on the floor throwing a tantrum: "I don't care, I don't care, I don't care, I don't like it anyway, it's all your fault! Why did you suddenly give me a hint? I never asked you for it!" ”
The TV was silent, only the hum of the cooling was heard. You wondered if you'd gone too far, and feeling guilty, you straightened up and was about to apologize, only to notice its antenna was bent. The screen was trying hard to type a line as fast as possible: "...... Sorry, next time I'll wait until you ask me." ”
You blinked, not expecting him to say that, and couldn't help but feel even more justified. You nodded as if it were only natural: "Yes, that's right! Don't give me a hint before I asked, or it makes me look silly......" You whispered, "Tenna might have heard that, or maybe she didn't. You're not sure."
This little episode passed quickly. You continued playing the game with great enthusiasm, eager to know how the game would end. But after smoothly clearing the room, you got stuck again. Holding the prop in your hand, you didn't know what to do for a moment. You clicked on each object carefully and tried to observe it, but still couldn't find the right direction. The game had no prompts, and the TV was quiet, just like an ordinary object.
You're a bit annoyed and can't help but start pointing and pointing again: "Tenna, why didn't you give me any hints? I just searched for ages and still couldn't find the answer......
The TV screen flashed for a moment, then slowly typed a line: "But...... You just told me I didn't need to remind you? ”
You cleared your throat twice, realizing you did say that earlier, and changing it now would seem a bit shameless—but you don't care! Anyway, this is your TV, so of course you need to know your preferences!
So you pursed your lips again: "I don't care, you can tell, right? I'm not in the mood to study this now, so you should give me a hint, right?" Just now...... Hmm, I was still interested in continuing to study that puzzle, so you shouldn't have given me a hint! ”
You spoke so confidently, but the TV probably didn't know how to respond. For a while, no new text appeared on the screen, almost making you anxious enough to go back up and film the TV again, until it slowly pieced together a yes.
So you nod in satisfaction, but still pat the TV with your hand: "Yeah, I knew it—you're my best friend!" Hmm...... Probably the only friend? ”
The TV's antenna stood upright again, slowly typing some characters on the screen, finally piecing together into one word: Forever?
And you definitely nodded: "Forever!" Hmm...... Speaking of which, "forever friends" is a bit strange, isn't it? I've never had friends...... But as long as we can always be together, that's enough, right? I roughly know—friends, family, lovers, all that...... As long as we can always be together, that's enough. "As you spoke, your eyes curved with a smile and you reached out both hands to give the TV a hug. You really don't know how to distinguish these words, nor how to properly express this kind of feeling.
But you know, at least you feel joy for it, and that's enough.
As for everything else—you don't care at all! No matter what your identity is, you'll always be together, right?
You shout that TV should be your bride because you hear other classmates say that if you get married, you'll be closer and spend your whole life together. You think you'll be together for life...... But you're curious—you really want to be closer, which is why you say that.
In short, you always like to act mischievous with Tenna, venting all the childish charm you've hidden from being mature onto him. You're happy, and Tenna seems happy too—well, you can't really tell the mood on TV, but every time you play around with him, you always lean over and kiss his screen.
Grandma occasionally kisses your cheek, so you copy the example and kiss Tenna too. But every time you kiss him and touch his screen, you'll find it gets even hotter.
Over time, Tenna became skilled at reading your expressions. He didn't even need you to say a word to know roughly what your next move would be, and skillfully displayed the prompts you needed on the screen.
Occasionally, when rushing homework and encountering problems you don't understand, you pester Tenna to show the solving process on the screen, assuming he can solve these childish problems.
…… Then, at that moment, a line of text will appear on his screen, blankly asking: "Why don't you solve it yourself?" ”
You confidently put your hands on your hips and said, "Because I don't know how!" ”
Ahem, although you say this is just child's play, it's precisely because you can't solve it that you ask Tenna!
The TV fell silent for a moment. You stared nervously at the screen, and then, Tenna, somehow managed to extract those symbols, actually displayed the problem-solving process on the screen. You scanned it and immediately understood, so you quickly wrote it down.
"I knew you could solve problems! Next time I come across a question I can't handle...... I'll come to ask you directly! "You said happily, writing down the answers to the last few fill-in-the-blank questions. Honestly, it's actually okay to take it over and ask your other classmates, but for you...... Building good relationships with others is really hard. You don't really want to talk to others, but just sitting here talking with Tenna is a very comfortable thing.
Sometimes you wonder if it's just your imagination, but when you look at the problems that can only be solved under Tenna's guidance, you firmly believe they are not hallucinations.
You originally thought that such a relaxed and joyful day, with a bit of monotony, would keep repeating.
Until that day.
Grandma...... Suddenly, that day you collapsed. When you cryed and rushed your grandmother to the hospital, you found she had already passed away. The hospital also sadly notified your family that your loved one had passed away.
You carried the small urn home, crying until you fainted. When you woke up again, a strange couple came to your door, saying they were your parents and wanted to take you back. It turned out your grandmother knew she didn't have much time left, so she went to the place where she found you, asked around for a long time, and finally found your biological parents. She handed you over to them.
You hold the TV, unwilling to leave alone with them, insisting on bringing it with you.
“…… A broken TV? What's the use of this thing? "Your mother raised her eyebrows high, looking surprised.
"This is my only family...... you sniffled and cried.
"Family?" "Is this the only thing?" Are you ......?" Your mother hesitated, your heart sinking. You thought, I really did think you were crazy.
Your father tried to smooth things over: "Forget it, if the child likes it, just take it home. It's just a TV after all. The child doesn't have many companions here, and after going back, he'll be fine for a while." ”
In the end, you still bring the TV back with you and solemnly put it in your room. You still chat with Tenna, but you have to be very careful when you do, after all...... You definitely don't want others in the family to find out.
But no matter how careful you are, you can't stop the child's curiosity. Parents usually go out to work, and you relax a bit while chatting with Tenna. After transferring to this school, you still don't have many friends, and even after entering high school, it's the same—you seem to be isolated without leaving a trace. Thin threads don't matter, as long as Tenna is with you.
You hugged your knees and sat on the floor, watching the door warily to make sure that little sister wasn't eavesdropping at the door before daring to talk to Tenna, quietly complaining about her recent life: "...... Honestly, the recent physics test is way too hard. I can't even answer the last two questions......
After a moment, the TV screen slowly typed a line: "So you admit it. Did you make yourself stupid before?" ”
“…… I didn't admit it! Besides, my liberal arts grades are always very good, so maybe I'm ...... Just not really suited for calculations or anything...... You blushed and denied it, then your voice grew quieter and quieter.
But suddenly, a voice came from the doorway, filled with surprise: "Wow, sister is actually talking to the TV!" ”
Your pupils contracted slightly. You instinctively stood up to stop her, but she had already run to the open-door door and threw herself into mother's arms: "Sister is talking to the TV she brought back!" ”
TBC.

title: Game Time 18 (end) (dntx you)
content:
In that instant, you felt as if all your blood was rushing and nothing but coldness remained, and your mind was completely blank. Instinctively, you stood up and blocked the TV behind you. Before you could say anything, your mother walked straight up and slapped you across the face, making your face twist and leaving you stunned.
She said with a tone of heartbreak, "How do I have a crazy daughter like you? If you want to go crazy, go ahead. Don't lead your sister astray, okay?" ”
You opened your mouth, not knowing what to say, just instinctively said, "I don't have ......."
Before he could finish, your father interrupted him. He frowned, "Enough, forget about whether you have it or not. Don't you know how to pretend better?" ”
Your face turned pale as you stared in disbelief at your father and mother, while they simply gathered around your sister and started caring for her, slamming the door shut with a heavy thrust. You slid slowly to the floor as if exhausted, kneeling on the ground, your knees aching, but you couldn't care about that—after all, the grievances and pain in your heart were far more painful than your physical pain.
You don't know why your parents do this, you don't understand, only the TV, still keeping a bit of warmth behind you, lets your cold body draw some strength from it.
Gradually, you shift into sitting on the ground with your hands hugging your knees, chatting idly with the TV: "I...... Are you really sick? ”
Tenna was very excited, typing several big words on the TV screen quickly: "No, you didn't!! ”
You softly hummed in response, even if you didn't need to look at the screen to know the answer. You just whispered, "...... You don't need to comfort me anymore. I know that to them, to this world, I am abnormal. ”
"......" You hear some crackling sounds. Maybe Tenna is piecing together characters again, but you don't care, nor do you know what he's actually written.
You just say to yourself, "...... If only I could live in another world." But that's only if—in such a world, how could there be another world? All the education you've received has taught you this.
You still didn't look at the answer on the TV screen, just sat there with your back to the screen, dazed. Your parents didn't call you out to eat, and you didn't pay much attention, just gradually drifted off to sleep.
When you woke up again, you were awakened by the heat, followed by thick black smoke that made you cough a few times, tears welling up in your eyes. The room was very hot; you could almost see waves of heat flowing, but there was no fire burning inside—it looked like it was burning outside. It looked like there was a raging fire outside the door, and you had no chance of escaping from this room. As the carbon dioxide increased, your vision darkened. You could only hold the still-cold Tenna to try to cool down, but amid the thick black smoke, you still lost consciousness.
…… When you wake up again, you are in the hospital. You don't recognize anyone, not even the person who claims to be your parents. The doctor said you fainted, and when you fell, there was blood congestion in your brain, which affected your memory.
Your parents moved you to another home, but you refused. For some reason, you insisted on staying in the old room, and you just felt...... What was truly important to you? In the end, they left you here to live alone. You always sat in the room, lost in thought. You did see characters on the TV, probably asking how you'd been lately, but you only treated those as hallucinations after a fire. After all, how could the TV be conscious? You always treated it as your own delusion and never paid attention to what was said on TV.
Gradually, the TV also quieted down, no longer making any noise.
In fact, you don't really understand why you live. You are just living, just learning, just moving forward. You don't understand the meaning of this until you get into university and on the day you receive your admission letter, curiously stepping into your bedroom, which is somehow filled with black smoke.
—Then, you came into this world, and from the moment you saw him, you fell irresistibly in love with Tenna. But you never had the courage to say this somewhat bittersweet feeling.
He always mocks you, and you always forgive him even though you cry, and then you repeat the same process over and over. Perhaps it's time to break this cycle.
After all, now that you've stepped out of the exit, you're standing again in your room, looking at that TV that was once abandoned, with its antenna wrapped in bandages after your careful repairs, and through the reflection on the screen, you see yourself.
Then you slightly bent down and hugged the TV.
“…… Tenna, long time no see." Your voice choked with emotion. You sniffled, wanting to cry, but mostly guilt. So you had ignored Tenna for so long, missed so many words from him in the past, but you felt his antenna gently touch you, then you lowered your hand and looked at his screen.
“…… Just a minute ago, we parted ways. Did your memory have trouble again? ”
You break into a smile through your tears, wipe your own tears, and even though he's become like this because of neglect in previous years—it's okay, Tenna is Tenna.
"I didn't, I just ...... Talking about myself at fifteen, and with you, long time no see. ”
After saying this, the TV screen went pitch black again, and then he slowly typed a few words.
“…… Long time no see. So, are you here to fulfill your promise back then? ”
You know what he's talking about—he's talking about the promise you made to always be together, the promise you made to make TV the bride.
And you nod vigorously, wiping away your tears: "Yes, I've come to fulfill my promise, I love you...... tenna。 As you spoke, your voice quieted and your face turned red, but you awkwardly lowered your head and scratched your own face.
You touch the outer shell of the Tenna, and it seems a bit hot too.
"Alright." This time, he quickly agreed to your request.
You rummage through your closets and find a poorly fitting black suit in the house. Put it on, then find a white tulle dress and veil, and cover Tenna with a wedding dress. This is a mismatched bride TV, a wedding that is also out of place. After all—this isn't a proper marriage, nor a serious audience, only you two take it seriously.
You cleared your throat and simply went ahead to deliver a piece of completely made-up wedding vows: "Whether in health or in sickness, whether in wealth or in poverty, whether in happiness or in sorrow, I will always be by Tenna's side. I vow to present all the beauty and joy to you and me. I vow to cherish this relationship, whether it be friendship, love, or family affection. I vow... to always be with Tenna, because this is a unique, special television on which I have invested infinite feelings. Because this will be my only friend, family, and lover."
After saying this, you hurriedly hung a relatively large, crude plain ring on Tenna's antenna. Forgive yourself—you had been searching for these items for a long time.
Then you kissed Tenna.
He seemed to be stunned for a moment, and then text quickly flashed across the screen in various combinations: "Whether in health or in sickness, whether in aging or in poverty, Anton Tenna will always be by Y/N's side. Anton Tenna is and will only be Y/N's family, friend, and lover."
You waited until the characters finished flashing, then put a ring on your own left ring finger as well. Then, feeling a bit embarrassed, you scratched your cheek and leaned in to kiss Tenna again. You could feel his screen and casing heating up, while you just smiled sincerely, removed the mismatched veil, and then put it on your own head.
After a while, you saw another line of text appear on the TV screen: "...I love you. I love you with all my heart."
And you just nodded, because you had known this truth for a long time, and you smiled as you said: "I love you too."
Then you touched the TV's antenna, finally reconciling all your inner knots, and walked briskly toward the entrance of the dark world. It was time to go back—it was time to see the true other side of your lover.
With this thought, you quickened your pace and ran through the gate of the dark world, then fell into an embrace.
You looked up to see it was Anton Tenna, still with a tense, expressionless face, and you noticed that his left ring finger was wearing that somewhat large ring. You thought these plain rings were probably bought by your fifteen-year-old self during a youthful crush—ah, indeed they were, because back then you were nervously planning how exactly you would marry the television.
You just smiled and tiptoed. Tenna still looked unhappy, but he obediently lowered his head. You put the veil on his head, looking a bit mismatched.
You just smiled, lifting your eyebrows: "Tenna... how about we have another wedding?" This time there would be an audience: all the employees of the TV world would be spectators at this wedding.
Tenna just silently nodded, staring down at you, then coughed twice. He lowered his head to bite your lips, lightly sucking twice before letting go, and hugged you tightly, as if you might run away in the blink of an eye.
You, on tiptoe, held the TV's head in both hands and kissed the screen, smiling: "Mm, I love you too."
END.

title: Game Time [Merge] (1)
content:
"Oh dear...... So boring...... You lie on the sofa complaining, swinging your legs casually, then bury your head in the sofa.
Of course—no one cares about you, or rather, the Dark People don't care about you. After all, you know what kind of person Anton Tenna is in this world. If she allowed you to stay here and cause trouble, that's more or less. Although you don't even know why he allowed you to stay here, it's probably because the Dark Folk are naturally caring for the Light Ones.
You didn't care about any of that—since no one answered you, you simply looked up, turned over, and sat back down on the sofa. Then you immediately saw Tenna sitting on the leather chair on the other side, the screen pitch black, as if she hadn't noticed what you were doing at all.
You couldn't help but feel speechless, walking over with your hands on your hips and looking down at him—well, that's not possible, since he's only about as tall as you when he's sitting down. In fact, you need to lift your head slightly to see him clearly.
You stand on tiptoe, a bit annoyed, trying to grab his antenna, but the next second his screen lights up, and the two antennas shake and slip away from your hand.
He looks at you expressionlessly: "What do you want to do?" ”
You saw his expression shrink slightly. Whether you said it or not, you were still a little afraid of him—after all, you knew he wasn't easy to talk to, but you still straightened your back and stared straight at his screen—after all, you couldn't see his eyes.
"Hmm, ahem, because it's too boring, I've decided to requisition your TV screen for gaming! After all, besides your TV, there's no other TV in your lounge that can be used." You put your hands on your hips and announced, even though you didn't know why, despite the room being meant for rest and entertainment, there was nothing else except the sofa—oh, and there's this one you instinctively found a bit annoying.
"What game?" His voice was cold and indifferent, and you couldn't help but take two steps back—after all, you started to regret coming to him directly. If you'd known, you should have looked for a TV somewhere else first. Anyway, there must be other TVs with big screens in this world, so why face such a ...... A guy you can't even quite put your finger on.
You pull out those few game CDs on you, hmm...... A fighting game, a two-player game, no need for this, you can't find anyone to play with you. A two-player survival game...... It's probably a drifting adventure on the sea, kind of like Life of Pi...... No, single-player is a bit too difficult, you can't play it. Two-player cooperative puzzle game...... Actually, you're quite tempted, but you sneak a glance at the guy in front of you and finally snort coldly in your heart, not asking if he wants to play games with you! He's really annoying; who knows what he'd say if we played together......
In the end, you chose a single-player adventure game—a simple Japanese RPG, a classic Dragon Quest story. After searching for a long time, you finally found a game disc you thought was quite interesting, then raised it high, your eyes sparkling: "This one!" "I want to play this!" Here, here you go. "You hand it to Tenna, looking at him expectantly.
Actually, Tenna had already noticed your sneaky glance earlier—he really wanted to say something more, but held back. After all, he knew that what he said was probably something you didn't want to hear, and for now, he didn't want you to leave here angry.
Tenna took the disc. I don't know exactly how he operated it, but he handed you a game console, then sat down opposite you on the sofa. He held the TV head and started projecting the game screen to you, while you happily sat cross-legged on the sofa and pressed buttons to start your adventure story.
Although there is a lot of textual storyline, this game still tests puzzle-solving thinking and skill, since it's somewhat of a 2D platforming puzzle-solving adventure game, and there are quite a few small monsters to clear along the way.
You seriously solve the puzzles along the way; those levels are a piece of cake for you—but in terms of combat controls, it's unclear whether your reflexes are slow or ...... The combat system in this game isn't very well designed. After all, you don't feel any impact at all, and the controls feel a bit sluggish. You even suspect it's a bit of a transmission issue, since pressing a button usually delays a little before the character actually acts.
Once again, the character dies. After the familiar GameOver CG, you purse your lips but don't lose heart. Instead, you regroup and decide to do it again. After so many times, you have to remember the boss's move moves and what you should do next.
But—while you were focused on attacking the boss, you heard Tenna's voice, casual and tinged with mockery: "...... Looks like you're bad at fighting games, no real skill. ”
He just watched you die several times, and even he knows how to get through it.
You choked for a moment, distracted by what he said, your hand instinctively trembled. The character who could have perfectly dodged the boss's finishing blow and landed the final blow shifted, landing in an inaccurate spot, and was killed by the boss's strafing fire. The gameover CG reappeared on the screen.
You angrily slammed the controller onto the sofa: "Yeah, I know I'm terrible. I've never been good at combat—but, but I was about to clear it just now, and it was you who suddenly said something that distracted me!" You started to blame him. After all, you were very self-aware, and you knew you were bad at playing. But as long as you enjoyed the game, that was enough. You didn't mind trying a few more times to clear it.
But you were originally quite interested, but after hearing that one sentence, your enthusiasm suddenly faded. Tenna just snorted coldly: "I've been watching all along, and your gaming skills really aren't great." ”
You glared at Tenna with red eyes—well, you don't even know if he actually saw it. You just raised your voice and said, "Bad at it, that's bad! If I try a few more times, I'll clear it. If you keep talking......"
After saying that, you still press the confirm button and decide to restart and challenge the boss again. But for some reason, after this restart, the screen actually starts to garbage, black-and-white noise appears on the TV screen, and even—intermittently and suddenly goes black. You try to control your character forward, triggering the boss again, but this time, because of the garbled screen and black screen, the character dies quickly.
Accompanied by the sound effect of death, Tenna's slightly mocking voice said, "I thought after so many times, you would remember it completely." ”
“…… The boss's jumping and moving positions are different! Even if I remember his attack order, I can't always guess where he moves! "You said angrily, feeling like your rage was almost full, but you still held back and started another round. This time, the screen was completely guttered. You didn't know if he was deliberately going against you. If he hadn't finished this boss and cleared the game, your intuition would have been that he wouldn't hand over the game disc so easily. You'd have already run the entire dark world looking for other TVs."
You puff out your cheeks, holding your breath as you control your character forward. Indeed, you've fought many times, so you have memorized the controls and map—you cleared that boss with a garbled screen and no visible scenario.
Tenna also raised her voice, speaking in a slightly surprised tone: "Oh? Isn't this something you can do?" ”
“…… Yeah, but if I hadn't died so many times before, how could I have done it! "You dropped the game console. Anyway, you've cleared this game, and you don't plan to play anymore. Besides, you just wanted to pass the time, but now you've been holding in all your anger, so you're completely fed up and not bored at all.
You feel like you're about to cry from anger—but in the end, you just step forward and pound the TV's head hard to vent your anger, your eyes red. You don't want to cry in front of him anymore, but you still have some shame: "Broken TV!! I'm not playing with you anymore, I'll go find another TV to use. I refuse to believe there are no other televisions in this TV world!" ”
You looked at the decorative screen in front of you, seemingly getting even more imposing, and you didn't care what else he would say—in short, it was probably something unpleasant. Anyway, you rushed out the door—yes, you pulled down the lounge door too, and you wanted Tenna to sit there and enjoy the cold wind!
But after running a short distance, you stop, panting, sniff twice, wipe the tears streaming down your eyes, and sob twice. You feel wronged, but you also know that if you really tell Tenna, at most he'll just apologize stiffly. But—but you don't want that. If things end up unpleasant, why not just do it well from the start? If you end up going our separate ways, then not meeting at first is probably the best choice—at least that's what you think.
You don't want a rigid apology, you don't expect that kind of apology—but if he comes after you to apologize, it's not that you can't forgive him for now.
You just ...... You just want to give him another chance. Even though you always tell yourself that this is the last time, there's nothing you can do—who told you not to really be ruthless with him? Who told you to ...... to like this guy? You don't even know why you like him; maybe this is just the origin of unpredictable love.
So your steps slowed down more and more, curling up in a corner and quietly crying. You felt a bit awkward, hoping Tenna would catch up and find you, but also wishing he never came back, so you could tell yourself that it really was time to give up.
Until you sneak around this corner, sneaking around and spotting a deep blue figure.
TBC.
You sniffled, feeling even more wronged, wanting to cry your heart out without caring why you were acting recklessly—fine, fine, you don't even know if crying would help, but your eyes rolled around, then you sobbed loudly, wiped the corners of your eyes, and sobbed loudly, choking and sobbing, crying until you could barely breathe. Just like every time before.
And just like every other time, the TV head turned around and walked toward you after hearing the sound. His screen was pitch black, and no one understood what he was really feeling about. And you didn't care, since he made you cry because of it, why care about all that?
Tenna squatted down in front of you, your face covered in tears and cheeks flushed from crying. His screen was still pitch black, but you knew very well that this was probably the biggest concession he could make right now. You sniffed, quieted down a bit, but still sobbing, then reached out and grabbed his antenna—avoiding the spot where the wound had been before, then shaking it wildly.
"I hate you...... I hate you the most, I hate you the most! Big villain! "You let out your emotions recklessly, uttering completely sarcastic remarks. Yes, you have tried to stop liking him...... But you can't do it. Maybe, in love, the first person to fall in love is always the one who gives in? You don't know.
Tenna just lowered the TV head a little, letting you hold the antenna and shake it. He felt his mind shaken, and as the antenna shook, the sea inside also wavered. He saw your sadness and your affection. He knows...... You love him.
So he wants to keep you, probably just because of a simple, simple wish. He doesn't know if he loves you; he just can't bear to give up, but he's unwilling to face these things—he's always been aware. He just feels he can't do that—he can't love you. After all, if you're just deceiving him, and leaving after everything is over, then what will Anton Tenna do?
So at this moment, he just lowered his head, letting you hold the antenna, casually, a bit coldly, and a bit stiffly saying, "Mm." ”
Then he tugged your hips and picked you up. You curled up in his arms, and he turned to walk back toward the lounge.
The pitch-black screen finally lit up again, but the corners of his mouth were still curved. He touched the tip of his nose, not knowing why.
You were stunned for two seconds, then naturally let go. Then you snapped back to reality, blushing, slapping Tenna's screen and shouting, "You...... What are you doing! Put me down!" You slapped your palm until it was red, but he showed no particular reaction. You spoke with a sobbing voice, while he kept his eyes straight ahead, speaking in a hoarse, somewhat cold tone: "Why should I listen to you?" ”
You're stuck. Indeed, he doesn't need to listen to you—after all, you have nothing to do with him. Still, your face flushed: "But...... But you can't do that! I don't like it this way! "Actually, you're feeling guilty. You don't even know if what you say will actually work—it hasn't been like this before. Most of the time, it's only after you faint from crying that he comes to find you. By the time you wake up, you'll already be lying in the lounge under a blanket. If you ask him, he'll say it was pippins who covered you up.
But he didn't answer you because he walked quickly. By now, he was back in the lounge, decisively sat down on the sofa, then sat across from you holding the TV's head. His screen went pitch black again, and then another scene flashed before appearing. It was a puzzle game you bought some time ago but never had time to play. You've always loved this series of puzzle games, and now that the sequel came out, you naturally bought it.
You glare at the unresponsive Tenna, suspecting he's doing it on purpose, but you still pick up the controller and start controlling the detective character on the screen—better not to go against the game.
Emotions come and go quickly. You quickly become fully immersed in the game. However, this sequel is actually a combination of open world exploration and puzzles. You're a directionally challenged person who searched for a long time in the game before finally finding your way. Anton Tenna kept watching your movements, and finally, unable to resist, the TV started playing again: "You don't look very smart, just spinning in place. Aren't you afraid of getting dizzy?" ”
“…… None of your business! How well I play the game has nothing to do with you. "You grumbled and took a detour for more than ten minutes before finally finding the right direction.
"It matters. I can't stand seeing such a dumb detective on my TV screen." He said. Alright, even though how you want to play the game has nothing to do with him, he's happy to watch you sit here a little longer—just a little longer, to focus intently on him. But since you've been lost all along, you open your phone to start looking up guides, figuring out the right route, while Tenna suddenly feels bored.
It took a lot of effort to calm down—or rather, you know that's just how he is. What just happened was a silent reconciliation between you two. But now you threw the controller aside, stood up angrily, and shouted, "You can't stand it! That other TV always works! I need to find a TV that won't disturb me while I'm gaming!" Saying that, you walked past him and tried to walk outside. Yes, I don't know why he threw you on the sofa opposite the lounge door, and you sat at the doorway. The next second, Tenna's big hand grabbed the back of your neck and easily lifted you up.
You frown, swinging your arms and legs back and forth, trying to shake yourself off, but Tenna's hand holds you firmly, and no matter what, you can't reach the ground.
"What do you want! I already said I hate you...... You want me to stay here—don't you feel bad yourself?" You felt like crying again, sniffled, but tried to stay calm as you spoke.
Tenna's screen went black again, he turned his head, and you felt he was watching you.
His voice was a bit stiff: "In the world of television, besides me, there's no other television." ”
Then he put you down.
You were incredulous, turned your head to look at him: "Why? Isn't this the TV world?" ”
"This is a dark world built from your home." His voice was flat, without any ups and downs. You paused, then thought about it and realized it was true—you had bought this somewhat damaged TV when collecting scrap before. Although you didn't watch much shows, you still had many game discs left unfinished. Later on, inexplicably, a dark world appeared.
"Oh...... Then I'll go back to the Light World to play games. At least you won't be able to talk." You muttered a few words, then prepared to find the exit from the Dark World. Honestly, playing games in the Light World is more fun. In the Dark World, you feel like you're just being the puncher every day.
Tenna didn't react, just moved a bit and blocked the lounge door: "You can't go back to the world of light." "If you return to the world of light—then what does he even think he is?" And he didn't want you to find out that he'd already had his staff lock the doors to the dark fountain and the main entrance. For now, you can't go back.
"You said if you won't let me go back, I can't leave...... Step aside!" As you spoke, you tried to pull Tenna's heavy mechanical body away, but unfortunately, you couldn't. You didn't even shake him in the slightest. You're so angry you want to kick him twice, but you're afraid you'll hurt your own foot.
His screen lit up. After a brief channel switch, the TV screen froze back on the game screen. This time, the game map opened without receiving your instructions and marked the correct destination markers. He had just checked the game channels that were still available. Fortunately, there were indeed some guides for this game, so he marked the guide as provided.
Your movements pause for a moment, then you look up hesitantly at the TV screen. To be honest, you don't understand why Tenna is doing this, but he just grabs the controller you just dropped and puts it back into your hand. Instinctively, you press the joystick as the detective character runs forward, gradually approaching the destination.
You pouted. If that's the case, then you could keep playing...... But you felt a bit awkward: "...... Fine, I want yogurt, but you're blocking the door, I can't get out." You started awkwardly changing the subject. Although you did pull the door away, Tenna was big enough to sit here and blocked the entrance, not letting you out.
Tenna didn't move, just pointed to the small door beside her: "There's a small door in the lounge. You can go get it yourself." ”
“…… Is it good? ”
"I don't know, I haven't tried it before."
"How long have you been sitting there?" You walked through that small door, and as soon as you opened it, you sneezed a few times. You never expected that the kitchen was covered in dust.
This question made Tenna hesitate for a moment: "...... About three or four years ago?" "Never replaced them...... Ah, a few years ago, they did replace a batch when he first arrived at this house. Back then, you would still excitedly hold the TV and say you liked it the most.
But later, you never said those things again.
You stuck out your tongue and closed the small door: "I don't want ...... It's been spoiled for ages, hasn't it? I want you to get me fresh yogurt! Preferably with a lower viscosity, I'm thirsty!" You started pointing around fiercely.
Then Tenna took out a cup of warm water and handed it to you: "Then you should drink more hot water." "After all, you feel thirsty.
You choked, then glared at him again: "No, I want yogurt, go get it!" "Actually, you just wanted to sneak out of the lounge while telling him to do something...... Somehow, ever since he took you back to the lounge, your sixth sense has been alerting you.
TBC.
You glared angrily at Tenna sitting there, then banged his TV screen twice.
“…… Let me out!" "You don't want to make any more excuses, so just be honest. Anyway, you're not in the mood to play games right now...... Even if he's already marked the path for you, you still don't want to keep playing.
Tenna really did turn back into a pitch-black screen. He stood up, looking down at you, and you instinctively took two steps back, thinking you really didn't need to be afraid—after all, control of this TV was still in your hands! So you pouted and looked at him with your head held high.

In the end, you chose to start gnawing on dried fruit.
And Tenna...... Actually, he was just throwing the merchandise from your room into the water. After all, isn't having him enough for you? He was even jealous of the merchandise made to look like him, so he threw it down the window. Of course, he called the former staff to take the items away; otherwise, it wouldn't be good to just throw them away.
Only when he tidied up your room and confirmed you could only see him did he nod in satisfaction and leave your bedroom again. Of course, he still looked at you and ordered, "Don't enter the room before going to sleep." ”
You tilt your head in confusion, not quite understanding what Tenna means...... Anyway, you nod and just sit obediently on the sofa. Tenna seems to really like you like this. He stares at you with a sharp glance, and once again you feel his burning gaze, so you can't help but look back. The moment you look, he just coughs and says, "I'm just thinking about what you'd like to eat for dinner." "It seems like a completely unrelated question, probably just changing the subject, but you still answer his question honestly.
"I want to eat grilled lamb chops, sprinkle a little fennel and cumin, that's enough." You definitely don't want to eat spicy food anymore.
Tenna nodded and sat down on the sofa too. He cautiously reached out his hand tentatively, finally holding yours tightly. You felt his hand still a bit stiff—maybe it was just your imagination...... But overall, his palm was a bit damp. You hesitated for a moment, then held his hand back, while Tenna let out a gentle sigh of relief, but...... You could feel that burning yet slightly damp gaze converging on you. Tenna was still staring at you with a hint of clarity, as if missing you at first glance would mean losing something.
You still can't help but turn your head to look at him, while Tenna just maintains that pose. His screen is off, and at this moment, you can't catch his expression. He just clears his throat twice and says, "I'm wondering, what kind of movie do you want to watch? Is it a suspense? An adventure genre? Or a horror movie?" ”
You were drawn in and indeed started thinking seriously about the question, then nodded: "Hmm...... Suspense and horror, right? I saw a synopsis of a movie yesterday, and I think it looks pretty good. ”
Tenna turned on the projector, and you enthusiastically started picking out movies, finally choosing a film called "Haunted House."
The movie begins. Tenna turns off the lights, and the room is filled only with the faint glow of the screen. You watch the movie with curiosity. It roughly tells the story of a team of archaeologists who accidentally discover a intact, undecayed house in an underground tomb. After discussion, they decide to send some researchers to investigate inside the mansion. The protagonist is a member of this research team. Because of her innate yin-yang eye, she discovers souls drifting inside the mansion and, as the team leader, redeploys their research plan. However, in the end, the researchers still die one by one inside the haunted house, because not only the ghosts inside the mansion but also countless mechanisms within the buildings, and even zombies hidden within the buildings. In the end, the female lead personally intervenes, interfering with the ghost's actions while dodging all traps and attacks, narrowly completing the scientific mission.
You watch the film with great interest. Honestly, the mysterious things inside don't really scare you...... But you can still feel Tenna's gaze, that slightly hot and moist gaze, and sense that he is frequently looking at you. You guess he probably wants you to be scared by the things in the film and hide in his arms, but unfortunately, none of these things scare you at all.
Tenna felt a bit unwilling. He was unwilling to just hold your hand. He wanted to get closer to you, even if it was just being held by you, it would be much better than now—he really couldn't accept it. And of course, he didn't really pay close attention to the movie. Most of the time, he was distracted and watching you. Of course, the scenes in the movie didn't scare him; he just thought you'd at least feel a bit flustered, or move closer to him—but you just stared at the screen with great interest.
He was unwilling to give up. He gripped your hand tightly, gritted his teeth, and simply shrank it down a bit—to about the size of a pet—then slowly moved closer to you: "Um...... Y/N, I'm a little scared." Even so, his voice was still dry and hard, not sounding particularly scared...... After all, you barely heard any pitch fluctuations.
But you couldn't ignore that burning gaze. In the end, you still picked him up, held him in your arms, and softly said, "Does this feel good?" ”
You only hear Tenna's small, somewhat faint voice: "Mm, this feels much better." And Tenna just naturally leans back like this, feeling perfectly justified, then nestles into your arms.
He really enjoys your embrace—warm and soft. And comfortable. Tenna certainly never cared about the plot on the projector, since no movie can compare to a TV show. He's just accompanying you, then enjoying your company. He craves your gaze, and now, he's content—because he can feel you looking at him again and again.
It wasn't until the movie ended, when you turned on the light, that Tenna reluctantly came out of your arms, regaining her size and expressionless appearance. In short, you suspected he wasn't truly afraid...... But it didn't matter, you were just...... Well, just treat some things as secret secrets you know.
After all, you also enjoy the feeling of being with him.
After watching the movie and having dinner, as usual, Tenna read you some books, applied medicine, gave her an antenna massage, and finally planned to go back to your room to sleep.
You quickly finished washing up, then followed by Tenna and walked into the bedroom together—after all, he wanted to sleep with you. You turned on the bedroom light and found it spotless and tidy, with only the music box you used to watch on the small commodity street that morning on the bedside.
You hesitantly looked at Tenna, but Tenna just turned her head. He crossed his arms tightly again and said coldly, "It's nothing. I just thought your room needed to be a bit cleaner, so I cleaned you up again." ”
You blinked at him, and he just lay down on the bed by himself, leaving you a spot. His voice was dry, and the screen closed: "Besides, I'm in your room. Don't you think that's enough?" "For some reason, you always feel that his words sound a bit sinister."
So you quickly nodded, "That's enough, of course it's enough." Then you lay down on the bed, nestled in his arms, curled up, and gently rubbed against him.
A night without dreams.
TBC.
You were woken up by being called out to her in a daze. It was Tenna's voice, still dry: "Alright, Y/N, you should get up and eat." But his voice carried a hint of anticipation, probably hoping you'd give him some feedback. You were a bit reluctant to get out of bed...... You even yawned, rubbed your sleepy eyes, and finally got dressed and got out of bed.
Breakfast during this period is usually the same: bread baked to your taste, jam prepared, plus freshly baked sausages, bacon, and soft-boiled eggs. You spread jam as usual and start tasting the bread, giving Tenna a thumbs up, and you see flowers bloom on his nose again. After breakfast, clear the plates, and Tenna brushes your hair. Today, he only tied your hair into a braid, letting it fall over your chest, looking gentle and gentle. You hadn't tried this hairstyle before and stared curiously in the mirror for a long time before putting it down.
Today's bet is up to you. After thinking for a while, you finally decide what the bet will be—well, let's play I WANNA in a match, whoever clears it first wins.
You really enjoy playing this game when you have free time. Although your skills aren't great, you've gotten used to it and become proficient, so it doesn't take long to complete it. Looking at Tenna, as a Dark Folk playing this game for the first time—or rather, a Dark Folk new to computer games—he was very reluctant, since he wasn't interested in computer games...... So in the end, he stumbled through this level, though it took him nearly three times as long as you did. So naturally, you won. You happily squinted your eyes. Aunt Zaang, Tenna didn't look very happy but didn't say much, just stiffly asked, "So, do you have any orders today?" ”
Tenna said, lifting her head as if looking at you, but all you could see was the pitch-black screen and feel his burning gaze. Ever since you woke up, that gaze had been fixed on you, with a damp, sticky feeling, as if she didn't want to leave you. You felt a bit helpless, but had no choice but to follow him.
"Mm...... Then say 'I love you' first and let me hear it. "You're a bit excited, you admit it, you do want to hear that—but to some extent, it's not wrong to reciprocate what happened yesterday."
"I...... I love you, I've always ...... I've loved you...... Tenna's voice was stammering and a bit hesitant, and by the end his voice grew quieter and quieter. Even though you heard him clearly, you still had the intention to tease him on purpose, just putting your hand to his ear and pretending not to hear clearly.
Then you pretended to be serious and said, "Hmm? What are you talking about? I can't hear clearly—" You dragged out your voice at the end, smiling at Tenna, waiting for his answer. To be honest...... You were really looking forward to him saying these things out loud.
Tenna took a deep breath and slightly raised her voice. He was no longer as flustered as before, but he was still reluctant to say such words, so he just whispered, "...... I love you." Although the volume was a bit higher than before, you still had to listen carefully to make it clear. So you pretended to be doing something, pretending to be looking at your phone messages, and after a moment, you looked up in surprise at Tenna, whose screen was dark and the antenna drooping.
"Hmm?" "What are you talking about? I still didn't catch ......" As you spoke, your voice carried a hint of apology. You looked at Tenna with a hint of apology, then you heard Tenna take a deep breath. Then he snatched the phone from your hand. His screen was still pitch black, as if flipping through something. He turned his phone screen toward you, pointed at someone in the contact list, and asked, "Who is this person?" ”
You glanced at it and waved your hand indifferently: "Ah, my brother who always asks me to help out. If it weren't for my parents' request, I wouldn't have added his contact info. It's kind of unlucky...... Delete it, delete it." "Then you tapped your phone screen twice and deleted that contact information."
Tenna was finally satisfied, though he was still scrolling through your phone. You didn't mind if he looked at your phone—after all, there was nothing shady inside.
Then he held up his phone in front of you, this time pointing to another contact number—after all, just like before, the name looked like a man's. He just asked, "What about this one? And who is this person?" ”
You sighed, deleted this person's contact information, and explained, "This is my college counselor...... We haven't been in touch for a long time; it's just that calling him during college sometimes makes it easier to solve problems. ”
Tenna happily puts the phone back. After all the hassle, you finally have no choice but to delete all your contacts directory, leaving only Tenna's contact info. You even open other social apps to show him so Tenna can be sure that his only contacts are left, or in other words—your whole world is just him.
"Satisfied now, right? You know perfectly well that those people are all people of light, and I can't possibly be able to contact their ......" You muttered to yourself, while Tenna's antenna stood up again. He still stared at the screen, just nodding. But in the end, he couldn't help but turn it on. This time, not only did flowers pop up from his nose, even the corners of his mouth couldn't help but lift, clearly showing he was extremely happy. You couldn't help but glance at him with disdain, but Tenna suddenly stepped forward and hugged you tightly. You could feel his TV head buried in the side of your neck.
And he just whispered softly in your ear, breathing warm breath: "I love you." Like this...... Did you hear me clearly? "His voice was low and hoarse. You felt your ears grow hot, and couldn't help but gently push him, murmuring, "I heard you clearly, I heard you clearly...... Don't get so close to me......"
You felt a bit embarrassed and gently shoved Tenna, who did let go of you with your strength. You cleared your throat twice: "Um, I'm going out alone, don't follow me." Saying that, you hurried out of the room. After running a few hundred meters, you patted your slightly flushed cheek, your eyes darting around. After a moment of wild thought, you still walked into a jewelry store. You happened to discover this when you and Tenna went out shopping for clothes before...... You thought you'd never set foot in a jewelry store in your lifetime, but today you still walked in.
Of course, not long after you left the house, you felt that burning gaze again. You sneaked a glance out of the corner of your eye, and sure enough, Tenna had followed, though his hiding skills weren't very good...... In any case, you just sighed silently in your heart and ignored him, just staring at the rings displayed on the counter and began to wonder what style you should choose.
Maybe because you had been inside the jewelry store for quite a while, and you chatted with the clerk a bit, you only felt that burning, sticky gaze growing even more damp, or rather, it seemed to carry a hint of darkness. You sighed helplessly, greeted the clerk, then crossed your arms and walked out of the store, speaking leisurely, "Alright, Tenna, come out. I know you're nearby." ”
But after you said this, there was no reaction from those around you; even that burning gaze vanished for a moment before returning to you.
You sighed softly in your heart, then deliberately raised your voice: "Oh no, it looks like my boyfriend got lost...... Where did he go? I can't go without my boyfriend. Maybe I should just find someone else, like the ...... in the store." As you spoke, you looked toward the jewelry store, about to walk inside, when you felt your arm being grabbed tightly—it was Tenna. Once again, he showed that gritted teeth expression. You instinctively shivered, for some reason feeling that his expression really carried a hint of horror and bloodiness.
“…… I'm your boyfriend. Who else do you want to find?" After saying this, he turned off the screen and turned his head away. He didn't look very happy, or rather, a bit embarrassed, but at least his voice was extremely rapid.
You blink at him, tilting your head slightly: "I'm not looking for anyone else, I'm just looking for you......" You want to add one more sentence, but Tenna suddenly steps forward and hugs you. You pause, only hearing his low, cold voice, sounding a bit listless: "Don't say things like that again next time." Also...... "Don't leave me alone and leave ......"
His voice grew quieter and softer, sounding stammering, and you could only helplessly hug him back, then cupped his head and gently kissed him on the screen.
"Alright, next time we go out, I'll call you to join me...... Actually, I just wanted to prepare a surprise for you. "You feel a bit helpless, but Tenna still holds you tightly and refuses to let go.
You have no choice but to soften your tone and lower your voice: "Do you want to see what surprise it is?" ”
Tenna didn't answer you; all you could see was him nod. You took a small box out of your pocket, opened it, and inside were two rings, each engraved with your name. The conversation you had just had with the jewelry store staff was about choosing a ring that fit Tenna's size.
"Ta-da...... Hmm, cough cough...... If you don't like it, I'll put it away...... Seeing Tenna showing no reaction, you rubbed the tip of your nose and felt a bit guilty, wondering if you were a bit too impatient...... You know that even though Tenna got the answer from you, he still wasn't very calm. Otherwise, why would he keep asking you to repeat that sentence?
Tenna was stunned for a moment, shook his head, and simply reached out his hand toward you. You took out a larger ring engraved with your name and slipped it onto his ring finger, and Tenna eagerly slipped the ring with his name onto your left ring finger.
You saw his screen light up again, and this time the antenna just drooped, gently shaking. You sighed, grabbed Tenna's hand, and softly said, "Alright, satisfied now, right? Let's go home." ”
Tenna just muttered, and once again, fresh flowers sprouted from his nose, some drifting and falling to the ground, while the corners of his lips couldn't help but curl up, revealing a smile that could be described as silly. He just whispered softly, as if his lips were off the mark: "Mm, Y/N, I love you." Then he returned and held your hand tightly. You were a bit troubled by his movement, but you still let him hold your hand, just responding casually.
"Yeah, I love you too...... Alright, alright, let's go home...... Actually, from the very beginning, the warmth on your face hasn't faded. If you didn't think love means you should give the other person something better, you wouldn't have done this. You don't know what love really looks like, you haven't experienced it, but maybe this sweet feeling now is love...... Maybe that's all there is to it.
You don't even know what love should do, it's just ...... Since Tenna wants you to be with him forever, then just stay with him forever; since Tenna wants you to love him, and you say you love him, then just say it out loud...... Maybe all these things are because you love him.
You don't know, you just know that at times like this, you yourself are happy...... That's all, because you also long for his company, for his love. Although perhaps neither of you truly knows what love should look like, just as it is now, it's good.
So you naturally reminded him, "Mm...... Then come with me to the shooting range this afternoon, and watch a movie with me tonight. What do you want to see?" You gave up on the order, but...... When you call out 'tenna' like this, you're still a bit unaccustomed. After all, you've used to calling him to keep you company with orders.
"Well, then...... Watch "Heartbeat." "Tenna said, you know, this is a famous romance film.
And you just smiled and nodded: "Alright, let's watch this tonight...... Oh, and um, you want to sleep with me." You said this, shyly pinching your fingers. Tenna just nodded gently, his dark screen turned on, and he smiled at you.
Tenna was sitting on the sofa at that moment, and you sat down and gently intertwined your fingers with Tenna. Tenna just casually said, "What else do you want to do?" ”
"I'm going to the bookstore! There was a book last time I had been eyeing for a long time, but it was on the shelf, and I couldn't reach it at all...... Tenna, go and help me get it. ”
"Alright."
You squinted and smiled, then moved a little closer, then leaned against Tenna's shoulder.
In this gamble, no one is a complete winner, nor is there a complete loser, after all...... This is just the story of two gamblers who bet on themselves and ultimately win against each other.
END.

title: Game Time [Merge]
content:
Maybe there's OOC, dntx you. By the way, I was really so angry I cried while writing......
——
"Oh dear...... So boring...... You lie on the sofa complaining, swinging your legs casually, then bury your head in the sofa.
Of course—no one cares about you, or rather, the Dark People don't care about you. After all, you know what kind of person Anton Tenna is in this world. If she allowed you to stay here and cause trouble, that's more or less. Although you don't even know why he allowed you to stay here, it's probably because the Dark Folk are naturally caring for the Light Ones.
You didn't care about any of that—since no one answered you, you simply looked up, turned over, and sat back down on the sofa. Then you immediately saw Tenna sitting on the leather chair on the other side, the screen pitch black, as if she hadn't noticed what you were doing at all.
You couldn't help but feel speechless, walking over with your hands on your hips and looking down at him—well, that's not possible, since he's only about as tall as you when he's sitting down. In fact, you need to lift your head slightly to see him clearly.
You stand on tiptoe, a bit annoyed, trying to grab his antenna, but the next second his screen lights up, and the two antennas shake and slip away from your hand.
He looks at you expressionlessly: "What do you want to do?" ”
You saw his expression shrink slightly. Whether you said it or not, you were still a little afraid of him—after all, you knew he wasn't easy to talk to, but you still straightened your back and stared straight at his screen—after all, you couldn't see his eyes.
"Hmm, ahem, because it's too boring, I've decided to requisition your TV screen for gaming! After all, besides your TV, there's no other TV in your lounge that can be used." You put your hands on your hips and announced, even though you didn't know why, despite the room being meant for rest and entertainment, there was nothing else except the sofa—oh, and there's this one you instinctively found a bit annoying.
"What game?" His voice was cold and indifferent, and you couldn't help but take two steps back—after all, you started to regret coming to him directly. If you'd known, you should have looked for a TV somewhere else first. Anyway, there must be other TVs with big screens in this world, so why face such a ...... A guy you can't even quite put your finger on.
You pull out those few game CDs on you, hmm...... A fighting game, a two-player game, no need for this, you can't find anyone to play with you. A two-player survival game...... It's probably a drifting adventure on the sea, kind of like Life of Pi...... No, single-player is a bit too difficult, you can't play it. Two-player cooperative puzzle game...... Actually, you're quite tempted, but you sneak a glance at the guy in front of you and finally snort coldly in your heart, not asking if he wants to play games with you! He's really annoying; who knows what he'd say if we played together......
In the end, you chose a single-player adventure game—a simple Japanese RPG, a classic Dragon Quest story. After searching for a long time, you finally found a game disc you thought was quite interesting, then raised it high, your eyes sparkling: "This one!" "I want to play this!" Here, here you go. "You hand it to Tenna, looking at him expectantly.
Actually, Tenna had already noticed your sneaky glance earlier—he really wanted to say something more, but held back. After all, he knew that what he said was probably something you didn't want to hear, and for now, he didn't want you to leave here angry.
Tenna took the disc. I don't know exactly how he operated it, but he handed you a game console, then sat down opposite you on the sofa. He held the TV head and started projecting the game screen to you, while you happily sat cross-legged on the sofa and pressed buttons to start your adventure story.
Although there is a lot of textual storyline, this game still tests puzzle-solving thinking and skill, since it's somewhat of a 2D platforming puzzle-solving adventure game, and there are quite a few small monsters to clear along the way.
You seriously solve the puzzles along the way; those levels are a piece of cake for you—but in terms of combat controls, it's unclear whether your reflexes are slow or ...... The combat system in this game isn't very well designed. After all, you don't feel any impact at all, and the controls feel a bit sluggish. You even suspect it's a bit of a transmission issue, since pressing a button usually delays a little before the character actually acts.
Once again, the character dies. After the familiar GameOver CG, you purse your lips but don't lose heart. Instead, you regroup and decide to do it again. After so many times, you have to remember the boss's move moves and what you should do next.
But—while you were focused on attacking the boss, you heard Tenna's voice, casual and tinged with mockery: "...... Looks like you're bad at fighting games, no real skill. ”
He just watched you die several times, and even he knows how to get through it.
You choked for a moment, distracted by what he said, your hand instinctively trembled. The character who could have perfectly dodged the boss's finishing blow and landed the final blow shifted, landing in an inaccurate spot, and was killed by the boss's strafing fire. The gameover CG reappeared on the screen.
You angrily slammed the controller onto the sofa: "Yeah, I know I'm terrible. I've never been good at combat—but, but I was about to clear it just now, and it was you who suddenly said something that distracted me!" You started to blame him. After all, you were very self-aware, and you knew you were bad at playing. But as long as you enjoyed the game, that was enough. You didn't mind trying a few more times to clear it.
But you were originally quite interested, but after hearing that one sentence, your enthusiasm suddenly faded. Tenna just snorted coldly: "I've been watching all along, and your gaming skills really aren't great." ”
You glared at Tenna with red eyes—well, you don't even know if he actually saw it. You just raised your voice and said, "Bad at it, that's bad! If I try a few more times, I'll clear it. If you keep talking......"
After saying that, you still press the confirm button and decide to restart and challenge the boss again. But for some reason, after this restart, the screen actually starts to garbage, black-and-white noise appears on the TV screen, and even—intermittently and suddenly goes black. You try to control your character forward, triggering the boss again, but this time, because of the garbled screen and black screen, the character dies quickly.
Accompanied by the sound effect of death, Tenna's slightly mocking voice said, "I thought after so many times, you would remember it completely." ”
“…… The boss's jumping and moving positions are different! Even if I remember his attack order, I can't always guess where he moves! "You said angrily, feeling like your rage was almost full, but you still held back and started another round. This time, the screen was completely guttered. You didn't know if he was deliberately going against you. If he hadn't finished this boss and cleared the game, your intuition would have been that he wouldn't hand over the game disc so easily. You'd have already run the entire dark world looking for other TVs."
You puff out your cheeks, holding your breath as you control your character forward. Indeed, you've fought many times, so you have memorized the controls and map—you cleared that boss with a garbled screen and no visible scenario.
Tenna also raised her voice, speaking in a slightly surprised tone: "Oh? Isn't this something you can do?" ”
“…… Yeah, but if I hadn't died so many times before, how could I have done it! "You dropped the game console. Anyway, you've cleared this game, and you don't plan to play anymore. Besides, you just wanted to pass the time, but now you've been holding in all your anger, so you're completely fed up and not bored at all.
You feel like you're about to cry from anger—but in the end, you just step forward and pound the TV's head hard to vent your anger, your eyes red. You don't want to cry in front of him anymore, but you still have some shame: "Broken TV!! I'm not playing with you anymore, I'll go find another TV to use. I refuse to believe there are no other televisions in this TV world!" ”
You looked at the decorative screen in front of you, seemingly getting even more imposing, and you didn't care what else he would say—in short, it was probably something unpleasant. Anyway, you rushed out the door—yes, you pulled down the lounge door too, and you wanted Tenna to sit there and enjoy the cold wind!
But after running a short distance, you stop, panting, sniff twice, wipe the tears streaming down your eyes, and sob twice. You feel wronged, but you also know that if you really tell Tenna, at most he'll just apologize stiffly. But—but you don't want that. If things end up unpleasant, why not just do it well from the start? If you end up going our separate ways, then not meeting at first is probably the best choice—at least that's what you think.
You don't want a rigid apology, you don't expect that kind of apology—but if he comes after you to apologize, it's not that you can't forgive him for now.
You just ...... You just want to give him another chance. Even though you always tell yourself that this is the last time, there's nothing you can do—who told you not to really be ruthless with him? Who told you to ...... to like this guy? You don't even know why you like him; maybe this is just the origin of unpredictable love.
So your steps slowed down more and more, curling up in a corner and quietly crying. You felt a bit awkward, hoping Tenna would catch up and find you, but also wishing he never came back, so you could tell yourself that it really was time to give up.
Until you sneak around this corner, sneaking around and spotting a deep blue figure.
TBC.
You sniffled, feeling even more wronged, wanting to cry your heart out without caring why you were acting recklessly—fine, fine, you don't even know if crying would help, but your eyes rolled around, then you sobbed loudly, wiped the corners of your eyes, and sobbed loudly, choking and sobbing, crying until you could barely breathe. Just like every time before.
And just like every other time, the TV head turned around and walked toward you after hearing the sound. His screen was pitch black, and no one understood what he was really feeling about. And you didn't care, since he made you cry because of it, why care about all that?
Tenna squatted down in front of you, your face covered in tears and cheeks flushed from crying. His screen was still pitch black, but you knew very well that this was probably the biggest concession he could make right now. You sniffed, quieted down a bit, but still sobbing, then reached out and grabbed his antenna—avoiding the spot where the wound had been before, then shaking it wildly.
"I hate you...... I hate you the most, I hate you the most! Big villain! "You let out your emotions recklessly, uttering completely sarcastic remarks. Yes, you have tried to stop liking him...... But you can't do it. Maybe, in love, the first person to fall in love is always the one who gives in? You don't know.
Tenna just lowered the TV head a little, letting you hold the antenna and shake it. He felt his mind shaken, and as the antenna shook, the sea inside also wavered. He saw your sadness and your affection. He knows...... You love him.
So he wants to keep you, probably just because of a simple, simple wish. He doesn't know if he loves you; he just can't bear to give up, but he's unwilling to face these things—he's always been aware. He just feels he can't do that—he can't love you. After all, if you're just deceiving him, and leaving after everything is over, then what will Anton Tenna do?
So at this moment, he just lowered his head, letting you hold the antenna, casually, a bit coldly, and a bit stiffly saying, "Mm." ”
Then he tugged your hips and picked you up. You curled up in his arms, and he turned to walk back toward the lounge.
The pitch-black screen finally lit up again, but the corners of his mouth were still curved. He touched the tip of his nose, not knowing why.
You were stunned for two seconds, then naturally let go. Then you snapped back to reality, blushing, slapping Tenna's screen and shouting, "You...... What are you doing! Put me down!" You slapped your palm until it was red, but he showed no particular reaction. You spoke with a sobbing voice, while he kept his eyes straight ahead, speaking in a hoarse, somewhat cold tone: "Why should I listen to you?" ”
You're stuck. Indeed, he doesn't need to listen to you—after all, you have nothing to do with him. Still, your face flushed: "But...... But you can't do that! I don't like it this way! "Actually, you're feeling guilty. You don't even know if what you say will actually work—it hasn't been like this before. Most of the time, it's only after you faint from crying that he comes to find you. By the time you wake up, you'll already be lying in the lounge under a blanket. If you ask him, he'll say it was pippins who covered you up.
But he didn't answer you because he walked quickly. By now, he was back in the lounge, decisively sat down on the sofa, then sat across from you holding the TV's head.
