Soon, you felt a cool liquid spray out. Looking down, you saw the white liquid splashing onto your hand, some landing on the sheets.
Yawn, you wipe your hands clean, turn off the lights, roll around with Spamton, and then solemnly announce, "Sleep!" ”
…… But the next day, you grit your teeth and find your nipples are swollen, rubbing constantly when putting on clothes, which makes you even more uncomfortable—a tiny, dense ache, and a slight pleasure transmitted to your brain through your nipple. In short, you've decided not to sleep with Spamton in your arms anymore. You absolutely have to lock him outside the bedroom to sleep! Otherwise, how can you sleep soundly and comfortably?

title: Hospice 1-Sptx you
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
...is sptneo and I think he seems to be out of options. This is probably really short (right?)
——
You pressed your slightly flattened stomach. Just moments ago, you were still sad about what to eat for lunch, and now you could hear the sound of your stomach rumbling.
…… Actually, if you want to eat something, it's not that you can't afford to buy delicacies, but you're not interested in those foods. Most people even feel nauseous after a few bites, and the effort they finally eat is simply to maintain their own physiological functions.
So, you decided to take a different path! You don't want to torture your body anymore, so start changing today! You decide to try different ingredients—maybe they'll make a difference......
Now, you decide to pick up a corpse and taste it first. After all, no one wants a corpse. If it's the kind with no relatives, that would be even better—the kind you like. And if the corpse were stewed, it would probably taste great. You guessed, but you guessed based on the aroma of cooked meat you normally smelled, since you couldn't eat it anyway. Anyway, just thinking about it now makes you crave it.
Wiping the drool from the corner of your mouth, you decide to wander around aimlessly; maybe you’ll stumble upon a corpse in some secluded corner. You’ve heard that the basement of the Queen’s mansion is a bit like a dungeon, secretive and mysterious, probably holding many corpses—though you don’t know why a normally tightly sealed basement is now so openly accessible. That doesn’t stop you from running wildly to the basement to look for new ingredients.
Unfortunately, you feel disappointed, because apart from the empty walls and the mysterious tracks, there's nothing else in the basement—oh, if the three people standing there and the guy lying on the ground count as anything too.
…… Wait, the one lying there? Could it be a corpse? Suddenly, you became interested, feeling a bit nervous and anticipating as you walked over, ignoring the sword raised behind you and the wary gaze. You just squatted down and looked around—hmm, it seemed dead...... It felt like your heart was beating no more. So you lifted the corpse up satisfied, humming a tune that was completely out of tune, and walked toward the basement door.
…… It's this corpse monster with gritted teeth. You have to think about whether these iron pieces are edible or if you have to peel them all off like skinning...... You were seriously pondering this question, completely unaware that your legs on your shoulders trembled slightly.
Until you hear a slightly electric cracking sound and a goosebump-inducing sound like iron scraping against each other: "How long will ...... [you] continue to [drag and pull]?" ”
You hesitate for two seconds. Your first reaction is shock and extreme disappointment: this corpse isn’t completely dead! Which means you can’t eat it directly! Your second reaction is to console yourself... even though it’s not fully dead, it seems close to dying; maybe one day later it’ll finally become a corpse, so using it as reserve food shouldn’t be too bad.
Later, you come to realize—oh, because this is a corpse, when being dragged, its head and half its body were dragging on the ground, occasionally bumping into stones along the way.
"Uh, I don't know, but anyway, Mr. Corpse, you probably can't walk on your own. Should I just throw this for you?" You said casually, but since the corpse is alive and can still talk, you do have a subtle conscience. So you turn around, first throw those two legs to the ground with a clang, then pick up his head and sit it on your shoulder. Finally, you nod in satisfaction. Hmm, that's good. Although now it's the lower body suffering, you can only add a light apology in your heart, without any regrets.
“…… First, I am not a corpse now. ”
As soon as he finished speaking, you quickly added, dragging him forward: "If you're not right now, you will be in the future." ”
…… He was choked by you, and after a while, things quieted between you and you. You didn't pay much attention. He didn't say no, so you planned to drag him back.
"...... in the future, it might not be a [corpse]!" His voice sounded somewhat annoyed.
And you just sighed with a hint of regret: "What? If it's not a corpse, then it turns into charcoal? That probably doesn't taste good...... But roasted wood should be edible too? Forget it, Mr. Corpse, you'd better not die yet—it's my reserve food. "You added another sentence at the end, not very serious."
“…… Stop calling me that, I have a [name]. ”
You scratched your head. To be honest, you didn't really care what Mr. Corpse's name was called. You didn't care much about the name of a corpse reserve food that was destined to die and probably turn into food. But you decided to brush it off and treat it as hospice care.
So you casually asked, "...... Alright, then what's your name? ”
“Spamton.G.Spamton,” you hear him say. Honestly, probably because his vocal cords are vibrating, you feel occasional tremors along your back—quite uncomfortable. You almost want to leave him here and pick him up once he’s completely dead... but what if someone else takes your reserve food? Thinking it over, you decide to grit your teeth and overcome the difficulty to bring him back.
"Oh, okay, Mr. Corpse, I understand." You nodded obediently, using your previous form of address. Actually, you hadn't even heard it earlier, and naturally didn't remember what his name was.
“…… I [seriously emphasize], I have [name].' "It sounded like his voice was tinged with fatigue.
Alright, you have to slightly regretfully give up this easy-to-remember and usable name and say, “Alright, Mr. Corpse... uh, spam...” Halfway through, you falter because you simply didn’t pay attention before and only now, after careful recall, do you get the answer.
“Spamton,” he sounds like he’s about ready to give up correcting you completely.
You awkwardly cough twice: “Oh, okay, Spamton. Now I’m notifying you—not asking—so I’m just telling you, you have no choice. I’m taking you back to my home, then once you die... um, to me, you’ll probably serve as reserve food. But don’t worry, I’ll make sure to provide proper end-of-life care!”
Saying this, you clench your fists and swing them a couple of times to psych yourself up, looking quite spirited.
Spamton held back, wanting to argue something more, but if he tried to argue further, he would probably just respond with a hum, then continue repeating these words carelessly.
In the end, he couldn't help but say again: "...... I don't need [hospice care]!! ”
You just spoke in a surprised tone: "Don't you need to?" I think you're almost a corpse. Honestly, I'm pretty sorry you haven't really turned into one...... Oh, if you don't need hospice care, I'll just leave you in the basement and wait to die. But the basement isn't that great—it's not very light-opaque, there's no breathable water, and no proper water supply...... If you're about to die, don't worry so much! To follow the strategy of not doing hospice care, I absolutely won't visit you, nor will I bring you anything. No, I guess the food reserves don't need anything else......
You probably haven’t spoken to a living person for a long time. You babble on since there’s no one to interrupt, unlike before when facing unresponsive things, and since Spamton shows no intent to interrupt, you naturally continue talking.
But he couldn't help but speak, and somehow you could hear a hint of humiliation in his words: "...... I [need][hospice care]. ”
You fell silent regretfully. You thought you could talk a bit more, maybe maybe sell the basement, but you couldn't help but add, "...... Wait, do you really need hospice care? I think the basement environment is pretty good. You're going to die anyway, so staying there isn't a bad idea. ”
"I really [need]. And my [life condition] [good and healthy]. ”
You expressed doubt: "Really?" I just saw you almost dead...... Forget it, since you're saying that, maybe you shouldn't live in the basement. Who knows when the basement will finally welcome a true owner who appreciates it......
Sighing, you finally return home, dragging him along. You open the door and lay Spamton’s head on the bed. With his legs still trailing on the floor, he ends up in an awkward posture.
You clear your throat twice, glance around the slightly messy room, seeing no other options, then place your hands on your hips and announce: “You can stay here! Well, I only have one bed, so you can only lie on this bed. But don’t worry, to prevent leaving your final words unheard in case you suddenly become a corpse, I’ll fully endure the possible stench of your corpse and lie next to you!” You declare solemnly.
“…I’m not going to become a [corpse],” Spamton repeats, sounding exhausted.
“Alright, whatever you say, I need to prepare something to eat first. For proper end-of-life care, I’ll prepare a portion for you too.” You shrug and head into the kitchen.
To be able to eat it yourself, although it's a bit of a pity there are no corpses, maybe changing the method would be okay......
You cut some carrots into a pot, sprinkle some orange peel strings picked out of boredom earlier as seasoning, pour in some rabbit blood stored in the fridge for a day or two, and finally hesitate before adding the whole pigeon you took out that morning—though skinned, probably still has the innards. Then, not really paying attention, you start adding sugar, shaking your hand accidentally, adding a lethal amount of sugar.
Anyway, the steaming hot pigeons with orange, shredded carrot, rabbit, and blood red soup stew are freshly made. When you take a bite, the sweetness mixes with the fishy and bitter flavors. Hmm, actually, the taste is pretty good for you.
Satisfied, you bring the soup out and take two bowls, placing one in front of Spamton.
What Spamton saw was a reddish-blooded soup mixed with an inexplicable mixture, stewing a pigeon.
He stays silent for a moment before asking uncertainly: “…Is this [food]?”
You serve yourself a bowl, happily sipping it, and nod encouragingly at him: “Yes, this is obviously food! Try it, I think it tastes pretty good, and I’m offering proper end-of-life care—you see, I even cooked specially for you…” You even pretend to wipe away fake tears.
In short, you won't hear his answer; you only see him silent for a moment before struggling to speak again: "I am currently [unable to move]." ”
You rub your chin and nod knowingly: "Oh, oh, you need me to finish pretending to feed you, huh...... You also said you wouldn't become a corpse and couldn't even move—this is basically dying. ”
Spamton shuts his mouth, feeling that answering would insult himself because no matter what he explains, you would have your own opinion anyway.
"In short...... This is the [current situation]. "He chose to ignore the issue and continue.
"Alright then, wait until I finish eating. I hope the soup won't get cold by then. I wonder how it will taste if it gets hot......" You muttered to yourself, finally speeding up your pace to finish the soup, ate some pigeon meat, and then refilled a bowl. You even brought over a new spoon, clearly planning to feed it properly.
Watching him drink it, you look at him expectantly: "How does it taste?" ”
Spamton was silent for a moment. He really didn't want to say that he had no sense of taste right now, so he couldn't taste anything. The taste of this soup was ...... At most, it only hurt a little.
But in the end, he gave a definite answer: "The taste is [acceptable]." ”
So you happily wave your fists and give him a thumbs-up, because he can't move right now. You even raise one of his hands and give a high-five.
"Wow, you really have taste! Is this soup really that good? I'll write it down and make it later...... As for the matter of sprinkling too much sugar all at once, just skip it selectively. Anyway, it's still quite tasty now.
“…… Maybe it's not a 'suitable' [recipe]. ”
You grabbed your notebook and happily started writing, and when you heard this, you started muttering, "So what? Anyway, normal methods don't suit me, I just can't eat it...... Oh right, I almost forgot about you. ”
You remember halfway through writing, so you put on disposable gloves, tear off the pigeon meat, and start feeding the corpse of this possibility.
After a while, the soup in the pot did get cold, but the pigeon meat was finished, so you happily went to wash the pots and bowls.
End.

title: Hospice Care 2-Sptx You
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
Sorry, I don't know if that's possible. I just, well, immersed myself in my own art......
——
After quickly cleaning up all the pots and pans, you came back to look at Spamton, and even crouched down, rubbing your chin as you looked at him. Maybe he'd been stared at for too long, and couldn't help but ask, "Why do you keep focusing on [Gazing]?" ”
You rubbed your chin, opened your mouth, and then, for once, fell silent. In the end, you just shook your head: "I don't know, so don't worry about it. Just think of it as me wondering what hospice care should do, right?" "You look dull and don't taste good at all. Maybe you should clean it up first......"
You muttered.
Spamton had a bad feeling and couldn't help but ask, "...... [wash]? [Bathing work]? How do you [carry it out]?" "Honestly, he's really afraid you'll suddenly throw him into a pool and forget to pull him out and leave him at the bottom."
"Uh, pour a bucket of water and then scrub it with a brush. What else are you counting on?" You shrugged.
Strangely, he actually felt a relaxed feeling he could still accept. It seemed that once he crossed the line, he could endure all this well...... To be honest, it wasn't good at all, but at least he didn't actually throw it into the pool for him to climb up.
So Spamton stopped talking and instead stared at you with that strange look. Even through a pair of glasses, you could see his expression. You couldn't help but shrug, shiver, and hug your own shoulder: "What are you looking at me for? Cleaning is considered kindness, but does hospice include washing you up or something...... Uh, that sounds so scary." You muttered, got up, went to the next room to fetch a bucket of water, and then dragged Spamton toward the bathroom.
"Hmm, to prevent water from being everywhere and hard to clean up, let's get it in the bathroom first." You muttered to yourself, then threw the Spamton onto the bathroom floor, poured the bucket of water over his head, and in a rather humane manner, poured water from top to bottom.
…… He was about to shiver from the cold water, but right now he couldn't move at all! Spamton instinctively became agitated. He wanted to do something, but nothing worked—he simply didn't have the strength.
So he could only try to glare at you with a fierce look. Of course, that look shouldn't kill anyone, and you pretended not to see his gaze. Maybe you still had some conscience, picked up a clean brush, gestured a few times, and finally decided to wash the part of your body that looked like some kind of steel mech.
To be honest, you don't even know what this part is. Probably, or maybe it's not that important, and it doesn't look very appetizing. The main issue is the strange color...... You grumble to yourself and accidentally pull off the high heels Spamton was somehow wearing. You don't want to scrub your shoes, and cooking them doesn't taste good.
Spamton didn't feel much extra when wiping the lower part of his body, but the thought that the brush would soon land on his face made him feel a chilling fear.
Well, at least for a while, it won't be like this, because you flipped Spamton over and started farming the back.
…… He didn't want to recall what happened afterwards; in short, it was definitely not a good thing! Spamton thought somewhat irritably.
Now he's lying weakly on your bed, his steel armor gleaming to a shine. You're very satisfied, so after drying him dry, drag him back and throw him onto the bed.
To be honest, when you picked it up, it was almost dinner time. Now that you look at it, after all the fuss you've been around and it's almost time to sleep, you're tired too. So you happily lie down on the bed, turn off the light, wrap yourself in the blanket, close your eyes, and get ready to sleep.
Spamton could hear rustling sounds nearby. He stared at the ceiling in the darkness for a while, then finally couldn't help but speak: "...... Don't I [own][quilt: ownership]?" ”
You were already sleepy and about to fall asleep, but hearing this sentence barely revived you. After struggling for a while, you didn't want to part with the blanket that wrapped you up like a zongzi and gave you a sense of security. In the end, you painfully let it go. If you could see clearly, you'd see your face full of reluctance.
"Alright, Mr. Corpse, good night. Getting you some rest is probably part of hospice care as well." You said casually, pulling back the blanket and thoughtfully covering Spamton with half of it.
He couldn't be bothered to correct your form of address. After you said it, you'd still do as you pleased, and Spamton pretended not to hear.
Honestly, how did things get to this point?! Spamton had no idea at all.
He widened his eyes and kept staring at the ceiling, hearing your shallow breathing beside him. "Good, you're asleep now, no one can control him." That doesn't mean he can do anything now, because the next second, he sees you rolling around in bed and rolling beside him.
He saw your eyebrows furrow instinctively, probably because you were too cold. Spamton thought somewhat indifferently, since your body was like this now, and there was no way to warm it up...... Before he could finish his wild thoughts, he felt your hand move, because he could feel his head and body being pushed against him. Although the feeling was not obvious because the threads were cut, a dull and wooden sensation, he could still feel your movements, and probably quite a bit of force.
…… Because he realizes his body is moving toward the edge of the bed, and your body keeps arching toward you.
…… Good, he finally managed to get pushed off the bed by you. In fact, this actually made things easier—at least he wouldn't have to feel the constant force of the pushing, Spamton thought expressionlessly.
And Spamton could hear that when he fell off the bed, there was probably a loud bang—at least the clatter of something hitting him—but he just heard you rolling around on the bed again, muttering 'Why are you so noisy?' and kept sleeping.
Very good, and your sleep quality is also very good. Now he will probably be lying on the floor all night. Although he was used to this kind of life, this was the first time he had experienced lying in bed while being squeezed onto the floor to sleep. Spamton thought expressionlessly.
In any case, in the end, he didn't know how he actually fell asleep. Maybe he had been staring at the ceiling all night and then briefly lost consciousness. After all, when he came to his senses, he found his eyes were still open.
…… And I can even hear your snoring.
Good, but now he doesn't know how much longer he'll have to lie on the floor. This time, Spamton felt his gaze on the ceiling carry resentment.
He didn't know how much time passed before he finally heard your groggy voice, and then he could see you probably sitting up from the bed.
You sat for a few minutes before slowly turning on the camera, remembering what exactly you had done yesterday, oh...... You picked up a corpse and brought it home. You were fully awake. You remembered he had slept in your bed last night, so you instinctively looked around but didn't see him. You also noticed you were right in the center of the bed, and the blanket had somehow wrapped around you again, like wrapping a zongzi.
Scratching your head, just as you were about to wonder where he could go, you heard a voice from under the bed: "...... I'm [above] the floor." ”
For some reason, you could hear a hint of grievance in his tone, so you cleared your throat twice, a bit embarrassed: "Ah, sorry to have you sleep on the floor, Mr. Corpse. But that place should have been your place to return anyway...... Ahem, I'm a territorial person, so I probably accidentally pushed you off to sleep on the floor, hahaha. ”
Even so, in the end you feel justified again, showing no sign of embarrassment.
Spamton fell silent. He felt so angry that he didn't need to eat at all today. But you were excited, changed clothes, jumped up, and dragged Spamton outside: "Come on, come on, I feel like I'm about to be slumped out." Let's go find something to eat! ”
What else can he say? He can't resist now, so he'll just be dragged away by you.
…… It wasn't until you threw him to the ground and you were still excitedly smearing honey on him, Spamton finally couldn't help but speak: "[Question: Purpose]." ”
You casually replied, "Ah, I applied honey. To attract ants, I don't have anything else but you, so I'm just asking you for a moment!" "While your hands kept moving, soon you poured all the jar of honey onto Spamton."
"...... [you] can consider [purely] lying on the ground." He said, his voice weak and weak.
"I know, but that makes it hard to collect, so I'll just leave it at that!" "Besides, you don't have to do anything. I'll provide you with food, clothing, and shelter, and you can rescue and do some chores. It's not really anything." "You shouted, squatting not far away and watching, soon ants crawled over following the sweet scent of honey, and of course, all kinds of flying little bugs—you chased them all away. After all, you only needed ants.
And there was another advantage: after all, Spamton was wearing steel, so the ants couldn't bite them and could only lick the leftover honey on the cold metal sheet. Soon, more and more ants gathered, gathering around Spamton, forming a dense crowd. If anyone with trypophobia passed by, they would definitely be scared to death by this scene.
And you happily dragged Spamton's head and brought him home. Today's ingredients are well stocked; having collected so many ants, it should be quite good.
Spamton chose to close his eyes and ignore the ants crawling on his face. He could only endure and could do nothing more, so he had no choice but to endure.
You dragged him home, collected all the ants, threw him on the floor again, and then happily led the ants to the kitchen.
First, take out the dried tangerine peel, then cook the ants. Anyway, seeing them floating on the water, they should be cooked. Then put the dried tangerine peel back in and pour in some salt...... The taste should be pretty good!
After cooking for a while, you finally took out the ants along with the dried tangerine peel. The ants usually rest on the peel. After thinking for a moment, you added some cabbage to the plate, then lifted it and put it in the steamer to steam for a while before taking it out. Mm, you nodded in satisfaction. No wonder you had already made a dish called 'Ants Climbing the Tree' so quickly.
So you walked out carrying the plate, placed it in front of Spamton again, and happily clapped your hands: "I'll feed you this. It's my first time making this dish, so I don't know how it tastes......" Before you could finish, Spamton glanced at the plate on the floor. Strange dried tangerine peel and ants lay on the inexplicably green broth, the strange mix of green and black mixed together, making him think it would be better if he fainted at this moment.
"[Question]? Is this food?" But perhaps because the mental stage was firm, he didn't faint immediately; instead, he calmly asked questions.
You nodded matter-of-factly: "Yeah, that's today's meal. Hurry up and eat, I think it's pretty tasty!" Oh wait, you can't move yet, so I have to feed you......" As you spoke, you started waving your hands and feet, then ran into the kitchen, ready to come out with a spoon.
Spamton fell silent. To be honest, he didn't even know where his strength came from, and even he felt horrified—he should have been powerless and at his mercy. But now he felt he had some strength again, or maybe, uh, he was so angry he could stand again. In any case, he didn't know how long this state would last, but he did feel Neo seemed to be working again.
…… So he stood up and headed toward the kitchen. Just as you were about to take the spoon and walk out, you saw Spamton heading over, and you couldn't help but open your mouth wide: "...... Wow, a medical miracle? "You exclaim with admiration.
You saw him walking over without saying a word. For some reason, you felt a bit scared, but instinctively, you stepped aside and watched him walk into the kitchen.
You prop your head up, watching Spamton open your fridge, then take out pigeons, eggplants, potatoes, and all sorts of other ingredients. Then comes the sounds of chopping, stir-frying, and the smell of cooking smoke.
You scratched your head. Although you didn't know how this medical miracle was made or why he came to cook, you still sat down at the dining table, ready to wait for him to bring the food up.
Then you see Spamton serve four dishes and one soup placed in front of you, and then collapse into a chair, seemingly just a last burst of life.
End.

title: Hospice Care 3 (end) - Sptx you
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
It ended quickly (. ) But this YN feels like she's taking care of her paralyzed husband (hopeful).
——
You glanced at Spamton, then at the dishes on the table, hesitated for a moment, and said, "Uh, can you eat by yourself now? Do you still need me to feed you?" You thought you were being considerate of asking this question, and then you saw Spamton seem to roll his eyes. In short, he was looking at you with a bad attitude.
You forced a couple of laughs: "Alright, can you eat it yourself? Just say it." ”
"...... [No]." His voice carried a hint of frustration.
In fact, Spamton was pleasantly surprised just now. After all, NEO had started working again, regaining bodily autonomy and freed himself from those foolish threads. It was the best situation, and he even felt excited and delighted by it.
But harsh reality told him that it was only a brief matter. Unable to suppress his impulse, he went to the stove and made four dishes and one soup to serve on his table. Then, as if his fuel had run out, he sprawled back in his chair, unable to move again.
You nodded knowingly and thoughtfully added, "Yes, I knew it. It seems that moment just now was just a last flash of hope. Don't worry, I'll provide end-of-life care and definitely won't let you die for no reason!" ”
Of course, it might just be your own thoughtfulness.
Because you notice Spamton's voice choking up again, then grit your teeth and add, "...... It's not [Last Burst]. ”
You nodded obediently: "Mm-hmm, no, then tell me, what exactly happened just now?" ”
He got stuck, and didn't know how to answer you. If it wasn't a last burst of life, he wouldn't be able to use another word to explain it, but if he wanted to explain the operating mechanism of Neo in detail, you'd definitely be sure of your 'who knows what kind of last burst of last hope' you are!
To avoid trouble, and probably feeling he couldn't change his mindset for the time being, he could only say with a hint of despair and helplessness, "It really is [Last Ray]. ”
You nodded in satisfaction: "Yeah, I knew it was true...... Alright, let's eat first. Since you can't move, I'll feed you later. Look how thoughtful I am, come and praise me." Saying that, you even proudly lifted your head.
His voice was still desperate and helpless: "...... [praise] you." ”
"Wow, that's not sincere enough. You should think about how you should say it, or else ...... Uh, I won't feed you lunch anymore!" "You thought for a moment and came up with a punishment that probably wasn't really a punishment."
In fact, Spamton thought he might be much better off if you didn't feed him, since he hated the current situation where his actions were at his mercy, but...... You looked enthusiastic, and he really was very "hungry."
…… He didn't want to endure hunger anymore. Of course, this had nothing to do with him deciding to please you or anything like that.
"[Praise] you, because you're [skillful], [clever], [friendly and considerate], [helpful]." He was expressionless, not even knowing what he was saying. Well, anyway, these were insincere words, not what he truly meant.
But you happily applaud, cheerful and your eyebrows raise: "Oh my. How could I feel embarrassed to praise me like that? Now this skillful, clever, friendly, and helpful person sits right across from you. I'm a great philanthropist! Thinking about it this way, you really got a good deal! ”
Spamton closed his eyes, so he wouldn't have to see your reaction when he said something insincere.
"That's the truth, you're kind-hearted." He closed his eyes, abandoning all other feelings and thoughts, and said this dryly, though he instinctively used a bit of technique...... Hmm, the tone he used instinctively when he was a salesperson.
At this moment, he even felt a bit hated for himself; he simply didn't want to say such things!
"Yes, yes, I'm kind-hearted. Otherwise, why would I help you with end-of-life care? Looking at it this way, I'm just too kind." You said casually, picked up a bite of the braised fish that looked delicious, and decided to give it a try.
You know that eating normally might make it hard to eat or even vomit...... But you decide to try again—what if this time you can change? Even if you don't have high expectations.
You chewed, picked up the piece of fish, and tasted it carefully. The braised fish didn't have the usual fresh, salty, and spicy flavor; instead, it was filled with a sour and astringent taste, even a hint of sour and bitter. In fact, this actually made it easier for you to eat.
After you ate the piece of fish, you fell silent, resting your chin on your hand and gazing deeply at Spamton. After thinking for a moment, you suddenly spoke: "I feel like I'm starting to like you a little." ”
After a pause, you pick up the next line: "So when will you die?" ”
Spamton was almost out of breath by your words. He opened his eyes and looked at you weakly: "...... [why]?" ”
You poked the fish and casually said, "Because I found the food tasted exactly to my taste...... I knew you had taste! And you could appreciate the dishes I made yesterday! But since you're going to die anyway, I've decided to be merciful and not eat your body. I'll just keep it safe, so I can take it out one day to mourn...... you mutter.
“…… Then why did I hope for my death? ”
This time, you thought for a moment before hesitatingly saying, "Because if you die, love will never decay or decay. Only then will love be eternal." No, if you die, who will cook for me...... You were silent for a moment.
Then you lift your head and say firmly and resolutely, "Then you shouldn't die. Try your best to live." ”
“…… I won't [die]! "Another angry and humiliated voice, but you just nodded perfunctorily.
"Mm-hmm, so you'd better not die yet." You just said casually, picking up a piece of vegetables to eat.
"At least now, I won't [die]." He decided to struggle a bit longer.
"Oh, so you'll die in the future too...... Forget it, let's not talk about that. By the way, is there any secret technique that can grant immortality or one-click resurrection? I want to use it for you...... You kept muttering.
"I [believe] that the so-called [secret technique] has no [possibility]." He said, his tone tinged with a hint of world-weariness.
You don't really care: "If there isn't any, then so be it. I still do hospice care as usual. Oh, it probably can't be called hospice care anymore. What should I call it now...... Forget it, whatever!" You pondered the question a bit confused, then skipped the topic, simply finished your meal, and then took out a new bowl.
"Alright, now I'm going to serve you a meal." You said seriously.
"Live well! You can't die or leave. You can only be my cook!" You started rambling nonsense, rummaging through vegetables and placing them underneath. Then you looked at the remaining fish and started worrying. Because you were afraid of trouble, you finished the belly. Now, all that was left was the fish's back with more bones.
Spamton didn't have the strength to reply to your question; he just stared blankly at the ceiling in the direction he was heading.
"Uh, can you trim the fish bones now?" You decided to ask cautiously.
"[No]." He answered the question straightforwardly. In fact, Spamton didn't know if he could actually do it now, but ...... He felt that even if he could, he wouldn't be able to deal with the remaining fish bones—in fact, he couldn't.
And he's also a bit curious about what you're going to do right now. Actually, he had just heard what you said, but he didn't want to respond to your words, and he didn't think it was necessary.
Even if he sadly realized that he probably really couldn't live without him, and he couldn't die now, and even if he did, the best outcome might be that he was eaten by you as food...... In any case, Spamton composed himself and decided to painfully accept the current situation.
You hesitated for a moment, mainly because you really couldn't be bothered to shave the bones. But then you thought about it, since the fish back part you were feeding Spamton was also bad, you accepted it with a clear conscience and happily started the bone-cleaning job.
As for how exactly it was made...... You just picked off that piece of fish meat, chewed it yourself for a while, spat out all the bones, then spat out the meat and put it in a bowl, so the fish meat was covered with shiny saliva.
After spending some time cleaning up the fish, you start to feel proud and proud. So you put your hands on your hips, hold your bowl and drag a stool, and sit next to Spamton, saying proudly, "See, I'm thinking of you, afraid you'll get stuck in the bone, so I even shaved off the bones for you. Praise me!" ”
Spamton naturally saw your movements. He also knew how these fish with suspicious liquids came to be, so he could only close his eyes in despair: "[Praise] you." ”
You don't care that this time he only has this one short sentence. After all, he's used a long string of adjectives before, so what's the big deal about that?
You just happily pick up the bowl and start feeding Spamton: "That's good, so don't waste my efforts. Eat quickly, eat quickly." You said happily.
He could hardly imagine how he managed to eat it. Fortunately, he didn't have a ...... of taste. No, strangely, he actually thought this kind of thing was acceptable, and there was nothing wrong with it.
At this point, Spamton felt a bit horrified, and couldn't help but wonder: could he have developed some strange feelings for you? Thinking about it, this kind of thing actually seems pretty scary.
After lunch, in the afternoon, you chatted with him again, but you didn't seem to be very good at chatting either. Instead, you enthusiastically shared what you had talked about with the tables and chairs in the room—whether it was complaints about not being able to eat or stories from times when you went out to play. Then you shared it with those things that can't speak, and now with spamton. Even though he wasn't very keen, he was forced to remember a few lines because you kept nagging.
But you probably look very happy, probably not like you'd leave his body out in the wild...... Why is he still affected by you? He's not a corpse, and Spamton is starting to spit on himself.
At dinnertime, you still want to use leftover ants from lunch to stir-fry dishes, and you're convinced the ants must be delicious. Only then does Spamton feel like he's regaining his strength. For some reason, Neo started up again—maybe Neo can't stand the strange, smoky green dishes you brought out. After making four dishes and a soup on the stove, he lay back down with no energy left.
You happily ate and thoughtfully feed him thoughtfully, and the dinner ended in this mess. Spamton breathed a sigh of relief, thinking the day was over, until you dragged him into the bathroom again.
His smile stiffened again: "...... [Morning], I think the [Bath Process] is already over?" ”
You nodded matter-of-factly: "Yeah, but this morning you only cleaned the outside and didn't clean the inside. You can't be dirty all the time, right? I'll pull off your coat and help you clean your body." "By the way, how exactly are you supposed to take off this mech......"
You muttered to yourself twice, not sure how you opened the steel mech outside. Spamton felt a bit desperate. To be honest, he hadn't expected you to do this on a whim, and he didn't even want to be exposed in this situation.
But no matter how unwilling, Neo couldn't move now, and with the mech removed, he couldn't move at all. So he had to close his eyes and pretend nothing happened. Suddenly, he felt you switch to a gentler thing like a bath sponge and start rubbing him around. At the same time, for some reason, the showerhead was turned into scalding water, and you still hadn't noticed.
He held back again and again, but finally couldn't help but speak: "The water is 'scalding hot!! 】”
You pause for two seconds, then say 'oh' and turn on the tap. Now it's cold water. Spamton couldn't be bothered to say anything more. Cold water is cold water.
After the shower. You dragged him back to bed, and he didn't even change into his previous clothes. You said you went to rinse that set, but now there's nothing suitable for Spamton here. Anyway, he's almost a corpse, so just endure it. So now he lies on the bed, staring wide-eyed at the ceiling.
Fortunately, you even brought him a new quilt to prevent him from kicking off again just because of a blanket. But in the middle of the night, when you were still sleeping awake, you still crawled over to Spamton's side, and then, probably because you were pressed against the blanket, your furrowed brows relaxed again.
…… Could it be that everything will be like this from now on? He felt a mix of despair and helplessness, but also a strange, inexplicable sense of security.
End.

title: Combined Edition of Hospice Care
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
...is sptneo and I think he seems to be out of options. This is probably really short (right?)
I found the persecution quite fun.
——
You pressed your slightly flattened stomach. Just moments ago, you were still sad about what to eat for lunch, and now you could hear the sound of your stomach rumbling.
…… Actually, if you want to eat something, it's not that you can't afford to buy delicacies, but you're not interested in those foods. Most people even feel nauseous after a few bites, and the effort they finally eat is simply to maintain their own physiological functions.
So, you decided to take a different path! You don't want to torture your body anymore, so start changing today! You decide to try different ingredients—maybe they'll make a difference......
Now, you decide to pick up a corpse and taste it first. After all, no one wants a corpse. If it's the kind with no relatives, that would be even better—the kind you like. And if the corpse were stewed, it would probably taste great. You guessed, but you guessed based on the aroma of cooked meat you normally smelled, since you couldn't eat it anyway. Anyway, just thinking about it now makes you crave it.
Wiping the drool from the corner of your mouth, you decide to wander around aimlessly; maybe you’ll stumble upon a corpse in some secluded corner. You’ve heard that the basement of the Queen’s mansion is a bit like a dungeon, secretive and mysterious, probably holding many corpses—though you don’t know why a normally tightly sealed basement is now so openly accessible. That doesn’t stop you from running wildly to the basement to look for new ingredients.
Unfortunately, you feel disappointed, because apart from the empty walls and the mysterious tracks, there's nothing else in the basement—oh, if the three people standing there and the guy lying on the ground count as anything too.
…… Wait, the one lying there? Could it be a corpse? Suddenly, you became interested, feeling a bit nervous and anticipating as you walked over, ignoring the sword raised behind you and the wary gaze. You just squatted down and looked around—hmm, it seemed dead...... It felt like your heart was beating no more. So you lifted the corpse up satisfied, humming a tune that was completely out of tune, and walked toward the basement door.
…… It's this corpse monster with gritted teeth. You have to think about whether these iron pieces are edible or if you have to peel them all off like skinning...... You were seriously pondering this question, completely unaware that your legs on your shoulders trembled slightly.
Until you hear a slightly electric cracking sound and a goosebump-inducing sound like iron scraping against each other: "How long will ...... [you] continue to [drag and pull]?" ”
You hesitated for two seconds, your first reaction was shock and extreme loss—the corpse wasn't completely dead! In other words, you couldn't just eat it directly! Your second reaction was to comfort yourself...... Although you weren't completely dead, it still felt like you were about to die. Who knows when you'd end up dead or just a corpse when you got back. Using it as a reserve food might not be so bad.
Later, you realized it slowly—oh, when dragging him, because he was just a corpse, his head and half of his body were dragged along the ground, occasionally hitting some stones along the way.
"Uh, I don't know, but anyway, Mr. Corpse, you probably can't walk on your own. Should I just throw this for you?" You said casually, but since the corpse is alive and can still talk, you do have a subtle conscience. So you turn around, first throw those two legs to the ground with a clang, then pick up his head and sit it on your shoulder. Finally, you nod in satisfaction. Hmm, that's good. Although now it's the lower body suffering, you can only add a light apology in your heart, without any regrets.
“…… First, I am not a corpse now. ”
As soon as he finished speaking, you quickly added, dragging him forward: "If you're not right now, you will be in the future." ”
…… He was choked by you, and after a while, things quieted between you and you. You didn't pay much attention. He didn't say no, so you planned to drag him back.
"...... in the future, it might not be a [corpse]!" His voice sounded somewhat annoyed.
And you just sighed with a hint of regret: "What? If it's not a corpse, then it turns into charcoal? That probably doesn't taste good...... But roasted wood should be edible too? Forget it, Mr. Corpse, you'd better not die yet—it's my reserve food. "You added another sentence at the end, not very serious."
“…… Stop calling me that, I have a [name]. ”
You scratched your head. To be honest, you didn't really care what Mr. Corpse's name was called. You didn't care much about the name of a corpse reserve food that was destined to die and probably turn into food. But you decided to brush it off and treat it as hospice care.
So you casually asked, "...... Alright, then what's your name? ”
“Spamton.G.Spamton.” You heard him say that. Honestly, maybe it was because of the vibration of his voice, but you felt your back tremble in waves, and it was quite uncomfortable. You even wanted to just leave him there, collecting him once he was completely dead… but if someone else took him, wouldn't your reserve food be gone! Thinking this through, you decided to grit your teeth, overcome the difficulty, and take him back.
"Oh, okay, Mr. Corpse, I understand." You nodded obediently, using your previous form of address. Actually, you hadn't even heard it earlier, and naturally didn't remember what his name was.
“…… I [seriously emphasize], I have [name].' "It sounded like his voice was tinged with fatigue.
Alright, you had no choice but to give up this good memory and name with a hint of regret, saying, "Alright, Mr. Corpse...... Uh, spam...... You got stuck, because you didn't remember at all, so you didn't listen carefully. Now, you only got the answer after recalling it carefully.
“Spamton,” he sounds like he’s about ready to give up correcting you completely.
You awkwardly cough twice: “Oh, okay, Spamton. Now I’m notifying you—not asking—so I’m just telling you, you have no choice. I’m taking you back to my home, then once you die... um, to me, you’ll probably serve as reserve food. But don’t worry, I’ll make sure to provide proper end-of-life care!”
Saying this, you clench your fists and swing them a couple of times to psych yourself up, looking quite spirited.
Spamton held back, wanting to argue something more, but if he tried to argue further, he would probably just respond with a hum, then continue repeating these words carelessly.
In the end, he couldn't help but say again: "...... I don't need [hospice care]!! ”
You just spoke in a surprised tone: "Don't you need to?" I think you're almost a corpse. Honestly, I'm pretty sorry you haven't really turned into one...... Oh, if you don't need hospice care, I'll just leave you in the basement and wait to die. But the basement isn't that great—it's not very light-opaque, there's no breathable water, and no proper water supply...... If you're about to die, don't worry so much! To follow the strategy of not doing hospice care, I absolutely won't visit you, nor will I bring you anything. No, I guess the food reserves don't need anything else......
Perhaps because it had been a long time since you spoke to a living person, you found yourself chattering a lot. After all, you could ramble a lot in front of those things that couldn't speak and weren’t afraid of being suddenly interrupted. Since Spamton didn’t interrupt you now, you naturally continued talking.
But he couldn't help but speak, and somehow you could hear a hint of humiliation in his words: "...... I [need][hospice care]. ”
You fell silent regretfully. You thought you could talk a bit more, maybe maybe sell the basement, but you couldn't help but add, "...... Wait, do you really need hospice care? I think the basement environment is pretty good. You're going to die anyway, so staying there isn't a bad idea. ”
"I really [need]. And my [life condition] [good and healthy]. ”
You expressed doubt: "Really?" I just saw you almost dead...... Forget it, since you're saying that, maybe you shouldn't live in the basement. Who knows when the basement will finally welcome a true owner who appreciates it......
Sighing, you finally return home, dragging him along. You open the door and lay Spamton’s head on the bed. With his legs still trailing on the floor, he ends up in an awkward posture.
You cleared your throat twice and glanced around the room. It was a bit messy, with nothing else to do. So you put your hands on your hips and announced, "You can stay here!" "Hmm, my room only has one bed, so you can only lie on this bed." "But don't worry, to prevent you from suddenly becoming a corpse and no one hears your last words, I'll fully endure the stench of corpses lying next to you!" You declared solemnly.
“…I’m not going to become a [corpse],” Spamton repeats, sounding exhausted.
"Alright, no matter what you say, I need to prepare something to eat first. To properly provide end-of-life care, I'll prepare a serving for you as well." You shrugged and walked into the kitchen on your own.
To be able to eat it yourself, although it's a bit of a pity there are no corpses, maybe changing the method would be okay......
So you cut a carrot and put it in the pot, sprinkle some orange threads you dug out earlier as a topping, pour in rabbit blood that had been refrigerated for a day or two, and finally hesitate for a moment, then pick up the whole pigeon you just took out that morning and put it in the pot—though peeled, the innards are probably still there. Then, carelessly, you start pouring sugar, but your hand shakes, you pour too much sugar, and you add a lethal dose of sugar to the pot.
Anyway, the steaming hot pigeons with orange, shredded carrot, rabbit, and blood red soup stew are freshly made. When you take a bite, the sweetness mixes with the fishy and bitter flavors. Hmm, actually, the taste is pretty good for you.
Satisfied, you bring the soup out and take two bowls, placing one in front of Spamton.
What Spamton saw was a reddish-blooded soup mixed with an inexplicable mixture, stewing a pigeon.
He was silent for a moment, then asked in a somewhat uncertain tone, "...... Is this food?" ”
You serve yourself a bowl, happily sipping it, and nod encouragingly at him: “Yes, this is obviously food! Try it, I think it tastes pretty good, and I’m offering proper end-of-life care—you see, I even cooked specially for you…” You even pretend to wipe away fake tears.
In short, you won't hear his answer; you only see him silent for a moment before struggling to speak again: "I am currently [unable to move]." ”
You rub your chin and nod knowingly: "Oh, oh, you need me to finish pretending to feed you, huh...... You also said you wouldn't become a corpse and couldn't even move—this is basically dying. ”
Spamton shut his mouth, feeling that answering this question again would be an insult to himself, because no matter how he explained, you'd always have your own perspective.
"In short...... This is the [current situation]. "He chose to ignore the issue and continue.
"Alright then, wait until I finish eating. I hope the soup won't get cold by then. I wonder how it will taste if it gets hot......" You muttered to yourself, finally speeding up your pace to finish the soup, ate some pigeon meat, and then refilled a bowl. You even brought over a new spoon, clearly planning to feed it properly.
Watching him drink it, you look at him expectantly: "How does it taste?" ”
Spamton was silent for a moment. He really didn't want to say that he had no sense of taste right now, so he couldn't taste anything. The taste of this soup was ...... At most, it only hurt a little.
But in the end, he gave a definite answer: "The taste is [acceptable]." ”
So you happily wave your fists and give him a thumbs-up, because he can't move right now. You even raise one of his hands and give a high-five.
"Wow, you really have taste! Is this soup really that good? I'll write it down and make it later...... As for the matter of sprinkling too much sugar all at once, just skip it selectively. Anyway, it's still quite tasty now.
“…… Maybe it's not a 'suitable' [recipe]. ”
You grabbed your notebook and happily started writing, and when you heard this, you started muttering, "So what? Anyway, normal methods don't suit me, I just can't eat it...... Oh right, I almost forgot about you. ”
You remember halfway through writing, so you put on disposable gloves, tear off the pigeon meat, and start feeding the corpse of this possibility.
After a while, the soup in the pot did get cold, but the pigeon meat was finished, so you happily went to wash the pots and bowls.
Tbc.
After quickly cleaning up the pots, pans, and dishes, you went back to look at Spamton, squatting down and rubbing your chin, staring at him. Probably because you had been staring for too long, he felt very uncomfortable and couldn't help but ask, “Why keep looking [at me]?”
You rubbed your chin, opened your mouth, and then, for once, fell silent. In the end, you just shook your head: "I don't know, so don't worry about it. Just think of it as me wondering what hospice care should do, right?" "You look dull and don't taste good at all. Maybe you should clean it up first......"
You muttered.
Spamton had a bad feeling and couldn't help but ask, "...... [wash]? [Bathing work]? How do you [carry it out]?" "Honestly, he's really afraid you'll suddenly throw him into a pool and forget to pull him out and leave him at the bottom."
"Uh, pour a bucket of water and then scrub it with a brush. What else are you counting on?" You shrugged.
Strangely, he actually felt a relaxed feeling he could still accept. It seemed that once he crossed the line, he could endure all this well...... To be honest, it wasn't good at all, but at least he didn't actually throw it into the pool for him to climb up.
Then Spamton stopped speaking and stared at you with that strange gaze. Even through his glasses, you could see his expression. You couldn’t help but shrug and shiver, hugging your own shoulders: “Why are you looking at me? Cleaning is just me being kind. Does end-of-life care include washing your body or something… uh, that sounds scary,” you muttered, then stood up, went to the next room to get a bucket of water, and dragged Spamton toward the bathroom.
"Hmm, to prevent water from being everywhere and hard to clean up, let's get it in the bathroom first." You muttered to yourself, then threw the Spamton onto the bathroom floor, poured the bucket of water over his head, and in a rather humane manner, poured water from top to bottom.
…… He was about to shiver from the cold water, but right now he couldn't move at all! Spamton instinctively became irritable. He wanted to do something, but nothing worked—he simply didn't have the strength.
So he can only try to glare you with a fierce look. But of course, his gaze can't kill. You just pretend you didn't see his gaze. You just have a bit of conscience. You pick up a clean brush, draw a few strokes, and finally decide to wash the part of yourself that looks like some kind of steel mech.
To be honest, you don't even know what this part is. Probably, or maybe it's not that important, and it doesn't look very appetizing. The main issue is the strange color...... You grumble to yourself and accidentally pull off the high heels Spamton was somehow wearing. You don't want to scrub your shoes, and cooking them doesn't taste good.
Spamton didn't feel much extra when wiping the lower part of his body, but the thought that the brush would soon land on his face made him feel a chilling fear.
Well, at least for a while, it won't be like this, because you flipped Spamton over and started farming the back.
…… He didn't want to recall what happened afterward; in short, it was definitely not a good thing! Spamton thought irritably.
Now he's lying weakly on your bed, his steel armor gleaming to a shine. You're very satisfied, so after drying him dry, drag him back and throw him onto the bed.
To be honest, when you picked it up, it was almost dinner time. Now that you look at it, after all the fuss you've been around and it's almost time to sleep, you're tired too. So you happily lie down on the bed, turn off the light, wrap yourself in the blanket, close your eyes, and get ready to sleep.
Spamton could hear rustling sounds nearby. He stared at the ceiling in the darkness for a while, then finally couldn't help but speak: "...... Don't I [own][quilt: ownership]?" ”
You were already sleepy and about to fall asleep, but hearing this finally made you a little more alert. After struggling for a while, you didn't want to part with the blanket that wrapped you up like a zongzi and gave you a sense of security. In the end, you painfully let it go. If you could see clearly, you'd see your face was full of reluctance.
"Alright, Mr. Corpse, good night. Getting you some rest is probably part of hospice care as well." You said casually, pulling back the blanket and thoughtfully covering Spamton with half of it.
He couldn't be bothered to correct your form of address. After you said it, you'd still do as you pleased, and Spamton pretended not to hear.
Honestly, how did things get to this point?! Spamton had no idea at all.
He widened his eyes and kept staring at the ceiling, hearing your shallow breathing beside him. "Good, you're asleep now, no one can control him." That doesn't mean he can do anything now, because the next second, he sees you rolling around in bed and rolling beside him.
He saw your eyebrows furrow instinctively, probably because you were too cold. Spamton thought somewhat indifferently, since your body was like this now, and there was no way to warm it up...... Before he could finish his wild thoughts, he felt your hand move, because he could feel his head and body being pushed against him. Although the feeling was not obvious because the threads were cut, a dull and wooden sensation, he could still feel your movements, and probably quite a bit of force.
…… Because he realizes his body is moving toward the edge of the bed, and your body keeps arching toward you.
…… Good, he finally managed to get pushed off the bed by you. In fact, this actually made things easier—at least he wouldn't have to feel the constant force of the pushing, Spamton thought expressionlessly.
And Spamton could hear that when he fell off the bed, there was probably a loud bang—at least the clatter of something hitting him—but he just heard you rolling around on the bed again, muttering 'Why are you so noisy?' and kept sleeping.
Very good, and your sleep quality is also very good. Now he will probably be lying on the floor all night. Although he was used to this kind of life, this was the first time he had experienced lying in bed while being squeezed onto the floor to sleep. Spamton thought expressionlessly.
In any case, in the end, he didn't know how he actually fell asleep. Maybe he had been staring at the ceiling all night and then briefly lost consciousness. After all, when he came to his senses, he found his eyes were still open.
…… And I can even hear your snoring.
Good, but now he doesn't know how much longer he'll have to lie on the floor. This time, Spamton felt his gaze on the ceiling carry resentment.
He didn't know how much time passed before he finally heard your groggy voice, and then he could see you probably sitting up from the bed.
You sat for a few minutes before slowly turning on the camera, remembering what exactly you had done yesterday, oh...... You picked up a corpse and brought it home. You were fully awake. You remembered him sleeping in your bed last night, so you instinctively looked around but didn't see him. You also found yourself right in the middle of the bed, with the blanket wrapped around you again without her noticing, like wrapping a zongzi.
Scratching your head, just as you were about to wonder where he could go, you heard a voice from under the bed: "...... I'm [above] the floor." ”
For some reason, you could hear a hint of grievance in his tone, so you cleared your throat twice, a bit embarrassed: "Ah, sorry to have you sleep on the floor, Mr. Corpse. But that place should have been your place to return anyway...... Ahem, I'm a territorial person, so I probably accidentally pushed you off to sleep on the floor, hahaha. ”
Even so, in the end you feel justified again, showing no sign of embarrassment.
Spamton said nothing. He felt so annoyed today that he didn’t even need to eat, but you, on the other hand, enthusiastically changed clothes and jumped up, dragging Spamton along, ready to go out: “Come on, come on, I feel so hungry I’m gonna shrink! Let’s find food first!”
What else can he say? He can't resist now, so he'll just be dragged away by you.
…Until he was thrown on the ground, and while you were still enthusiastically spreading honey on him, Spamton finally couldn’t hold back and spoke: “[Inquiry: purpose of action].”
You casually replied, “Ah, ah, spreading honey, to attract ants. I don’t have anything else on hand except you, sorry for the trouble!” while continually moving your hands. Soon the entire jar of honey was poured over Spamton.
"...... [you] could consider [Pure] lying on the ground." He said, his voice weak and lifeless.
"I know, but that makes it hard to collect, so I'll just leave it at that!" "Besides, you don't have to do anything. I'll provide you with food, clothing, and shelter, and you can rescue and do some chores. It's not really anything." "You shouted, squatting not far away and watching, soon ants crawled over following the sweet scent of honey, and of course, all kinds of flying little bugs—you chased them all away. After all, you only needed ants.
And there was another advantage: after all, Spamton was wearing steel, so the ants couldn't bite them and could only lick the leftover honey on the cold metal sheet. Soon, more and more ants gathered, gathering around Spamton, forming a dense crowd. If anyone with trypophobia passed by, they would definitely be scared to death by this scene.
And you happily dragged Spamton's head and brought him home. Today's ingredients are well stocked; having collected so many ants, it should be quite good.
Spamton chose to close his eyes and ignore the ants crawling on his face. He could only endure and could do nothing more, so he had no choice but to endure.
You dragged him home, collected all the ants, threw him on the floor again, and then happily led the ants to the kitchen.
First, take out the dried tangerine peel, then cook the ants. Anyway, seeing them floating on the water, they should be cooked. Then put the dried tangerine peel back in and pour in some salt...... The taste should be pretty good!
After cooking for a while, you finally took out the ants along with the dried tangerine peel. Now the ants were all lying on the peel. After thinking for a moment, you added some cabbage to the plate, then picked it up and steamed it in the steamer for a while before taking it out. Mm, you nodded in satisfaction. No wonder you had already made the Ant Climbing the Tree dish so quickly.
Then you carried the plate out and placed it in front of Spamton again, happily clapping your hands: “I’ll feed you this one, I’m making this dish for the first time too, so I don’t know how it tastes…” Before you finished speaking, Spamton first glanced at the plate on the floor, the weird dried orange peel and ants lying in a strangely green soup, the eerie mix of green and black made him wish he could faint right then.
"[Question]? Is this [food]?" But perhaps because his mind was too strong, he didn't faint immediately; instead, he calmly asked questions.
You nodded matter-of-factly: "Yeah, that's today's meal. Hurry up and eat, I think it's pretty tasty!" Oh wait, you can't move yet, so I have to feed you......" As you spoke, you started waving your hands and feet, then ran into the kitchen, ready to come out with a spoon.
Spamton fell silent. To be honest, he didn't even know where his strength came from, and even he felt horrified—he should have been powerless and at his mercy. But now he felt he had some strength again, or maybe, uh, he was so angry he could stand again. In any case, he didn't know how long this state would last, but he did feel Neo seemed to be working again.
…… So he stood up and headed toward the kitchen. Just as you were about to take the spoon and walk out, you saw Spamton heading over, and you couldn't help but open your mouth wide: "...... Wow, a medical miracle? "You exclaim with admiration.
You saw him walking over without saying a word. For some reason, you felt a bit scared, but instinctively, you stepped aside and watched him walk into the kitchen.
You prop your head up, watching Spamton open your fridge, then take out pigeons, eggplants, potatoes, and all sorts of other ingredients. Then comes the sounds of chopping, stir-frying, and the smell of cooking smoke.
You scratched your head. Although you didn't know how this medical miracle was made or why he came to cook, you still sat down at the dining table, ready to wait for him to bring the food up.
Then you see Spamton serve four dishes and one soup placed in front of you, and then collapse into a chair, seemingly just a last burst of life.
Tbc.
You glanced at Spamton, then at the dishes on the table, hesitated for a moment, and said, "Uh, can you eat by yourself now? Do you still need me to feed you?" You thought you were being considerate of asking this question, and then you saw Spamton seem to roll his eyes. In short, he was looking at you with a bad attitude.
You forced a couple of laughs: "Alright, can you eat it yourself? Just say it." ”
