You pull up the chandelier, turn off the lights, and the night is all silent. Your hands crossed over your chest, you fall into a dark sleep, you fall asleep.
That night was very quiet, nothing unnecessary. The next day, you opened your eyes and sat up in bed. You glanced at Spamton beside you and saw him sleeping neatly, curled up in a ball, wearing the white shirt you had handed him yesterday.
You got up, took off your loose underwear—or rather pajamas—and changed into a bra and regular outerwear, ignoring the shocked gazes from behind. You simply walked outside, casually took a few slices of bread from the fridge to bake, spread jam on them, popped them into your mouth, and then took Spamton's clothes from the dryer and handed them to him.
She also spread strawberry jam on freshly made bread and handed it to him.
Then you walked outside, just saying in a calm, understated tone: "You can start working today." ”
With that, you picked up an unused typewriter at home, confirmed there was still ink, then stepped out and walked into the small library next door, skillfully sitting in the same spot. After thinking for a moment, you found a small table and chair, placed the typewriter on it, and made it convenient for Spamton to work for you.
Then you hear the library door creak open, and you see the little puppet walk in. You push the chair and gesture for him to sit down.
Spamton paused, but after all, he got in. He seemed to have a lot to say, but didn't know what to say. And you picked up the book "Diconca's Nearby Night Talks" and started reading. Seeing his hesitant expression, you decided to help her resolve her questions.
So, for once, you asked kindly, "What's wrong?" ”
"...... [No problem]." He stammered for a long time and only gave you this answer, his voice inexplicably becoming sharp. In fact, he had many questions, but he felt he shouldn't ask you, at least right now.
So you nodded, didn't press further, and simply spoke calmly: "Alright. I'll start telling today's story. Remember to record it." ”
You cleared your throat, and that slightly hoarse but slow yet clear sound rang out again, accompanied by the metallic tapping of the typewriter.
[Did you know? Liars turn into big trees, become monsters in the forest, turn into crimson sunsets, turn into the mud and sand at the bottom of a sunken river, oh?
So, don't walk into that unknown, monster-filled forest, don't stare directly at the sun, don't swallow the silt from the river—maybe you're swallowing a person.
Liars must swallow a thousand needles—no, no, no, how can a child's joke be trusted? But the story I'm about to tell is actually a real and believable one. Please believe me, those who break promises will be punished. Of course, evil is punished, but good deeds also come at a price. Everything is an equivalent exchange; there's no such thing as getting everything without giving.
Why do I say this? Please keep listening.
A long, long time ago, in a small village, the atmosphere was simple and simple. The people were very warm, and every household knew each other. Children were out running, playing, and playing games every day. But the adults always warned them that they couldn't go into the forest, because monsters would eat you—because once you go, you can never come back! Because there's no turning back!
Children are always curious about this, and some ask adults, 'What's really in the forest? Why can't we all go in?' But why can adults go in? Why are there always guards ahead of the forest, not letting us children go through? Why do some people go in and never come back? Why do some people go in and leave unharmed?
But the adults always roughly push away the children with many questions, speaking in somewhat rude tones, saying, 'Go on, go on, every child has so many questions. There aren't so many whys, nor so many answers. If you can't go, you can't go. Just remember this.'
So the children stopped asking and behaved themselves. But even though they stopped asking, these questions seemed to take root in their hearts. At night, as they went to sleep, they would always wonder what was in the forest, and why the adults wouldn't let them go. In the morning, while playing, the children would gather together to chat secretly, making up stories about the monsters in the woods.
Some children said it was a terrifying black beast with fangs that kept bleeding, but they feared the light and hid in the shadowy woods, refusing to come out. But once someone passed by, they would immediately devour the child!
Some children said they were actually monsters that looked human-like, but their skin was pale and they looked more like monsters than humans. However, they would disguise themselves as humans to make themselves look less like monsters, then quietly approach people, luring them into their lairs to eat them. They didn't dare leave the forest because if they went out and were discovered, they would be driven away.
Some children said there were no monsters anywhere; it was just that the forest was full of poisonous creatures, snakes, wolves, tigers, and leopards. That's why the adults wouldn't let them in, even making up stories about monsters to scare them.
Some children, trembling and cautious, said that adults don't like them discussing these things, so it's better to stop talking.
So the children, still wanting more, stopped and continued the ball throwing game, only returning home at dusk. There were many opinions, no definite answer, but the more sternly the adults warned, the more curious the children became. Until one day, while the children were playing the usual ball tossing and catching game, a little girl missed catching the ball and it ran far away. She hurriedly chased after it, but the ball rolled into the deep forest. It happened to be shift time, and there was briefly no guard ahead of the forest. The girl gritted her teeth and ran into the woods. Naturally, her heart was afraid. She didn't know what lay ahead, what monsters might exist, or whether she might disappear—if she could, maybe she wouldn't have entered this forest either.
But the ball rolling far away was only a fuse; she had long wanted to go into the forest. This rolling ball merely made her make up her mind, take a step, and walk into the forest. She had long wanted to know what kind of monsters were really in the forest, and why the adults kept warning her so insistently.
So she swallowed her saliva and then resolutely stepped forward, walking into the forest.
Unexpectedly, the forest was actually very quiet. There weren’t the deep red, overwhelming thorns and leaves that children imagined, nor were there the black, man-eating monsters that adults spoke of. Curious, the girl walked forward, and somehow the trees naturally parted to make way for her. In front of her spread a path that was slightly winding but led straight ahead.

What she saw was no longer branches blocking her sight, replaced instead by rivers; what she heard was the melodious chirping of birds, the rustling of green leaves, the fluttering of white doves, and flowers sparsely blooming on the grass.
—This shouldn’t be a forbidden place, it shouldn’t be a land where one dies without a grave; perhaps it should be an Eden instead. Suddenly, this thought occurred to the girl.
As for the so-called land where one dies without a grave, it was a name the adults gave based on the occasional deaths that happened in this forest.
But, the girl didn’t see any monsters at all; what she saw was another kind of life, one that could even be said to overturn her understanding—
At this point, you abruptly stop, and Spamton’s typing process halts as well.
You frown, clear your throat, and cough twice: "...Sorry, I need to take a break. Let's stop here for today." You feel too weak to continue the story; your hands are trembling, or rather, your whole body is shaking, falling into a numb and powerless state. In that moment, perhaps pure anxiety occupies your heart. Your hands weakly release the book, and it thuds onto the ground.
And you just hug your knees tightly, curling up in place.
Spamton hesitates for a moment. At first, he doesn’t speak because he has no obligation to help you. But after much consideration, Spamton decides to offer assistance. Whether due to your current employment relationship, or because you are a being of light and he needs your soul, it is a reason for him to help you.
So he asks: "...Is there any【help】I can【provide】? I am very willing【to serve you】."
You lift your head to look at him, weakly blinking your eyes, and shake your head hesitantly: "No... I’ll be fine in a moment." Unconsciously, your eyes meet his, or rather, those glasses, and somehow you change your mind.
Then you open your arms, speaking in a slightly awkward, deliberate voice: "If possible, please give me a hug, please... um, that's not correct, it should be, let me hug you for a moment."
Then you press your lips together and give a flustered laugh: "Sorry, this request is a bit sudden—" But before you can finish, your eyes widen. You see Spamton jump down from the chair, then grab your hand, or rather, hold your hands tightly, wrap his arms around you, or, give you a hug.
You remain silent, holding him in your arms, resting your chin on his head, and start to stare blankly. You maintain the pose of hugging him with both hands, not even knowing if it causes him any discomfort.

title: It's okay not to forgive - Confession
path: articles/en/spt/一千零一夜/不原谅也没关系-自白.html
content:
I don’t know what I should say anymore. Maybe all language and words are powerless, forever unable to express my true thoughts. But I can only use these; I have nothing else. Only the time immersed in words truly belongs to me. There are so many things to consider in living in this world, so many things to be busy with every day; to survive, to achieve personal happiness and fulfillment, there are so many efforts to be made... yet I only wish to have time that truly belongs to me. I already have a lot of such time, but I can’t help myself from letting my thoughts sink into the abyss.
... If I could only immerse myself in the vast ocean of books, if I could only curl up in the narrow gaps between dim bookshelves, lose myself in reading a book, record my thoughts and ideas, how wonderful that would be. Unfortunately, this is just an unrealistic dream, probably never achievable. I am human, and being human means needing to survive, needing to act, not just hide away. Although I am weary of all this, I must continue in order to live.
... I must continue, even though I am tired of all this, even though my heart screams that what I need is rest, complete relaxation, to immerse myself in my own world without concern, otherwise I will never truly feel happiness. But perhaps I am using reason to suppress emotion. My inner experience tells me to let it all end, to let my life end here too, as there is little attachment left for this world. Yet my reason tells me that to live better, I must do these things, I must live more orderly in order to live better.
But what’s the point of living better? Is it just to die better, with no regrets? I cannot understand any of this, and I have no right to explain. I admit, perhaps I cannot see through my own heart. But I don’t want to fake happiness. I don’t want to face others with a false face, though sometimes I still subconsciously put on armor and wear a mask, because I know it’s the only way to satisfy them, the only way to make others happy.
... But why do that? Even if I don’t, why should other people’s thoughts matter to me? Why should I care about them? I cannot explain or understand. Perhaps I am just a child who has never grown up, still needing others to tell me the answers, because I am trapped, trapped in a certain day, unable to ever leave. Everything is probably just a disguise for the self. If it didn’t bring pain, that would be good. Yet it does bring pain and embarrassment, perhaps because my inner self is struggling with it.
I am trying, trying to make my life look a little better, yet it seems useless. Who can tell me that my life has meaning? Or can I even tell myself that I must continue living? Why are we born, and why do we die? If I had never lived, I would not have felt this pain. But if I had never lived, perhaps I wouldn’t have experienced even fleeting moments of beauty. Should we endure all the pain of life just for those brief moments of happiness?
... What is my connection with this world? I don’t really know. What I do know is that I probably don’t truly love anything or like anything, I only have fleeting moments of joy. I also don’t truly hate anything, but have I even lost the ability to feel that way? From the bottom of my heart, I want to hate something, yet that feeling has faded over time.
... Or maybe that isn’t a bad thing. Perhaps completely forgetting the past is not impossible. Maybe all my attempts now are just efforts to love something, attempts to give myself an object to be persistent about. Am I overthinking? Should I not think about these things? Can I just escape? But I don’t want a life of passive acceptance; I want the courage to face it all.
Yet my courage seems to have gradually worn away. In the end, isn’t all this just the struggle of an ignorant child? What am I, after all?
... Or perhaps being nothing at all would be the best ending.

Stepping on the stone steps, through the misty clouds, the scholar wearing a white and loose robe came in and out of this prestigious academy. He touched the marble columns and looked up. Many people were sitting in a circle, probably arguing about something, so much so that their faces were red, and perhaps no one could convince anyone else.
After all, clever words and flattery, and theories outlined with vivid rhetoric, may sound convincing at first, but everyone tends to hold onto their own views, making it difficult for others to persuade them.
The young man noticed this. He saw that some of them wore masks with sheep faces; they were probably on the same side, as they were sitting together, speaking with certainty about something. Then there were others who didn’t wear masks; they had different expressions, each holding their own opinion, seemingly in disagreement, each speaking for their own side.
So the young man thought that perhaps he could also express some opinions. Thus, he walked up the steps, went over to the people sitting in a circle, and listened to what exactly they were saying.

So she couldn't help but reach out and hug the woman back.
The woman said, 'Child, you are the child I have searched for for so long, and today I finally found it...... You are the child I have lost for so long.
The girl said, "Mom, long time no see, I miss you so much."
Yes, for some reason, she was already in tears. She realized the word, and although she didn't know what it meant, she knew it was meant to address the woman in front of her.
The woman smiled, "I miss you too, child." It was all those annoying men who took our child away...... And we were powerless. Fortunately, I can still see my child; thankfully, before I die, I can still see you.
The girl sobbed and asked, "Why is that?" What exactly happened? Why did those people take these children? What are they trying to do?
After all, she was just a child who knew nothing. She desperately wanted an answer, even if it was something she didn't want to know. Even though the truth might be cruel, she had to know. At this moment, she seemed to have grown up, as if she was no longer the child she once was.
Another woman in a green robe approached, also kneeling on her knees, slowly telling a story to the two who were sobbing uncontrollably.
For some reason, men and women lived separately. Maybe they lived together long ago, but later they were customarily separated, and those men no longer disturbed life in the woods, that is, in the Garden of Eden.
Conversely, they also met one condition. Every October, the woman would provide five children to the outside world. From then on, there would be no chance to meet again, because these women would die after raising two children, so they could no longer see their children and could only enjoy some tender moments before the exchange.
Girls who grew up outside would return to Eden, never getting another chance to leave, while boys raised outside would still stay there. Conversely, as a trade-off, women required men to fulfill five promises each year.
Some women are kind-hearted, only asking to bring her a flower. Some are pragmatic, asking to be built a wooden house to bring food from outside. Some women deliberately make things difficult, asking the man to pluck the moon from the horizon and give it to her.
Because only when promises are not fulfilled do women have ways to torment these men. They don't blame those who make simple demands, after all, they are not their enemies.
As for the men who failed to keep their promises, some screamed in terror as they were devoured by monsters disguised as women; some turned back into matter, becoming sand and silt at the bottom of the river; others looked exhausted, their bodies stiff and stiff, then turned into identical trees. Others rolled on the ground in pain, as if a thousand silver needles were stabbing their throats, and finally died on the ground, dying on the ground.
This is the truth that people in the forest will go missing and die.
After all...... Breaking promises comes at a price, and of course, doing bad things also comes with a price. Their experience at this moment is the cost, and the promises they had to fulfill to steal those five children were also the price.
…… You want to ask me what the price of doing good deeds is? Then please listen to the rest of the story.
The girl learned the truth of the story and decided to change everything. She didn't want to see her own people suffer again, and she didn't want such things to happen again. But the women advised her not to keep trying; maintaining the status quo was fine, and perhaps it was fine. As they said this, their faces showed unwillingness and frustration.
So the girl's anger—perhaps because she was young, still had the courage to move forward, and the determination to change everything. She angrily asked, Is maintaining the status quo really good? Is it good to remain a victim? Is it really good to have anger and fear in your heart?
The women looked at each other, and finally, the first to kneel and embrace her was her mother, saying she was willing to try again. More and more women joined in, some indignant—some picked up stones, others picked up branches to use as protective weapons, even though that might be nothing.
Then, for the first time, they left the forest together, chased away the guards at the entrance, defeated the men who treated them like monsters, and became the rulers of the village. So the remaining children learned that there were no monsters in the forest; they were stories made up by the adults, or rather, men.
Yet isn't all of this just a beautiful fairy tale? The girl, or rather the boy, raised her arms and shouted, hoping more people would join her, but those people had long since become numb and lost the courage to struggle; only a few were willing to follow. She carried the truth and led those women out of the forest, but most children did not believe her words, and the adults only treated her and other women who came out of the forest as monsters and monsters, attacking them. After struggling to resist and speak out, they ultimately fell into despair, and all that awaited them was death.
This is the price—the price of doing good, using life as the foundation of justice, freedom, courage, and kindness.
A long, long time ago, people lived together in this Garden of Eden, regardless of gender, without distinction, simply running and laughing freely among the shade of trees and the babbling stream, enjoying a happy life. After all, virtue is happiness, and joy is the supreme pleasure.
But one day, things changed. A man—at least as we call it now—was a man. They had tasted the forbidden fruit, and they probably knew something, so they put on their clothes and left Eden in a proper manner. And the women remained in the Garden of Eden, not knowing what had happened, but because the words of those men had also put on clothes.
Yet they continued to freely enjoy unrestrained happiness in the Garden of Eden. But one day, everything changed. Those men once again entered Eden—because after leaving, they were no longer welcomed. The men who entered forced the remaining women in Eden to have sex—in other words, to have intercourse. The women wept, beat them, and begged, but found no release, only receiving even more violent assaults.
Afterwards, the men left again. Behind were women left in disarray and devoid of any desire to live.
But as their bellies grew larger and painful, happiness also emerged. They felt love and sincere affection for their unborn child, and this rekindled their hope to survive.
Unfortunately, the good times didn't last—after that, after ten months of painful pregnancy, the women held their children in tears, loving them, but then the men broke in again, took the children, and assaulted them once more. Compared to a real person, or rather, it was just tools and machines.
So, they could only painfully continue this process, repeating the cycle and hating those men. But without weapons, they could do nothing. Those girls who were taken away would return to Eden when they grew up, becoming tools themselves; the boys who were taken would grow up carefree in the outside world, continuing all this evil.
—This is the truth of the story.

You held up your phone, stiffly spinning your head to glance at the photo displayed. You even zoomed in to check the details, then looked at the tiny one in front. In short, you couldn't quite tell how big this thing was. It looked like some kind of puppet displayed in a store window, and the passing children could only drool in envy.
The clothes definitely don't match, so you remain skeptical and zoom in on the head part of the photo...... Uh, well, the hairstyles do look a bit similar, but the puppet's hair is noticeably longer, with ends, and it wears inexplicable pink yellow glasses.
You respect others' artistic choices; perhaps this is just an art style you haven't encountered before.
In short, it's probably half and half. While it could be the same person, it could just be cyber art processing, and the place where you meet now is a strange alley with a pile of garbage right next to it. And—you saw it before you appeared in this alley! This puppet is rummaging through a trash bin!
Well, you don't reject people who dig through trash; everyone has their own way of survival, and you choose to respect and bless them.
And seeing her clothes so neat, it's obvious she even showered herself before leaving. Yet she still feels inexplicably moved.
Put away your phone, squat down, and stare at him wide-eyed—even though you can't see his eyes.
Then you carefully asked, "...Is this Spamton, uh, sir?"
He nodded.
Your mood grew heavier, and after gathering your emotions for a while, you continued to ask: "...... Was it an online dating scam? ”
For some reason, you always feel like your little soul is hurt. Although the probability of online dating scams isn't low, you never imagined it would happen to you beforehand.
Visibly, you feel like the puppet in front of you is on fire, probably a warm sensation: "Me!" No! Using [fraudulent means]! ”
You just nodded perfunctorily: "Mm-hmm, no." ”
It seemed like his fever had gotten even worse.
So how did things end up like this?
Just to clarify, you're not addicted to the internet. You're just bored alone in Cyber City and want to search for a friend on your phone. Then you see their profile picture looks pretty good, so you add them.
After all, who isn't obsessed with looks? At least you didn't bother others to send you abs photos...... Ahem.
In short, although the text from the other side is always strange, you can understand it anyway, and you find this way of speaking quite fun. After all, you respect others' characteristics, maybe it's just artistic style!
Although we don't chat every day, several years have passed. I don't know why the account has been offline recently. At least you're a bit worried, and no matter what, you're a bit curious.
Anyway, you say, let's meet in person.
At first, the other person is unwilling, but after you threaten them with some small tricks, they reluctantly agree.
Actually, you're just saying that if you don't meet in person, don't contact each other anymore. Even if you do reach out to me, you should lower the frequency of chats and such. That way, the other person won't be able to stand it.
…… You also feel that sometimes you nag too much, even feeling guilty and annoyed.
——
Anyway, now you feel like his temperature has dropped. After hesitating for a moment, you speak: "So...... Is it performance art? ”
“…… I don't have the [preference] of a performance art enthusiast. "You feel like the puppet that just cooled down is burning again.
Honestly, you think this process is pretty fun, but that's about it. Actually, now you're about 80% sure that the person on the other end of your screen is actually the same person, and that photo...... Well, maybe it's just makeup!
You respect others' choices and send blessings.
Anyway, cough dryly twice, then stand up. After all, squatting all the time is tiring to your legs.
"Alright, so now is it a date, uh? Is there anywhere you want to go?" "You were already a bit unsure about it, since we hadn't discussed what exactly to do when we met...... Uh, to be honest, you regret it now. If you'd known, you would've chatted online.
Although she appeared calm on the surface, inside she kept shouting, "Oh my god, I broke up!! ”
The little puppet walked a few steps toward you. You estimated that if he raised his hand and you held it, this height would look like an adult taking care of a child.
…… You reiterate that you are not pedophile, and it is obvious that the other party is not a pedophile.
"So...... Cyber Barbecue Restaurant? I wonder if you're willing?" "The puppet's voice sounded...... Anyway, it wasn't very pleasant, but you didn't care about these things.
"Shall we eat? This time of year should be about right...... Then let's go eat first. "You scratched your chin. To be honest, you don't really like barbecue; you always think it's greasy.
But it's okay, and you've tried this shop before—basically, you can accept it.
“Do you walk fast? Should I carry you over?” To be safe, you asked Spamton once more.
"Me!" "Sure!" "Absolutely can!" "Set off on your own!" "You feel like this puppet is about to jump up.
Alright, you nod indifferently. There's still some time before lunchtime, so you choose to walk over, and it's not too far. The puppet really keeps up with your pace. It just feels like it's struggling to walk, and it's fast—basically two steps as big as yours.
You sighed, slowed your pace, squatted down to take his hand, then stood up and walked forward. Although you slowed down, your steps didn't shrink; the small steps were still too torturous.
Anyway, you eventually reached your destination. There weren’t many people at this time. You successfully found a seat by the window and watched Spamton climb into the opposite seat, then sit down.
…… From this spot, you can only see the tips of his hair, and you fall into deep thought. So, will he stand up and eat later?
Out of respect, you didn't ask, just handed him the menu and let him order first.
Then you watch as the little puppet climbs up, stands in your seat, and starts reading the menu.
…… Hmm, you definitely aren't laughing.
He finished his order quickly. You checked the menu, checked for some vegetables, some alcoholic drinks, and handed the menu to the waiter.
The food arrived quickly. You propped your chin up and watched the little puppet sitting in the chair eating hard. You only picked up some meat to make sure you had enough energy, ate some vegetables, and finally started drinking.
You can guarantee your mind is absolutely clear! But after a few drinks, you still can't help but slam your glass down heavily on the table.
The Spamton opposite you was startled, interrupting his eating — to be honest, he seemed to be wolfing down the food; you truly didn’t know how long it had been since he had a decent meal.
Then you maintain a calm expression. You don't even know why you want to say this—maybe it's because you've been holding it in your heart for a long time. In any case, you are very calm, truly calm: "I... broke up." ”
Once you say it, you'll regret it. What exactly are you talking about!
The puppet opposite was so frightened that his fork fell off: "I swear, this [completely] [completely unrelated] has nothing to do with me!" ”
"No, it's entirely about you." You shook your head.
"Then. [Compensation measures]? Maybe you [need]? ”
You're sure this is definitely a guilty conscience from an online dating scam, absolutely true!!
"Yes, I need you to pay for it." So you nodded firmly.
"[Specific measures]?"
You rubbed your chin, put on a feigned thoughtful expression, then inexplicably smiled and reached your hand toward the puppet across from you: “Then, give yourself to me, Mr. Spamton.”
You really don't know what you're saying, and then your memory blurs. Or maybe after saying that, your head suddenly drops onto the table, and then you start to fall into a deep sleep.
In short, when you wake up, all you see is a cold, empty barbecue grill and some empty plates in front of you, and a little puppet sitting there. All you can see is a hairpin.
You shook your head, patted your face, confirming that you were fully sober, then pulled Spamton along to pay the bill.
Of course, you pay. After all, none of this matters to you. It's just that the waiter noticed the little puppet next to you and gave him the same look as if he were a pretty boy.
That really is pretty pale, and you wouldn't deny that.
In short, after paying, you left the cyber barbecue restaurant with Spamton, and you silently vowed that the next meal would absolutely be sushi! You just wanted to clear away the smell of grilling smoke.
"Alright, where are we next?" Standing at the intersection, you watch the cars roaring past and glance down at the little puppet still being held.
Honestly, it's quite fun.
“…… So, your previous [statement], [authenticity]? "Because he was just too short, you couldn't see his expression; you could only tell from that sentence that he seemed very nervous.
You scratch your hair: "Well, well, I guess it's true. Although I was deceived, honestly it feels okay. Life is just like this, I'm more open-minded." ”
"Then, it's up to you to make the [decision]."
You feel as if you've relaxed a bit, at least your hand isn't so tight anymore.
"Wow, then I'm going to the amusement park, and then I'm going to have sushi for dinner!"
So you happily make the decision.
"Yes, no problem, very [perfect plan]."
"Then it's settled! Mm...... I'll take a taxi over. To be honest, when I went before, I always had to wait in line, so I lost the mood to play. "You muttered to yourself, flagged down a car, and soon you arrived at the entrance of the amusement park.
It was a weekday, so there weren’t many people. You bought two tickets and entered with Spamton. You had actually thought about possibly getting a child’s ticket given his height… but then you figured against it.
You think this counts as fraud, but that's not good.
After looking at the amusement park facilities, you start thinking about which one to play first. By the way, if the puppet gets wet, will it break? Probably not, right?
So you clapped your hands: "I want to go ride the water roller coaster first." ”
Then you specifically looked at Spamton’s reaction; he didn’t have any special reaction, which made you feel a little disappointed.
But as for the amusement park, it was indeed a bit childish! Nonetheless, you didn’t care and excitedly pulled the little puppet along. Then you bought two disposable raincoats to put on. As for Spamton, all you could do was wrap him in a disposable raincoat.
And it's wrapped quite tightly—two full wraps in disposable raincoats. Probably considering the different sizes of people in Cyber City, the large raincoats are really big—when you put them on, the sleeves always hang down. And just to be safe, you bought two large ones.
Anyway, squat down now, look at the pink-yellow glasses wrapped in your raincoat, then nod in satisfaction, and sneakily pat his head in return.
"Not bad, let's keep it this way. Let's go." After all, you're about to get the line.
You could see Spamton blushing again, but this time you ignored it — it would be fine after a while!
The water roller coaster would soon finish one round, since the distance was short, and you curiously sat down on the seat, fastening your seatbelt and gripping the handrail...... Then you looked over next door. Fortunately, the belt could at least be fastened around the puppet's waist, but it had to be shortened. Well, after all, this was a bizarre cyber city.
“I think we should [prevent] [similar incidents].” You heard Spamton’s muffled voice through the raincoat.
“…… But I want to play. "So you put on that deliberately pitiful expression, but actually, you're not pitiful at all—you just want to play. If that's the case, why not act cute!"
"......" The puppet fell silent. It couldn't possibly be someone who had muted him. You glanced at it and saw the eyes behind the glasses were already closed, so you could only look ahead regretfully, waiting for the car to depart.
After gliding slowly on the water for a while, the height rises before it drops sharply, landing again in the water, sending up huge splashes. The car speeds through the air, the wind whistling past your cheeks, and your raincoat bubbles up in big bubbles. The wind keeps pouring in, while you hum a joyful tune, completely focused on enjoying yourself. After all, the water roller coaster is truly thrilling. Although it's not exactly to throw people off, just experiencing the feeling is fine.
Only when the pace slows down do you have the energy to pay attention to the puppet sitting beside you, which still keeps its eyes closed.
For some reason, you feel a bit guilty: "...... How do you feel? ”
"[Extremely][Super][Absolutely][Absolutely Terrible]!"
Well, you heard Spamton loudly criticizing the project with a bunch of unknown recordings.
You cleared your throat twice, then led him down from your seat: "Then let's switch to a different activity later, no roller coaster." ”
No way, you still want to ride a roller coaster.
Tbc.
But since you still want to keep your promise for now, you really didn't go to the roller coaster. Instead, you turned and headed to another water ride. After all, you're already wearing a raincoat, so it's a waste not to come! If you put it on and take it off, you'll have to buy it again later—what a waste that!
But before that, you mischievously first pulled off the raincoat off the little puppet, then pretended nothing had happened and slowed your pace forward.
Because there are several facilities ahead, who knows which one you're going to? As long as you don't say anything, no one will guess.
At least Spamton had no idea. He just watched you walk forward, clearly unsure of the destination, yet still clearly focused. After a few seconds of pause, you saw him stop, bend down slightly, and grab the puppet's hand, ready to move forward.
It just didn't pull for a moment, and you heard the puppet's voice.
"[Guess]? You're planning a [Haunted House Project]?" ”
You and he stared at each other for a while, looked ahead, reacted for a moment, and suddenly realized—well, there really is a haunted house not far ahead, but before that, you really wanted to see the puppet soaking in water.
Although soaking wood in water must be heavy, and you don't know when it will dry, and what if it affects your travel plans...... You start thinking about this issue at an inappropriate time.
"Ah, no, no, no, the haunted house is the next destination. We're heading somewhere else first." You shook your fingers.
"By the way, if you get soaked in water, can you still move normally?" Then you rubbed your chin and seriously asked the question.
You see the puppet in front of you stiffly spinning, spinning around and glancing back at the water amusement rides over there. Honestly, it's childish, and you know that—after all, it's just a place where fountains constantly gushing out of the floor where people play water gun games!
You shyly cleared your throat, but you didn't feel guilty at all.
"I don't think the project is desirable."
Naturally, you hear the puppet's dry voice.
So you once again show that pitiful expression—at this point, just act cute! Of course, only those who fall for this trick are useful; if not, you won't be cute! You even squat down and stared intently at the puppet in front of you.
"But I think that should be a lot of fun. Look, I'm still wearing my raincoat. I really want to go play for a bit." You even made a gesture with your hands pressed together. Of course, only you know how much of it was truly pleading.
"But, my [raincoat], you [committed] [discarding]!" Spamton was flushed again, and you felt like he was about to jump up.
You coughed twice, slightly looked away, and still sounded justified: "Then I thought that raincoat was too long for you, didn't I? Look, it's so inconvenient for you to wear!" ”
You just found a reason for yourself and gave yourself a thumbs up—this reason is truly wonderful.
In short, after much persuasion, you managed to pull Spamton over and got a heavy, dripping puppet.
At this moment, you took off your raincoat too, rubbed your chin again, squatted down to look him up, and suddenly suggested, "How about taking a roller coaster? Maybe you can get a feel for the dry shakeoff, or maybe you'll be dry when you get down." ”
“…… I [don't agree], but there's a [possibility] of a 'shake-off project.' "You feel like the eyes behind your glasses are glaring at you.
Well, you might be a little disappointed, but you keep insisting: "Wow, let's just give it a try. Maybe it really works!" As you spoke, you pointed to the roller coaster not far away, which was bursting with laughter and screams.
"This is every thirty seconds, just thirty seconds to experience the feeling of shaking dry!"
After all, you really think this super-fast roller coaster is super fun.
This time, you rested your chin on both hands, putting on that look of anticipation as you looked at Spamton.
You see the small eyes under your glasses close: "...... I, [agree]. ”
"Yay!" You cheered, tugging at the puppet—no, you really can't pull it anymore, it's still too heavy after sucking water, so you awkwardly let go and pretended nothing was wrong, whistling as you walked aside nearby.
After all...... Hmm, it seems he's walking around normally without any problems, so just pretend nothing happened!
Soon, it was your turn for the roller coaster. Maybe because it was indeed a bit late, there weren't many people in line. It felt like most people had gone to the Ferris wheel, since the line there was really long! It's the kind of thing that makes you decide to leave the top left corner of the current amusement park map just by looking at it. Why not try a different time or a different place to experience it?
Same as always, you fastened the seatbelt on Spamton, then grabbed the handrail in front, and started screaming wildly as the roller coaster started—at the same time, you did feel some splashes splashing on you. As for the direction? It was the Spamton next door. Think about it, there's definitely a chance of getting drunk.
But after getting off the train, looking at the half-dried puppet, you feel a bit guilty and don't say whether you want to ride the roller coaster again, maybe this time you'll really be done with.
"We're almost [arriving] [closing time]. Would you like to [experience] the [Ferris wheel] ride?" Just as you were still wondering what to do next, you heard Spamton's suggestion for the first time since entering the amusement park.
To be honest, when you saw so many people over there, you felt a bit intimidated, but since this was the little puppet's first proposal, you agreed.
So you say, "Alright, then let's go!" ”
Anyway, you're not that hungry yet...... Although I just had a wild round.
At least you can now pull the Spamton and run, so you squeeze into the line of the Ferris wheel, aimlessly waiting. The line moves forward slowly, and just as you start to feel drowsy, you see a marshmallow stall by the roadside ahead. The bored people waiting in line have all bought a marshmallow to eat.
So you bought two too: one pink, probably strawberry flavor, and the other you guessed mango...... Anyway, it was yellow, so you handed the yellow one to Spamton, then looked at him with satisfaction as his face was completely covered by marshmallows.
"Anyway, it's sweet. Let's just treat it as a way to stave off hunger before dinner." You casually made up an excuse, took a bite of the marshmallow while chewing, and said, well, it was indeed a bit sweet—so sweet it was cloying.
Out of the corner of your eye, you see the little puppet fiercely battling with Marshmallow, and you can't help but laugh.
"Or you can give me that one. I don't mind eating two." You sincerely suggested, since there aren't many marshmallows. They look fluffy, and after a couple of bites, they're gone. By the time you watch the yellow marshmallow finally get bitten off, you've already regretfully finished eating the one in your hand and can only throw it in the trash as trash.
"No, [Firmly veto], I can [challenge alone]."
Although you can't see his face, you guess the puppet is blushing again, okay, okay, you respect his thoughts, so you just shrug.
"Then enjoy it at your leisure." You say.
By the time it was your turn, Spamton's cotton candy still hadn't been finished—it looked like it was about halfway gnawed. At least you could see his eyes clearly.
You thoughtfully hold the marshmallow for him, resting your chin on your hand as Spamton slowly climbs into the chair and sits down before handing him the marshmallow.
He sat right across from you, still struggling with that cotton candy, and then the Ferris wheel slowly started moving, rocking as the carriage slowly lifted. It was a bit boring, and it felt too plain. You simply propped your chin up and stared out the window, lost in thought.
As I watched, I let out a surprised sound: "Wow, I can't believe you can see fireworks at this hour!" ”
Yes, it's already nighttime, and of course there are fireworks blooming in the sky. Overall, you'll be quite happy, since the fireworks are beautiful and colorful. Although you won't hear the sound of fireworks popping inside the carriage, quietly enjoying the scenery is a wonderful experience.
As you watch, the carriage is about to reach the top before you know it. At that moment, you suddenly hear Spamton's voice: "...... [Request]?" ”
You tilt your head and turn your face, but you don't hear clearly; you only notice the puppet's face flickering in the light.
So you simply changed seats and sat next to him: "Hmm?" What are you talking about? ”
Only then did you realize he had finished the marshmallow. It seemed the Ferris wheel was too slow, but slow has its advantages—at least you have the mood to enjoy the scenery outside, and that feeling of being above is really great.
"Do another [repeat], a [kiss] and a [request] at the top of the [Ferris wheel]?"
You feel the eyes beneath your glasses staring at you intently.
You scratched your cheek, searched your mind for related information, and suddenly realized—so this was the whole thing!
"Oh, I see, in that case...... Well, of course no problem. "You shrugged.
So when you reach the top of the Ferris wheel, you smack the puppet on the forehead.
Honestly, so this is what it feels like to kiss wood? This is your first time experiencing it; next time try a tree...... Uh, forget it, the smell of tree bark is unimaginable.
Then you happily sit back across from you, humming a tune and looking out the window again, ignoring Spamton's incredulous, even condemning gaze.
"Then let's go have dinner once the Ferris wheel stops! I'm hungry anyway...... Well, listen to me, I'm going to eat sushi! "You start counting on your fingers.
"And then, let's call today's date a happy ending." You happily put your hands together.
Spamton didn't say anything, and you didn't mind; actually, you were a bit too afraid to look. Well, anyway, you admit you did it on purpose.
…… So, let this little puppet burn for a while—it's just a red warmth, no big deal!
"[Yes], I can definitely [accept] your [suggestion]." You only heard his voice when the Ferris wheel was about to stop.
In fact, even if he doesn't answer you, you won't care; you'll just happily go to the sushi restaurant and pull Spamton along.
Today, you have to drag him along with you, or who'll compensate you for emotional damages?! You were scammed by an online dating scam and lost a (nonexistent) boyfriend, and as for him, he just needs to waste more time on it!
So you took a cab to the sushi restaurant and had Spamton sit across from you. Luckily, the place had a low table paired with tatami, so you sat cross-legged across from you...... Well, kneeling is really tiring!
And you can finally see the little puppet sticking its head out of the table normally. Somehow, you suddenly feel a bit gratified, like wiping away tears and saying, 'Wow, one day will finally come.'
You held back, you just ordered a bunch of sushi according to your own preferences, and then handed the menu to Spamton.
Soon, the waiter cleared the menu. Not knowing when the food would arrive, you simply bent down and slumped over the table in a very unimpressive manner.
Honestly, after playing all afternoon, you're really sleepy now. You just feel like you're sleepy...... No, at least go back to sleep after dinner! And if you fall asleep here, no one will be able to send you back. You don't want to wake up and find yourself in a pile of garbage with a dirty little puppet beside you.
Since that's the case, close your eyes and rest for a while. After all, if you just let your mind wander for a while, you can't fall asleep, so you close your eyes.
But after just a short while, you hear Spamton's voice.
"So, after dinner, should we implement a 'go to our own homes' [strategy]?"
You opened your eyes and tilted your head to look at the little puppet in front of you, which for some reason seemed a bit nervous. After all, it was sitting with his hands pressed together on the table, gripping it tightly.
From this angle, you happen to meet his gaze.
You thought for a moment and casually said, "Oh right, oh!" I almost forgot...... Your memory isn't very good, hmm, since today counts as a date, the next part should be ...... Living together? ”
You think seriously about this issue.
"Then you can stay at my place." You clenched your fist, clapped your palms, sat up straight, and suddenly understood.
After all, you don't want to live in a garbage dump!
The puppet's face turned bright red again, and it seemed to cough a few times. By the way, can puppets catch a cold too? You apologized for playing with water at the wrong time.
"We're living together, in a relationship?! I don't think we [haven't] reached an agreement." ”
Hey, didn't you make it clear? You're lost in thought.
"Didn't I say before that I'd compensate you? Of course, I'm going to compensate for a romantic relationship. I think we reached an agreement back then." You explained this very seriously, and you really think so.
Then you prop your chin with both hands, puff out your cheeks, and watch as a few wisps of smoke vividly rise from the puppet's head.
Tbc.
You enjoy your sushi happily, ignoring the little puppet that suddenly falls silent across from you, and simply take a cab home.
Speaking of which, your home doesn't have much to offer; everything is arranged in the simplest style because you're too lazy to tidy up—having to clean the room every day is already exhausting! You definitely don't want to spend time tidying up other things.
You just have a few books on your bedroom desk, and a bunch of frozen food stuffed into the fridge...... And a drawer full of eggs.
Scratching your cheek, you notice that the fridge still has frozen lamb chops you didn't know when you bought them...... Ah, probably just a few months ago?
Anyway, as soon as you got home, you dragged your tired body to bed, then without looking back, waved at Spamton, who was still standing dazed at the door: "Ah...... Just find anywhere to sleep. If you have anything to say, we'll talk about it tomorrow......
Then you fall asleep. Come on, you're really tired. You didn't collapse, just your mind supporting you! You feel like today is a year's worth of exercise. Next time, don't do that......
Drifting with these thoughts, you drift off to sleep.
When you groggily open your eyes, you still feel your arm being shaken continuously, and you find it annoying, so you take a look.
Oh, so it's Spamton! You checked your phone again—it's only nine in the morning! Then let's keep sleeping...... By the way, I really did go to bed very early last night.
You yawned, then simply turned over, pulled Spamton up and held her in your arms, then turned to lie on your side, smacking your lips and peacefully falling asleep again, even bumping your chin against the puppet's head.
…… Honestly, hugging wood while sleeping feels strange, but it's not a big deal. As long as you don't fall asleep and dream of grinding your teeth with wood, that's enough......
What if you get hungry and dream of some delicious food......
Thinking this, you really did dream of a big meal—wow, a super delicious cake studded with blueberries, and matcha-flavored cookies...... No, no, no, skip the desserts—there's nothing but shiny delicacies over there! Crispy roasted suckling pig, fried steak still sizzling with butter, finely plated lamb chops sprinkled with fennel, and charcoal-grilled chicken legs skewered with salt and pepper......
You feel so eager that your mouth is about to water, and you can faintly hear some cursing sounds, but you selectively ignore them. You just run over excitedly and then bite into the chicken leg—
Good, you were woken up by the kowtow. Now you're fully awake. You look at the puppet below whose saliva and teeth marks still remain, and awkwardly clear your throat: "I didn't mean to, I'm just dreaming!" ”
As you spoke, you became even more confident—after all, you really were just dreaming!
By the way, you checked the time—it was almost eleven o'clock. No wonder you were so hungry...... After all, you'd slept for about twelve hours, and you pushed yourself up from the bed to get up.
"I [believe] your explanation, but this has to be [compensation for emotional distress]."
You watched spamyon jump off the bed first and reach out a hand toward you. Although smoke was rising from their face again, you guessed it was probably from anger... haha, after all, you had bitten them like a chicken drumstick.
You cleared your throat twice, clearly feeling a bit guilty: "Alright, alright, I know! I'll make it up to you—uh, how about I treat you to a little cake?" You seriously made a gesture of putting your hands together in a gesture of begging, tilted your head slightly, and blinked one eye in a wink gesture.
He thought for a moment, then reached out and made a five.
You immediately understood and quickly nodded, "Alright, alright, I'll treat you to five small cakes." ”
“…… It is five [pauses]. "Spamton modified the measurement term.
"Five meals it is, take care of me." You patted your chest, super confident, since this money isn't much to you anyway.
"But in that case, you should ...... Uh, by the way, how much does a puppet actually hold? "You start chirping quietly.
"[Don't] worry about my [capacity] [not enough]! That far exceeds your [imagination]!" "The puppet looks like it's about to jump up again.
You think about what happened yesterday. Makes sense, your small body can't believe you can eat so much. Actually, you used to think puppets didn't need to eat......
"Ahem, alright, I'll go cook first...... You coughed twice. Although you weren't confident about your cooking skills, you still cared about your pride! You can't just be clueless, right? That would be too embarrassing......
In reality, you really don't know anything—even though you took out two steaks, carefully cracked an egg, carefully took out a few servings of butter, and even studied the tutorial several times.
But you can't do it. A few minutes later, you see the eggshell mixed with the egg white, the broken yolk, and the poor steak you scooped out of the pan and left on the counter because of the burns. Holding your hands swollen and red from oil splashes, you leave the kitchen.
At least rinse your burned hand with cold water first......
You looked at Spamton, who was sitting on the sofa, his legs barely touching the floor, awkwardly waving his legs in midair. He coughed awkwardly twice, trying to save face: "I just calculated that today isn't suitable for cooking. Let's go find somewhere to eat!" ”
“…… By the way, have you been awake for a long time?" You belatedly realized you hadn't actually had breakfast either, feeling a bit guilty. You usually skip breakfast and eat lunch directly.

“…… I want to use my [love] to make a [trade] and get your [love]." Spamton said.
You paused, searched through your mind, and found something you'd said some time ago—well, that night you did say that liking and loving are different to you, and what you have now is just liking.

You never really understood this, only vaguely sensing that there should be a difference between the two. Otherwise, you would love too many people!
"To me, liking someone probably just means it's fun, just because I find it fun and brings me joy. I don't care what the other person thinks; I'm just considering my own feelings. Of course, I'm even willing to do something, anyway—well, that's why I wanted to drag you out to play before." You coughed twice as you spoke.
After all, you're just afraid of loneliness.
"Besides, what you were really thinking at the time wasn't really important to me. This kind of liking is more innocent than for a person, just treating something that can be enjoyed for fun." Lowering your gaze, you murmured to yourself. Fortunately, Spamton didn't speak at that moment, probably just listening carefully to your words.

Maybe it's a feeling that comes from the heart, takes on responsibility, and gives rise to infinite courage for it? ”
You shook your head and finished reading this passage, then looked at Spamton. You blinked and asked seriously, "So, which one do you want?" ”

By the end, you start to feel uncertain, since you don't know if this counts as a valid deal, and you might even feel a bit guilty.
But you only saw Spamton extend his right hand, then rest it on yours, and hear his voice: "...... [Deal]." ”
"Oh!" Alright, it's settled then. But let's discuss this later. For now, let's have some barbecue! "You happily withdrew your hand, then clapped, and placed the little puppet on your lap. After all, you two are already in this relationship...... Uh, anyway, let's just give up on those etiquette rules; it's not that important.

Maybe they're still urging you to give up early and switch to another one, but think about it—you probably never will. A pretty boy is just a pretty boy! Worst case, I'll do his makeup next time I go out!
You happily made the decision and carried the Spamton out the door.
"So, can you [place] me on the ground?" Staying in your arms with no touch to the ground made him afraid to struggle, so he had no choice but to ask for your opinion.
You thought for a moment, then put him down on the ground: "Alright, anyway, we'll just walk slowly for a while, and we'll be home soon." ”
By the way, you held Spamton's outstretched hand, and this time he actually reached out his hand on his own.
Although you may not be entirely sure what these subtle changes mean...... But in any case, it's just getting better little by little!

Although you used to sleep hugging a puppet, you still do it now. The only difference is that now you give Spamton's head a kiss every day while you sleep.
This has become a habit, and if one day you can't do this, you might feel quite disappointed—well, maybe you shouldn't even make that kind of thought.

The eggs have grown mold before and haven't been thrown away, and when some things need to be replaced at home, you don't bother buying them and just go through the motions. Everything at home is a mess.
Then you just squatted there silently, not daring to say a word, watching Spamton tiptoe and throw away all your hairy eggs, then let you carry him to buy groceries—well, you obediently listened.
He can even cook! Even though you still need to hold it, and the dish doesn't look very good, it actually tastes quite good—in short, much better than you. You eat the bowl of pasta in front of you, tears in your eyes. Yes, you can only cook noodles obediently.
But this kind of life has settled down, even more peaceful than before. You've gradually gotten used to the feeling of letting others share most of the burden—you'll be the one to pay, and as for other goals, we'll deal with them later.
On this day, you sat in the cake shop. After all, Spamton had promised to owe you five cakes, even though what he actually used was still your money—you were just giving him money.
You poke the matcha cake in front of you with your fork, gently lift your eyes to look at the little puppet sitting across from you, and tilt your head slightly.

For once, you felt a bit nervous, just lowered your head and unconsciously poked the cake with your fork, then you saw Spamton's shadow floating on the table nodding.
So you smile happily, then call the waiter to serve Spamton a matcha cake.
"Okay, one for each of us."

You stared at Spamton for a while, until her body stiffened, and you really thought you'd said something wrong. Then you slowly nodded, your tone tinged with hesitation and disbelief.
"Alright...... I understand. ”
He breathed a sigh of relief and pointed to a small door behind the kitchen: "That door leads to 'Ruins Beautiful.' You can go there for 'relaxation and entertainment.'" ”
You tilted your head, not quite understanding: "What is ruin beauty?" "Although you can mostly guess based on the actual objects and context, you really don't understand this."
Spamton coughed dryly twice, his voice growing quieter: "...... Garden. ”
You blink, about to say something more, but Spamton just pulls you in another direction, and you enter a spacious room.
"This is a [leisure and entertainment facility]. [Miss] can enjoy [your free time]." He explained that you noticed the living room had a long sofa, a coffee table, and a bookshelf. Other than that, there was nothing else to do. Spamton then pulled you out. It was a small corridor with a spiral staircase leading to the second floor. He held your hand and led you up. The second floor, besides the large bathroom he had just mentioned, was also quite simple. There were two rooms of moderate size, except one had a tightly locked door.
Spamton glanced lightly at the room, then pulled you into a relatively large room, which had a large double bed. Spamton opened his arms and introduced you: "This is our shared residence. This house has only a [single residence], so the lady wants to share some rest time with me." ”
For once, you felt a bit stuck. You blinked at the big bed in the room, imagining what might happen the day after tomorrow, and blushed belatedly.

title: Contract Lover 2 (sptx you)
content:
You instinctively waved your hand, because the other hand was holding Spamton's hand—so you only waved one hand, even though you were somewhat lacking in common sense, you knew it was wrong.
“…… Living together is fine, but we shouldn't sleep in the same bed, right?" Your voice was still a bit stammering, and there was a burning sensation on your face...... In short, your heartbeat seemed to quicken, but you didn't understand why. All you knew was that this feeling was terrible, very bad, so bad that you wanted to escape.
So you instinctively take two steps back and try to let go of Spamton's hand: "I...... I'll just sleep on the floor. I don't mind where I sleep, or the sofa downstairs is fine......
But Spamton interrupted you, gripping your hand tightly to keep you from retreating. He just kept smiling: "Ah...... But, Miss, according to the way love works, we should share the same bed. ”
Your eyes widened slightly. Indeed...... If you had needed this according to your initial terms of the deal, and he also provided you with a method, then ......
You no longer hesitate, just took his hand back and said softly, "Ah...... I understand, then...... I, I will share a bed with you. ”
As you spoke, you scratched your cheek, feeling for some reason it only felt hotter and hotter. Maybe it was just your imagination? Spamton looked at your flushed face, just smiled and said nothing.
"Then ......" He was about to say something more, but you suddenly stopped in front of him as if remembering something.
"Well, that's right...... Although I know what you want is important, it's not good to just eat and drink freely at your house all the time. I'll give you money. "You thought about it. Although the operation is complicated, it's true that currency in the Light World can be exchanged for Dark Coins, and you'll probably be living in the Dark World for a long time, so exchanging a bit more isn't a problem.
Spamton opened his mouth, wanting to reject your proposal. After all, he doesn't need your money. He just needs you to step in occasionally. With the Light Founder's hype, he can make several times over.
But you ignored his hesitant words and continued on your own: "And then...... So, do you need me to do anything else? Because if you calculate it this way, I'm your lover now, so I have to help you too...... Right? "You're not sure, so your tone ended with a hint of doubt. You've never been in love, just know some knowledge from books, and know that both parties in a relationship should give to each other. But come to think of it, you did only say you wanted to learn about love, never what kind of relationship you would have with Spamton.
But now, Spamton just smiles and silently watches you.
You cough twice, your voice growing weaker with a hint of uncertainty: "We're ...... now Are you lovers? ”
Then Spamton nodded seriously: "Yes, because of the [Love Transaction], we are now in a [lovers] relationship." ”
You quietly responded with an 'oh,' feeling a fleeting melancholy in your heart for some reason. But you quickly pulled yourself together and eagerly asked, "Is there anything else I can do for you?" After all, as lovers, doing something for you is something I should do quickly......" Before he could finish, Spamton extended his index finger to cover your mouth.
He tilted his head slightly and smiled, saying, "Ah...... I only need to attend the ceremony; I don't need to pay extra. ”
You had your mouth covered, so you could only blink and look at him. Spamton coughed dryly too, belatedly realizing how soft the lips under his fingers were, so he quickly withdrew his hand.
"And [housework: from Baidu Encyclopedia], I'll take care of everything, like [kitchen operation services] and [daily household management services]...... What you need to do is [enjoy life]. "He's explaining to you very seriously, and you look at this guy, who is a bit shorter than you, listening in surprise. You really hadn't thought about housework, but now that he's brought it up, you just remember.
"No need, I can leave these things to me. I'm used to it...... How could I trouble you? "You waved your hand again. But Spamton just held your hand and walked down the stairs.
"I think, Miss Y/N, what you need is [enjoying love], [enjoying life]—and since I have made a deal with you, the [heart-shaped item] is a valuable item, so you don't need to make any more [redundant steps]." He spoke softly, slowly explaining everything to you. Although he didn't need the heart-shaped object for now, he had a feeling he might use it someday—maybe someday in the future.
You pressed your lips together, suddenly feeling uneasy. You weren't used to this kind of life. After all, in the past, what you truly had—was only obtained through genuine effort. The clothes you wore, your school tuition, your school supplies—all were earned by doing housework at home and by your parents. And now, it's just a transaction, yet another person is willing to give so much. What is it all for?
…… Or maybe that deal really does mean a lot to him, you think. And that unrealistic, somewhat light, even floating feeling like floating on clouds kept going until Spamton pulled you into the car and stopped at the entrance of a store. He politely held your hand and let you get out, then led you into the store.
"You should be missing [personal items]?" Please [spend as much as you like]." He nodded slightly at you, then pointed to the clothes in the store cabinet.
You hesitated, pursing your lips, your toes spinning on the ground.
"I...... Can I pick whatever I want? "You asked, not sure—except for the necessary change of clothes, there weren't many extra clothes at home. You could only go to school wearing faded clothes. Even though you didn't think it was a big deal, inevitably some eyes that were hard to ignore were directed at you.
"Of course, feel free to choose your hobbies." He said.
Even though you still find his way of speaking a bit obscure and hard to understand, after half understanding it, you finally get what he means. He gently squeezes your hand, and you take a deep breath before heading straight into the shop. The colorful look dazzles you, but for you, as long as the clothes are comfortable, that's enough. Many of the clothes you don't need are really needed. So, based on the current weather, you pick out two sets of white shirts and black sweatpants, plus a jacket—these are enough for you to change into. Turning the jacket inside and out will last another month, and it'll be about time to change clothes.
Spamton stood at the counter, watching you. The owner of this shop was a yellow Addison, if you didn't see it wrong...... He seemed to have just hidden something inside? But you had no interest in pursuing it. You just walked over to the counter with those five pieces of clothing and cautiously glanced at Spamton: "...... I've picked out. ”
Spamton flipped through the five pieces of clothing you brought, then fell silent. You swallowed hard, almost thinking Spamton thought you had chosen too much. Just as you were about to ask to put two more pieces back, you heard Spamton's somewhat puzzled voice: "Just bought [daily necessities]?" "[Miss]'s [Aesthetic Concepts] need to be updated." ”
You hesitated and blinked, and the few pieces of clothing in your hand were placed on the counter. Then Spamton pulled you aside and started sweeping through each shelf one by one. He asked about your size, then held up the clothes matching the size and gestured toward you. At first, it was just a regular shirt and pants, just a matter of patterns and patterns.
"I...... I don't need that many clothes in daily life...... You try to stop Spamton, but he just waves his hand casually: "There's [extra space: walk-in closet] at home. I'm not just picking out for you, but also my personal [picking preferences]. ”
As soon as you say that, you shut up, but Spamton keeps holding the clothes and gesturing at you. No matter how you look at them, these clothes must have been chosen for you, right? White, blue, and pink shirts; green, blue, yellow long-sleeved shirts; and some pink, white, and beige short knit sweaters. He just picked out each one and tossed them toward the cash register. In no time, the clothes piled up into a small mountain.
And from start to finish, you're just a clothes hanger. Spamton gestures the clothes around you, thinks it's about right, and then buys them with a wave of his hand. He shows you through everyday clothes and finally stops at the front of a series of Lolita clothes. These dresses are generally quite expensive, the kind you wouldn't even dare to look at. In fact, you hardly ever wore a dress in the world of light—because it's extremely inconvenient, inconvenient for your movements, for housework, or for working outside.
And you don't dare to dress too pretty...... After all, your parents have told you about many girls being harmed by bad people because they dressed too revealingly and too pretty. You don't dare to gamble on the possibility that you won't encounter danger.
But Spamton casually took a dark green dress from the shelf and gestured on you: "Hmm...... This outfit is just what I want." As he spoke, he tossed the dress to the cashier, about to get another set, but after hesitating for a long time, you finally mustered the courage to speak: "Mr. Spamton, you don't need to buy me a dress or anything...... I probably wouldn't wear it either. ”
The previous clothes were still suitable for everyday wear, and you'll wear them to some extent.
"No need to add 'Sir'...... Also, these [incredibly beautiful dresses] I think suits you very well. "He didn't look up at you, just casually rejected what you had just said.
"But...... You wanted to say more, but he interrupted you again.
He smiled warmly: "We...... Now we're lovers. So...... I think I need "pleasing to the eye," and I also need you to be "joyful." ”
