title: Contract Lover 3 (sptx you)
content:
It feels like this story is always talking in my sleep.
——
You swallowed that sentence back, your eyes showing a hint of confusion, while Spamton was still gesturing her little dress toward you, casually tossing it toward the cashier. You always felt like you couldn't win an argument with him, but if you did it as he said, then the opposite—
You muster up your courage before you speak: "I, then, can I pick out clothes I think look good for Mr. Spamton?" "Since you can't stop him, you have no choice but to buy some instead."
Spamton was taken aback. Indeed, what you said was true. He couldn't deny you—but copying the rules doesn't suit your current relationship. The books he once read in his mind can't offer any experience at this moment. He can only ask himself: do you really want ...... Or does he want to get these? Does he want to feel joy? Does he want you to be happy because of it?
The answer is yes. When choosing clothes for you, what they see most is the shock and panic on your face. You probably haven't fully adapted to this identity, or rather, you're adjusting to the current situation.
So he lifted the corners of his mouth and smiled, "Of course, the [plan's approval and feasibility]—I'm really looking forward to your choice." ”
He took a quick look at the shop...... They had both men's and women's clothing. He thought, 'Let's just check out together later.'
Your eyes lit up as you pulled out a wallet: "Great, then I'll use my own money to buy clothes for Mr. Spamton." You were delighted, probably because this way, you wouldn't feel that inexplicable guilt rising inside you.
Spamton's eyes widened instinctively: "First of all, you don't need to call me 'Mr.' And you shouldn't—"
You know what he's about to say, so you interrupt him. You don't want to keep pushing and pushing him around: "No, these are what I wanted to give you, so I should be the one paying for them." You've adjusted your mindset, even though it's still a reciprocal ...... But this is probably the first time you've truly given a gift, and the first time you've received a return gift.
Spamton quietly fell silent. If it were a hand-to-hand gift, he had no intention of refusing. After all, it's normal to give things to each other in a relationship, right?
You didn't hear Spamton's voice anymore, so you happily walked over to the men's section next door. You thought, Spamton's build should be about your size, so you picked up the number, grabbed a black suit, and tried it out on him.
I have to say, you were quite spirited—you happily grabbed another white suit, and Spamton could only stretch out his arm to act as a hanger, letting you pick and choose. Then, you liked the vintage European outfit next to you, one with a cape and a gemstone decoration slanting downward on the chest. Honestly, looking at the sign, you gasped—so expensive—but this set was just too good, and it came with matching red boots, so you couldn't resist letting Spamton try it on.
He did as told, spinning around in front of you, his cloak fluttering in the air, and you clapped happily and smiled sincerely: "This outfit looks amazing! Can you ...... wear this at home every day?" You asked cautiously.
Spamton turned to look at you: "If it's your [Offer Notice], then [Agreement Permit]." ”
"Not only that...... But based on your [preferred opinions]. ”
His words were a bit abrupt, you didn't quite understand, but you still knew that Spamton promised you could wear this at home every day. As for that last sentence...... Maybe he wanted you to do it according to your own preferences?
You waved your hand and picked up another set. This time, there was no cloak, but it was decorated with various metallic accents, and the chest was still wide open, with only ruffles as decoration. To be honest, you thought this outfit was too avant-garde and too bold, but the red and black color scheme was ...... You also really thought this outfit looked great. In the end, you carefully took off the outfit, looked at Spamton, and didn't even dare to look up at him, just cautiously asked, "Hmm...... So, is this outfit okay? ”
Spamton patted your head, and you instinctively shrank your neck. After all, you weren't used to being touched by others, while Spamton simply cupped your face with both hands, making you look straight into his eyes.
He said softly, "Of course you can. What you need is to first consider your own [opinions and insights], then others' [thoughts and content]. ”
You nodded half-understandingly. Honestly, you really hadn't really thought about yourself, since your top priority was always the opinions of those around you...... It seemed those emotions were already overwhelming you.
But in the end, Spamton agreed, so you happily held the outfit and gestured to Spamton. Since it was a bit revealing, you felt embarrassed to let Spamton wear it for you right now. But after confirming the size was right, you awkwardly placed it on the checkout counter, piling it under the suit you had earlier.
Yellow looked at today's huge deal, grinning so hard he couldn't close his mouth, and naturally wouldn't disturb your fun—though you'd probably blush and deny it.
You fiddled with your fingers, glanced at Spamton, then at the unremarkable, almost uniform men's clothing beside you, finally swallowed hard and whispered, "Since ...... If my opinion comes first, I think the rest of the clothes don't look very good. Mr. Spamton, can I pick out a few dresses for you? ”
The more you spoke, the brighter your eyes became, looking at Spamton with anticipation, making him feel a bit embarrassed. To be honest, your gaze was truly sincere. Although he was a bit embarrassed and annoyed when he heard the skirt, but—strangely, he didn't want to refuse your request. He didn't know what was going on; maybe it was the racing "heart" in his chest urging him to agree.
So he just smiled awkwardly: "Of course you can. Also, don't call me 'Sir' anymore." ”
"Alright, Spamton...... spamton。 "You still tried hard to change your name, then excitedly held up a sky-blue dress decorated with white lace and bows and gestured toward Spamton.
This dress really suits Spamton, so you bought it in high spirits and asked in a low voice again, "...... Um, can Spamton wear a dress at home to show me?" "Unconsciously, you've changed your tune and called that building you just saw today 'home.' You have to admit, at least you've relaxed a lot, and the home you used to live in made it almost impossible for you to relax. You vaguely understood something—at least, home is a place where people can relax, at least someone should be there...... They're waiting for you to come back.
Spamton, on the other hand, didn't know what you were thinking. He just noticed you holding that dress and starting to zone out, then patted your head and lowered his voice: "Of course, [no problem], but...... Only [roaming around the house] is allowed. "No matter what, he's a well-known figure in the cyber world. If someone recognizes him while wearing a skirt, what does that count as!
…… Although thinking about it carefully, it does seem quite challenging, but forget it, better not to overthink it.
You just stood there blankly and nodded, counting your current Dark Coins. You decided to buy these clothes first, so you walked toward the checkout counter to pay. Spamton followed behind you, and you moved even faster, buying the clothes Spamton had just picked out for you as well.
Spamton was still a step too slow, glaring hatefully at the smiling yellow, then put on a somewhat hurt expression and looked at you: "These clothes are my [voluntary gifts], so I should be the one to [pay for them]." ”
You coughed lightly twice and quietly explained, "But these clothes were all bought for me. I don't want you to spend so much money......
Before he could finish, Spamton poked your head with his index finger, his tone tinged with amusement and a hint of frustration: "Those are my [voluntary gifts], my [beautiful gifts] to you. You don't need to feel [guilty]. ”
You held your forehead. Although it didn't hurt much, you still pursed your lips and cautiously glanced at Spamton: "But that's too much...... "You just can't wear them all......
Before you could finish, Spamton interrupted you irritably: "Alright, since our [sizes] are about the same, why don't you just treat the [extra clothes] as my [personal items]?" "As he spoke, he picked up the bag Yellow handed over and walked out of the shop first, with you following closely behind.
For some reason, you feel that although Spamton looks smiling, he's definitely angry. After all, not only did he not say a word to you all the way, he was walking so fast that you almost couldn't keep up with his pace. It was only then, as if a pang of conscience, that he slowed down slightly and held your hand with his empty hand.
"[I'm very sorry.] Just now, [ignore: from Baidu Baike] made you feel about it...... You can [reprimand me for breaking the contract.] "As he spoke, he slightly lowered his head toward you.
And you stared at him blankly, tilting your head slightly, confused: "Why should I blame you?" "If I ignore you out of anger...... That's perfectly normal, right?
You will just feel a little, a little unhappy, that's all.
Spamton was momentarily taken aback by you, and you just winked innocently at him. In the end, he just sighed helplessly: "What I mean is, focus on your own [emotional experience], and prioritize [self-perception]." He even emphasized those words so you could understand what he was really focusing on.
You nodded thoughtfully, then shook your head and smiled: "I know why you're angry, and I know I was the one who didn't do it well...... So, I should be the one apologizing to you. I'm sorry...... I'm still a bit acting according to my own ideas...... The more you spoke, the quieter your voice became, the more anxious you became, your body instinctively shrinking back, like—you remembered that day, when you took it upon yourself to prepare a birthday present for your father, only to be scolded and slapped in the face in return.
But before you can fully recall that day, your memory is interrupted by Spamton: "No, that wasn't [self-assertion], it was just your [personalized] idea. No one has a reason to [blame or blame] you." ”
Only then did you realize, probably...... You even mentioned that you took it upon yourself to prepare a gift.
"I am very sorry for not considering [emotional experience], and your so-called [self-opinion] and [self-perception] are all [ought to exist]; no one has any reason to [interfere with the options]."
You dazed and let out an 'oh', then was led forward by Spamton. For some reason, you suddenly felt like crying—for some reason, the emptiness in your chest was filled with a feeling that seemed like grievance, or sadness.
So tears slowly streamed down your cheeks, and you silently shed tears.

title: Contract Lover 4 (sptx you)
content:
Spamton naturally saw the tears streaming down your cheeks. He had planned to pretend not to see and that he should have cried for a while before it would end—but the silent crying continued, and he didn't quite understand. There was no sound, so why could you cry for so long?
In the end, he sighed, turned around, and gently wiped the tears running down your cheeks. His fingers brushed over your cheeks, and you felt a bit cold, even though you hadn't made a sound...... You didn't know when he saw you, so you quickly wiped your tears back and put on a smile again. But to Spamton, that smile seemed a bit forced. He looked at you carefully two or three times, then nodded and shook his head.
"If the crying plan passes, then you should cry out loud." He said.
You don't quite understand what he means, just shake your head: "No, no need...... Right now, I don't really feel like crying. ”
This sentence is serious. When someone is watching you, you really can't cry—you always feel embarrassed.
Spamton stared at you for a moment, said nothing more, just turned around, took your hand, and walked to the side of the red car, then put all the clothes he had just bought into the trunk.
You were daydreaming until Spamton suddenly spoke and snapped you back to reality.
"[Seeking opinions], what do you want me to [wear and equip] first?"
You paused for a moment and replied, "Mm...... Just wear what you like." "You don't know what this has to do with you."
Spamton sighed and insisted, "I'm asking about [your views and preferences]. ”
However, he wasn't really sure what to do, but at this moment, he understood that maybe making you happy was actually quite simple.
So...... So, he just wants you to be happy, even though he doesn't know why you're crying, but it's true—no matter how you look at it, Spamton hopes you'll be happy. Even though he himself doesn't really understand why he has such expectations, maybe he just simply hopes his employer will be happy.
You hesitated, blinked twice, glanced carefully at Spamton, and confirmed he was speaking sincerely, asking for your opinion. Only then did you start to think it over.
"Ah...... Then let's go with that blue skirt! It should be more convenient to wear. "You gestured with your hand, and Spamton nodded, even though wearing a skirt or something like that...... He always felt a bit embarrassed, but to cheer you up, he decided to go ahead with it.
You got in the car. Spamton drove at full speed. Luckily, you didn't get carsick, and soon the car stopped at the villa entrance. Spamton got out, took out all the bags from the trunk, and then led you through the villa's main gate. The villa had two keys, and he gave you one as well. After entering, without his instructions, you didn't know what to do and just sat awkwardly on the sofa.
“…… No need to be so strict. [Constraint: from Baidu Encyclopedia], here is [Navigation: Your Home Address]. ”
Spamton said, holding your hand as we walked upstairs. Then he opened the empty wardrobe and tossed the bags filled with freshly bought clothes aside.
"Next, arrange as you wish." He nodded gently at you.
You feel a bit embarrassed—after all, this is Spamton's house, so you bring up something similar: "Maybe I'll give you a bit more Dark Coins?" ”
Spamton gently nudged you and shook his head: "No, the [heart-shaped object] is enough." ”
In fact, as long as you, the Citizen of Light, are here, you can bring him enough benefits.
You hesitated, but in the end picked up the purchasing group for self-study, hanging each item on the rack. Soon, the wardrobe was filled with dresses and the like. You glanced at the wardrobe, scratched your head, and suddenly blushed: "Exactly...... "Well, actually, I haven't bought any intimate clothes yet...... Your voice was soft, but enough for Spamton to hear clearly. He was stunned for a moment, then his face turned red as well.
Spamton cleared his throat twice: "Then should I take you to the [Lingerie Store] now?" ”
You nod slightly.
So not long after you got home, you went out again. This time, Spamton skillfully turned the streets of Cyber City and finally stopped in front of a women's lingerie store. Out of gentlemanly politeness, Spamton didn't get out of the car. You took a deep breath, got out, and walked into the shop. You have to admit, probably because the Dark People had so many varieties, and their lingerie came in all sorts of sizes.
You pick out the bra that fits your size best, then hurry out the door to pay—you don't want Spamton to wait too long. But when you reach the cashier, the shopkeeper, Blue Addison, tells you that the Dark People have already paid for you.
You paused, looking out the window. Spamton was opening the car door and hurriedly sitting back down, clearly as if he'd secretly paid you but didn't want you to find out, even though he wasn't hiding anything.
And when Blue saw you looking out the window, she just smiled and said, "Yes, that gentleman." ”
As he spoke, he handed you a bag filled with underwear.
“…… Thanks, I'll head out now." You nodded quickly and walked out, while Blue watched your back, then glanced at Spamton, who was waiting for you in the parked car. You have to admit, he was a bit curious, but unfortunately, the red car started up and drove off after you got in, giving Blue no chance to enjoy the excitement.
You sit in the back seat of the car, watching Spamton look at you in the rearview mirror. You take a deep breath and finally muster the courage to ask the question you've been thinking about but never getting answered.
“…… Why are you helping me pay?" "Even though you're basically staying at his place, you haven't given him a single cent. You're already feeling embarrassed......
"It's just ...... 'Reciprocity of Courtesy.'" He said this. Earlier, he hadn't seized the chance to pay, and Spamton still had some longing for it. Now, he finally paid it.
"But...... But! You don't need to pay me...... I'm already a bit embarrassed to live in your place...... You raised your voice, but spamton interrupted before you could finish.
"We are in a [romantic relationship], and the house is our [joint property], a [voluntary gift] belonging to me." He raised his voice, emphasizing this matter again.
“…… Because they're lovers, does that mean all these things are allowed?" You ask quietly, saying you don't have any personal views on the relationship between lovers.
Spamton just nodded and shook his head: "No, the 'decision-maker' in something lies in the 'mood indicator.' I hope you can make the decision before you [choose the decision-making power]...... Feel [joy and happiness]. The premise of a [relationship] is your sense of pleasure. "He tried hard to explain to you, but actually, he didn't quite understand. He was so emotional when he told you that he wasn't sure what words he was using—in short, it was probably a bit hard to understand.
But in reality, he just wants to tell you that no matter what, you should always consider your own emotions first.
You nodded half-understandingly, but then asked, "So...... For my sake, I hope you accept this money, or I'll feel guilty. Are you willing to accept it? ”
He probably didn't expect you to use his words to refute his own opinion. Spamton thought for a moment, then finally nodded helplessly: "So, after this, are you willing to [enjoy residency]?" ”
You nodded firmly, then took out your wallet and counted the appropriate amount of dark coins. Just then, the car stopped at the villa's main gate, and you handed the dark coins to Spamton, who was sitting in the driver's seat.
Actually, you were a bit nervous when handing it over, since you weren't very familiar with the prices in the Dark World. Spamton glanced at the dark coins, his eyes darting around, and thought of another good idea.
"These dark coins far exceed the [quota amount]. I think the dark coins you gave me are enough for you to enjoy the [right of residence] house for the future. ”
Taking advantage of your unfamiliarity with the prices of houses in the Dark World, Spamton decided to quietly coax you. After all, if she really took money from you every month, what would that count as? Was it a friend's fee or rent? Spamton muttered to herself.
But in reality, this amount of dark coins could only buy a one-square-meter house.
You paused, glanced at the villa, then watched Spamton casually put away the money. Your sixth sense told you something seemed off, but you couldn't figure out exactly what was off, so you just mumbled and asked, "...... Are these dark coins enough?" "So houses in the dark world are really that worthless?"
Spamton nodded firmly.
You stroked your chin thoughtfully. If that's the case...... Then you could buy a few more properties in the dark world, wait until prices go up, and then sell them. By then, you'd make a huge profit in Dark Coins.
Spamton doesn't know what you're thinking. If he did, he'd definitely buy the entire property you want to see before you go to see it, otherwise the money he's lying about now will be enough...... One poke and it's exposed.
But you only think about it, not take action. You put the lingerie you just bought in the wardrobe, and by then, it was almost evening, and you felt your stomach growling. When you went downstairs, you saw Spamton wearing an apron he didn't know where he had bought it, walking into the kitchen, ready to go all out.
For some reason, you have a bad premonition, and the next second, that feeling comes true because you hear a violent explosion, and then thick black smoke keeps drifting out of the kitchen. Your heart tightens, and you rush into the kitchen.

title: Contract Lover 5 (sptx you)
content:
For some reason, the thick black smoke was especially pungent to your nose. You coughed twice, covered your nose, and anxiously looked around the kitchen—even though you thought he probably wouldn't let anything happen to you, you couldn't help but worry.
The closer you got to the center, the higher the temperature seemed to get. When you leaned in to look, you realized the oven had exploded. Spamton's face was pitch black, his whole face completely out of place with his white body, making you want to laugh a little. He still sat on the floor a bit dazed, probably not understanding why the oven exploded. You quickly dragged Spamton out of the kitchen. Fortunately—he wasn't heavy, and after you dragged him a couple of steps, Spamton reacted, grabbed your hand, and pulled you out of the kitchen.
After running out, Spamton belatedly covered his face, since it was pitch black, and the black smoke from the oven explosion had blackened his face.
"[I'm very sorry], this is a very inappropriate [dining experience]......" He spoke so fast, almost like he was mumbling, while you patiently took a wet towel from the emergency restroom nearby and handed it to him.
"Wipe your face first, spamton...... spamton。 "You changed your words halfway through. To be honest, you didn't expect the consequences to be so serious...... Fortunately, nothing happened to her.
But Spamton simply lowered his hand, closed his eyes, and leaned his head toward you, as if signaling for you to wipe his face. After hesitating for a moment, you covered his cheek with a wet towel, gently wiping his cheek, and his face turned slightly with your movement.
"Mm...... How about I go cook later? "You suggested. If you keep putting Spamton in the kitchen, who knows what might happen. His suit is now dirty from the explosion, and he's covered in dust. And because he's wearing an apron, the area on his chest is spotless. You can't help but laugh.
Watching him obediently turn his face and let you handle it, you gently wiped his face, but it only changed from completely black to gray. It improved a bit, but still not very clean.
When Spamton heard that, he quickly spoke up: "[Project application rejected]. I think...... It should be me who [prepares the meal]. "Because we made a deal, because...... Whether it's real or not, you're both in a romantic relationship now, so it's only natural for him to do something for you.
You hesitated, pressing harder to wipe the dust off his face. The gray marks finally disappeared, replaced by pink marks, showing you were using a lot of force.
"Actually, it doesn't really matter. It doesn't matter who prepares the meal...... You can help me out, or do something else too." You suggested taking off the towel covered in mud. Spamton's face was finally clean, and he opened his eyes, took the towel from your hand, and went to wash it.
"No...... I think I should be the main force, and you should be the assistant part. Spamton insisted.
You looked at him, hesitated a little, and finally nodded and shook your head: "Alright, let's give it a try." ”
You walked back into the kitchen. Spamton hadn't changed off his clothes, meaning he was still wearing that tattered suit from the explosion. At least there was no black smoke in the kitchen, but the oven was still warming—probably from just a very high temperature—no wonder it exploded—because you saw the damaged plastic bag still inside.
Besides that, there was still some dust on the kitchen floor. We'll probably have to wait until all this is over before cleaning it up properly. In short, the oven probably can't be used anymore. If you look closely, the half-exposed plastic bag is probably ...... Is it a pizza wrapper?
You almost want to laugh: "Spamton, you didn't just stuff the pizza in without opening the package, did you?" ”
Spamton scratched his head, a bit guilty as he turned away, refusing to meet your gaze: "[Packaging Bag Label][Temperature Prompt]." "Alright, he admitted he really hadn't read the instructions carefully...... After all, he usually enjoyed things outside—either other Darkfolk were treating him, or a bunch of Addisons went to the Cyber BBQ Restaurant...... But now he didn't have any, and now he was the only one going alone.
“…… Forget it, the oven isn't even usable anymore, so let's wait for someone to fix it." In the end, you shook your head, opened the fridge to check, and found that besides a few bags of near-expired fast food, there were only a few bags of steak nearing expiration...... Hmm, butter and black pepper sauce and the like were also nearing expiration.
You take out two steaks, ready to fry them for a bit, but Spamton stops you.
"Please let me handle it. [Uphold the main force policy]." He said this.
Seeing his serious expression despite his smiling face, you hesitated for a moment, but finally handed him the two steaks and butter, then added nervously, "Then follow the steps I hinted to." ”
Although you're a bit worried...... But you think it's not good to refuse him at this moment, so let him go and do his best. At worst...... If it really comes to mind, just go out for a meal!
So you instruct him to pour butter first, and once the oil is hot, slide the steak along the edge of the pan.
He poured the steak in, but the pressure was a bit strong, and a bit of hot oil splashed with his movement. You quickly pulled him back, but luckily the hot oil didn't splash on him—only a few drops spilled onto his apron.
The pan sizzles and you peeks in to remind you, "Mm...... When you think this side is about done, flip it over. ”
Spamton really listened to you, frantically scooping up the steak, but no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't succeed; instead, the steak side was getting older and older.
You sigh and take the spatula from his hand: "...... Let me do it instead." As you spoke, you smoothly flipped the steak, but once you flipped it, you both could see that side was already overcooked, or rather, a bit charred. With the sizzling sound of oil, the burnt smell grew stronger. Spamton quickly turned off the stove and carefully poured the steak onto the plate.
You both stared at the steak in silence. One side was old, even a bit burnt, while the other side was tender, even streaks of blood, not cooked at all—after all, it didn't look like something edible.
Spamton coughed awkwardly twice: "This [pending junk food]...... I'll handle it." As he spoke, he sprinkled black pepper sauce on top. He picked up the knife and fork and struggled for a long time but still couldn't cut it off. Finally, he managed to get it off, but after chewing a few bites, his expression changed. Then he spat out the steak and threw the rest into the trash can.
You rubbed your temples, a bit helpless, but you didn't blame him—after all, the first time you cooked, you made a mess in the kitchen. But then your mother scolded you harshly, saying you weren't virtuous at all and wouldn't be able to support yourself in the future, so...... After that, when you cook again, you were always cautious.
You don't want to see Spamton end up like this, so you just say, "Want to try again?" ”
You don't think that if you snatch it now and help him do it...... What benefit will it bring him? That would just be a disguised denial of him.
Spamton glanced at you hesitantly, thinking...... You would forbid him from cooking again, but you just smiled at him.
He took a deep breath. Although he knew he had done terribly just now—maybe even worse next time—he instinctively gave a confident smile, as if he were the best of everything.
This time, you didn't remind him again. Spamton took a deep breath, poured butter into the pan, then added the steak. This time, he tried flipping it in advance, and after several attempts, he finally succeeded. Although it didn't cook to a satisfactory doneness, at least when taken out of the pan, it looked quite good.
Pouring in the black pepper sauce, this time he easily cut open the steak. Spamton hesitated for a moment, but when the steak cooled down a bit, he first forked a piece and brought it to your mouth. You leaned in slightly and swallowed the steak, chewing it carefully, then smiled and nodded: "Hmm, this time it tastes great!" ”
Hearing this, Spamton cut off a piece and put it in his mouth. It wasn't exactly delicious, just ordinary...... At the very least, it couldn't compare to the things he used to eat. He glanced at you hesitantly, and you just smiled and gave him a thumbs-up. Spamton couldn't tell you were lying; he could only tell you were sincerely complimenting him.
Although he still felt a bit of a failure now, the corners of his mouth couldn't help but lift into a smile, filled with joy. The area on his chest felt warm and light, as if it had been filled by something.
He just smiled, split the remaining steak in half, and gave you half to share. Using the same fork, he picked up the steak and brought it to your mouth. You swallowed it as you pleased, and he ate the remaining half. Sharing the same fork, nothing seemed wrong—but this scene seemed more like a couple than some untimely performance.
After finishing, Spamton touched his stomach. Clearly, half a steak wasn't enough to fill his stomach. He glanced at you again, and you tilted your head in confusion: "Is there something you need?" You can just say it directly, Spamton. "Anyway, you're considered a couple now...... Between couples, what's there to hide from each other?
Spamton paused for a moment before speaking: "I'm [thinking], maybe...... You don't have a [full stomach], so let's go to a restaurant outside, okay? ”
TBC.

title: Horror Game Port 1 - Old House in the Forest 1 - sptx You
path: articles/en/spt/恐怖片大逃杀 end/恐怖游戏端口1-林中古屋1-sptx你.html
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
…… Poe got hooked, so the style of this series leans a bit more toward Poe's writing style. Also, since it's a horror game with a genre similar to infinite stream (? ) It's not entirely based on the original work.
——
…… To be honest, you have no idea why you've come here. Just a moment ago, you were drinking beer at a barbecue restaurant, enjoying a tipsy sensation and thinking about what to do next. But the next second, you're sitting here shrouded in darkness, gloomy leaves pressing down overhead, on soft ground where only faint light filters through the gaps between the lush leaves. You casually touch the soft ground, and the first thing you feel is the slightly rough, dry surface of the leaves. Then, with an unintentional press, you hear the crunching sound of the fallen leaves piled together.
You can't just sit and wait for death, so you brush the dust off your clothes and stand up, ignoring the pain in your tailbone from suddenly sitting on the ground. Then you gradually adjust to this drowsy darkness—honestly, you really hope to find a way out so you can leave here quickly, and you don't care what exactly is happening to you, or what is happening beside you. Because you know that it could only mean bad omens, because you have uneasy signs, and you are a selfish person—so you only plan to leave alone.
Unfortunately, just as you recognized the direction of the wind in the forest and planned to follow the wind and step on the creaking leaves, you heard a sound like a pop-up window. In short, it was a bell, and it sounded like an explosion in your mind. You had to stop, almost annoyed, staring at the transparent window before you, which even glowed faintly.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest together with your companions. ]
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'killer.' ]
You looked at these two lines of text helplessly, so you looked around, then lowered your head and saw another but identical pop-up window—in the subtle dimming, you could barely recognize it as the tiny figure that had been standing nearby before, its outline almost like a puppet. To be honest, at the time you even thought it didn't really exist, after all, this was a forest, and maybe ...... Maybe it was just the incarnation of some tree.
But now, through the screen's light, you can finally see his pale face—or maybe it's his own complexion. He wears a pair of ridiculous pinkish-yellow glasses, so you can't see his mood. Of course, you're not very curious about it. You just crouch down, looking him up and down, and he seems wary, but doesn't say a word. After hesitating for a moment, the puppet finally reaches out his hand to you.
"I think we need to cooperate with [you] and I to leave this [world]." His voice sounded strange, with a crackling sound like electricity. You scratched your ear and felt a bit uncomfortable, but for you, perhaps having another companion in this darkness was actually a blessing—after all, you all saw that panel, and he had no other missions, so perhaps you could let go of your unfounded vigilance and just take this little puppet and escape this forest together.
Of course, as for that side quest, it's probably fine not to complete it...... Just as you were thinking this, you saw the text on that panel update.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest with your companions.] Reward: Survive successfully and have seven days off, immune to all lethal factors
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'Killer'.] ] Reward: 10,000 gold
You smacked your lips in annoyance. Honestly, this was like suddenly getting involved in some kind of horror game—honestly, ten thousand dark coins made you a bit envious, but you had no deductive skills. You've always believed in physics and cryptography. If you can't unlock it, just break it outright!
So you looked down at the little puppet again, raised your eyebrows, and reached out your hand to him: "Alright, since things have come to this, we can only reach a partnership. But just to be clear, since I can't handle side quests like this kind of deduction and cryptography, I'll leave it to you." You said it as if it were only natural, and without waiting for him to refuse, you continued to add more.
"As for the main quest—don't worry, I'll take you with me and leave here. I don't know how you should address me, but just call me Y/N." You shrugged, watching him reach out his hand toward you. You casually grabbed his hand and shook it, then grabbed it and lifted it up, placing him on your shoulder.
After all, you just heard an unsettling rustling sound from the leaves not far away. It wasn't the sound of wind, but clearer, more obvious human voices. Someone was walking through the woods in this direction, probably just patrolling normally. After all, you had just tried it. The light screen couldn't be broken, so maybe it wasn't because you saw it.
Before he could answer, you heard footsteps getting closer behind you. After all, the sound of stepping on withered leaves was too obvious, not to mention the sound of chainsaws starting the wheels, the sizzling sound, and a faint, terrifying smell of blood—so you just grinned: "Forget it, these things can wait a bit. For now, let's run!" "Better hold on!" ”
With that, you pushed off the ground and dashed out. Honestly, you're quite good at sports, so running a distance is easy—even fast, not difficult. Right now, you're only slightly out of breath, with lactic acid accumulating in your legs and a slight ache. You didn't mind at all, just weaving through the woods, listening to the ominous sound of a chainsaw moving farther away, while you found a more lush, densely packed spot and rushed in.
You were still running, and before Spamton could answer, he was forced to clutch your clothes. Honestly, he didn't want to be thrown off in a place like this—although for the main quest, you'd probably go back to save him, but he didn't want to experience that kind of anxiety. Just as he was about to speak, a gust of wind blew him in, twisting the words he wanted to say and spreading eerie sounds.
"My [name] is—" Unfortunately, the voices behind him were all faded by the wind.
And you just raise your voice and ask, "You—are—saying—what—"
Spamton hated his current situation—unsettling, confusing, and precarious. He always had to come up with a plan to protect himself, always figure out a way to live a better life. Of course, he was willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, even if it was just a brief experience of being a despised rat, as long as he still had the ability to choose, as long as he had the ability to think, he would never let himself willingly remain in that situation.
And he recognizes you. He knows you are a Citizen of Light he met a few years ago. Unfortunately, he didn't get what he truly wanted from you, but was sent off by money.
But now, relying solely on his own abilities, he couldn't accomplish anything. He was confident that if you hadn't taken him away from that place, he would have been finished, declared his death, and declared it all with deep resentment and displeasure.
If it weren't for you, maybe he wouldn't have ended up in this situation—but without you, he absolutely couldn't have escaped it. If you didn't seem completely unaware, he'd almost think all of this was your deliberate design.
He despised and hated the feeling, but he had no other choice. He could only lie down, clutch your clothes tightly, perform some useless prayers, then close his mouth, saying no more or repeating it.
Only when you can no longer hear the chainsaw behind you do you slowly stop, wipe the unwarranted sweat from your forehead, glance at the Spamton on your shoulder, and feel the weight on your shoulder—you know he's always been there, so you just treat it as a simple burden and run away.
Only after stopping did you realize the trees before you were sparse, even seeming to have a faint glow. You cautiously took a few steps forward, and then everything suddenly opened up—it was actually a small wooden cabin. Surrounded by trees and among the fallen leaves, there was actually a small wooden cabin. It looked somewhat old, but at least with the naked eye, it was clearly not made of new wood, at least some time ago. There was even an iron pot in front of the mansion, but probably no one had used it.
After all, a thin layer of dust had even accumulated on the iron pan, at least two or three months ago.
You hesitated for a moment, touched your belly, then felt it for a moment, looked at Spamton, and said gravely, "...... I think it looks like we need to eat, drink, and rest normally. I just don't know if there are any suitable ingredients left here...... At this moment, you even feel a bit relieved to have discovered such a wooden house. There are probably still candles burning inside, which is why a faint light is emerging.
"Maybe we can take turns keeping watch at night. Also, for the repetitive work, my [name] is Spamton G. Spamton. " said the little puppet.
You nodded and softened your footsteps. After all, there were no fallen leaves near the cabin, so simply keeping your footsteps quiet was fine—you just didn't want anyone to notice your movements, just in case there were others in the cabin.
So you just lowered your voice and asked hopelessly, "Then, maybe you could go in and help me check the situation now?" "After all, you heard something strange coming from inside the house just now. You definitely don't want to end up in the face of a killer after finally coming here. Of course, letting your 'companion' go is no big deal, and he looks small and clearly won't be easily discovered!"
"I think we should [act together]." Your intention was too obvious, after all, you wore that regretful expression on your face right now—as for just now? It was the look of someone racking your brains to plan, so now you have no choice but to regretfully abandon the plan, sigh, and continue walking forward with Spamton.
You climbed the wooden steps and quietly poked your head out from the window to look inside. There was no one there, just candles burning on the table, looking like the wick was about to burn out. You continued to carefully observe the inside of the house, and at that moment, you noticed a heat-insulating cage near the wall, inside which humans were imprisoned—who looked like a Child of Light? You thought this way, since you were also a Citizen of Light, and you had some feelings for your kind. As for how you knew? You had just accidentally entered the Dark World.
And that experience left a bad impression on you—the money you had so hard to bring was swindled away by a slick-talking, smiling salesman!
So now that you remember, turn your head and ask the Spamton on your shoulder: "Uh...... Are you a Citizen of Light or a Citizen of Darkness? ”
Naturally, you didn't recognize that this was the salesperson who had tricked you back then.
You feel as if he glares fiercely at you through his glasses, and you don't care at all, just hoping for an answer from him.
"[People of Darkness]." He didn't hesitate at all, but you always felt his tone carried a hint of gloom. You glanced at him probingly, but couldn't see anything.
So you just scratched your hair and glanced through the window to confirm that the killer was indeed not there, but probably back at any moment. In the end, you climbed in through the window, ignoring the terrified eyes of those inside the cage who then looked at you with pleading eyes—please, you're not that kind, you don't want to save others, and they're probably not real, just characters created by this horror game, so life and death have nothing to do with you. Only after climbing over the window do you realize you could have used the front door.
Then you rummaged through the locker and found a few baguettes, sandwiches that looked like they'd only been stored for a day or two, and of course, some cured meats. In any case, having these foods was already pretty good in this situation. You put Spamton on the table, picked up the food and handed it to him, grabbed a piece of bread yourself, and started wolfing it down.
Spamton didn’t eat, but just looked around the little house, then spoke: '…He is 【raising】 prey, waiting for the 【right moment】 to carry out the 【hunting process】. Meanwhile, these 【prey】, out of fear, are constantly in a 【mentally weakened state】.'
He kindly explained it to you. You slowed your movements a bit, paused, and nodded at Spamton. Of course, you understood what he meant—even though his choice of words was a bit strange, it’s not that you’re dumb, you’re just not good at thinking things through!
'Phew… thanks for the deduction, but for now, let’s just rest. Will you keep watch first?' After eating, you burped and continued to ignore the resentful gazes from the people in the cage behind you.
Spamton nodded, so you grabbed the back of his neck, found where the bedroom was, and then lay down holding Spamton.
You were drowsy, but didn’t forget to remind him: 'Wake me up in the later half of the night; it’ll be my turn to keep watch. Also, if you sense anything unusual, wake me up too.'
Spamton nodded, so you went to sleep peacefully.
Tbc.

content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
…… Poe got hooked, so the style of this series leans a bit more toward Poe's writing style. Also, since it's a horror game with a genre similar to infinite stream (? ) It's not entirely based on the original work. It might be quite long.
——
You slept drowsily in a dark dream world. Calling it completely quiet and peaceful isn't entirely accurate, because after passing through that darkness, you still fell into the dream. To be honest, you almost forgot this memory, but in the dream world, everything remained so clear. Now you looked with some resentment at the salesman in front of you, still dressed in a red suit and smiling, while you had no control over your own actions.
So you know it's just a lucid dream; as long as you watch the process of the dream and wake up again, everything will end. But honestly, to you, it's like a nightmare, so you firmly believe you might wake up before Spamton calls you. After all, having nightmares often means it's hard to have a good sleep experience. But think about where you're falling asleep now...... You won't have so much resentment.
You'd rather encounter more darkness in your dreams, even if it's boundless, just a patch of pitch black that makes you uneasy, even if just a glance makes you shiver uncontrollably, even if, at this very moment, besides this narrow dream street, you stand there with the salesman across from you, and all that's left is darkness.
Alright, since you're here, you can see the other person's lips opening and closing rapidly. You want to hear clearly, to fill in your hazy memories, but no matter how hard you try, you still can't make out clearly. Even if you focus intently, you can only catch the faintest words. You only know that from your impatient tone, you must have made some kind of deal at the time, then you take out your wallet and hand all the coins to the salesperson across from that time. Then comes darkness again. You don't know what happened next—you probably returned to the world of light.
In your dream, you were still trying to recall something, trying to find the vague or lost memories from before. But before you could continue thinking or enjoy a deep, dark sleep, you felt something violently shaking your arm. The crackling sound of electric currents or the unpleasant scraping of wood echoed beside you, sounding like something was being said. So you couldn't help but pull out your pillow and give it a quick blow to the source of the sound.
Now the other person completely quieted down, and your head rested on the bed board. The bed board was quite firm, and if you landed directly on it, it would probably hurt quite a bit. Fortunately, your head wasn't far from the bed board at that moment. Now you were fully awake, quickly picked up the pillow and put it back on the bed, roughly restoring its position.
Then you hear sounds from outside—the door is closed, but the sound is getting closer and closer. You believe that in the next second, that person will be gripping the doorknob. The footsteps have already stopped in front of the door. You can imagine that hand is already resting on it, you hear the clicking sound of the doorknob turning—you swallow hard and instinctively hug Spamton, who seems about to say something, but you cover his mouth. You know your heart is pounding fast; you can almost hear those clear thumping sounds, right beside your ears.
The next moment, he opened the door, and footsteps entered the room. The empty bed was empty. The killer simply scanned the room, then paused for a moment, stopping in front of the bed. He paused for a while, probably observing something, then slowly faded away, just as he had when he arrived—gentle, unhurried.
Lying on the ground, you easily heard amplified footsteps, accompanied by a heartbeat, growing more intense, louder, and more impatient. In that instant, you hugged Spamton tightly and rolled off the bed, instinctively hiding under it—the only place left to hide.
Through the gap in the edge of the bed—or rather, the gap in the hanging sheets—you saw those feet resting not far from the bed, standing for a moment before leaving. You heard the rustling sounds outside, but to be honest, these sounds were drowned out by the pounding of your heart beside you. You almost couldn't hear the sounds outside.
But you know, it was the killer distributing food to those in the cages. Through the gaps in the bed's edge, you could barely see it—you could see the shadow reflected on the sheets, the elongated reflection on the ground—then you watched the man raise the axe and bring it down hard. You clutched Spamton's shoulder and shivered instinctively. Then you heard the sound of blades hitting the cutting board, smelled roughly the scent of blood. You thought, it was probably chopping meat.
The process was almost torturous. You tensed your nerves, and the drowsiness you still felt faded away at that moment. Honestly, if you weren't afraid of accidents, you'd wish you could sleep a little longer. So you lowered your head to look at Spamton, who also looked up at you. But in reality, even if you looked at each other, it was just staring at each other—after all, you couldn't tell what was hidden in each other's eyes.
After a while, you hear footsteps fading away, hear a loud door slamming, and guess the killer is gone. So you peek out through the gap in the bed's edge. You no longer see that long reflection, only the countless cages cast shadows on the floor. Finally, you climb out from under the bed with Spamton, letting go of the hand covering his mouth.
You were still a bit timid and guilty, after all, the people inside the cage outside saw you two walk into the room openly. How could nothing happen? But when you look outside, all you can see are those people's angry or innocent eyes. You don't know what to ask, and in the end, Spamton tugged at your sleeve: "I [believe] [we] should hurry up [time] to search for [clues]." ”
Only then did you realize what was happening, and hurriedly nodded: "You're right...... Anyway, we've already reached his bedroom. Let's first see what clues are inside." ”
After saying that, you chose to check the nightstand first. Naturally, aside from an old calendar and a photo frame placed by the bedside, there was nothing else. You felt a bit discouraged, but instinctively glanced at the photo frame—you knew the person in the center was probably the killer who had left in a hurry, since the person in the middle looked a bit inexperienced. But the two people beside him were completely blacked out, making it impossible to tell their backgrounds.
Frowning, you finally remembered the contents of the photo. Then you waved for Spamton to come over and look at it. Seeing him turning his back, seemingly studying something on the bookshelf, he was even standing on tiptoe because he couldn't reach it, so you simply called out to him.
"Come over here and take a look, Spamton." Anyway, you don't plan to leave the decryption to yourself; you're just lazy...... Besides, it seems your companion is pretty smart, so it's fine to use it, right? You thought this with a clear conscience, then saw him walk over and casually stand up to make room for him.
But when Spamton arrived, he handed you a newspaper. You glanced at it—it was from October 11, 1923—honestly, the year was way too far from you. You instinctively glanced at the calendar again and saw that today was April 5, 1945.
You exhale a sigh of relief. A newspaper that has been around for 22 years still appears here, and apart from the paper's inherent wrinkles and yellowing from age, there are no visible signs of damage, not even dust. This is itself strange.
He shook the newspaper, and to his surprise, this well-preserved old paper only had two pages left. You see, Spamton was still studying the bedside table, so he decided to check the contents of the newspaper first.
[The xxx couple suddenly had an accident in Honshu. The crime scene was in a local forest. The bodies of the two were hard to identify, with flesh and blood mixed together. Their bodies were located in the trunk of an RV. Witnesses estimated that they had been dead for more than twenty-four hours when they found them, but the exact time of death is difficult to determine. It is speculated that the two were attacked while traveling to Honshu while having a picnic in the woods......]
You glanced at the date and instinctively frowned, endured the discomfort to finish reading the report, including the black-and-white photo of the corpse printed on the front page, then turned the page, intending to see what else was written in the newspaper.
Turning to the next page, you instinctively glance at the heading of the question, only to find that the date has changed. It was originally 1923, but now the header is now June 13, 1925.
You muttered to yourself, barely recalling that this day happened to be Black Friday. It was all mysterious, and you didn't really care about it. You just glanced at the report.
[Shocking: The xxx couple once jointly cheated on another couple. The husband treated the other woman's affair as a partner, and the wife in turn treated the other husband as the affair partner!] This incident has stirred up a two-year uproar in this prefecture. The verdict regarding the perpetrator's violent acts has been difficult to determine, and public opinion calls for lenient sentences. According to relevant laws, murder is punishable by life imprisonment or even the death penalty......]
…… What kind of mess is this? If you still want to complain, you shake the newspaper and realize it's probably a photocopy, because behind this page is the content printed on the back of another newspaper dated another day.
By now, Spamton had finished thinking about the nightstand and walked toward the bookshelf. Once again, though probably out of reach, Spamton called out to you: "I need your [help]." ”
You quickly responded with a couple of 'ohs' and walked over to him. You didn't have time to read the newspaper carefully, only glancing at the headline and the approximate date—it was November 10, 1932.

More than that, probably because they had been placed for a long time, red or yellow fluids had flowed out, and the blood mixed together was nearly dried up, the skin shriveled and gradually turned dark brownish-black. The cut surfaces also turned black, and you could see the greasy yellow dripping down before slowly drying up.
You pinched your nose. Besides that, there was a magic circle carved on the ground. These heads looked like offerings, perhaps simply for worship—who were they worshipping? Because when you looked up, you saw two tombstones directly ahead.
Spamton didn't say anything, just closed his eyes, then grabbed the clothes at your pant leg. You felt the pressure on your pant leg and looked down at him—well, you could only see the top of the little puppet's head, so you couldn't be bothered to think further. You just circled around the two tombstones and looked up, only to find that the walls were actually filled with various photos—including cropped printed text.
You get dizzy just looking at these characters. You don't want to decrypt them, so you pick up Spamton and sit on your shoulder. It's still more convenient for Spamton to see directly.
You turned your head to glance at him, pursed your lips, and said, "In that case, I'll just leave these text and photos for you to see. If you say you want to see something, just let me move a seat." "At this moment, you're just a ruthless commuting machine."
Spamton meets your gaze. Well, fine, he can only see sincerity and clear foolishness in your eyes, and it's clear you have no desire to decode—but from his guess, you actually do think anyway, just a bit slow to react. But since you want to, he still looks at the wall.
First are the photos—you saw those too, most of them solo shots, faces you don't recognize. Only two were of two people, and then you thoughtfully nodded at one of the pictures: "Ah...... These two people, I've seen before, are the people who appeared in the group photo that the killer didn't ruin—probably his parents. ”
Spamton nodded and turned to another photo, which also showed a married couple. Between the two photos were several letters, which looked handwritten, though it was unclear how the killer had found him. In short, it looked ...... letters from them pouring out their hearts, with handwriting both male and female.
So Spamton pointed to the photo: "That photo is his [parents''s] [affair partner]." ”
You nod thoughtfully: "Ahh...... I see. So what about these people? "You've given up thinking, and you don't want to look. Let Spamton take a look."
"Then [you] need to move to the [left]." he said.
So you move a few steps to the left to make it easier for Spamton to look. He read the text hanging on the wall. To be honest, it was all commentary—not just printed, but also cropped from newspapers. Most were comments about previous reports, mocking his parents for both cheating on another couple and deserving of their deaths. Some comments were calling for lenient sentences, but it seemed people in this world despised cheating even more. Maybe it was a world where both spouses could kill one of the cheaters.
So he turned his head to you, and possibly to the light screen that appeared at some point, explaining: "After the [death report], the person who appeared on the photo wall mocked the [report's content] and [parents]. Therefore, he decided to [take revenge], and at the same time, [mourning] and [sacrifice] to his parents. And the [hunting behavior] is meant to make the [targeted] and [former perpetrator] feel [fear] and experience [the same confusion they once had]. The only question is how he [chooses the target]......"
You all saw it. With his words, the completion rate of side quests kept rising, only stopping when he reached 80%.
You rubbed your chin, wondering how to pick a target, how to get people to come here...... Then you thought about the car you saw in that clearing and casually said, "This place is a tourist destination...... It used to be the place where his parents drove over here? ”
You see the progress bar for side quests has turned to 88%
So you nod involuntarily, and Spamton quieted down. He quietly watched your profile, realizing that even if he thought he understood you, he could still notice something different the next moment.
And you didn't notice his gaze, just continued talking to yourself, or maybe guessed: "And as long as you spread some rumors and rumors that the couple who died here have become vengeful spirits or something, only by coming here to worship will they avoid being entangled. Those with hidden feelings will fall for it!" ”
But you're not just guessing. In fact, when you arrived at that clearing earlier and hurriedly glanced past the few campervans parked there, you caught sight of candles and other items left in the car, along with bouquets—clearly meant for those coming to pay respects.
So you still combine your previous findings with your speculation, and then you'll find that the side quest progress has reached 100%, with flowers and fireworks appearing on the screen—probably congratulations on completing the quest.
You cheerfully say, "Wow, this task is done—ten thousand dollars, that's ten thousand!" You were excited, but the next second, you realized that ten thousand coins had turned into ten thousand dark coins, and you lost your smile. To be honest, although most of it was done for Spamton, at least 20% was done by you. And without you, Spamton wouldn't even know what would have happened at this moment!
So you glanced at Spamton quietly; he probably felt guilty too. You sensed the little puppet's body was probably stiff, but you didn't care about it. You just grabbed his shoulder and started shaking him.
"I don't care...... You have to give me half of these ten thousand. Dark coins are dark coins, and I want the currency circulating in the dark world too! I can't give you everything, or what would I be! "You grumbled in annoyance, tugging at Spamton, watching him make a surrender gesture, and only then did you feel a bit satisfied.
"So, quickly tell me the address...... When I get back, I'm going to the Dark World to catch you out......" you said in a sinister tone, grabbing him by the back of his neck and lifting him up in front of you. You stared at him fiercely, very clearly. You could tell Spamton was about to tell you something—you felt satisfied.
But before you could get an answer, you all heard the door ringing. Listening in the darkroom would sound dull and blurry, and you instinctively grew nervous. You have to know, the bookshelf hadn't been restored to its original state; the killer would definitely come to check the room, and maybe you two would die here—so you quickly ran to the window trying to open it, not caring whether Spamton answered you or not. You shook it twice and found the window was completely nailed shut, unless ...... Unless you smashed the window and got out.
You gazed quietly at the pitch-black window, then at the Spamton in your hand—instinctively, you reached out and pinched the little puppet's skin. Hmm, it really did look like wood, but it still had some hardness, so smashing the window might be fine! Watching your movements and extensions, Spamton had a bad feeling, and the next second, that feeling came true.
Because you raised him up with both hands, then really smashed a huge hole in the window—the crisp sound of glass shattering. The next second, you could hear the killer quicken his pace, the heavy footsteps approaching the dark room. There was no time to say anything else. You looked at the gap in the window you had smashed and struggled to clutch the Spamton and crawl out. Honestly, the Spamton was actually quite useful, you thought to yourself.
As for Spamton...... Honestly, breaking glass or being scratched by broken glass is really painful, but probably because the force is too large, that long-lasting pain actually fades after a while.
And you didn’t care about so much; who cares what it really looks like when you’re about to die? You just ran forward holding Spamton, then instinctively looked down at him. He silently pointed you in a direction, so you continued running that way until a light suddenly appeared ahead, until the crunching of leaves underfoot stopped, until you stepped once more onto soft soil. You saw vehicles stopped ahead, and you found one with the key still in it, not taken out… well, to be honest, it seemed like the keys of all the cars hadn’t been taken out. Probably the killer put them there? After all, giving a little hope makes the hunt more interesting, and you get to see the human flaws of competing and betraying each other.
You couldn’t think about so much. You quickly climbed into that car, put Spamton in the passenger seat, and then shakily started driving. You could hear the chainsaw getting closer to your direction, and when you looked back, you could still see the killer.
The car kept swaying, and Spamton didn’t have time to fasten his seatbelt, just raised his voice a bit: “【Request: Smooth ride—】”
You also raised your voice: “Ah—I don’t have a driver’s license, I’m just driving blindly, hang in there, anyway, as long as we can get out—” You pressed the accelerator to the max, speeding up to the top, and soon the sound of the chainsaw faded away. The trees ahead gradually thinned, revealing an exit to the outside, faintly showing a few houses and a distant road.
“Oh, right, so where exactly are you—address—”
Before reaching the end, you were out of breath, speaking loudly. You turned your head to look at Spamton’s mouth moving, but unfortunately, you couldn’t hear him. Because as you crossed the finish line, a blinding flash of white occurred, everything around melted in that instant, and you couldn’t help but close your eyes. When you opened them the next second, you were sitting up in your small, dark rented room.
You barely remembered Spamton’s lip movements… garbage, does he live in a dump? No way! You suspected it was just your own dream, but the next second, a strange voice sounded, reminding you that all of what just happened wasn’t a dream.
“Ding dong, main quest completed successfully, congratulations, player.”
Ancient Forest Cottage · End

title: Horror Game Port 6 - Interlude - Monday 1 - sptx You
path: articles/en/spt/恐怖片大逃杀 end/恐怖游戏端口6-间章-月曜日1-sptx你.html
content:
You calmly patted your cheek...... Forget it, not calm at all. You glanced at the time—it was still 3:30 a.m., just as you finished your part-time job and were about to go to bed, and somehow it ended up in that game—it must be Spamton's fault, how could it be your own fault? You firmly believed this, pushed aside the quilt with tore threads leaking through, got out of bed, passed over the stacks of instant noodle boxes and chocolate wrappers on the floor, closed the old computer with its screen lit up, and took a look at the door.
…… There's a bill on the door urging you to pay your water, electricity, and gas. You glance at the old calendar hanging on the wall, think for a moment, count on your fingers, and realize tomorrow is the payment deadline. Of course, since you can also move out of the lease, it doesn't really matter whether you pay or not. This is just next month's fee.
And after you got fired, you don't have money left to pay the collection and rent. You plan to pack up the last bit of things tomorrow and head to the Underworld—mainly to get your money back! Anyway, you think renting in the Underworld is fine!
…… So, let's sleep first. You closed the door. Luckily, in this weather, it was still a bit cold, but it was barely manageable. And you made it through the coldest times, so it didn't matter at all. You just skillfully curled yourself up, wrapped yourself in a quilt with a few holes, and drifted off to sleep.
The next morning, you still woke up punctually at nine, because normally you'd be going to the hospital at ten o'clock to work as a morgue porter, but yesterday you happened to be fired. You opened a box of instant noodles, boiled some water, ate a little, threw away the box, changed into decent clothes, and packed some luggage—all you could pack was just a slightly bigger backpack.
Then you thought about the location, touched your still empty belly, mustered your strength, and headed to the place where you remembered the intersection of the light and dark worlds. You passed through that entrance and entered the dark world. To be honest, you were a bit nervous. After all, last time you had entered by mistake and had no particular purpose, so it didn't matter. But today, you still had other motives, and you knew nothing about the paths of the dark world.
Forget it, since you're here, it's better to settle in. You tugged at the strap of your backpack, looked at the blue-black buildings and the neon signs hanging on the tall buildings, then at the neon lights slowly lighting up as you walked by. The shadows stretched longer and then lit up again with the next light—well, it looked like they were welcoming you. You calmly thought, what is there left to welcome someone like you?
But that thought lasts only a moment. You keep moving forward, forward—and then obviously, you're lost. According to Spamton's previous statement, do you think he probably lives in some kind of garbage station? Surely he can't live among the trash...... But now, looking at the brightly lit streets and the cars speeding by, you stop and look around. Good, it seems there isn't much to stop for and ask for directions, because all the faces you've never seen are quietly watching you. They think you haven't noticed at all, but you have noticed long ago, just pretending not to notice.
Maybe it's because you're a citizen of light. You find joy in hardship, but in fact, you're a failed citizen of light. Patting your cheek, you decide to move in a different direction and stop dwelling on these emotions. But as you take a step forward, you almost slip. Looking down, you see a foot stepping on a billboard. The bill is very old, wrinkled at the edges, and the image is no longer vibrant, but has turned a withered yellow. You've probably been drifting in this city for several days, since you've noticed several footprints on it.
You pulled your foot back, slightly disdainfully lifting a corner of the ad to take a look. Ah...... Actually, the design was pretty good, with the text and images arranged just right...... But that's not the point! You pulled back your drift and glanced at the image on the ad—oh, it was that annoying salesperson you encountered when you accidentally entered the dark world earlier. As for the name...... Your movement froze. Originally, it was just a casual glance, but now your eyes were fixed on that name.
Spamton G. Spamton.
…… Aha, you laughed silently twice inwardly, without any amusement. To be honest, you really did want to laugh out loud, maybe just ...... You wanted to mock yourself, maybe that's how it is? Your hand weakly loosened the flyer, watching it drift away with the wind that appeared at some unknown moment, not knowing whose foot it would land on or whose face it would hit, but you didn't care.
You were just a bit annoyed, but also a bit curious—after all, you were curious, and you never recognized him from start to finish. Now you still find it hard to believe—the gap is just too big.
But who it is and what their real identity is—it doesn't matter to them. It won't stop you from asking them to share the money that should have belonged to you! So you're just heading in the direction you chose. You know, that direction looks rather dull, and the walls are a bit old—maybe the direction of the garbage dump. You guess like this and try to lighten your mood.
Sure enough, but this place should probably be called a garbage heap too...... I really can't think of a good word to describe it. You walk around those piles of trash, then frown and pinch your nose. Honestly, you absolutely don't want to rummage through trash! Your life isn't that down-and-out. So now you hope Spamton can step out on its own, since you haven't found any residents at the garbage station.
You walk forward, and instead of piles of trash ahead, there are trash bins of all sizes. You finally don't have to cover your nose anymore. So you let go and start looking around, then your gaze settles on one of the large trash bins. You stroke your chin.
After all, you saw the lid of the trash bin move twice, and it looked even less tightly closed. If it were just like that, it would be fine, but after that, it moved several times after a while. So guess who's probably inside, and you think that's your target this time.
So you take a deep breath, get ready, suddenly open the lid of the trash bin, and then pull the Spamton out.
He seemed a bit stunned, but upon seeing you, he quickly recovered and said, "It's [you]." ”
You nod, loosen the lid of the trash bin, and reach out to Spamton to make a gesture for money: "Yes, it's me, hand over the money! My five thousand yuan, that's my five thousand!" ”
As you said this, you grabbed the Spamton and glared at him fiercely.
“…… Maybe [you] need [usage recommendations]? "I don't know why, but you felt this little puppet shivering—maybe it's a bit guilty?"
And you just snorted coldly: "No need. Now I know, you're the salesman who cheated all the money from me back then, so this time I won't trust you again! Just give me the money directly!" ”
Then you meet the gaze of the little puppet in front of you. You watch him silently for a moment, then reluctantly nod: "Then, I'll [lead], [you] will follow the action." ”
"That's more like it." You set him down on the ground with satisfaction, nodded, and watched him walk forward. You followed him slowly—to be honest, you hadn't noticed there was a hidden door just now, and it was a shortcut. You silently sighed in your heart.
Seeing that you were about to walk a bit further, you lowered your head to look at the back of the little puppet ahead, hesitated for a moment, and finally asked, "That ...... So I want to know, why did you make a deal with me back then?" ”
Actually, you thought you would forget about it, since it was mysterious back then and sounded like a scammer. You talk about getting what you most want for a tiny price, but you wonder how the other person knows what your dad's wish is, and the trivial price—you say you wouldn't care at all, but who knows what this salesman is really for?
In short, you only wanted to spend money to avoid disaster, so you painfully gave all the money you had to Spamton. Honestly, that was your newly paid salary! So after that, you never wanted to come back to the underworld, and you felt that day's stumble was truly unlucky.
Spamton paused for a moment, and a bit distracted, you almost kicked him in. Luckily, you noticed in time and hurriedly stopped, ready to hear what he was going to say—no, before that, you should complain about why he stopped!
But before you could speak, you already heard his voice: "I believe [you] can [cooperate]...... Or, for [you], I can [provide a use]. I believe [you] [need]. "But he did not specify exactly what he could provide, nor did he say what he hoped to require.
You gazed at his back, in this eerie silence that almost made people panic, in the quiet sound of the wind, you softly spoke: "Are you lying...... No, maybe you're telling the truth, but you're just dodging the issue. You never answered my question directly, and I didn't want to know what you could offer. ”
You follow in his footsteps, and the destination seems just within reach. You see a shop at the end of a garbage heap. Why would a shop be in a place like this? You really can't understand.
"...... [Sky]." When you were distracted, you heard him whisper, probably answering your question.
So you couldn't help but speak, and your curiosity was piqued. You asked, "What?" ”
"I believe we can reach a higher and higher sky through you, observe, or even climb higher. I believe perhaps by touching you, we can fulfill our expectations." You can't see his expression, only hear his somewhat dull and slow voice.
So you fell silent. To be honest, you didn't quite understand—but you could roughly grasp what he meant. Probably hoping you could find something like freedom through you.
But why you? Is it just because you're a Citizen of Light? Does that mean no other Light Folk come to the Dark World? Uh...... Well, maybe he hasn't seen it before.
So you simply chose to remain silent, following in his footsteps, and didn't ask any more questions.
Then you walked into the shop—cramped, with walls painted blue—or maybe blue skies and white clouds. You casually scanned the narrow shop, watched Spamton slip behind the counter, then took out five thousand Dark Coins and handed them to you. You nodded in satisfaction and put away the Dark Coins.
But suddenly, you hear Spamton speak: "How do you plan to [use] these [silver dollars]?" ”
It took you two seconds to realize what he was talking about. Then you looked down at the Dark Coin that had just been put in your bag and hadn't been warmed, and hesitated for a moment: "Hmm, Dark Coins can only be used in the Dark World, right? So I'm planning to rent a place there and stay here for now." ”
Anyway, you've been fired, and you don't have cash on hand right now. You might as well stay in the Dark World for a while.
"Not [return] [Light World] to conduct [Residence Activities]?" Spamton asked.
But you just shook your head, shrugged indifferently: "No, my rental over there just expires today, and I was fired yesterday. The only job I have left was laid off, so it's fine to stay in the dark world for a while." ”
…… What else could it help you escape? But you didn't say these things. After all, you and Spamton are just familiar strangers; you don't think you can talk about these more private matters. If it were just a casual remark, forget it.
For some reason, he suddenly got motivated: "So, I'm very sorry, and maybe you need a [housing recommendation]?" ”
You stared at him with wide eyes, wanting to say that you didn't need it at all—well, actually, you did, after all, you were completely unfamiliar with this dark world and didn't even know the way.
But you still asked cautiously, 'So, how many Darkness Coins do you need as payment?'
'One thousand [Dollars],' he said.
You drew in a sharp breath—so expensive, that's a fifth of the money right now! But perhaps the prices in the dark world really are like that? You had never bought anything here, so you reserved your doubts and just asked one more question: 'Is this the normal price?'
'[Yes], [definitely].'
Hmm… anyway, you'll still go into a shop later to check properly. For now, you half-believingly agreed with Spamton.
'Alright, deal. But I won’t fully trust you; I’ll check it myself!' You reached out your hand, not forgetting to add sharply.
Tbc.
