Then you glance at your desk and don't find any ballpoint pens. So you shake your head at Spamton and shrug: "No, or let's head out now. There's a grocery store nearby anyway, so grabbing a ballpoint pen is pretty quick." ”
Actually, Spamton already knew the answer when he asked this question...... He just wanted to buy time. After all, he couldn't recall the full content; he wasn't someone who studied this area.
You rush out of the research institute, run to the nearby grocery store, grab a ballpoint pen, and hand it to Spamton. In fact, Spamton has been pondering how to interpret this string of keys.
Holding that ballpoint pen, Spamton made a request: "Now, go back to that [laptop], then [place] me. I need to crack the [Key Generator]." ”
You nodded, fulfilled his request perfectly, and ran back to the research institute. The hall was now empty, with nothing else to distinguish except for the zombie you had just knocked down. Following Spamton's directions, you returned to the laptop and placed it on the table.
Then you leaned against the wall, hands on hips, watching the little puppet write something on that piece of paper. You couldn't understand it, but you were just holding the water pipe—yes, after you killed that monster earlier, you switched back to the water pipe. You just watched your surroundings warily, trying to prevent more zombies from attacking you.
Sure enough, another zombie emerged from a door. After smelling your scent, it sped up toward you, while you swung the hose and beat this seemingly low-level zombie hard. Soon, he collapsed to the ground and couldn't get up again. But more and more zombies kept closing in. Although they were all low-level, and a single pipe could knock down a large area, over time you would still feel irritable. You just did your best to clear out the zombies, wiped his sweat, and looked at Spamton, asking, "...... Not healed yet?" ”
He didn't look up at you, just gestured five fingers at you. You couldn't help but ask, "Five minutes?" And he nodded.
You took a deep breath, wiped the sweat from your forehead, and continued to beat the zombies with all your might. Fortunately, you still had plenty of strength left, so just sweeping them was enough to hold out. But with the sound of impact, more and more zombie corpses fell to the ground, blocking the doorway, and the remaining zombies couldn't get in.
You were speechless for a moment, though things were peaceful now...... But when you left, you still had to find a way to clear the way. You turned to glance at Spamton—about five minutes had passed. He ran over and entered the password on his laptop. With a click, a pleasant music sounded as the laptop was opened. You couldn't help but walk over and glance at the note, then picked up Spamton.
The note read: I am about to enter death. You twitched the corner of your mouth, glanced at the twenty-six letters written on it, and at a few crooked characters that had been blacked out. After thinking for a moment, you didn't ask Spamton how he solved it, but sincerely praised, "Amazing! You solved it all! I'm really glad you're the one who teamed up with me." As you spoke, you raised the little puppet and spun it around a few more times.
You see the little puppet's face blushing, and it seems smoke is rising from its head: "...... [place] me [on the flat ground]!" ”
You just recklessly spun him around twice, pretending not to hear what he said, and then you finally put him down. You seemed to hear Spamton exhale, and you—after all, couldn't contain that excitement anymore—which meant you could freely explore the secrets in the computer, which must be filled with many secrets.
So you hugged him and kissed him on the face with a loud smack, then put him back on your shoulder and started checking the contents on the computer desktop. The puppet was still smoking, as if it had been cooked, but you didn't care about that, just poked open the folder on the desktop.
The name of this folder is Research Use, probably including research materials. What disappointed you was that there were no maps inside, just countless documents. After a quick glance, you finally selected two research reports on the use of potions.
[File One
Research shows that this potion can greatly enhance human vitality, even revive corpses, activating cell activity to regrow. At this level, rapidly proliferating active cells are like cancer cells, but their production is limited, causing rapid death and regeneration, maintained within a certain limit.
However, the use of this potion does not fully restore the resurrected person's sanity; instead, it enhances their cellular activity and primal animal instincts. Through human experiments and research, we found that this potion can restore youth to the living, granting vitality beyond ordinary people's abilities. However, it gradually causes the loss of sanity and reason, turning into a beast and attacking others.
Therefore, this medicine is temporarily sealed before further research and will not be widely used. Nevertheless, if it could bring the dead back to life, or even achieve immortality, many people would flock to it, eager for the formulation of this medicine.
The chemical formulation method is as follows:
■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■
Part Two:
After adjustments, the proportion of one drug was lowered while the other was raised, improving the effectiveness of the drug and potentially enabling widespread adoption.
The authorities did not approve it, and the approval was rejected, so the study was reconsidered.
Note: Hehe...... What does it matter if you don't accept it! I want to use this potion, regardless of whether others allow it...... I hope everyone can be happy. If I can see the loved ones I have lost, I guess I will be in tears no matter what......
Comment again: Things seem different from what I imagined. Why do these resurrected beings recklessly attack the living? Could it be that the medicinal potions on their bodies...... No, no, or rather, viruses are actually active and can infect others? Now it's all over...... The others have also become those revived beings who recklessly attack others.
Another note: I know I was wrong. In fact, I have already created a potion that can restore sanity to those who have come back from the dead. But there was no time to experiment with it, nor can it be promoted further. After all, now everyone has become that kind of monster, and I too am heading toward death. Let's end here. I have destroyed this world. ]
After reading it, your feelings were complicated. You clicked on another document with a similar name. The contents were simple, just recording the recipe for the sanity-restoring potion, and you earnestly asked the person destined to discover this document to take the reagent out. He prepared a tube and sealed it in the innermost office of the research institute.
You glanced at the task panel—the side quest had already reached 100%. Whether you followed his instructions or not didn't really matter, and you selfishly didn't intend to bother with it. Still, you glanced at Spamton, choosing to ask your companion for advice: "Do you think we should go?" ”
He hesitated for a moment but nodded. You then walked forward. Fortunately, there were hardly any zombies left blocking the way. However, outside the innermost office, there was a huge zombie. You raised your axe and skillfully took it out, then opened the office and took out the vial of potion. You walked out the door and happened to see a low-level zombie bracing toward you. You stopped him and just poured the potion into his mouth. His eyes became clear. You nodded, picked up the unconscious guy, placed it in front of the laptop, and then walked out with Spamton.
You yawned: "Phew...... Is that enough...... "Actually, you really don't care. Maybe you don't have much empathy; your parents haven't given you the ability to love." Spamton just stayed silent, leaning in and hugging your neck.
Everything was resolved satisfactorily. Simply surviving in this world for seven days wasn't difficult. After completing the main quest, a flash of white light appeared, and once again, you heard a congratulations message for completing the task. Then you appeared again on the bed in the Dark World.

content:
You grabbed that check you got for finishing the game, sat up in a flash, grinning from ear to ear. Spamton, on the other hand, just glanced at the large pile of dark coins and never looked again; he just stared at you intently.
After you pressed that check to your cheek, you finally snapped out of that excitement. At that moment, you looked at Spamton and asked in confusion, "...... Why are you looking at me?" ”
But he just shook his head without saying a word. Or maybe he just saw you happy because of money and reminded you of how he first started. Unfortunately, everything is in the past, and it's too late to look back again.
You glanced at him in confusion again, not wanting to pursue the issue further. Instead, you raised the Spamton again and gave him a big smack on the face, beaming: "Thanks to you this time, otherwise we definitely wouldn't have gotten the side quest rewards!" So you don't mind if you have to praise him a bit more.
Or rather, you just want to praise him a few more times right now. You're racking your brains, trying to use every word you know to compliment him. Spamton was already a bit flustered when you lifted him up, not to mention you kissed him on the cheek. Of course, his face turned red—even puppets blush! Then you started praising him again, as if you could use any word, making his face blush even more and smoke rising from his head again.
After saying it tiredly, you smacked your lips, still a bit unsatisfied. But seeing Spamton's demeanor, you couldn't help but feel puzzled: "...... What's wrong with you? Did something just happen to go wrong?" As you spoke, you started shaking him.
Spamton's voice sounded somewhat frustrated: "I have no fault that needs repairs! Now, [you] have placed me at [ground coordinates], I just need [program cooling methods]. ”
You made two 'oh ohs' sounds. To put it bluntly, he just needed to calm down, so you laid him down on the bed, blinked twice, and looked at him: "Alright...... I'm putting you down! Come to think of it, it's getting late...... Yawn...... After the excitement just wore off, you couldn't help but cover your mouth and yawn, tears welling up in your eyes. Honestly, you really need to rest. Even though you slept in the game world, you weren't fully rested at all!
…… And after fighting so many zombies afterwards, you must be tired. Looking at the time, it's only 3 a.m., so you lie back down and fall asleep on the bed with a clear conscience.
And naturally, I forgot to ask Spamton about it again.
After calming down for a while, he turned around and heard your steady breathing, falling silent. After a two-second pause, he finally crawled over to your side and fell asleep with you. After all, in the past month, you had actually slept like this a lot. Even if you slept separately on the first day, the next day you'd still squeeze together, and for some reason, maybe it was yours, maybe his. Sometimes you'll find you're not sleeping in your original spot, other times you notice Spamton leaning in. Over time, you have tacitly accepted this situation.
Actually, at first, you were the one who noticed the two of them leaning against each other and frightenedly insisted on sleeping separately. You even placed a pillow in the middle, but early the next morning, you found the pillow had disappeared, and for some reason, you leaned in and slept against the spamton. You had no choice but to panic and pretend to be calm, announcing that from now on, you could sleep however you wanted.
And now, as night falls, you drift into sleep. For you, it's a dreamless night's sleep. So you open your eyes feeling refreshed, casually grab the Spamton beside you who is sleeping next to you, play with his arm, and lazily say, "Get up, get up—" You glance at it casually; it's eight o'clock in the morning, about time to get up.
Spamton was indeed shaken by your movement, because now he was facing away from you. You couldn't see his expression, only his somewhat flustered voice: "I'm not your toy!" As he spoke, he tried to pull his arm back from your hand, but your grip was a bit too tight for him to pull back.
And you pouted, deliberately speaking in a pretentious voice: "Hey...... I'm so pitiful, sincerely calling you to get up, but your good intentions were treated like donkeys' lungs. You don't cherish it at all...... You even wiped away your tears with a fake sense of indifference. Honestly, if you weren't so close, you wouldn't say that—after all, only people you know can tolerate your occasional pranks...... Thinking about it this way, you somehow started to feel close to Spamton. But maybe that's the benefit.
Spamton felt a chill in response to your words, his body trembling involuntarily twice, and he said nothing more. You knew when to stop, didn't continue, just shrugged: "Alright, alright, let's go out for breakfast anyway. Then when I get back, I have to keep working on the problems. I have class tonight...... You muttered to yourself, grabbed your clothes and put them on, and tossed Spamton aside to put them on.
Soon, you both went out together. You wore the clothes you brought earlier, while Spamton wore the suit you bought him last time. Seeing Spamton, you nodded in satisfaction, lifted him onto your shoulders, and then cheered, "Let's go!" ”
Breakfast was still a sandwich, but this time you bought two steaming hot bottles of milk, inserted a straw, and casually slipped one bottle into Spamton's hand. He started drinking milk too. When breakfast was almost over, you returned home feeling refreshed, pulled out your workbook to start writing, and casually placed Spamton on the table. After all, you can't let him always sit on your shoulder—you'd get tired too!
So with a serious face, you held a pen and opened the exercise book with high spirits, glancing at spamton, who was currently sitting cross-legged on the desk… overall looking inexplicably tall, who cleared their throat and said, 'Ahem, I'm going to start doing the exercises. Do whatever you want, as long as you don't disturb me!'
Spamton glanced at you speechlessly; he wasn't interested in figuring out what exactly was in your workbook...... After all, he couldn't understand most of it! When solving puzzles in the game world, the things he remembered were only things he might have used before, so he remembered them. Everything else...... Why bother mastering useless ones? But now, watching you focus intently on solving the problems and then looking at those problems, he just felt drowsy. He simply stared at your face.
But being stared at all the time, of course you noticed, and you actually don't like being stared at while working, so you put down your pen and glared fiercely at Spamton: "Why are you always staring at me! There's nothing on my face...... If you're that free, find something to do for yourself!" Your ears were a little red, because when you turned around, you happened to meet Spamton's gaze, which made you feel a bit strange. So you just hurriedly waved your hand, wanting to get Spamton to leave.
Spamton glanced at you quietly. He wasn't insisting on looking at you, but after all, there wasn't much to look good about you...... Or rather, he just thought you looked better. But he still nodded: "[Okay], I have other [to-dos] items." "And after hearing that, you picked him up and set him down on the ground." Then you used your hand as a fan to fan yourself, feeling a bit embarrassed inside, and for some reason, your face still felt hot and restless—maybe it was just your imagination.
In short, after putting down Spamton, you once again immerse yourself in the sea of questions, completely lost in the world and completely unaware of what else is happening outside. Spamton quickly tidied his clothes, then pushed open the door and walked out, arriving at his shop located in the junkyard—to be honest, he didn't think his shop was anything bad. Unfortunately, no Dark People came to visit. Today was still deserted, but Spamton wasn't discouraged by this; he was long used to all this.
…… But he felt he had to find a way to change everything, so his eyes darted around as he thought of you. After all, you're a citizen of light. As long as you spread this gimmick, lots of people will come here. When the time comes...... Maybe I can become like I once was again.
Having made up his mind, Spamton glanced around the desolate little shop, calculated that it was about time, and closed the shop to head back.
He doesn't care much about those dark coins; it's just that you must rely on them to survive in this world, and he knows that money is a major factor attracting you. And he still needs the help of you, the people of light.
…… At first, it was just a form of use and testing, and at some point, some changes occurred. Perhaps as time mercilessly passes, everything is in a state of relentless change.
When he got home and opened the door, he found you still sitting at the desk, gritting your teeth, resting your chin on your hand with a worried face, staring at a problem in front of you.
He climbed up from another chair next to the table, then crawled to the table, and sat back down next to your workbook. You glanced at Spamton, not asking where he had just been. You're not close enough to report your schedule, and it's not normal for him to have his own things to do. Of course, you did hear the door opening. But at that moment, you couldn't help but wonder where he might go. Of course, your attention was still focused on the workbook.
So you lower your head again to look at the exercise book. But your thoughts are still a bit off the question. At that moment, you hear Spamton say, "[Inquiry: Course schedule]?" ”
You paused for a moment, then thought about the class schedule you had received earlier on your phone, and said, "On weekdays, classes are held in the evenings, while on days off, classes are held around the clock...... That's probably how it is." "That's why you have such a free time during the day, working through problems here.
Spamton stares at you steadily, and you belatedly notice this gaze, so you can't help but put down your pen and meet his gaze.
"Maybe you're willing to accept the job I offer?" As he spoke, he reached out his hand to you.
Your expression was a bit strange, and you shook his hand up and down twice: "It's fine...... It's just work. Are you talking about the shop you opened at the junkyard?" "You still remember that place. Of course, you wouldn't criticize his taste...... It's also possible that he chose to open a shop in such a place because he was truly poor.
Spamton nodded, "The [salary issue] can be [resolved satisfactorily]." ”
Your expression grew even stranger. You pointed at yourself, then at him: "Are you sure? Didn't all those dark coins come from me and you earning together in the game world? So you should be sharing half with me too!" So basically, it's left hand to the other—you just gave me the money I earned...... You muttered to refute his point, but in the end, you didn't refuse him.
“…… Besides, I know that if you rely on just you for that shop, you probably can't sell anything, right?" You took a deep breath and asked again. To be honest, you were a bit slow to react, but you were not bad at thinking things through...... Now that he thought about it, he suddenly invited you to work, so he must have ulterior motives.
However, given the time spent together, you decided to trust Spamton.
But he just stayed silent, looking at you. You could read a strange sincerity in his expression, and you couldn't help but shiver.
"Alright, I'll go anyway! Isn't that the only employee in your shop? Am I really busy...... You scratched your head, let go of his hand, and looked back at the workbook in front of you.
Out of the corner of your eye, you notice Spamton shake his head: "[No.] [You] know that there is no [Visitor] at all." ”
You shrugged, actually a bit skeptical of his story, but in the end, you were convinced: "Alright, you talk like a beast. I hope you won't lie to me." ”
Spamton lowered his head slightly. Of course, he wasn't lying to you. After all, what he said was the truth, but he was talking about the store's previous situation, not the situation he had expected after you became a clerk.
…… As for what would happen after that, he had no idea, so naturally, this wasn't a deception.
At that moment, you stretched lazily, covered your mouth, and yawned: "Alright, then I'll go to your shop tomorrow—anyway, I really do need to find a job in the Underworld! Since you're willing to offer it, I'll accept it with a smile." Mm...... But since things have come to this, shall we have dinner first? "Saying that, you stand up, pick up Spamton, and head outside.
You finished lunch simply. In short, you ate your fill and burped before going to pay. The waiter looked at you and Spamton with a strange look, but you didn't pay much attention. You picked up Spamton and placed it on your shoulder, whistling off-key: "Alright, let's go to your shop. I roughly remember where it is...... But if I go the wrong way, remember to remind me. I'm not very good at finding directions. ”
You muttered a few times and headed toward the junkyard. You did make it to the junkyard, and obviously, you got lost too. You had no idea which direction to go, so you shot Spamton a pleading look.
Spamton paused for a moment, then pointed you in the right direction: "First, [vertical movement]." ”
You hum twice, try to avoid the trash ahead, then brake suddenly, because you hear Spamton say again: "Then turn left." So you stop mechanically, make a 90-degree turn in place, and continue walking left.
When you heard Spamton sigh, he probably found it too embarrassing to watch. And you coughed lightly, a little awkwardly: "Ahem...... There's nothing I can do. After all, I don't know the way, so I can only follow what you said! ”
Spamton thought you were treating him as a navigator again, so he kept a blank expression—or rather, he was happy to play with you for a while—so he glanced and said, "Then, at [100 meters ahead], perform the [right turn]." ”
You made a couple of 'oh ohs' as if suddenly enlightened, walked about a hundred steps, then turned right and moved forward. You glanced at Spamton, who was sitting on your shoulder, swinging her legs, and thoughtfully said, "It really does look like a navigator...... Why don't you just be my navigation system full-time from now on?" "Of course, you were just saying that casually.
Spamton, however, seemed to be choked up and suddenly coughed twice: "[No], I'm not doing [your] navigation service full-time." "He had no desire to do this job at all...... Or rather, he didn't want this job to be the only one for the rest of his life. Of course, he was still happy to serve you.
"Is that so? Alright, then forget it! Actually, I don't need navigation services often, so just give me some help in those moments." You shrugged. Since he didn't give any further instructions, you continued along this road. Finally, behind the endless pile of garbage, you saw that familiar shop again. Although small, it was obvious it had been carefully maintained, except it had already closed and the door was tightly locked. You went up and fiddled with the lock a couple of times before it opened.
You fell silent, then looked at Spamton, whose shoulders were a bit stiff, and raised your voice slightly: "You're just setting up the lock like this—aren't you afraid someone will come to steal things?" ”
His voice sounded straightforward and righteous: "No, my [shop] has no [value] and is not a [free product]. Even if [Dark People] enjoy [discounts], they cannot get [full discounts]." ”
You tugged at the corner of your mouth, thought for a moment, then cautiously asked, "Uh...... So your shop sells junk? Or rather, it's junk ......? "After thinking for a long time, you still can't describe those possibilities as treasures. You can't imagine it, so you simply push the door open and walk in. Well, there really aren't many items displayed on the counter.
“…… It's not the [Garbage Recycling Bin]! "He retorted, still making it so firm.
You took Spamton off his shoulder, placed him on the table, and then leaned down slightly to meet his gaze. Well, you did sense a hint of honesty, reliability, and innocence in his expression...... Although, based on your initial bad impression of the salesman, you probably shouldn't have trusted him.
But in the end, you still sighed: "Alright, since you're not selling trash, then tell me what exactly you're selling. Honestly, since you want me to work here, you have to tell me what you're selling, otherwise how am I supposed to help? Unless you want to tell me those are some shameful treasures." "When you mentioned shameful things, you raised your voice. Honestly, you don't think Spamton can really produce anything priceless. After all, if he could, he wouldn't be sitting here anymore.
…… But since he said he's not trash, then what exactly is it? You'd be willing to listen.
Spamton fell silent. His gaze shifted for a moment, probably looking at the items on the counter, while you crossed your arms and raised your eyebrows, wanting to see how he planned to make it up. To be honest, although you couldn't fully understand what he just said, your intuition told you. He probably...... Uh, selling some counterfeit and inferior goods.
Of course, you don't think being flashy or deceiving is all that bad...... But it's just amusing to watch the other party make up excuses knowing the truth, and I'm afraid both of you know the truth.
In the end, he seemed to have made up his mind, turned to meet your gaze, his eyes full of sincerity: "These are all [Stamina Recovery] potions, [Increased Aggression] weapons, and [Additional Defense] accessories." He said with certainty.
…… You're a bit confused about the Underworld's setting. Honestly, you probably never understood it. In fact, you're a complete materialist...... At the end of the day, you don't believe in all this nonsense, which sounds like an RPG, so you tugged at the corner of your mouth, feeling it had nothing to do with you, just gave a perfunctory "Oh, oh."
…… Well, that really has nothing to do with you. You watch as Spamton takes out a potion and a bow from the counter, and besides that, there's another weapon he mentioned...... You glance at it—it's a different form, but none of them are as useful as ordinary water pipes to you.
So you just dragged out the sound of "Oh—" and then scratched your hair, feeling a bit awkward. Even though you think these things are completely useless, it's no wonder Spamton would feel comfortable using an unreliable lock—no one would even come to get them. Of course, you overlooked that he probably just couldn't afford to replace a lock. Of course, you've been through three game worlds and have already earned so many Dark Coins.
"Alright, I understand. But does this little shop really need help? I feel like no one is coming...... you say hesitantly.
"I need your help. I need the presence of angels." And Spamton just persisted like this.
You glanced down at him. To be honest, you hesitated a bit...... But in the end, you nodded and reluctantly agreed with his suggestion: "Alright, I'll stay here and help. But I need to bring my homework and such...... Otherwise, idling around here is nothing." "Instead of wasting that time, it's better to learn more—at least that's what you think."
"Yes, and about my salary...... How much is it per month? Of course, it's fine for me to help out out of friendship, but at the very least, you should give me some dark coins as a token, right? "You rubbed your chin.
“…… One thousand Dark Coins【one month】? "Spamton hesitated a bit too.
"Deal." You actually agreed to the salary regulation quite readily. To be honest, you don't really know much about prices in the Dark World...... But one thousand Dark Coins is indeed quite a lot. Although for both of you, it's like switching hands to the other.
After a brief discussion of these issues, you watched as Spamton's shop reopened. You didn't go back to bring those textbooks over, since it was only an afternoon—a rare leisure time. It's good for you to stay here and chat casually.
Anyway, looking at the quiet shop, then at Spamton, you couldn't help but ask, "...... To be honest, if no customers come, why do you insist on opening a shop here?" "If you changed places, the foot traffic would be much higher. Honestly, even outside the garbage dump—uh, but maybe there's a ready-made place here—you always feel like it's some kind of abandoned container repurposed.
“…… There is no [legal right to operate the shop]. "He simply answered your question. For some reason, you always felt that his mood was a bit down. You stroked your chin, sized him up twice, then looked at the cramped shop, lost in thought.
"Alright, but now we have money too, right? Why not move somewhere—uh, I get it. It's related to why you've become like this now. Sorry, I won't mention it, I just blurted out." You quickly covered your mouth halfway through your sentence. Although you don't know exactly what legal terms exist in the Dark World, I suppose the outside world isn't very welcoming to Spamton, which is why he opened a shop here.
To be honest, although you think outside opinions can be completely ignored, it does affect certain aspects. So you just glanced at Spamton with sympathy.
He seemed not to notice your gaze, just sitting there at the counter, resting his chin on his hand and looking outside. Following his gaze, you could only see the pile of garbage, but Spamton didn't answer your question.
You shrugged, not minded, just sat down casually in the shop, then started to zone out.
After a moment of silence, you actually hear Spamton ask you a rather strange question. Calling it strange isn't exactly strange, but you don't think it's something you should say under the current conditions: "...... angel, what is your [dream]?" ”
"By the way, why do you call me that? Is this some special title...... You pursed your lips but still answered his question, "As for me, ideally, after graduating from adult university, I can look for a job based on the professional skills I've learned! Then live well, and if possible, completely get rid of my parents—if only we weren't on the same household registration! Of course, I want to live freely, live the way I want to be, and then show off to them." As you spoke, your eyes lit up with excitement, and you started giggling, forgetting your original question.
“…… But as for dreams! Actually, of course, there's money I can't spend all, and then I can do whatever I like, but it's probably not possible. "You shrugged.
"[Things you like]?" He simply asked.
"Ah, things I like...... Well, speaking of which, I actually like adventure, or rather, I like to travel. I like visiting all kinds of places, I enjoy learning about unique customs...... Standing firmly on another piece of land feels completely different. Saying that, I actually quite like the underworld—after all, it's fresh enough here. "You shrugged.
At this point, you propped yourself up with both hands, stared at Spamton's back, and dragged out your voice: "Speaking of all the questions you've asked, I've told you everything—then tell me, what are your dreams? What do you like? Your ideals, your expectations, and how do you want to live?" "You casually threw out a question, but of course, I suppose you don't necessarily need the answer...... After all, everyone has their own secrets and things they are unwilling to easily tell others. It's just that you think it's unfair, and only by revealing everything is it is truly unfair, so you want to ask for an answer.
Then, the narrow shop fell silent, with only shallow breathing for a moment. You waited for his answer, while he remained silent, as if deep in thought.
Then you hear his voice—as usual, strange and inexplicably hoarse, with the sizzling sound of electric currents and the hoarseness of the videotape: "...... I think it's [becoming a big shot]. ”
You rub your chin: "So this is your dream...... Your ideal? Are you living just for this goal?" "At the end, you raised your voice, feeling somewhat incredulous."
Spamton just stayed silent, not answering your question for a moment. And you shrugged, feeling a bit bored: "Is that all? That's just too boring...... Don't you want to see something else, don't want to see higher and farther places? Don't you want to know the unknown of the past? ”
This time, you hear him answer you at an extremely fast pace: "[I want to]." ”
You rubbed your chin, lost in thought, then suddenly understood: "So that's how it is...... So what you love is freedom?" "Of course, this is just a sudden inference. Your words carry hesitation; you're not sure about it."
He just stayed silent and didn't answer your question. Maybe he accepted your answer, or maybe that attitude was just a way to resist. So you know, he probably doesn't want to keep talking, maybe he doesn't want to analyze his own heart to outsiders.
You just shrugged and drew out your voice: "Alright—I know! You probably don't want to say it! But I can promise you, if possible, I'll take you to higher and farther places." ”
This time, he turned to look at you. Now he was looking at you directly, reaching out his hand: "[It's a deal]?" ”
"Of course, it's a deal." You held his hand and shook it.
Although he didn't answer your question directly, and all of this was just your guess, you thought you probably got to know Spamton a bit better...... No, why bother getting to know him better! You don't need that either! You shook your head in panic and met Spamton's gaze, seeming a bit puzzled.
So you straightened up, cleared your throat, and said seriously, "Uh...... It's nothing, I was just thinking about some things in the world of light. Yeah, that's it. "No matter how you hear that, it feels like you're trying to cover it up. But you can't just be honest—seriously! If you really said something about him or something, that would be way too embarrassing!
At least you can't do it. So you just cough twice and change the subject: "Alright, what's for dinner?" "Better to talk about something else."
"...... Cyber Barbecue?" He spoke in a puzzled tone, but you still felt there was a hint of certainty in that tone.
You nodded your chin, and actually, you didn't really care what you ate...... Anyway, it's all the same, just a bit different in taste. So you nodded and readily agreed: "Alright, let's have some barbecue then!" ”
Then you sit in that spot, propping your chin up in a daze. To be honest, time passes quickly, but no one from the shop has come by. You start to wonder why he opened this shop—but forget it, watching his back, you inexplicably feel he won't like this question, so in the end, you bottle your doubts back.
Dinner time was almost over. You stood up, stretched, grabbed your spamton, and headed outside. You closed the shop door and hung up the lock that seemed useless. Then you put the spamton on your shoulder, looked at the pile of trash around you in silence, and sincerely said, "Uh...... Or tell me which way you're heading? ”
Spamton silently looked at your profile, then pointed in the direction: "First, [go straight], then [turn right]." ”
You nodded in satisfaction, glad you had a navigation, followed his instructions, and finally arrived at the Cyber BBQ Restaurant.
I don't know why he seems a bit nervous, but when you step into the barbecue restaurant, that tension eases again. You glance at him in confusion, but you don't get an answer, so in the end, you can only blame it on maybe overthinking it.
In fact, Spamton was just relieved that he hadn't run into any other Addisons.
You found an empty seat by the window and sat down. After ordering, you casually picked up Spamton and let him order, so he wouldn't be unable to reach the table—well, he should still be able to reach the table, as long as he's standing in the seat.
Soon, the ordered dishes arrived. You put the meat slices on the grill, but you still know your limits—after all, Spamton definitely can't touch the grill—so you chimed in, "You have to thank me properly, I'm serving you." Uh, how do you put it? According to your terms, it's like a citizen of light serving a citizen of darkness...... Well, though I don't know what's special about that. ”
You shrugged, took off the grilled meat slices, placed them on the plate in front of Spamton, and then took the meat slices to yourself.
Then you see Spamton dipping a slice of meat in a lethal amount of seasoning, and you're a bit shocked: "...... Hey, it's not like you need to dip it in so much seasoning, right? "You take a look—that's a lethal dose of pepper salt—it's going to make you crazy."
But Spamton only glanced at you, then swallowed it without changing his expression. Well, maybe he just likes that flavor...... No, that's not right. Thinking about the dining experience before, you finally have a belated guess about his situation.
So you clapped your hands and suddenly understood: "Oh! So it turns out you have a taste disorder...... You can't really taste these flavors, right? ”
Spamton nodded silently. He hadn't intended to hide it at all, but he hadn't expected you to take so long to realize it. Probably...... Your reaction was indeed slow, wasn't it?
After hearing this, you happily went off to eat barbecue. Before long, the dinner was over. You burped satisfactorily, went to pay, picked up the Spamton and set it on the floor, then squatted down and poked the little puppet's face, then sternly said, "Ah...... Just finished eating, so go for a walk! I'm not responsible for taking you away, just exercise on your own! ”
That's what he said, but actually, you walked very slowly yourself, just curiously observing the buildings around you. To be honest, you hadn't stopped to really observe the world before, since you were busy preparing for exams and didn't have time to stay. Now, looking at the surrounding buildings and the shining neon lights, you couldn't help but sigh.
At first, Spamton was just walking beside you, and it seemed like he could walk faster. But now that your pace was slow, he couldn't help but slow down.
Watching you curiously look left and right, he couldn't help but say, "Maybe I can introduce [must-see places] to you?" ”
You just shake your head: "Forget it, I'm not here for tourism, just casually taking a look......"
After saying this, you fell silent—probably because no one wanted to break the atmosphere. Before you knew it, you had walked back home.
The days that followed were no different, except this time you didn't stay at home pondering textbooks and problems. Instead, you sat in Spamton's shop and continued studying. At first, you found it a bit novel, but over time you got used to it, since the Dark People had never visited.
Until that day...... Finally, a Dark Folk came to visit, probably the day before you were about to re-enter the game world. You actually don't know any other Dark People except Spamton, and at this moment, you look at the one in front of you with a completely confused expression. Coincidentally, Spamton wasn't there—to be honest, you were a bit annoyed that he suddenly ran out at that moment. Didn't he usually treasure his shop? And now he suddenly said he was going to buy goods and left?!
In any case, you still received this Dark Citizen with a smile, gave him the goods he needed, and collected a certain amount of Dark Coins. However, the Dark Citizen looked flattered, looking very happy, and kept muttering as he left: "I was actually received by the Dark Citizens......" or something like that.
You felt something was off, and after a while, Spamton did come back. It looked like he had indeed gone to buy goods, especially since he had brought back a small cart to push quite a few things. You didn't dare question him further, hesitated to speak but hesitated for a moment. After arranging the items, he looked at your expression and was the first to ask, "...... do you have some kind of [problem]?" I'm very happy to [answer you]. ”
You hesitated for a moment before saying, "I just realized that those Dark Folk ...... Are they very welcoming to the Light Folk of Darkness?" "Or is it that those Dark Folk have never even met the Light Folk before, which is why they're so excited?"
Spamton nodded and answered your question: "Of course, all the [People of Darkness] are happy to serve the [People of Light]. All [People of Darkness] welcome the arrival of the [People of Light]. ”
You rubbed your chin and stared at Spamton. He moved a couple of times, feeling a bit uncomfortable, probably not used to your gaze, since you'd been staring at him the whole time.
So he couldn't help but ask, "...... Y/N, do you have any doubts about this? ”
You couldn't help but nod, paused, and then asked, "If that's the case, then you should be very welcoming to the People of Light—that is, you should welcome me...... But I feel like you actually don't have any special fondness for the People of Light." "You still hold a grudge about the first time we met, even though now you can trust him...... But there are still things from before!
Unexpectedly, he nodded decisively, which surprised even you: "You're absolutely right. Of course, I also welcome the People of Light to visit and take a look." But ......" He hadn't finished speaking before you interrupted him.
You waved your hand and said somewhat indifferently, "But you actually put interests first...... Or rather, what you care about more is yourself? Is it whether you can benefit from it? ”
He remained silent, not agreeing with your answer, but not denying it either. And you didn't mind that much, just shrugged: "Alright, I understand...... Uh, I have one more question—did you deliberately keep me here just now? Maybe you already knew the People of Darkness were coming to buy goods? ”
This time, silence spread between you two once again. You weren't in a hurry; you just stared at him, waiting for him to give you an answer. Maybe he couldn't stand your gaze anymore, or maybe after weighing it out, he decided it was better. After hesitating for a moment, he nodded and admitted decisively: "Yes." ”
You nod thoughtfully, even though he admitted he did it on purpose...... But you don't know why he's doing this. Honestly, you haven't figured it out yet. Thinking about it all the time isn't a good idea. You look at Spamton again, hesitate for a moment, then ask again, "So why?" ”
Alright, you'd better just ask directly!
This time, Spamton was just speechless. Watching you smile, that smile felt a bit strange, so you crossed your arms, touched the goosebumps on your arm, frowned at him, and muttered, "If you won't tell me, then so be it...... Why are you laughing like that! It's kind of scary! ”
He simply kept smiling, then slowly shook his head: 'As you said, no comment.'
Spamton didn’t want to tell you his true intentions. Honestly, maybe even if he told you, you’d still choose to stay, or perhaps you would just leave angrily… and then awkwardly participate in the game again. Either way, you’re both fixed teammates.
But he didn’t dare to take that risk. He didn’t dare to bet on the chances that you would choose the former; he didn’t know what your attitude would be once you discovered his true intentions. Well, maybe he was just scared; he admitted that he cared a little.
So he paused again and said: 'Also, I will keep an appropriate distance, to facilitate your practical work.'
You frowned and looked him up and down: 'Uh… I admit that, but this isn’t exactly the kind of work I enjoy… Anyway, you’re really not lying to me, right?' You were suspicious of this, after all, he had a record, and now, inexplicably, you were on guard.
He, on the other hand, simply shook his head decisively, shutting off both your words and doubts, leaving you no choice but to relax slightly, puffing your cheeks in displeasure: 'Alright, then I hope you’re telling the truth this time… You really aren’t lying to me, right?'
Spamton just smiled: 'Of course, I have no deceptive behavior, Miss Y/N.' When he said this, he was open and honest, and you couldn’t detect any sign of lying.
And indeed, Spamton had a clear conscience; after all… he only kept something from you, how could that count as lying? He hadn’t deceived you about it.
You nodded, still somewhat skeptical: 'Alright, then I’ll trust you… I hope you’re not talking nonsense!'
However, there wasn’t actually much time for you to verify whether this was true or false, because the next day was already the time to enter the game world again. That night, you were unusually nervous, or rather, your heart was pounding. Normally, you could rest a while before switching worlds, but now you couldn’t sleep.
So you decided to disturb Spamton, who was sleeping beside you. You turned and gently shook his shoulder. Spamton opened his eyes and looked at you. Clearly, he wasn’t asleep either.
You smiled satisfactorily and started a casual conversation: 'By the way, what do you think the next world will be like?'
'I don’t know, and why are you lowering your volume?'
You realized you had indeed been speaking softly just now and coughed twice, a bit embarrassed but still self-assured: 'I… I was trying to create an atmosphere! Anyway, I can’t sleep and you seem awake too, so let’s just chat casually!'
You felt Spamton just stared at you speechlessly, and you didn’t feel any embarrassment at all.
'Alright, what’s your topic of discussion?'
You blinked: 'I don’t know.'
After saying this, you both fell into an awkward silence. Honestly, you were just looking for something to talk about… The excitement faded after a few casual words, and you turned over, casually patted the little puppet’s head, and fell into a deep sleep.
When you woke up again, you were already in the game world.

content:
Sptx: I've been watching too many witch hunts: Salem 1692 lately, so this is a more documentary literature ......
20,000 words.
——
[Main Quest: Survive successfully, evade Religious Judgment] Reward: One month of rest
[Side Quest: Ban the Religious Judgment and Save the Remaining Ones] Reward: 100,000 cash + 100,000 Dark Coins
You landed here holding Spamton—why you held him? It's a long story. After all, there was no other way now, at least there was nowhere for him to stay, so he could only let you hold him.
And you hesitantly looked around—or rather, you didn't even have time to take a look, since the surroundings were full of people, or as Spamton put it, all around were people of light, a dense mass that left no time to observe your surroundings. Even a deep breath on your face could only smell human flesh and the stench of rotten iron, and all you could hear were screams, wails, and chaotic pounding.
You silently covered your ears, and after a moment of silence, you still lifted the Spamton onto your shoulder and set it down. Otherwise, if you covered your ears, he'd fall off. There was nowhere for him to land on the ground, especially with the crowd pushing and shoving. If this little thing landed, he'd probably be stepped on.
Spamton also silently covered his ears.
To be honest, you don't even know where you are—after all, it's chaos now. All you can see are heads and silhouettes, and occasionally panicked expressions. You seem to be right in the center of this giant cage—the reason you know it's a cage is because when you look up, all you can see is an iron ceiling, and the crowd around you can't disperse, so you know this must be a cage.
Immediately after, you feel your body sway—not just your imagination, because the others around you also start shaking—after hesitating for two seconds, you realize you are actually behind a carriage, probably outdoors, in other words, this cart is carrying your cage of prisoners somewhere unknown.
You hear the cries of those people grow louder; they seem to be banging on the railing, mumbling something, because you can faintly hear their cries even if you cover your ears.
The carriage seemed to be accelerating, because you felt your body suddenly shaking again, and the people around you were shaking too. The Spamton on your shoulder nearly fell to the ground with the shaking. You quickly let go of your ear and pulled him back, now holding him in your arms again.
And you finally understand what some women are really saying in their loud screams: "I'm not a witch! I didn't do any of those things. The torment those girls suffered has nothing to do with me. I admit there was an evil spirit attacking me, but I have nothing to do with those devils!" ”
And you suddenly realize, what year is it now—it's the 17th century, the worst era of witch hunts, or rather, in this era, women suffered more injustice than usual. You swallowed, hugged the spamton tightly, and suddenly felt a sense of nervousness. Honestly, if there were many people across from you, you really wouldn't be sure you could escape. After all, even if you claimed you had nothing to do with the devil, they would still distrust you and come up with some reason to tie them to the word 'witch.' Some women were even framing women, exposing each other, even for baseless crimes.
Are you really not sure you can succeed, even though you actually haven't done anything—maybe you just have to figure out how to escape? With some hope and speculation, you looked at Spamton in your arms, saw him still covering his ears, took his hand away with one hand, then leaned down slightly and whispered in his ear, "...... Uh, how likely do you think we are to successfully escape?" ”
Spamton silently turned his face to glance at you. He naturally heard those words now, but he didn't know much about history, so he couldn't fully guess what time it was. And you know, the dark Middle Ages were filled with religious trials and abusive punishments, as if church power always stood supreme, standing tat against royal authority.
"I don't know, maybe I need to [check the overall prison rules] to find the best buying strategy?" He hesitated for a moment before quietly answering your question, and you rubbed your chin, stepped back two paces as the carriage shook again, and stopped, hugging Spamton tightly.
"Uh, escaping from a 17th-century prison shouldn't be too difficult...... right? "You whispered, but still a bit uncertain. Maybe you should ask the game system if they're willing to give you your previous weapon. As long as you have an axe or something, you're confident you can break the cage and complete your escape."
Before you could continue discussing, the carriage stopped, and before you could feel suffocated in this crowded cage, you were all driven off and out of the cage. To be honest, the air in the 17th century was indeed fresh, but you didn't have time to feel the chill of the air, because what awaited you next was the trial of the court.
It seemed that fifty or sixty people were held in this cage, and under the strict supervision of the priest, you formed a long line and entered the trial courtroom. To be honest, the courtroom was indeed very simple. The defendant stood behind a wooden railing, the judge sat high on the platform, and several recorders were handwriting something, perhaps not fully recorded, sitting on either side below. The witness sat on one side, while you, the witch candidates waiting for questioning and trial, stood on the other.
Of course, they're all women, only a handful of men, and Spamton in your arms. So you can't help but give him a strange look. Honestly...... Although there are indeed male witches, in this era, they're extremely rare. Right now, you can't guarantee whether he'll really be executed, since the residents of the Dark World seem to have some magic to some extent...... But it probably won't be a problem.
The crowd was packed into a dense crowd, noisy and noisy. The judge knocked on the wooden pole, shouting for silence, and only then did the simple courtroom finally quiet down. You swallowed twice and looked at the defendant standing behind the wooden fence. The woman looked like she was in her sixties or seventies, but her hair was already graying. Even as she walked to the defendant's seat, she trembled continuously, probably unable to take a single step, but her back remained straight, probably believing she had nothing to do with that devil.
But the judge glanced at you first, then the priest standing nearby gave you a meaningful look and said, "One of you is a devil." ”
You pressed your lips together. Honestly, this situation was just too frustrating.
After another round of commotion, you see the girl in the witness stand across from you striking a twisted pose, showing a pained expression and baring her teeth as if being squeezed and squeezed hard. Such a twisted posture seems impossible for ordinary people to pull off. Anyone who sees it would say it's an evil spirit causing trouble.
So the judge knocked on the wooden rope and asked, 'Do you admit to colluding with the devil?' The old woman denied this and declared herself a devout believer. Laughter seemed to spread among the seats as the recorders recorded but were altering something.
The judge ignored his answer, frowning, probably not very happy because he hadn't gotten the answer he wanted. So he simply scolded sternly, "How did you collude with the devil!" ”
"I've already said, I'm not colluding with the devil. I'm not a witch." The old woman repeated this sentence.
"Then tell me, what exactly are these girls?" The judge said, pointing at the girls still moving their bodies, their faces twisted in pain, whose bodies seemed to bear bite marks.
The old woman looked over, then slowly shook her head: "I don't know. In fact, it might be a kind of illness." ”
As the old woman looked over, several of the girls were screaming loudly, claiming they had been brutally tortured by the ghosts she had conjured, twisting parts of their bodies, even twisting their arms.
The judge knocked hard twice more on the wooden rope: "Then how do you explain their current situation?" That's obviously not something a witch could do. ”
"Alright...... I admit, it was the evil spirit that had invaded their bodies. The old woman took two deep breaths; the situation was not favorable for her, so she changed her story.
"So how did you collude with the devil?" The judge repeated the question, and the old woman repeated her earlier answer, firmly stating that she was a devout believer. This remark only caused laughter at the table again, though no one on the witch's side was laughing.
Looking at all of this, you know this trial is inescapable. Rather than being tormented here under trial, it's better to confess to the trumped-up charges early, admit to being a witch colluding with the devil, enter prison sooner, and then figure out how to get out of the place. To be honest, just escaping would be much better for Bi to be interrogated in court.
The trial lasted several hours, and the crowd was once again restless. They were tired of standing, and the elderly woman in the defendant's seat was clearly the same, but the judge still tirelessly asked similar questions.
At this moment, two of the girls screamed and pointed at the beam, claiming that a ghost just like the old woman was hovering on it, mocking them. The other girls also testified that they had indeed witnessed it, and not only that, they also saw another woman conspiring with the old woman to torture them.
Others in the witness stands also began to testify, confirming that they had indeed witnessed the scene.
And the other woman the girls testified about happened to be the next person to be tried, so she too was brought to the defendant's seat.
This time, the woman straightforwardly admitted that she was indeed colluding with the devil. One night, the devil visited her home, strangled her, forced her to sign a contract, and promised that after she achieved her goal and met the target of torturing the girls, she would be given luxurious clothes and beautiful gems in exchange. Not only that, she admitted that she, the old woman, and others would regularly ride sticks into the forest to gather, eating bread, drinking red wine redder than blood, and discussing the next target of torment. She admitted that, besides that, she had seen a tall, strong Black man, probably also a member of the devil. She admitted, or rather, that she was just making up stories—after all, those recorders had gone from drowsy moments ago to now in a lively state, writing furilessly.
You swallowed hard, feeling both fear and admiration for her imagination. In short, no matter what questions the judge asked, the woman admitted it decisively and fabricated a vivid story about it. At this moment, the girls also stopped their contorted movements and pained expressions, as if at that moment, the witchcraft had paused.
Then the judge lowered the wooden rope and declared their crimes, sending them to prison awaiting judgment. But before that, the judge required them to recite the law of faith once to judge whether their faith was faithful. The old woman and woman stammered and only managed to recite it five times in a row. The judge then waved with satisfaction, signaling others to take them away and escort them to prison.
After watching this farce, the next woman was immediately escorted to the defendant's dock, and you whispered in Spamton's ear, whispering, "When we go upstairs, just declare ourselves guilty. There's no need to wait for them to ask anything. I don't want to make up stories...... Just send us straight to prison." ”
Just watching this trial process is exhausting.
Spamton just shook his head, not quite agreeing with your opinion: "I think we still have an opportunity, maybe we can get an acquittal, since those girls are complete strangers." ”
Indeed, no one knows you. Maybe that's the best case, but maybe it's also the biggest problem, so you gently shake your head and dismiss Spamton's opinion: "But no one knows us, which only proves we're devils who came from nowhere...... Those witnesses will definitely identify us that way; we can't believe they would speak for us. ”
Indeed, although you don't know why these people attack each other, you can't stop maliciously speculating about human nature. Even if you know this isn't the right thing to do, maybe you should believe there is still a good side to human nature, but at least you can't trust these people right in front of you.
Of course, the main issue now is still to persuade Spamton...... Thinking this, you hear his voice again: "Maybe we can consider [giving it a try]?" ”
Honestly...... You think there's no chance of even trying. Even though Spamton says this, you have no expectations at all, so you just look down at Spamton in your arms: "Are you sure you want to give it a try?" "You think that's completely impossible."
Spamton nodded, "You decided to trust him this time. If it's just a try, you won't lose out. At most, you'll just waste a little time in this game world, but that's not a big deal." After all, time in the outside world isn't really passing away.
So you took a deep breath and continued whispering, "I'm not sure if they'll count us as one ...... Anyway, I'll take you up with me later, but I think it's better if you don't speak. After all, even though I understand what you're saying, there's no guarantee these people won't think you're strange and might have turned you into a wizard before you can defend yourself." "It's not impossible. After all, you actually used a bit of mental power to figure out what he really meant."
Spamton looked up at you, and you couldn't help but feel a hint of reproach in his gaze. So you couldn't help but cough twice and argue, "I'm telling the absolute truth! That's just how it is...... Alright, stop looking at me like that! ”
During the conversation, another woman ahead of you was brought up for trial. The judge's wooden rope was lowered once more, adding a sense of tension for no reason. You swallowed hard; even knowing you had to go up and defend yourself, you probably wouldn't escape being imprisoned. Thinking about it this way, it really is easiest to confess your identity as a witch right away.
…… But since we wanted to give it a try, we might as well give it a try.
So you pinched Spamton's cheek again and casually added, "So I'm warning you again, don't say a word...... Otherwise, I have no idea what the judge will rule. "You said, poking the puppet's little face.
He seemed silent, or maybe he simply didn't want to deal with you. In any case, you didn't really care, just quieted down and waited for the priest to bring you to the dock.
Soon, the priest tied you up and led you to the defendant's bench, or maybe you were simply following behind him, since you were still holding Spamton. But when you walked to the defendant's bench, seeing the dark crowd below the witness stand and the eyes staring at you as if waiting for you to make a mistake, you suddenly felt nervous and didn't know what to say.
A commotion erupted from the witness stands, as if they were arguing something. Some said, 'What you're holding is definitely a demon!' Some say maybe it's a puppet specifically designed for witchcraft! Others say it's blatantly showing that you've signed a contract with the devil—you're carrying the devil's incarnation!
…… You started to feel a headache coming on. To be honest, just now you only thought that getting Spamton to speak might cause misunderstandings, but now, even if he didn't speak, just disguising himself as a puppet would still cause misunderstandings. You glanced at the witness stand, racking your brains over what to do.
At that moment, you hear Spamton in your arms speak: "I'm not a [devil]." You are so frightened you quickly cover his mouth, wanting to tell him not to speak anymore, but with so many eyes in the witness stand watching you, you don't have time to say that.
Then you hear someone gasp at the witness stand, then loudly shout that this puppet is definitely a devil, can even speak, or is possessed by an evil spirit. And you, carrying this puppet, are definitely a genuine witch, possibly cursing everyone right away!
Immediately, everyone gasped in shock, as if all of this was extremely likely to happen.
You can't help but take a deep breath, thinking to yourself, if only you could actually cast spells, I'd immediately silence these people and escape from here.
The judge knocked twice more on the wooden rope, ordering everyone to quiet down, and only then did the witness stand gradually return to its quiet.
Then you see the judge look at you seriously, stroke his drooping white beard, and ask, "Do you have any explanation for the puppet in your arms?" ”
You were silent for a moment before struggling to organize your words and speak: "He is a living being, not just a simple puppet." ”
You hear the crowd gasp again; those girls are moving their bodies, striking even more twisted poses. You deliberately keep your gaze from looking that way.
The judge tapped the wooden rope twice more. You felt Spamton reach out to take away the hand covering his mouth, but you just tightly covered his mouth. Then he began to struggle in your arms. To keep him from falling, you had to hold him tightly with your other hand, while the judge stared at you intently.
"If that's the case, how did you use the witchcraft puppet in your hand to perform the curse?" He seemed completely ignorant of your explanation earlier, or maybe he heard but simply didn't care.
You sighed silently in your heart, thought for a moment, and answered, "I have never engaged in any witchcraft. Besides, this puppet is not a witchcraft puppet; it is a living being." ”
When answering this question, your grip on your hand inevitably loosens a bit, and Spamton finally breaks free from yours. Before you can cover his mouth again, he speaks quickly: "There is absolutely no connection to [Witchcraft] or 'Free Measures,' only 'Value Procurement' services." ”
You silently covered your face, slapped your cheek, and thought to yourself, this is really bad—we had promised him not to speak, yet he still wants to interrupt...... Now everything has become complicated.
Sure enough, you hear the crowd on the other end whispering again. Some mutter, they must be possessed by evil spirits, or how could they speak such twisted and unintelligible language, noisy and harsh. Some say she's definitely a witch colluding with the devil, and the puppet you're carrying is definitely a devil. And because of its deep connection to the devil, it's the reason you brought the devil to court. Another says, maybe the devil has already fallen in love with the witch, so he wants to go with you...... Soon after, the others seem convinced by this excuse and start gasping for breath.
The judge tapped the wooden rope twice more, then asked the next question: "What kind of witchcraft did you use to torture those girls?" He was referring to the girls whose bodies were twisted and their expressions twisted.
And you can only helplessly repeat, "I have never performed any witchcraft." ”
Fortunately, Spamton didn't interrupt this time. Perhaps he realized that a miraculous comeback in this situation was unlikely.
The people in the witness stand and those girls are watching you carefully again, and then they start a new round of argument, but this time the topic is a bit different.
You hear them whispering and gossiping, saying they've never seen you before. Maybe you're a witch from the outside world who comes to cast curses, or maybe you're sent by the devil to torture them. Some people start trembling, afraid that the next person to cast spells will be themselves. Others suddenly show expressions of pain, their limbs twisting in strange ways. They look at you, claiming that although you don't look at them, your soul is flying high above the beam, looking at them with mockery. Honestly, you didn't want to damage the crops, since they were all painstakingly cultivated by farmers of this era. And as you walked along the road, maybe it was just your imagination, but you actually heard the sound of hooves.
You stopped and saw that about a thousand meters ahead, the army was rushing toward you. Perhaps you didn't even need to go out specifically to report this to the army; they would come to forcefully suppress the heretical trials—or perhaps an even harsher trial was about to begin, something you cannot imagine.
So you looked at Spamton on your shoulder, and just then, at that moment, he was also looking at you. You cleared your throat a bit awkwardly and asked, "...... Do we still need to report to that army?" ”
Spamton's voice turned serious: "No, I think [you] need a [perfect dodge]. ”
You understood what he meant, but the area around was all wheat fields, and there seemed to be nowhere for you to hide—you did spot a tree not far away, and it seemed like a forest farther away, maybe you could hide in. Now, gritting your teeth, you ran toward that tree.
The army moved quickly; before you even reached the tree, swords and knives were coming at you, probably seeing you as an enemy.
You curse silently twice in your heart, while Spamton tugs at your clothes to keep you from throwing you off. Seeing that you might not be able to dodge your current position, you roll on the ground to dodge the attack coming at you. You curse twice more in your heart, saying these people are killing people indiscriminately—a bloody, brutal army. Even if this army conquers that place, those witches might not have a good end. Your heart suddenly sinks. Perhaps it would be better to go back now and try to break the cages and let those women out, but of course, you have no time to run back.
You gritted your teeth, dodged the gun that was thrusting at you again, and ran toward the woods. No one caught up. At first, a few people tried to catch up, but they were quickly pulled back. Maybe they felt that chasing only someone like you was too lowly, and since you were a woman, not a man, you posed much of a threat to them.
…… Thinking of this makes you inexplicably angry. It is precisely because of ignorance and discrimination without any reason that countless women have ended up like that, and why there is the witch trial. But this kind of thing isn't suitable to discuss at this moment; you just ran into the woods, hoping to hide for a while.
Coincidentally, a carriage was parked by the edge of the woods. You glanced at it and asked Spamton, "Do you remember the way to the prison?" "You think that army is unreliable, so you should release the people yourself."
Spamton nodded.
So you relaxed, untied the horse, shook the reins, and started galloping. To be honest, you weren't very familiar with how to ride a horse, so your posture was a bit awkward and it always felt uncomfortable, but you couldn't worry about that because you only had 22 hours.
"Then, you will guide us." You took a deep breath and said.
Spamton sits on your shoulder and grabs your neck. Although it's hard to find direction on this barren land, he at least remembers how the car moved.
So he said, "First, go straight, then after about six hours, perform the right-turn procedure, and after twelve hours, proceed with the left-turn procedure." ”
You swallowed hard. Well, time was tight, and I didn't know if I would make it in time. And if I happened to get lost, it would be even worse—so as you steered your horse forward, you said, "Alright, if it's time, just remind me and I'll turn again." ”
Spamton just nodded aimlessly against the wind. Then, when the time was about right, he checked the time on the screen and reminded you to turn. You worked well together, and in the end, you arrived at the outskirts of the prison with less than two hours left.
The countdown had turned red, and you couldn't help but swallow nervously, stopping your horse. You carefully bent over, using the tall cornfield as a cover to approach the prison gate. That was just the place outside where stone bricks were randomly stacked, or rather, the stone walls were all towering, but it was obvious that they hadn't been carefully maintained, since the mottled and mossy on top were visible. There were two guards, yawning at the entrance to the prison.
You recognize these two guards, or rather, you are very familiar with them, since during those days when you were imprisoned, it was these two guards who brought you meals. It is evident that they weren't really strict about guarding their posts, after all, one of the guards was almost asleep, probably thinking that the prisoners couldn't possibly escape and that the outside world couldn't do anything to help them.
Unfortunately, you arrived. You continued to follow the cover of the cornfield around to the side of the prison, but you couldn't get any closer, after all, the surroundings were all barren open land. Spamton also lay on your shoulder, trying to keep a low profile to make sure you weren't discovered.
And you looked at the two guards, thought for a moment, and chose to quietly discuss with Spamton: 'You should be fast. Can you run ahead to attract their attention first, while I knock them out from behind?'
Spamton glanced at you, but because of his glasses you couldn't see his emotions clearly, so you just coughed twice.
He was silent for a long moment before softly responding, 'Okay. But I hope you can succeed.'
You patted your own chest, full of confidence: 'Of course I can, trust me!'
Then Spamton jumped off your shoulders. And you took a deep breath, fully aware that you could hear the sound of your own heartbeat. You stared intently at the two guards, and sure enough, when Spamton appeared, the two guards moved, seemingly murmuring something about a witch's cursed puppet. You also sprang out from the cornfield, sprinted behind them, and before they could turn around, struck each of them on the neck. They had already closed their eyes and fallen to the ground before the two guards could turn their heads in stunned terror.
You took a couple of deep breaths, your whole body relaxing from the tense state, crouched down and took a bunch of keys off one of the guards, and then picked up the Spamton walking towards you and put it back on your shoulder.
At this moment, the countdown is only just under an hour, and you don't even know why time has passed so quickly. But now you are overly excited, perhaps as a result of staying up all night, and it is only just dawn.
…Dawn, the moment of daybreak, is also a time of rebirth; everything should become bright and beautiful. So you hurriedly crossed the prison gate carrying the bunch of keys, opening the doors of their cells for the women under their surprised gazes. There were also unfamiliar faces, seemingly new witches who had been imprisoned just yesterday, and you unlocked their cells one by one as well.
And then, when those witches—no, just ordinary, pitiful, and innocent fragile women—walked out of the prison, you waved your hands and casually said, 'God is merciful and has forgiven your sins. If the court still wants to judge you, just tell them that the angels have forgiven your sins and purified the traces of making a pact with the devil on you.'
When saying this sentence, you inappropriately thought that perhaps you were indeed infected by Spamton, and now you even speak this kind of deceptive words.
And those women, with tears of gratitude, bowed to you, nodded, and some even knelt and kowtowed, saying thanks to God's mercy, thanks to the angel's redemption, and only then did those women run out.
You also don't know where those women will go, because you looked at the screen and saw that there were only a few minutes left, and the side quest progress was still only at 50%.
You were exhausted and gave up, simply sitting cross-legged on the ground with a wry smile. Later, when the guards finally woke up and rushed in to try to capture you, you smiled and disappeared in front of them while holding Spamton.
And then you heard the system's virtual fireworks.
