content:
You exhaled and came back to your senses, only to realize you were still standing in the alley where you left, as if time around you hadn't flown at all. You saw the Dark Folk, who had just started to take a step, slowly land the next. You still held Spamton in your arms, and everything seemed the same—except you felt a bit nervous. What if you were teleported away on the street in one go? But fortunately, it seemed like there was only one game left. At worst, you'd just find an excuse later, you thought.
Then you looked at Spamton. You lifted the corner of your mouth, deciding to temporarily forget about the previous game world, nor to worry about how this world might connect with the light world you were in. You just lowered your head and looked at Spamton: "...... So, please show me the way from the main road to the Queen's mansion, or else I'll really get lost. After all, I would get dizzy from walking through all these messy alleys." "I wonder how he got used to it...... You mutter to yourself, but Spamton didn't pay much attention to this. He didn't intend to explain it to you, since he had spent a long time wandering through these dark alleys and had tried to find a way out. That's why he set his sights on the armor in the basement of the Queen's mansion.
He ...... He wanted to change his fate anew, completely and thoroughly. He didn't fully believe in that so-called game system, the so-called heavenly wishing machine; he would rather have done it himself.
Spamton nodded; he had no reason to argue with you, so you breathed a sigh of relief and followed Spamton's advice and circled back. Honestly, you almost got dizzy again—but Spamton yanked your face hard, and you finally snapped back to reality.
At this moment, you both stood at his shop door. You were quite familiar with the road that wound from his shop to your own home, so you quickly returned to your doorstep, which was at the top of a main road. Then you looked at Spamton with great interest, lifted him up, and met your gaze; "Once you're here, walk from this avenue to the entrance of the Queen's mansion. It should be feasible, right?"
Spamton seemed to sigh helplessly, but he was aware of some of your habits. In fact, when he took you around the alley before, he had somewhat forgotten that you might be a bit directionally challenged and your memory was inconsistent...... Well, this was a lesson he taught himself. From now on, he shouldn't expect your navigation skills to be good.
And now he just nodded: "Of course, the cooperation terms have been confirmed. I will [start navigation service] for you." ”
Alright, he agreed to endure it himself, and Spamton understood that, but being held in your arms felt better than sitting on your shoulder, and ...... His head was actually resting on the soft spot on your chest, so sometimes he would stutter when he gave you directions.
Whenever this happens, you start to wonder: "Spamton, what's wrong? Are puppets also having performance issues...... Is it time to replace the parts?" "As you spoke, you picked him up and examined it carefully.
For some reason, Spamton's little puppet's face was flushed red, and steam was rising from above his head. Whether it was out of anger or anger, his voice had become smoother again: "No [Performance Issues]!" "My [Program Running Well]!" "He felt like he was being confused by you. There's no such thing as maintenance performance for puppets, and he's not exactly a puppet...... Well, Spamton couldn't quite explain what state he should be in right now.
You blinked, feeling that something was off about him, but you couldn't smell it, so you dragged out the sound with an 'oh' and then picked Spamton back into your arms.
In short, it seems like every time you hear his voice stutter a bit, you repeat the same routine. You seem to be endlessly holding up Spamton, asking almost the same questions in different ways. Spamton is quite patient, but each time he answers you with similar answers.
And as the walking journey unknowingly stretched on, you finally reached the destination—the entrance of the Queen's mansion. Unexpectedly, there were no Dark Folk guarding the entrance. If you weren't so uninterested, you'd probably want to sneak in and take a look.
But now you just blinked, looked at Spamton, and no matter what, confirmed again: "So, I have to go back into the Queen's mansion basement too?" ”
Spamton hesitated for a moment, then nodded: "Yes, when I was moving from [Commercial Store] [Coordinates: Location]. ”
And you nodded knowingly, indicating you probably understood: "I understand...... Then let's head back now. After wandering around for a long time, I'm tired too." "Besides, just now, you inexplicably entered another world and embarked on a rather thrilling journey...... Although your body isn't exhausted yet, your mind is indeed very exhausted.
"Or can you complete the [Self-Return] task without relying on the [Navigation System]?" Just then, you turn around and then hear Spamton's puzzled voice.
You pondered for two seconds, then nodded with difficulty: "Alright...... Then shall I give it a try? "To be honest, you're actually a bit eager to try. You also want to know if you can actually walk back on your own."
As it turned out, although you almost turned into a fork and ended up in the opposite direction, after countless hardships, you still arrived at your destination—your front door. Yes, Spamton kept his word and really didn't give you any hints. Even when you walked completely into the fork, there was no other reaction. This little puppet was quite good at pretending, you thought to yourself. But because the surrounding buildings were so unfamiliar, after walking a long distance, you finally realized something was wrong, so you hurried back.
At this moment, standing at your doorstep again, you finally breathe a sigh of relief. Then you look down at Spamton and complain, "You really know how to pretend...... Why won't you say anything to me? I didn't say a word even when I reached a fork in the road. "But actually, you didn't mean to blame him. You know that if he disappeared later, you'd be the only one on this road by yourself, with no company or navigation system.
…… Just like your life path, the person who accompanied you will disappear at some point, so you don't dare promise Spamton forever, because you don't know when you'll disappear, or if one day you'll break your promise and stop accompanying you. Only then do you realize your words are actually contradictory, seemingly ...... Even your own heart is contradictory. Maybe it's just because of that sentence, like warm water...... So what?
Spamton's response was pretty much what you imagined, except the last half of his sentence left you stunned for a moment.
He seemed to be speaking very seriously: "Because for the upcoming [Road Voyage], I can't accompany [you], can't serve as your [navigation system], so [you] have to work your own. But after that, I will always [fulfill my duties] of your [navigation system]. ”
You were stunned for a moment, lowering your gaze. Unexpectedly, you didn't answer his question. Spamton was nervous for a moment, wondering if he had said the wrong thing, but he was certain this was his true feelings. He thought maybe you would like it too.
But you just silently hugged the Spamton, skillfully returning to the shop inside the garbage dump, opening the door, sitting in your familiar spot, and placing the Spamton on the seat by the counter.
At this moment, you were looking at each other directly, since Spamton's seat was a bit higher. But when you looked into his eyes, even though through those glasses you couldn't really tell what emotions he was feeling, you still said seriously: "...... Alright, I don't know how to answer you, but why can you so easily promise me forever? ”
You know, that word is never from his faulty recording, so it could only be his true feelings. You tremble at the weight of those words.
Spamton also noticed the faint worry on your face. To be honest, he didn't really know what you were worried about—after all, the word 'forever' was something he could say very easily, since he used to sell things like 'Always offer you a discount.' But for you, it was probably different. Of course, he could also sense the weight behind his words.
He also had no intention of changing his wording...... Because during these days, he had already made up his mind.
So Spamton just lowered his head, seemingly trying to hide his emotions, but he simply spoke: "For you and me, it will always be [Dying of old age]." His voice carried a hint of determination even he couldn't notice, perhaps ...... It was a kind of reckless resignation.
Since he was to die peacefully, it meant that, no matter what, he could only be entangled for the rest of his life...... When they first met, he hadn't thought about it that way, nor did he know things would turn out like this, but he was content with it.
You bit your lip: "So you mean growing old together?" Although I still don't understand why you said it so easily...... But I think, according to what you said before, that since I'm like warm water, I think one day I will face a fate of self-destruction. "As you spoke, your voice began to tremble.
Indeed, you know very well that without this system, if you had always been in the world of light and never knew the existence of the dawn and darkness, you would have always clashed with your parents over your own life, and you would have been driven to self-destruction by the unbearable pressure from your parents and ongoing work pressure. Maybe at that moment, you would choose to end your own life. Maybe it was because your previous perspective was too narrow, and you could only see these things, so you couldn't escape the whirlpool dragging you down. But now, no matter what, you don't really care much about what happened before.
Because you see a wider world, you meet so many people, you can accomplish many things, you get to know Spamton, or actually, you learn a lot from him as well.
“…… Maybe I'm heading toward a [self-destructive program], but I need a [chance to try], and I also need [your] sincere help.' Spamton simply replied like this, still not looking up at you.
“…… That's exactly why I don't dare say 'forever' anymore. I always feel...... Wait, what are you saying? "You wanted to keep talking to yourself, but noticed Spamton's words, so you hurriedly cut it off.
"[Self-Destruct Procedure]." He patiently explained to you.
At this moment, you feel a bit lost. If that's the case...... Spamton is not a complete atheist either; he is also a half-believer, or rather, you are also lost on your own path. Without anyone else intervening, it may ultimately lead to one outcome: destruction.
Or rather, there is only the established path of madness and failure.
You swallowed hard: "Since you say that, then in some ways, we're actually similar people?" "For some reason, you suddenly feel like laughing, but you know now is not the right time to laugh out loud.
Spamton didn't answer your question; he just looked up and gave you a deep look. You couldn't read the meaning in his eyes and were about to ask more, when you saw the man named Kris walking over with something to discuss.
Sitting here in your seat, you can easily see the guests coming and going outside the window. Most of them are Dark People. This is the first Light Folk you've seen in Cyber City besides you. However, you have no interest in inquiring with him, and you don't know what Spamton had just said to him earlier. In any case, you just nudged Spamton: "Your Light Folk guest has arrived." Your voice was very calm.
But the unanswered questions still linger in your heart, urgently hoping for an answer.
However...... At least for now, there probably won't be any chance. You watch as Spamton receives this Citizen of Light, and then, for some reason, they actually transfer it to the floppy disk Kris holds. The shop naturally closes. Your mouth twitches, but you still know this is probably the timing Spamton mentioned, so you walk out of the shop too.
That Citizen of Light quickly walked away, though no one knew where he went. Anyway, although it was a bit troublesome, you still worked hard to dig up your memories and quickened your pace toward the Queen's mansion. Although there were no guards at the entrance, there were some in the corridor, and ...... You got lost in the mansion again, splendidly wandering inside.
You helplessly scratched your head, searched for a long way, bypassed several color card butlers, and finally found what seemed to be an entrance leading underground...... Obviously, it was just a hidden entrance, perhaps not intended for anyone to discover it. Somehow, you had a bad feeling, hoping Spamton hadn't done anything bad...... Anyway, you swallowed hard before slowly walking down the stairs. In this dim room, the steps were long, as if they could never see end. No wonder Spamton called this place the Underground Abyss. You kept thinking, but after all, you had reached the very bottom.
The sound of water, ethereal and unknown, echoed through this ethereal yet vast room. All around was silence, with only the sound of water coming from who knows where. Then what you saw was green moss crawling over the walls. It was clear the basement was an abandoned place, uncleaned for a long time, but you had come through unimpeded—the barrier at the basement entrance looked like it had been broken.
And you don't know if you're late. If you ask me, this basement actually feels more like a prison. Go a bit further and you'll see three tracks, and then you follow the tracks—the first thing you see is the silhouettes of three small cars, the familiar Lightborn, and two others whose names you don't know, and they're holding weapons...... Well, then guess the first two are Lightborn. Because the last one doesn't have a weapon, you have to roughly label him as a Darkborn.
And Spamton, for some reason, actually changed his form. Now...... It seemed like he was wearing a suit of armor. In short, he looked taller and larger, with a pair of wings behind him, though those wings didn't look very useful. And above him hung countless green threads...... You saw those threads, then fell silent, finally shaking your head helplessly. This scene looked like something like a puppet controlled by threads performing the final drama.
Because those three had their backs to you and didn't notice your arrival, Spamton raised his arm, and you saw the tip of that arm looked like a cannon barrel, looking like it was about to fire some kind of laser. Spamton clearly saw you arriving here from the basement entrance. You were a bit far away, and through your glasses, you couldn't tell what kind of mood he was feeling. But it was obvious that his earlier anxiety had improved a lot, leaving the three across from him a bit confused. And obviously, his movements were much more cautious. It was the first time you learned that this world had a battle mode, more like some kind of bullet hell attack game...... Might as well just smash it into the water pipe directly, you muttered to yourself.
Of course, you also saw him mouth shape toward you, telling you to hurry and [help] him, to [lend a hand]. You feel the veins on your forehead bulge. You've never been familiar with this combat style before, so of course you have no idea. Besides, no matter when you enter the Dark World, you never have a weapon! Unless you treat the books you transfer from the Light World every time as weapons!
Although you grit your teeth and get annoyed by Spamton's lip movements, you still focus your attention carefully. Fortunately, the game system is still usable, so you pull out a water pipe.
Then you silently carried the hose forward. Their battle had reached a tense, or rather white-hot state. On the track, Spamton was moving, and the three small cars were moving as well. You had to run to catch up with them. Of course, what if those moving cars hit you later? Forget it, you couldn't worry about that. By the time you were almost there, Spamton was only hanging with a single thread. You always feel that if the last green thread breaks, the whole show ends. So you don't care about it anymore. You immediately smash the water pipe at the purple Lightfolk in the center. She reacts quickly, countering your attack with her axe. Looking at Spamton, it seems like she's losing her mind, shaking violently for a while. You can't bother to continue this hasty and pointless battle, just hurriedly running along the track.
After all, you could see that the thread already had a crack in the middle, gradually tearing, stretching, and stretching. It would probably snap completely soon. You ran over, put away the hose, and when the thread finally snapped, you caught Spamton—well, you only held his upper body, since it was too heavy for you. You cursed in your heart, thinking the armor looked useless except for its fur. You didn't understand why Spamton was so persistent.
You're not an idiot, just a bit slow to react. Of course, you can guess that Spamton had Kris help him obtain this set of armor. Maybe this was originally a secret hidden in the basement.
The three people opposite you are still watching the two of you warily. You have a headache coming on, not knowing how to explain this situation. Speaking of which, you noticed that after Spamton broke free from those threads and fell off, he became completely immobile. So, the drama of the final act is basically over.
So you sighed deeply. No matter what, you genuinely felt troubled by the situation, but you had no choice but to explain. So you pointed at Spamton: "We're partners, and he still owes me money and hasn't been repaid. I can't just stand by and watch him die here." You just made up an excuse offhandedly, then you saw Spamton glaring at you fiercely. You didn't know where he got the strength from, but you glared at him too. Then you activated your dark coin system—after all, your assets were already split evenly. After calculating the compensation, you took out the dark coins for the three of them.
Then you rubbed your brow, looking a bit troubled, and said, "I can only compensate you for this money first. As for the incident where I hit someone with a hose in a panic just now...... If you want to blame someone, blame Spamton. He asked me to help, and you can settle the score with him later." You felt Spamton glaring at you fiercely again. Well, maybe he thought compensation was completely unnecessary...... But this isn't some game. You just need to beat the boss and clear it; it's just a necessary task, that's reality. So every single item needs to be clearly distinguished.
However, when you arrived, you vaguely heard the term 'heart-shaped object' again. It seems Spamton hopes to obtain what he once hoped for through other Lightfolk.
The three opposite sides accepted your dark coins. You watched them huddle together, chattering and discussing something unknown. You couldn't hear clearly, just knelt on the ground holding Spamton, then lowered your head to look at him. You saw those chaotic, broken threads wrapped around this body, as if it were an endless path of fate.
You tried searching for the spot of that floppy disk on this body, and you actually managed to touch it. You tried to withdraw the floppy disk, but the body had completely lost its owner and collapsed to the ground. The floppy disk disappeared from your hand, replaced by Spamton sitting on the armor, though the green threads still wrapped around him as if they were restraints.
You pondered for two seconds, then lowered your head and carefully untangled the threads, then held him back in your arms. As for that useless body, you tossed it to the ground.
The three on the other side seemed to have made a plan. Anyway, they've gotten out of the car and turned to leave the basement. You carry Spamton toward the exit as well. Once you leave that body, Spamton is free again. Nestled in your arms, it seems he's regaining some strength. Maybe everything just now has gone beyond what he imagined. He's still a bit unwilling to accept it, and that's how it goes...... You think you two seem like villains again. Look, you just gave someone who looks like the protagonist's team with a steel rod.
Anyway, you cleared your throat twice and gave Spamton a look to tell him not to speak recklessly, but he still spoke: "No, we're not just a 'business partner'—we're in a 'boyfriend and girlfriend relationship.'" You wanted to cover his mouth, but it was already too late. In this empty basement, that unpleasant sound with the crackling of electric currents echoed back and forth, countless echoes. You were feeling a bit hopeless, but you still covered his mouth and shot him a fierce glare. Spamton glared back at you. You knew what he meant—that he was telling the truth. You had no reason to stop him. After spending so much time together, you could at least understand his thoughts.
You lowered your voice, sounding rather annoyed, and said to him, "When we get back, isn't it the same for us to discuss these things in private?" "Anyway, those three people ahead aren't even acquaintances, so we probably won't run into each other again."
But Spamton just shook his head, as if to tell you that of course it was different. Even though you don't know exactly what was different, because you saw the three people in front now turned to look at you. That familiar Dark Citizen's hair seemed to cover his eyes, and he remained expressionless. In short, you couldn't tell what emotions he was feeling—maybe he just turned to glance at you. The mood of the second Purple Citizen of Light was easy to see through her expression. She was full of shock, pointing at you as if wanting to say something, but was stopped by another Dark Citizen...... Hmm, this Dark Citizen looked like a sheep.
You still don't know what's so different about all this. Spamton probably wouldn't want to tell you either, but those three turned around and hurriedly walked down the stairs, leaving through the basement door. No one knows where they went. Of course, their future has nothing to do with you; right now, you only care about your future with Spamton.
You let go of Spamton's mouth and, out of curiosity, asked one more question: "So why did you insist on saying that just now? You should know that what I said back then was just to save you and make up a lie......
“…… But I believe that since [you] have agreed to a boyfriend and girlfriend relationship, we should help others [fully awaken]. ”
You tugged at the corner of your mouth and whispered, "But that's not necessary, is it...... I think some things are enough as long as the two of us know each other, right? ”
Spamton nodded and then shook his head, still insisting: "Some things are natural, and this one is blatant." ”
You scratched your hair and shrugged: "Alright, if you want to do this, then so be it...... So, is it really forever?" "So many people are curious, and so many, maybe because of a fleeting moment of anxiety, you can't help but ask this question.
Spamton nodded: "Of course." ”
You opened your mouth, wanting to say something for a moment, but your mind was in turmoil, and you didn't know what to ask first. So in the end, you just sighed: "Alright, then let's head back first. It's almost noon, let's just pick any place to eat...... Ah, is there anything you want to eat? ”
"I think it's the [Selectable Recipe]."
“…… Oh, then let's go have hotpot together! I don't care, I've worked hard today anyway, I need to treat myself well. "You puffed out your cheeks as you spoke. You know, you got pulled by Spamton twice this morning, went through a game, and finally came to the basement to carry out Spamton's rescue plan. Your stomach was already starving.
Spamton seemed to sigh: "[Arbitrary Choice]." "He didn't intend to stop you, but you didn't quite understand what he said, so you couldn't help but ask him again."
"In that case, is there anything you want to eat? I'll order it when we get to the hotpot restaurant." ”
He helplessly looked up, thought for a moment, then shook his head: "[Indulge] your [best preferences]. ”
You muttered something under your breath again, probably wondering why Spamton had no choice at this point. Of course Spamton could hear it, and you knew that at such close range, he definitely could hear.
So you double-check: "You really don't have anything you want to eat?" Even the taste is fine. ”
He sighed again: "Repeat broadcast again, it's a choice of [arbitrary]." ”
After all, for Spamton, his sense of taste is numb, barely tasting anything, so it doesn't matter what he eats. He thinks you know this too.
Sure enough, you just pressed your lips together and looked at him with some annoyance: "Alright, of course I know that whatever you eat tastes pretty much the same...... I just want to know what tastes relatively good to you. ”
Spamton was silent for a moment. Actually, to him, the flavors were almost the same...... The same bland taste, without any extra flavors, unless he used excessive seasoning, to taste the same. But if you only talk about which food tastes a bit better...... As for texture, he hesitated for a moment before answering your question.
"Maybe it's the [ice-cold cold drink moment]? [Unlimited free ice cream]?" "If that's the case, the texture is actually pretty good, after all, it's cool and smooth...... It's not that other foods aren't tasty.
You rubbed your chin and nodded, "Alright, I'll order you an ice cream later." "Anyway, if it's a hotpot restaurant...... There probably are snacks like this too, right? If not, I'll just go buy it outside.
As she spoke, you also arrived at the hotpot restaurant. It was the same place you used to frequent. The owner of the Dark People here knew you and warmly welcomed you to your usual seats.
However, before you even sat down, you noticed that the usual neat and clean place had a piece of cheese on top, which looked perfectly intact. You didn't know why there was cheese here, and you couldn't help but glance at the owner of the Dark People.
He wiped the sweat from his forehead, grabbed a broom, and was about to sweep the cheese away. But as soon as the broom touched the cheese, a group of purple rats suddenly jumped out—you know, these are also Dark People, though you've never bothered to remember their names. Including this Dark Folk boss, who seemed to be one of the butlers who previously worked at the Queen's mansion.
Then you silently hugged Spamton, somehow getting swept into this bullet-hell turn-based combat game. On your side, besides you and Spamton, there was no one else, and the other side was only a bunch of rats.
You grit your teeth a bit: "This counts as the restaurant not cleaning properly...... Honestly, can't I just use a hose to kill these rats directly?" As you spoke, you eagerly pulled out your own hose. You didn't care about the turn-based rules of the bullet hell, and surprisingly, you didn't feel too bound by these rules. Maybe it's because you never believed in them deep down.
For some reason, Spamton, who was holding him in your arms, inexplicably trembled, and just as you looked down at him in confusion, he tried hard to shake his head: "...... [no], maybe [you] absolutely must [not try]." ”
You scratched your head and hissed, "...... Is it just because these mice are also Dark People? "You thought for a long time, and the one that seems to look most like a real mouse seems to be the real one. If you remember correctly, the Dark Folk are somewhat made from objects, but you just can't figure out what Spamton actually is.
Spamton hesitated for a moment; in fact, he didn't care much about how you handled these rats...... But since you are a citizen of light, in some ways you might be different.
So he still seriously told you: "To some extent, your behavior pattern might be similar to murder." From the Baidu Encyclopedia entry: Murder. ”
You scratch your head again and shrug: "Ah...... But honestly, I don't really mind. But maybe it's better not to do it this way. I don't want to return to the Light World and see my property damaged or tell me I have someone else's property because I was damaged......
You grumbled reluctantly, but in the end put away the hose and operated the mousetrap—to be honest, you're quite familiar with this method of catching mice, since your previous rental room always had mice and cockroaches, so you easily caught those mice and threw them all out with ease. You don't want to be accused of damaging someone else's property tomorrow and having to pay compensation.
At this moment, the bullet hell turn-based rules disappeared. You saw the boss who had been hiding somewhere and stomping around now stand beside you again, bowing respectfully: "Thank you, miss, for resolving the possibility of a kitchen crisis." Today's hotpot is free for you. "As he spoke, he wiped the invisible sweat from his forehead, probably genuinely embarrassed by his earlier act of staying far away.
You don't hold back; if you get free orders, you actually feel you deserve it...... After all, you don't want to go hungry hunting mice.
So now you sit in your seat holding the Spamton, open the menu, and order a whole series of dishes. If you can't finish it, you'll have to deal with it. Plus, it's free to order, basically a buffet—order as much as you want!
You ignore the owner's slightly pained expression and order Spamton a box of ice cream. You see that the menu actually includes ice cream cones and ice cream, but you're afraid they'll melt, so you decide to order later.
The pot with the hotpot base was served, and soon the dishes you had just ordered were also brought out. And now, waiting for the pot to boil, you finally have a chance to ask Spamton some questions. The earlier questions still hadn't been answered, and you had always wanted to ask him.
But there had been no opportunities before, and now he finally had some free time.
So you carefully spun the spamton, now facing you, and you lifted it slightly higher to look at him intently.
“…… Well, I want to ask. You haven't answered my question before. ”
"What kind of question?" He was just asking knowingly, or rather, he didn't really know how to answer you.
You hesitate as you look at him, then shake him vigorously twice. You know there's no way he's about to forget and that it's only possible he said that on purpose. So now you grit your teeth and say, "Let me ask again, do you think we're similar people?" ”
Spamton still didn't answer your question, because the owner was walking over with a bowl of ice cream, and you had to turn Spamton back over and sit on your lap; otherwise, he wouldn't even be able to reach the bowl, and his head would just stick out of the table.
"Maybe I should enjoy the [Unlimited Ice Cream Supply] first." Spamton said. He hadn't figured out how to answer your question yet—at least not yet. In fact, he confirmed that you two are similar, but perhaps in some ways you actually have completely opposite thoughts and choices. For example...... When it comes to seizing someone else's [heart-shaped object], or rather their [soul], you definitely wouldn't agree with his choice. After all, to you, it's like choosing someone else as a scapegoat to avoid hurting you, and you still chose to help him. In a way, his willingness to help him at any cost is indeed somewhat despicable. But if you choose to help him, maybe...... Is it just as despicable? He doesn't know. But at least he knows that, in his eyes, you are an angel.
You propped your face up with one hand, leaning against the table, watching Spamton scoop up the ice cream bowl with a small wooden spoon. Honestly, his eating style was quite refined at this moment, though for some reason, his speed was quite fast. In short, you just couldn't figure it out and couldn't be bothered to dwell on it.
As Spamton ate, he seriously lifted his head and glanced at you. The sound was still mixed with the crackling of electric currents, unpleasant to hear, but you felt his voice was actually a bit gentler at this moment: "At least, to me, [you] are a [spiritual harbor]." "[You] are my [angel]." ”
He was trying his best to emphasize this, and you were instinctively stunned, not knowing why he said that...... No, maybe you know why he said that. Although at first it was indeed because of the game system's restrictions that you had no choice but to find Spamton and stay with him, later on, you chose to stay by his side willingly, and despite some deception, you chose to trust him again. For you, Spamton has indeed become a completely different existence without knowing where it started, at least to you with a different meaning. Despite living in so many rented apartments before, you have never felt a sense of belonging or home. But precisely because Spamton is in your rental now, you start looking forward to going home.
…… For Spamton, that's probably the case. If that's the case, you might have some idea how to interpret that phrase.
After all, you not only have a home but also a lover, and have learned something from him to some extent...... Although that's not what you want to learn, you have subtly picked up some of his tricks in lying and sales pitch.
So, you are two similar beings...... You can't really call yourself human, because Spamton isn't really human either. It's because of similar cores that you get close. As the saying goes, you are both lukewarm beings, and perhaps you will eventually face self-destruction. But after meeting, everything changes. After all, because of fundamental differences, different possibilities are written along the path of intersecting destinies.
Although Spamton didn't answer your question, you still got your own answer—maybe the answer you got was far more genuine than what others told you. So you finally smiled with relief: "Well, if that's the case, then you're also my spiritual haven...... Well, I know maybe it's not the right word, but I don't know what better word to describe it. As for what you mean to me...... I can only say it's a completely different existence. ”
If that's the case, maybe you can say 'forever' too. After all, on your life journey, you'll never meet such a special person again, and no other memories will be more vivid than those months spent together or in the gaming world.
"Ah, so... maybe I can also promise you that we will always be there for each other." Of course, if one day he doesn’t want to anymore, you’ll have to use those life-saving money he tricked you out of the first time as a threat—whether it works or not is another matter, but in any case, your fates are tightly intertwined.
This time it was Spamton who looked up at you in surprise. He made eye contact with you for a moment, and you just smiled and winked at him, even leaning over to plant a kiss on his forehead.
This immediately left him a bit stunned, just staring at you blankly… to be honest, he was originally thinking about how to explain that sentence, but he didn’t expect that now you looked like you had completely figured it out yourself. He couldn’t tell if you really understood it or not.
So he anxiously nodded and buried his head again. After all, his face was bright red, and of course, smoke was coming out of the puppet’s head, which you could clearly see.
You didn’t intend to expose him, just put the meat and vegetables into the pot that had just boiled, then after Spamton finished that ice cream bowl, you ordered him a cone as well. You didn’t think a puppet could get a stomach ache from eating ice cream… well, maybe, but probably not.
Spamton held the cone in both hands, nibbling, while his lenses were fogged up from the steam rising from the hotpot, and the cool ice cream actually helped dissipate some of the heat on his face. You covered your mouth and giggled quietly, feeling as if you heard Spamton glare at you. Of course, when you turned your head, Spamton was just looking down, nibbling the cone, the fog on his glasses still thick.
In short, you skillfully held Spamton and fed the little puppet, and you both enjoyed a satisfying meal. The ice cream bowl and cone you ordered had a nicely cold texture, which felt good even if he couldn’t taste sweetness, so Spamton was in a good mood.
Then you ordered a popsicle as an after-meal dessert. It had started to get a bit hot, and you wanted something cold. You waved farewell to your profit-pained boss, humming a slightly off-key tune as you walked out.
You took a bite of the popsicle. It was milk-flavored and soft, with a bit of frostbite to it, making you shiver, but the soft texture made it taste good.
You then unconsciously held the popsicle to Spamton’s mouth. For some reason, he seemed silent for a moment, and you didn’t understand why he hadn’t eaten it, so you nudged him: "Go on, eat it."
Finally, he bit the part you had just taken a bite from. You seemed to hear the chewing, and after a while, he replied, "Well… thank you, Miss Y/N, for the [Kangkai]."
You nodded in satisfaction, prepared to bite the popsicle yourself again, only to stop. You finally understood what he had been hesitating about… the popsicle was now covered with his saliva.
Well, you took a deep breath and bit it anyway; after all, this was the relationship you were in now, so no big deal.
But before you finished the popsicle, you suddenly felt a white blur before your eyes—you knew that familiar sense of detachment was coming. Your heart jumped; you knew it was the game system at work, and you didn’t know why it happened so suddenly this time—what happened to the promised month-long break!
Unfortunately, you didn’t have time to think further, nor to finish the popsicle in your hand, before losing consciousness. Spamton did too.

content:
[Main Quest: Get one of them clear and leave smoothly] Reward: One wish, the game system will end forever.
[Side Quest: Restoring the Truth of the Accident] Reward: 100,000 gold + 100,000 Dark Coins.
You scratched your head. The system's light screen cracked even further, and the crackling of electricity grew louder, and the flickering lights flickered as if they might explode at any moment. Those glaring white words were firmly etched into your eyes. You believe this was true for Spamton—because at this very moment, you were rarely together.
Taking advantage of the fact that no one else was in the room, you quickly took a look at what it looked like. A cold, dark iron table and walls. Although there were a few windows on the walls, you couldn't see outside. You were also handcuffed, probably to guard against sudden uprising. You turned to look behind you—it was the door to this closed room. You noticed a flashing red dot in the corner—probably a surveillance camera. Just as you turned your head, the door opened, and a rugged face you didn't recognize walked in, dressed in a police uniform. At this point, you clearly knew what to do next. It was basically the kind of scenario where you were the one being interrogated.
When the officer saw you turn and face the main door, his expression grew even colder. He slammed his baton the table: "Who gave you permission to turn around? Turn around now!" ”
You obediently turn around. You don't want to get hit with a baton. Unless necessary, you still don't want to get hurt.
The officer was satisfied. He pulled over a chair and sat across from you, tapping his knuckles lightly on the table twice, raising an eyebrow: "Go ahead, what exactly happened that day?" ”
You swallowed hard and belatedly realized that to you, you actually knew nothing—after all, although you had come to this game world, you had no memories of the past, and of course, you had no idea what had happened.
However, it was too late to try to pretend to have amnesia to fool the officer. After all, from the moment you entered, you hadn't disguised yourself and accepted your identity as a matter of course. Only then did you realize that you shouldn't have accepted the new environment and integrated so easily—it was all the game world playing tricks. You cursed silently in your heart, but on the surface you still looked obedient, just gently shaking your head. That confused expression wasn't an act—after all, you really didn't know anything.
"Are you talking about which day it was, officer?" So you asked.
The officer frowned, snorted coldly, and simply tossed a few photos in front of you: "Stop pretending. You were standing at the accident scene at the time, and your clothes were stained with blood. There's no way you're completely uninvolved in this case. The forensic doctor has examined you, and the blood on your body matches that of the two victims." ”
You casually glance at the photos the police officer had thrown onto the table, then your eyes widen—oh my god, if you're not mistaken, the two deceased lying on the ground in those photos are your parents, your father's face twisted with rage, and you can even imagine what he said before he died—probably expressing regret for giving birth to someone like you. Meanwhile, your mother's face showed an instinctive fear of death, probably...... She wasn't prepared to accept death right now.
You were silent for a moment, though you didn't know whether their deaths had anything to do with you—even though you instinctively believed this case was your doing—you still looked up, blinked, and tried to put on an innocent expression, just like you had seen earlier at Spamton—well, you might think that expression was not only innocent but also cunning, otherwise why did the police officer across from you look so disgusted?
And you just obediently said, "Yes, officer, with a little investigation, you'll know these two are my biological parents...... It's only natural that I became a suspect, but I have no reason to kill my biological parents. No matter what, they raised me, and I still remember this kindness. Filial piety is more than enough—how could I possibly kill them?" "You almost feel sick when you hear that."
After all, their attitude toward you before was indeed decent, but there was always neglect and disrespect. After all, you were never as favored as their later sons. Although they were somewhat dissatisfied, they could tolerate it. But when they gave up on sending you to university and instead made you go straight to work, everything changed. They started blatantly demanding money from you, and if you couldn't give them a satisfactory amount, they would verbally abuse you over the phone. Honestly, you have endured this kind of life for a long time. Sooner or later, you won't be able to hold back, and it's normal to do such things driven by anger.
But I don't know why...... You always feel a bit out of place at this scene. You just want to get away from your parents, and it's not yet enough to kill them. What exactly happened? If that's the case, maybe you're just being framed by someone else?
But the officer just sneered twice and took out a sealed plastic bag. Looking over, it was the collected evidence. It was a knife—a kitchen knife, still stained with blood. You looked at the photo—a kitchen knife was stuck in your father's chest, probably the knife. The mother's abdomen was cut with a huge wound, making it look like she died from excessive blood loss. That was why her face showed a fear of death...... Feeling her body grow cold and her consciousness fading, not everyone can endure this or have such tenacious willpower. Facing the fear of death is probably the most instinctive kind of human fear.
You stared at the evidence in silence for a moment, then the officer took out several autopsy reports and spread them out on the table. He asked coldly, "The autopsy report shows your mother, that is, Mr. X, died from excessive blood loss, with only a wound to her abdomen. Your parents, Mr. Y, died from fatal wounds to the chest, and the kitchen knife stabbed his heart. Besides that, both of them had the same drug in their bodies. Fortunately, there was no sound outside the door at this moment, but he couldn't guarantee that the policeman in a rage might be hiding somewhere nearby, preparing to ambush him. So Spamton pushed open the door, cautiously rummaging through the crack to look left and right. Indeed, there was no one else in the surrounding corners, but a half-dried bloodstain was dragged across the doorway. Spamton took a deep breath, carried his sleeping doll out of the office, and ran toward the place closest to the door according to the layout plan.
He hadn't heard any sounds along the way. Spamton was starting to suspect that the cop had already left this world, but he still didn't dare to let his guard down, since maybe he'd show up in the next corner.
Meanwhile—you haven't even woken up yet, still half-asleep, when the police call you to court. So you instantly sober up more than halfway, hurriedly shake the spamton twice, hoping he'll wake up then, since he's told you not to speak unless you're sure you'll go to court.
Unfortunately, you can't wake him up at all—his eyes are still tightly shut. If you weren't sure he still exists and lives in this world, you'd suspect he really isn't adapted to the environment of the Light World. But that's not the case; he probably just ...... Not awake, or maybe never waking up at all.
You suspect he might be sleeping in some kind of dream, but you can't find any evidence or enter the same dream as him, so you secretly anxiously carry him into court.
You stand behind the wooden fence right in the middle of the crowd's line of sight, just like you were facing witch trials in previous worlds, and you exhale a sigh, at least not panicking like you did on your first court. Indeed, you can even calmly observe your surroundings and analyze your current situation.
Look to the left, you'll see a prosecutor representing the public security system; look to the right, you'll see a lawyer sent from above to serve as your defense attorney. The trial hasn't started yet, and you hesitate for a moment, then raise your hand and ask, "Judge, can I defend myself at the right time?" "You can't trust this lawyer. After all, you've never met him before. What if he's in the same league as everyone else?"
The judge pondered for two seconds, nodded, and knocked down the wooden rope: "Grant this proposal." ”
You quietly breathe a sigh of relief, thinking that even without Spamton, you can still do things well. You don't know when Spamton will wake up, and before that, you must work hard to ensure the judge won't knock down the rope and convict you. You swallow hard, feeling a bit nervous for no reason, but at the same time, a passion rises, a desire to try.
Finally, the court hearing officially began. The prosecutor first read out the charges against you, then presented several pieces of evidence.
"There were two defendants in this case. They conspired to first add a lethal dose of potassium cyanide to the meals prepared for Mr. X and Mr. Y. Although the drugs were not the main cause of the victim's death, this crime can only be considered attempted murder by dosing. However, immediately afterward, the defendant Y/N used the murder weapon with a kitchen knife to brutally kill Mr. X and Mr. Y, resulting in their deaths. This constitutes a definite crime of murder." The prosecutor solemnly announced his summary of your actions.
Then he presented several pieces of evidence: a photo of a kitchen knife stabbed in his parents' chest, the autopsy report of both people, the gloves with no fingerprints on the surface but inside bearing your and Spamton's fingerprints, the bottle of potassium cyanide containing Spamton's fingerprints, and the knife that hadn't been stained with intact blood.
You take a deep breath. The lawyer doesn't say much, just simply replies, "Our defendant admits to these crimes and has no objection." ”
…… He's lying. You have issues with all this, but that lawyer seems to be conspiring with the prosecutor, just hoping your verdict will come quickly.
The judge above nodded solemnly, about to knock down the wooden rope and pronounce your guilt, then decide on the severity of your crimes. Hurry and raise your hand.
"Sorry, judge and prosecutor, I do not admit to these crimes. I have other questions and opinions. I want to know, since there are fingerprints of me and Spamton inside the gloves, how do you explain how Spamton's fingerprints appeared inside?" "In fact, the fact that the Light World can collect Spamton's fingerprints is itself a suspicious thing.
The crowd began to discuss among themselves. You could hear some louder voices shouting, saying that if the verdict was announced so quickly, it would be pointless. Some people were also complaining, saying that this lawyer had no intention of defending the defendant at all and insisted the defendant handle it themselves, so it would be better if there was no lawyer at all.
The judge knocked twice on the wooden rope, and a stern voice rang out: "Silence!" ”
The crowd had quieted down at this moment, though whispers could still be heard.
The prosecutor calmly said, "We extracted fingerprints from the kitchen knife, which included Mr. Spamton's fingerprints, proving he initially held the knife with his bare hands, and then remembered to wear gloves." ”
You took a deep breath. Just from that sentence, you couldn't find anything wrong, but you still tried hard to think before asking, "So, may I ask when he picked up the kitchen knife?" ”
The prosecutor was momentarily stuck, seemingly not expecting you to ask such a question. You held Spamton tightly, only thinking about maintaining this situation until he woke up. You didn't know when he would wake up, so until then, you could only hold on a little longer. And for some reason, the others seemed unaware that Spamton had fallen asleep, just proceeding with the trial proceedings as usual.
The prosecutor clapped his hands: "Then, we need witnesses to come forward and explain. Now, please have the defendant stand next to the defense counsel. ”
Your hands were still handcuffed, probably afraid you'd suddenly get up and hurt someone. But you didn't think you would do that, just reluctantly holding the Spamton and standing in the defense attorney's seat.
Then, the defense lawyer walked onto the stage, and you widened your eyes—if you read right, the person standing there was your brother, Mr. Z. I don't even know why he was the witness. Oh right, it's New Year's. Since you've gone back, of course others will go back too, so it's normal for him to see the details of your crime. No, that's not right. You think it wasn't you who committed the crime at all. Now it seems very likely Mr. Z accused you of false accusations.
Thinking this, you sneak a glance at the progress bar on the game's light screen. The progress has already reached 90%, which means your earlier guess is very likely correct.
You choose to calm down first and listen to what this person will say.
Z glanced discreetly at the prosecutor, who nodded slightly before he began to explain. You frowned, realizing his testimony might have been fabricated as well.
"My sister has always suffered from oppression by her parents. Maybe she finally couldn't hold back that day. She put potassium cyanide into her meal. I saw her fighting Mr. Spamton over the medicine bottle. Originally, my sister wanted to put the medicine in, but Mr. Spamton snatched the bottle and poured potassium cyanide into the food."
After he finished his testimony, he was quiet for a moment, glanced at the prosecutor again, as if confirming whether his earlier statement was mistaken, and you took a deep breath and raised your hand again.
"So, do you have any evidence of how the medicine bottle appeared? I never bought potassium cyanide." "You know that, at least you discussed it with Spamton, and you found a shopping receipt at his home—though you're also a bit puzzled, aren't you supposed to live together?
Mr. Z didn't say anything, but the judge spoke first: "At Spamton's home, which is your shared residence, we found a purchase receipt for potassium cyanide." As he spoke, he showed the receipt.
You took a deep breath. Just having a receipt wasn't enough, so you raised your hand again: "But there's also a potassium cyanide purchase receipt at Mr. Z's home. Am I wrong about that?" "You still remember what that police officer told you earlier.
Mr. Z's face turned pale, as if his little scheme had been guessed, and the prosecutor waved his hand, signaling him to leave first. Immediately after, the police officer who had questioned you earlier took the witness stand. But no matter how he looked at it, his state was different from before. When he told you earlier that he would find out the real culprit, his eyes sparkled, filled with hope for everything and his own future, filled with longing for justice. But now, his eyes were dark and lifeless.
You swallowed hard. Honestly, his state struck chills you. You had no idea what was happening to him, but you felt an almost intuition-like panic—could this be related to the dream Spamton was currently falling into? You grew more and more anxious. What if Spamton left that dream in the same state? You couldn't offer any extra help, so you could only present your defense in this courtroom, refuting that seemingly perfect yet actually flawed statement.
The officer spoke up, his voice mechanical and chilling to your ears, but others didn't think much of it: "We did find a potassium cyanide purchase receipt at Mr. Z's home, but it was bought six months ago." ”
Out of the corner of your eye, you see Mrs. Z let out a breath, then immediately put on a smug look—this is what annoys you the most. Cold sweat dripped down your forehead, and you felt there must be some other way...... No, or rather, some other piece of evidence.
And just before the judge could nod and knock down the wooden rope, you raised your hand again: "Then, the defense requests a careful examination of the evidence regarding the potassium cyanide vial." ”
The lawyer beside you glanced at you, a bit shocked. He hadn't expected you to do this, and you simply stared calmly at the prosecutor. The prosecutor and judge finally agreed to let you examine the evidence. You leaned the sleeping Spamton against the table, carefully picked up the small medicine bottle through your gloves, and glanced at it. The production date on it was exactly half a year ago.
You look up confidently: "Then, the production date of this medicine bottle is also half a year ago. I reasonably suspect that the Z family purchased the medicine and distributed it." ”
Z seemed to be sweating nervously, but he still argued, "If I bought the medicine half a year ago, why didn't I use it six months ago?" ”
You tilted your head, shrugged, and picked up Spamton again: "How would I know that? You'll have to ask yourself. But maybe you found out we also bought potassium cyanide, which is why you came up with the drug and framed us." ”
“…… Alright, then I want to ask, why are you buying potassium cyanide? "Mr. Z's face seemed flushed with anger.
But you just looked at the judge, raised your hand, and said, "Reporting to the judge, I believe this issue is unrelated to the current case. I request not to answer." "In fact, you don't have the original memories, so how would you know what you intended to do with this bottle of medicine back then?"
The judge simply tapped the wooden rope, then shook his head: "Application rejected." In other words, he believed the answer to this question was related to the case.
…… Alright, since you can't think of a reason for now, let's dodge the question for now. So you respond with a question: "Before I answer, I request to ask the accuser a question first." ”
The judge nodded: "Request permission." ”
You rubbed your chin and deliberately paused for a moment. Seeing that Mr. Z was about to break out in a cold sweat, you slowly said, "May I ask, have you each investigated the market where your shopping receipts are located? Have you seen what the medicine bottles look like?" ”
The prosecutor nodded slowly: "Indeed." The police investigated it, and the bottle was purchased by Mr. Z. "He reluctantly admitted it, and you quietly exhaled in your heart, relaxing your tension a little.
"So, I raise an objection. Since the bottle was purchased by Mr. Z, logically, his fingerprints should have been on it during the process. But the current bottle doesn't have his fingerprints, so—he could have committed a crime. Or rather, he was the one who actually carried out the drug administration. ”
After saying that, you swallowed hard. Honestly, this was just your unproven guess, or maybe just bold reasoning—just nonsense. You didn't even know if you were right, but seeing Z's pale expression, you guessed you were probably right, even though you didn't know how much you guessed.
The crowd erupted in uproar, a commotion, and amid the commotion, you quietly watched Mr. Z, your brother, as if he were looking at a stranger—indeed, you have no feelings for the people in your family, so calling them strangers wouldn't be an exaggeration.
The judge knocked heavily on the wooden rope and called for silence, and only then did the crowd quiet down. Then the judge asked Mr. Z if he had anything else to say, but Mr. Z just shook his head with a pale face. To your surprise, you thought he would at least defend himself a bit more, resist for a while, and not let the charge fall on him. But indeed, this was just an attempted murder, far less than the murder suspicion you are now heading with.
But you still didn't dare let your guard down, staring at him intently. Then Mr. Z took a deep breath and instead began to testify about the murder case. It seemed he had completely given up resisting, yet you still couldn't believe it—was it really that simple?
Meanwhile, Spamton had already circled several corners to make sure he hadn't heard the police anymore, and finally breathed a sigh of relief as he arrived at the police station entrance. But the unexpected silence only made him feel even more anxious and uneasy. He stood on tiptoe and barely managed to touch the password input screen at the police station. To be honest, he found it baffling and didn't understand why a password was set inside the station to prevent people from leaving—after all, keys usually only get upon entry.
…… But it's also possible—maybe this space was designed just for him. That thought vanished in an instant. In any case, he didn't dare delay any longer, and simply entered the keychain he had deduced from the documents in the office just now.
Then the door rumbled and slowly opened, and Spamton's alarm bells rang in his heart—the sound was so loud it easily attracted the police officer who had been chasing him. Sure enough, he heard the policeman's footsteps approaching—one step, two steps, three steps, and the sound of an axe dragging across the floor. He could faintly hear the sound of blood dripping down, but the door was still slowly opening at a steady pace. He glanced back, and the officer had already raised his axe, ready to strike at him the next second. Spamton turned back and saw the door finally open a gap he could squeeze through, so he hurriedly fled the police station holding his little doll. But outside the main gate was just a pitch-black space, as if nothing existed, yet this darkness was very familiar to Spamton.
…… After all, the People of Darkness are born in such pitch-black environments. He fell into that darkness, not knowing exactly what would happen. He only felt a wave of exhaustion and inexplicable pain, as if he had been having a long nightmare. Only now did he wake up. When he opened his eyes, the first thing he saw was your anxious gaze looking at him, and the second time, he realized you were in a courtroom at this very moment.
He's back, he's back to reality. Spamton couldn't be sure what had just happened; he just managed to lift his arm, then wrapped his arms around your neck. Seeing him finally wake up and breathe a sigh of relief, you can't be sure...... If he's been in a state of deep sleep all this time, can you win this appeal?
Mr. Z's testimony began at that moment, his voice slow and clear: "After the medication was administered, you had a conflict at the dinner table with your parents, Mr. X and Mr. Y, so Spamton picked up the kitchen knife. Then he realized his fingerprints would get on the knife, so he put on gloves. At first, he only scratched his mother's abdomen, but when he put down the knife, you were dissatisfied with your father's words, put on gloves, picked up the knife, and stabbed it straight into your father's chest. ”
His testimony is very strange, but you open your mouth but can't really comment on it. Or rather, your brain has short-circuited, and you probably gave up thinking as soon as Spamton came back. After all, once he came back, you felt at ease, and your mind wasn't so tense. You believe you can handle and resolve all of this.
Spamton glanced up at Mr. Z, thought for a moment, and didn't initially present his own defense. He hoped that if possible, this testimony could directly clear both of you, instead of wasting time with him here.
While you were daydreaming, you glanced at the game's light screen, only to be shocked to find that the main quest progress bar on the screen had already reached 25%. You had no idea what had happened—maybe it was related to the dream Spamton had just had? At least, that's your guess.
You hold Spamton, lift him up, shake your head to shake off your earlier thoughts, and decide to hear what Spamton plans to argue with. At the very least, you should get through the trial first.
Then you heard the sizzling sound of electric currents mixed with strange fragments: "I believe it was you who [administered the drug: potassium cyanide], and also your [violent combat], committing torture and murder against Mr. X and Mr. Y. Not only this [glove evidence], but also a [glove evidence] inside [covered in your fingerprint marks]. I think it was because Y/N and I wanted to [stop your delusional actions] at the time, so we tried to touch you, which is why we [stained with blood]. At the same time, the missing [glove evidence] also bore my and Y/N's fingerprints. ”
Mr. Z's face flushed and then turned pale. Seeing his expression change, you finally felt relieved. Then the prosecutor waved his hand, signaling Mr. Z to leave, and the previously apparently no longer sane officer stood in the witness stand again.
Spamton frowned when he saw this scene. No wonder another cop wanted to kill him in that world...... That would be equivalent to wiping out his sanity. He couldn't help but feel a chill run down his spine. What if he had died at that moment? Maybe he would never wake up in this world—no, or rather, he was originally just a Dark Citizen, who shouldn't exist in the world of the Light Ones. He was just a tiny spam email on your computer.
You also find the scene a bit strange, but you can't quite explain why he would change. At that moment, Spamton leaned in, leaned close to your ear, and whispered, "In the [Dream World], he was [killed]. I think that's the reason he [lost his soul]." ”
And you can't help but widen your eyes—so that's how it is. No wonder he looks so strange, and no wonder your interrogators have changed to someone else. This world, or rather the game system, probably never intended to clear you of guilt from the start.
But the officer simply said in a stiff voice, "There is no other glove evidence in our evidence investigation." ”
Liar, I was showing you another pair of gloves just a couple of days ago—you instinctively wanted to retort, but then immediately realized that such rebuttal was completely meaningless. And now, besides that, there were other things you were worried about. You leaned in and whispered to Spamton, "Then wouldn't it be dangerous for you in that world?" "You can't imagine what exactly happened."
Spamton just shook his head and made a gesture for silence, signaling that all this would be discussed later.
You watch Z's face grow paler and paler, and you know Spamton was actually right—at the same time, you suppress your curiosity for a moment. You just open the game screen to check, and are surprised to find that side quests have reached 100% progress, while main quests have reached 50%. You don't know how that was actually determined.
Spamton only added after the officer finished speaking: "However, what remained on [our gloves] was not [splash-like bloodstains]. Rather than [immediate contamination], it looked more like [post-factly fabrication]." His words were firm, Mr. Z's face grew even paler, and the prosecutor weakly leaned against the table, unable to speak for the moment. Your defense lawyer stared at you in shock, probably unable to imagine that you had actually succeeded.
The prosecutor finally nodded with difficulty: "...... Our side admitted that the bloodstains on those gloves were later found to be not the splatter-like blood that should have appeared during the brutal killing, nor were the traces left on the ground splattered blood. Therefore, the cause of their deaths was potassium cyanide. ”
From afar, you saw Mr. Z's eyes widen, never imagining that the drug administration he had easily admitted earlier would now ring out as the final funeral bell. Everything that followed was simple: the judge acquitted you and Spamton, then sentenced Mr. Z and sentenced him to punishment. You started to zone out, sneakily opening the game screen to glance again. However, progress was only at 75%. Even though both of you had successfully cleared your sentence, you still had no idea what the remaining 25% was.
Just as you were casually thinking, Spamton suddenly tugged at your sleeve. You looked up, only to be surprised to find time had somehow stopped at this very moment—so many supernatural things had happened, and now it was understandable to pause time for a moment—what could you understand! You looked at the crowd's diverse expressions, the wooden ladder the judge was about to knock down to declare you innocent, the prosecutor's helpless rage across from you, and Z's pale-faced body trembling. Finally, all your attention focused on a single footstep—heavy, as if some iron tool was being dragged.
Spamton, on the other hand, scolded your arm with a serious expression: "[Run!!!] 】”
You barely realized that it would only be over after the judge knocked down the wooden rope, so your progress was stuck at 75%. Although you didn't quite understand why Spamton said that, instinctively, you still started walking and ...... You also saw the source of that heavy footsteps—it was the one sent by the police officer who questioned you yesterday. But for some reason, his face was blurred now, and you couldn't see clearly in the rush.
You ran forward holding the Spamton, trying to reach the judge and press the wooden rope. But everything before you changed—the judge's direction turned into a beam of light, and ahead was just a forest—the forest from the game level you first encountered that day. You ran skillfully, hiding among the trees, shaking off the heavy footsteps behind you, yet still faintly visible.
Running further ahead, countless mermaid phantoms appeared. You couldn't see their faces clearly, only knowing they were probably thanking you. Ahead was a cliff, and beyond it was a mechanical door. Fortunately, the gap wasn't large, and merfolk were blocking the way behind. You crossed the cliff and reached the other side. Spamton skillfully flipped the switch, entered the SOS message, and the door quickly opened. Behind them were the so-called witches you had let go that day. They signaled you to run quickly, leaving all future troubles to them.
You nodded gratefully, seemingly unable to hear the heavy footsteps, but you still refused to let your guard down. Although you didn't know why the sky was approaching dusk, you still crossed the bridge ahead—a bridge that only appears at moments of demon encounters.
Then, the journey reached its end. You finally reached the judge. Before you could take your next step, you watched as the soul of the girl from the previous world playfully winked at you, pulled her eyelids into a funny face, then slipped onto the judge, knocked down the wooden rope, and shouted heavily: "I hereby declare Miss Y/N and Mr. Spamton innocent!" ”
Everything is over. Everything behind you turns blank, and so does your vision. You see the main quest on the game's light screen changed to 100%. Then, a flash of bright light passes before your eyes. You hug the Spamton and sit back down on the ground. The Dark People come and go, seemingly unaware of you.
But you know it's all over because you hear the crisp cracking sound. You try to summon the game screen again, but it can't be summoned anymore.
You hugged Spamton tightly, saying nothing.
