content:
To be honest, you don't even know what kind of wish the game system has helped you achieve. You just feel a bit dizzy, and your body feels light...... You always feel a strange excitement, as if the shackles on your body have been lifted. Although you can't open the game system screen anymore—after all, it's already shattered—you're sure your wish has probably already been granted.
You blinked, suppressing your excitement and the urge to experiment, and just lowered your head to look at Spamton in your arms. After all, the passing Dark Civilians didn't comment on the two of you—whatever. But you still picked up Spamton and walked toward home. Honestly, sitting on the floor all the time was a bit awkward.
"Spamton, what is your wish?" You asked casually, saying this casually, but out of the corner of your eye, you caught Spamton shaking his head, his expression inexplicably serious: "I [don't know], [I don't know] if what I fulfill is the [expected] expectation." ”
You pause in your steps, realizing a bit belatedly—right, the game screen is gone. Who knows what wish it actually granted...... Honestly, having a game system grant wishes is pretty surreal in itself, but with so many surreal things happening, having another game system doesn't matter.
So you just shrugged: "Alright, then we'll have to verify it ourselves......" Finally, you make it home. You open the door, then collapse onto the bed holding the Spamton, staring blankly at the ceiling. Honestly, you've lost your target in such a short time and don't know what to do next.
"Don't you have any other questions waiting for consultation?" At that moment, you heard Spamton's voice.
You didn't look at him either, just spoke with some confusion: "...... I've already left the game world. Is there anything else I need to ask you?" "Honestly, you don't think there's any urgent problem waiting for you to solve right now.
You heard Spamton sigh in frustration, cleared your throat a little guiltily, then sat up in bed and still held Spamton. This time, you stared at him more seriously.
"I really don't know what else I need to ask...... So, what exactly did you encounter in the other world before? "You asked casually.
Spamton pinched your cheek. You let out a hiss, looking at him pitifully. Honestly, he was a bit rough now, but it didn't hurt much—you were just pretending.
Then he shook his head: "It's not about this precaution, but that world is extremely dangerous, so we really need to be extra cautious." "Although he felt that you had no chance of re-entering that world either.
"Oh...... But no matter how dangerous it is, I can still make it through. It's nothing, and you left there smoothly. "You dragged out your voice, feeling like you had caught a faint idea and understood something, but you still didn't know what Spamton wanted to ask.
“…… But [you] [imagine: I have no chance of leaving smoothly]." His expression was serious, and his tone was also serious.
You frowned and just shook your head: "I won't allow that to happen. If you keep sleeping, trapped in dreams, I will definitely find a way to enter that dream." ”
"Besides......" You scratched your hair and tilted your head slightly, not looking directly at Spamton. After all, you felt a bit embarrassed. "I trust you. At least you can guarantee that nothing will happen inside again. If you can't break your dream, then I'll help you break it." I believe you won't die in that world like that cop. "Your words sounded so natural and confident that Spamton was left speechless. He stared straight at you and didn't say a word for a long while. You thought you might have said something wrong and quickly added another sentence afterward.
"Ahem...... And before you wake up, at least I can guarantee that nothing will happen to me," you said, giving a thumbs-up and praising yourself with a hint of pride, "Look, I did very well in court too!" ”
Spamton just sighed. To be honest, his heart—maybe the heart—gently swayed with your words, and he was about to get lost in it. But he knew it wasn't the issue; what he desperately wanted to share with you was not this topic.
So he simply knelt on your knees, cupped your face, and met your gaze. He said something he hadn't said before, but you actually had some vague feelings: "[You] didn't [discover consciousness], and our [separation ritual] was deliberately done by the [Heaven's Wishing Machine]?" ”
You stared into Spamton's eyes. Honestly, even if you noticed something, you wouldn't dare say this guess out loud. After all, who knows if all of this is real or not? What if what happens to you is just an illusory dream? You don't dare to gamble. But after he said this, everything around remained the same, as ordinary as ever. Suddenly, you realized again that everything was just reality.
You sighed, cupped Spamton's face as well, and nodded solemnly: "...... Actually, I vaguely realized that from the very beginning, everything was an accident. Clearly, if the police had just kept investigating, we could have gotten results, but suddenly a different cop replaced us and pushed us into trial...... Clearly, neither of us is good at what we are about to face, yet we are still cruelly separated, forced to face the current situation alone. Clearly, cooperation between you and me is the most advantageous thing—it's just that at this moment, the game system has cut off the possibility of our cooperation. "As you spoke, you couldn't help but laugh again. To be honest, you don't understand why the game system would do this, as if it deliberately didn't want you to pass the final level.
“…… And if we hadn't completed the [Side Quest] before, then [End of the Game] would have been a dead end. "Spamton thought about it. In the end, like a relay race, parts of every previous game—or rather, parts of fantasy or reality—appeared to help you, and I still feel a bit scared. Without those people, you probably wouldn't have escaped.
You scratched your head and chuckled twice: "Trust me—it definitely won't be a dead end. Even without that help, I can still find a way to escape. And at worst, I'll just fight that guy. I might not lose; maybe he just looks scary." "You're saying that a bit carelessly. You even want to try carrying an axe now. Maybe it really works."
“…… Don't say 'freedom of speech.' And Spamton just covers your mouth, and you blink a bit innocently at him.
"In any case, fortunately, we have the [other side's capital]." He sighed and finally reached this conclusion.
You removed his hand from covering your mouth, tilted your head, and looked at him in confusion: "I must have learned a lot from you...... Speaking of which, I should thank you. But you haven't learned much from me either, have you? ”
After all, what you have is just brute force or something like that, not something suitable for learning. Saying this, you feel a bit guilty, since aside from that, you really don't have any other strengths.
But Spamton shook his head, his tone inexplicably more serious than before: "No, [you] have benefited me a lot." After saying this, he looked at you with a complicated expression. To be honest...... In fact, Spamton even felt a sudden sense of guilt. After all, if it weren't for you, he probably wouldn't have escaped his predetermined fate, nor would he have had a second choice. But your appearance actually showed him new possibilities. That's why, at that moment, he made such an effort.
“…… How did I end up benefiting you so much? Why don't you tell me about it?" You shook Spamton, trying to get an answer from him, but Spamton just shook his head and refused to say more. You puffed out your cheeks, a bit dissatisfied, but in the end gave up pressing further.
"Alright...... Anyway, I still thank you. If it weren't for you, what happened in that game world would probably be what I really have to face, probably my future. "You let go of Spamton's shoulders and just smiled sincerely.
Spamton opened his mouth to say something, but just then, your stomach growled, proving you were hungry. So now you two stared at each other, feeling a bit awkward for no reason.
You cleared your throat again: "Alright...... Let's go out and find any restaurant to eat! Two game worlds in a row really exhausted me...... "But if you really ignore that brief night of gaming, maybe three. Anyway, you need to get some good rest. It's decided. After dinner, go submit your resignation and tell the hospital you plan to quit."
And then...... In fact, you can keep stocking in any world, since you have plenty of capital. Lost in thought, you carry Spamton into that familiar hotpot restaurant again.
Spamton was speechless. To be honest, he didn't want every meal to be hotpot...... Although he didn't care what he ate, he didn't want his glasses always getting foggy with white fog.
So he spoke: "[You] don't plan to [change the shop]?" ”
You only snapped out of it when you heard his voice, glanced at the hotpot restaurant in front of you: "...... But in the game world, we haven't had any good food. If we had hotpot, it would be a treat for us, right? ”
Spamton closed his eyes and casually pointed in a direction. After all, this street was full of restaurants, so no matter what, it wouldn't be bad: "Then let me select a [shop location]." ”
You nodded as if it were only natural: "You're a hero too—fine, then today I'll eat whatever you choose. But let's be clear, tomorrow it's my choice." ”
Spamton nodded without objection, and you glanced in the direction he pointed, your expression a bit subtle. Hearing you remain silent for a while, Spamton opened his eyes and followed your gaze, then realized he was pointing to the Cyber BBQ restaurant.
Spamton fell silent. To be honest, he couldn't guarantee he wouldn't run into old friends at this shop, nor could he guarantee anything else would happen afterward. But since it was like this, and he hadn't tasted barbecue for a long time, he just said expressionlessly, "Yes, it's the location of this shop." ”
You hesitate, glanced down at Spamton, but saw him nod at you. Sighing, you still carried Spamton into the cyber barbecue restaurant. Since there weren't many people at noon, you found a seat by the window and sat down, placing Spamton next to you. When he sat in the chair, his head could only barely stick out of the table.
As a waiter, the Dark People quickly brought over the menu. After you checked out the dishes you wanted, you handed it to Spamton, then propped up your chin, looking at the shop's facilities with a bit of boredom. Just as your gaze casually swept over, you noticed a table not far away—although your ability to recognize people was poor, you could still recognize it as a table full of Addisons, and it seemed the pink one was the representative?
You weren't very clear about this, just lowered your head to look at Spamton, who was still seriously ordering, and quietly asked, "Your former colleagues are all sitting there. Should we move somewhere else?" ”
After all, Spamton's mood is more important, even though you prefer your current position.
Spamton also looked up, and the puppet's face seemed to have turned paler again—well, it was already white, so you couldn't tell much had changed. You stared at Spamton, and he just shook his head: "No need for [Location: Transfer permissions]." ”
After all, although ...... He did avoid these guys a bit, or rather, had a certain fear, disgust, and anger, but he couldn't go on like this forever. Moreover...... Spamton knew that everything was no longer what it used to be.
You choose to respect Spamton's choice, so after you order, you call the waiter to take the menu, and the Addisons at the table look over at your call. When they see Spamton, their expressions and bodies freeze.
You nervously swallowed nervously, glanced at Spamton, and saw the little puppet flash a cocky grin, then flipped the middle finger at the table of Addisons.
You choked up for no reason, then you saw that pink Addison seemed furious, wanting to rush over and beat Spamton or something. I wasn't sure if you were mistaken, but you felt the veins on his head bulging. The other Addisons stopped him, grabbing his arm to tell him not to act impulsively. You seemed to hear some kind of persuasive voice.
You were speechless for two seconds, then simply chose to cross your arms and watch the show. After all, it wasn't really your business—this was Spamton's previous lingering relationships and disputes. Honestly, you didn't fully understand his personality.
You just saw that pink Addison also give Spamton a middle finger, and then your mouth twitched. You pulled Spamton away and simply picked him up and placed him on the inside, so he wouldn't be silently flipping the other side of the table. It was like some kind of arena match. Then the waiter happened to bring out all the dishes. You grilled the meat slices and stuffed them into Spamton's bowl, and some stuffed into his mouth, saving him from saying anything else.
Spamton glared at you, and you glared back at him, unwilling to back down. He finally chewed and swallowed the meat you had just put into his mouth, but before he could speak, you shoved another piece of meat into his mouth, so he could only keep chewing.
You hummed softly twice, then whispered to Spamton, "Just eat your meal! Stop doing such childish things." "As you spoke, you gently shoved him.
Fortunately, after that, Spamton didn't make any further noise. He just stood at his seat and continued picking up the barbecue to eat. After that, you got through the rest of the time peacefully. The Addisons finished eating earlier and deliberately passed by your table. Then the pink Addison gave Spamton the middle finger, and Spamton returned the favor.
You pat your forehead, feeling a bit tired for some reason. Fortunately, the shop quiets down afterwards, and after you finish your meal, you leave the Cyber BBQ Restaurant with Spamton.
You complained casually: "Why did you just make an international friendly gesture with those guys? I know you don't like those Dark People...... But what if a fight breaks out? I'm confident I can beat those people on the other side......"
Spamton was silent for a moment. Indeed, things were just as you said, but he also knew these Addisons cared about their reputation and reputation. After all, they still had to advertise everywhere, so of course they wouldn't start fighting inside the store—at most, they'd handle it privately. That's why he did it on purpose.
So Spamton simply said softly, "No, they will absolutely not【make a scene and fight】." ”
"Then it's just like you said...... You're not right, aren't these guys waiting for us up ahead!" You whispered cursing to Spamton, because you saw those Addisons blocking the alley that Knife Residential District must pass. You skillfully picked up a discarded steel pipe from the ground and placed Spamton on your shoulder.
"Alright, then I'll just give you a good beating. I can finally get your revenge." You beamed with excitement, then swung the steel pipe at Addison opposite you. You didn't care about turn-based combat in this world; what did it have to do with you? You're not a game in real life. Addison on the other side clearly hadn't expected you to play completely against the rules. After all, turn-based combat doesn't follow these rules. In the chaos, colorful magical lights flashed by, but you didn't care about any of that. You just swung the physics holy sword in your hand—well, it wasn't a crowbar, but it was about enough. Then you knocked Addison on the neck, and out of kindness, you only knocked them out.
Then you casually tossed your hair, tossed the pole to the floor, and took big strides to walk forward. But before you could take two steps, you felt someone grab your pant leg. Impatiently, you glanced down and saw it was still the pink Addison. You patiently stopped, ready to hear what last words he had left. At the same time, you felt an itch to grab the pole from earlier.
And Addison just trembled as he flipped Spamton the middle finger, then collapsed again without saying a word. You looked speechlessly at Spamton on his shoulder, and he just glanced at you innocently. You sighed, brushed off the nonexistent dust on your palm, and this time truly took Spamton and strode away.
By the way, you complained to him, "I told you to provoke those guys...... Now look at it, you still have to put effort into persuading them. If it were just you, what would you do? This time, it's all thanks to me." ”
Spamton's demeanor became unusually obedient, making you hesitate and glance back at him twice, while he simply said, "It's precisely because I know your existence that I'm willing to step into the unknown." ”
It's precisely because he knows you're here, and that you won't let things unfold, that's why he does it.
You paused for a moment, because his words made you feel a bit embarrassed. You coughed twice, scratched your head, then turned your head to the side and whispered, "Ah...... Alright, I understand what you mean. You're right. I really won't just leave you alone. "Of course, you wouldn't take the initiative to cause trouble.
As you spoke, you cleared your throat seriously: "Alright, I plan to go back to the Light World first. I think my wish has already come true...... Do you need to go check it out? By the way, what kind of wish did you make...... "You're curious about this, but it seems Spamton really doesn't want to tell you. He shook his head mysteriously, just making a gesture for silence. You sighed, just about to say something else and put him at home for now, when you heard him speak."
"But I think I can now go to the Light World with you." He said, standing at your doorstep, about to open it. Hearing this, your eyes widened, pointing at yourself and then at Spamton.
"Are you sure...... Can you really go to the World of Light now? But isn't your presence in the World of Light just some kind of junk email...... You muttered, then turned and left the door, heading toward the entrance to the world of light and darkness you had previously traveled back and forth. It was a blurry beam of white light, impossible to see ahead. It just existed at the end of the road.
You take a deep breath, just close your eyes, then reach out to touch that pure white light. After the dazzling light flickers, you return to the world of light.
You let out a sigh of relief and instinctively glanced at Spamton's shoulder, noticing that Spamton was indeed sitting on your shoulder. Curious, you grabbed him and squeezed him, and it really was real—after all, the texture was exactly the same. You didn't know exactly how Spamton did it, so you just asked curiously, "Is this the wish you made?" ”
But Spamton just smiled without answering your question, and you weren't that annoyed. In short, he's not answering your questions more than once or twice—everyone has their own little secrets, and that's normal.
You couldn't be bothered to study what happened to Spamton. You just took out your phone to take a look, scrolled through contacts and social apps, then clenched your fist and shouted 'Yes.' Of course, you didn't mind sharing your joy. Maybe Spamton had guessed a bit, so you just said animatedly, "My wish to play has indeed come true! I want to break away from my family forever, even though I don't know how this game system manages it...... But indeed, it worked." "You're very happy, because this means you're free from now on and won't be bound by your family anymore. After all, you've already hated your family from the bottom of your heart."
…… Maybe it's not for any special reason. Although they're stingy materially, it's not a big deal. But you've never experienced emotional giving, and they actually ask you to reciprocate in return—both materially and emotionally. Honestly, that's why you dislike them—after all, your relationship isn't equal, and what you get isn't equal.
Whether or not you regret it later, at least for now, this is your wish, so you will never regret it.
"Your wish should have come true too...... I'm not sure either, but as long as it's a good thing, that's enough." You whistled out a bit off-key, put away your phone, and honestly, you have nowhere else to go in the Light World, so you'll better take Spamton back to the Dark World.
But before you could move, Spamton called out to you: "I think we should [check the newspaper information] first." ”
You blinked, a moment too late, and remembered that Spamton was talking about what happened in the game world. After all, those game worlds should have happened in the real world of light, so you still looked up those events in the order of the game world, since you were also somewhat curious about the outcomes of those events.
You first looked up information related to the first world. After a long time, you only remembered the [Forest Murder Case] and something like that, but quickly came to the conclusion: [Thanks to the efforts of all the tourists, the serial murder case at the forest tourist resort has been officially closed. The police have uncovered the truth and learned that it is related to a recent wrongful conviction. The case has now been overturned, and the culprit will be punished......]
You blink, thinking this might be a good outcome, so you start looking into the second case...... To be honest, you're not really sure what this is, just searching [Building Arson Case]: [The mysterious event inside the building has come to an end!] The legend of the mermaid really exists—it's a mermaid's curse that caused the resurgence and hallucinations inside the building. Here, I remind everyone to have a compassionate heart and not to be evil or greedy......]
You exhaled and instinctively met the look of Spamton on your shoulder. Although your names weren't on either case, you knew these were gifts the world left you after you completed the side quest.
You swallowed hard. Honestly, the third case should exist in an impossible future, so you didn't know what to search for. You just looked up the name of that research institute. Fortunately, you still remembered it.
You looked at the search results in disbelief and clicked in to take a second look.
[Shocking! A research member from a certain research institute actually conducted unauthorized research on the zombie virus without approval of the report application, causing multiple deaths and mutations into monsters! ]
You look at the monster pictures you posted and they really are the ones you defeated back then in the post-apocalyptic world.
Looking further down, you were eager to know what happened next.
[Fortunately, a member of the research institute discovered the cure for the zombie virus, saving the besieged institute, and even the entire world! The involved researchers have been apprehended and are awaiting further investigation...]
You exhaled and felt somewhat relieved. Although your names did not appear and everything was erased, you had truly done something to save the world, and at this moment, you felt happy about it.
So you continued searching. This time, you only looked up [17th Century Witch Hunts], and a lot of information popped up, making your eyes a bit dizzy, while Spamton swiped a few times on your phone and then precisely clicked into a report.
[It is rumored that in the 17th century, angels descended to the world and released those 'witches' who were imprisoned and hopelessly awaiting death. The subsequent witch hunts ceased, reducing casualties, but the losses that had already occurred remained. Luckily, due to the immediate halt of the witch hunts, the visibly observable crop and meat harvests that year were higher than in previous years...]
You sighed in relief. Although not everyone had been saved, it seemed that the outcome was actually quite good.
So you confidently searched for the next item. You hesitated a bit, but in the end, you typed in the name of this hotel.
You opened the most sensational news.
[Public opinion conflict and war broke out! Revealed truths about a certain hotel sparked public outrage. The police have apprehended all involved personnel inside the hotel, but the disseminator of the information has not yet been found...]
When you got to this part, you swallowed hard and tapped your forehead. 'Oh no, I forgot to switch to a different account when sending the message back then.'
For the penultimate incident, you had also used your own account.
Spamton said nothing; he simply picked up the phone and typed in the name of XX company, which was your penultimate world.
You saw the latest report: the father of the girl was confirmed guilty and had been taken away, while the disseminator of information was still not found, the same person as in the previous hotel incident.
You cleared your throat: 'I better register a new account...' and Spamton nodded in agreement.
'I can [provide help], [your] new account will have no connection to the [information disseminator],' he added.
You nodded, naturally agreeing: 'Alright, I’ll leave it to you.' Saying that, you took the phone back, hesitated for a moment, and finally entered your parents’ names.
There was all sorts of chaotic content, but nothing related to that case, and you smiled with relief, as all this had not yet actually happened.
By this time, it was almost evening, and the moon was slowly rising. You put your phone away, stretched, and said, 'Alright, now that we’re in the light world, you can have dinner with me, and then we’ll head to school together… maybe you can even get a diploma or something. Although this year’s recruitment season is over, it will probably have to wait until next year...' You muttered your plans, and Spamton just listened quietly.
Suddenly, he glanced at the sky and then said to you, '[The moonlight is beautiful tonight].'
You were momentarily stunned and instinctively looked up at the night sky, then wondered aloud, 'What, there aren’t any monsters falling from the moon either, what are you talking about?'

Title page 1
Title page 2
Preface
Road
【】1
…… To be honest, you have no idea why you've come here. Just a moment ago, you were drinking beer at a barbecue restaurant, enjoying a tipsy sensation and thinking about what to do next. But the next second, you're sitting here shrouded in darkness, gloomy leaves pressing down overhead, on soft ground where only faint light filters through the gaps between the lush leaves. You casually touch the soft ground, and the first thing you feel is the slightly rough, dry surface of the leaves. Then, with an unintentional press, you hear the crunching sound of the fallen leaves piled together.
You can't just sit and wait for death, so you brush the dust off your clothes and stand up, ignoring the pain in your tailbone from suddenly sitting on the ground. Then you gradually adjust to this drowsy darkness—honestly, you really hope to find a way out so you can leave here quickly, and you don't care what exactly is happening to you, or what is happening beside you. Because you know that it could only mean bad omens, because you have uneasy signs, and you are a selfish person—so you only plan to leave alone.
Unfortunately, just as you recognized the direction of the wind in the forest and planned to follow the wind and step on the creaking leaves, you heard a sound like a pop-up window. In short, it was a bell, and it sounded like an explosion in your mind. You had to stop, almost annoyed, staring at the transparent window before you, which even glowed faintly.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest together with your companions. ]
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'killer.' ]
You looked at these two lines of text helplessly, so you looked around, then lowered your head and saw another but identical pop-up window—in the subtle dimming, you could barely recognize it as the tiny figure that had been standing nearby before, its outline almost like a puppet. To be honest, at the time you even thought it didn't really exist, after all, this was a forest, and maybe ...... Maybe it was just the incarnation of some tree.
But now, through the screen's light, you can finally see his pale face—or maybe it's his own complexion. He wears a pair of ridiculous pinkish-yellow glasses, so you can't see his mood. Of course, you're not very curious about it. You just crouch down, looking him up and down, and he seems wary, but doesn't say a word. After hesitating for a moment, the puppet finally reaches out his hand to you.
"I think we need to cooperate with [you] and I to leave this [world]." His voice sounded strange, with a crackling sound like electricity. You scratched your ear and felt a bit uncomfortable, but for you, perhaps having another companion in this darkness was actually a blessing—after all, you all saw that panel, and he had no other missions, so perhaps you could let go of your unfounded vigilance and just take this little puppet and escape this forest together.
Of course, as for that side quest, it's probably fine not to complete it...... Just as you were thinking this, you saw the text on that panel update.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest with your companions.] Reward: Survive successfully and have seven days off, immune to all lethal factors
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'Killer'.] ] Reward: 10,000 gold
You smacked your lips in annoyance. Honestly, this was like suddenly getting involved in some kind of horror game—honestly, ten thousand dark coins made you a bit envious, but you had no deductive skills. You've always believed in physics and cryptography. If you can't unlock it, just break it outright!
So you looked down at the little puppet again, raised your eyebrows, and reached out your hand to him: "Alright, since things have come to this, we can only reach a partnership. But just to be clear, since I can't handle side quests like this kind of deduction and cryptography, I'll leave it to you." You said it as if it were only natural, and without waiting for him to refuse, you continued to add more.
"As for the main quest—don't worry, I'll take you with me and leave here. I don't know how you should address me, but just call me Y/N." You shrugged, watching him reach out his hand toward you. You casually grabbed his hand and shook it, then grabbed it and lifted it up, placing him on your shoulder.
After all, you just heard an unsettling rustling sound from the leaves not far away. It wasn't the sound of wind, but clearer, more obvious human voices. Someone was walking through the woods in this direction, probably just patrolling normally. After all, you had just tried it. The light screen couldn't be broken, so maybe it wasn't because you saw it.
Before he could answer, you heard footsteps getting closer behind you. After all, the sound of stepping on withered leaves was too obvious, not to mention the sound of chainsaws starting the wheels, the sizzling sound, and a faint, terrifying smell of blood—so you just grinned: "Forget it, these things can wait a bit. For now, let's run!" "Better hold on!" ”
With that, you pushed off the ground and dashed out. Honestly, you're quite good at sports, so running a distance is easy—even fast, not difficult. Right now, you're only slightly out of breath, with lactic acid accumulating in your legs and a slight ache. You didn't mind at all, just weaving through the woods, listening to the ominous sound of a chainsaw moving farther away, while you found a more lush, densely packed spot and rushed in.
You were still running, and before Spamton could answer, he was forced to clutch your clothes. Honestly, he definitely didn't want to be thrown off in a place like this—although for the main quest, you'd probably go back to save him, but he didn't want to experience that kind of anxiety. And just as he was about to speak, he was blown into the air, so the words he wanted to say were twisted by the howling wind, spreading and spreading with eerie sounds.
"My [name] is—" Unfortunately, the voices behind him were all faded by the wind.
And you just raise your voice and ask, "You—are—saying—what—"
Spamton hated his current situation—unsettling, confusing, and precarious. He always had to come up with a plan to protect himself, always figure out a way to live a better life. Of course, he was willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, even if it was just a brief experience of being a despised rat, as long as he still had the ability to choose, as long as he had the ability to think, he would never let himself willingly remain in that situation.
And he recognizes you. He knows you are a Citizen of Light he met a few years ago. Unfortunately, he didn't get what he truly wanted from you, but was sent off by money.
But now, relying solely on his own abilities, he couldn't accomplish anything. He was confident that if you hadn't taken him away from that place, he would have been finished, declared his death, and declared it all with deep resentment and displeasure.
If it weren't for you, maybe he wouldn't have ended up in this situation—but without you, he absolutely couldn't have escaped it. If you didn't seem completely unaware, he'd almost think all of this was your deliberate design.
He despised and hated the feeling, but he had no other choice. He could only lie down, clutch your clothes tightly, perform some useless prayers, then close his mouth, saying no more or repeating it.
Only when you can no longer hear the chainsaw behind you do you slowly stop, wipe the unnecessary sweat from your forehead, glance at Spamton on your shoulder, and feel the weight on your shoulder—you know he's always been there, so you just treat it as a simple burden.
Only after stopping did you realize the trees before you were sparse, even seeming to have a faint glow. You cautiously took a few steps forward, and then everything suddenly opened up—it was actually a small wooden cabin. Surrounded by trees and among the fallen leaves, there was actually a small wooden cabin. It looked somewhat old, but at least with the naked eye, it was clearly not made of new wood, at least some time ago. There was even an iron pot in front of the mansion, but probably no one had used it.
After all, a thin layer of dust had even accumulated on the iron pan, at least two or three months ago.
You hesitated for a moment, touched your belly, then felt it for a moment, and looked at Spamton, your expression grave: "...... I think it looks like we need to eat, drink, and rest normally. I just wonder if there are any suitable ingredients left here...... At this moment, you even feel a bit relieved to have discovered such a wooden cabin. There are probably still candles burning inside, which is why a faint light is emitted.
"Maybe we can take turns keeping watch at night. Also, for the repetitive work, my [name] is Spamton G. Spamton. " said the little puppet.
You nodded and softened your footsteps. After all, there were no fallen leaves near the cabin, so simply keeping your footsteps quiet was fine—you just didn't want anyone to notice your movements, just in case there were others in the cabin.
So you just lowered your voice and asked hopelessly, "Then, maybe you could go in and help me check the situation now?" "After all, you heard something strange coming from inside the house just now. You definitely don't want to end up in the face of a killer after finally coming here. Of course, letting your 'companion' go is no big deal, and he looks small and clearly won't be easily discovered!"
"I think we should [act together]." Your intention was too obvious, after all, you wore that regretful expression on your face right now—as for just now? It was the look of someone racking their brains to plan, so now you have no choice but to regretfully abandon the plan, sigh, and continue walking forward with Spamton.
You climbed the wooden steps and quietly poked your head out from the window to look inside. There was no one there, just candles burning on the table, looking like the wick was about to burn out. You continued to carefully observe the inside of the house, and at that moment, you noticed a heat-insulating cage near the wall, inside which humans were imprisoned—who looked like a Child of Light? You thought this way, since you were also a Citizen of Light, and you had some feelings for your kind. As for how you knew? You had just accidentally entered the Dark World.
And that experience left a bad impression on you—the money you had so hard to bring was swindled away by a slick-talking, smiling salesman!
So now you remember, turn your head and ask Spamton on your shoulder: "Uh...... Are you a Citizen of Light or a Child of Darkness? ”
Naturally, you didn't recognize that this was the salesperson who had tricked you back then.
You feel as if he glares fiercely at you through his glasses, and you don't care at all, just hoping for an answer from him.
"[People of Darkness]." He didn't hesitate at all, but you always felt his tone carried a hint of gloom. You glanced at him probingly, but couldn't see anything.
So you just scratched your hair and glanced through the window to confirm that the killer was indeed not there, but probably back at any moment. In the end, you climbed in through the window, ignoring the terrified eyes of those inside the cage who then looked at you with pleading eyes—please, you're not that kind, you don't want to save others, and they're probably not real, just characters created by this horror game, so life and death have nothing to do with you. Only after climbing over the window do you realize you could have used the front door.
Then you rummaged through the locker and found a few baguettes, sandwiches that looked like they'd only been stored for a day or two, and of course, some cured meats. In any case, having these foods was already a blessing in this situation. You put Spamton on the table, picked up the food and handed it to him, grabbed a piece of bread yourself, and started wolfing down it yourself.
Spamton didn’t eat, but just looked around the little house, then spoke: '…He is 【raising】 prey, waiting for the 【right moment】 to carry out the 【hunting process】. Meanwhile, these 【prey】, out of fear, are constantly in a 【mentally weakened state】.'
He kindly explained things for you. But your movements slowed down a little, paused, and you nodded at Spamton. Of course you understood what he meant—although the wording and sentences were a bit odd, you just weren't good at thinking, not a fool!
'Phew… thanks for the deduction, but for now, let’s just rest. Will you keep watch first?' After eating, you burped and continued to ignore the resentful gazes from the people in the cage behind you.
Spamton nodded, so you grabbed the back of his neck, looked for the bedroom, and then held Spamton and lay down on top.
You were drowsy, but didn’t forget to remind him: 'Wake me up in the later half of the night; it’ll be my turn to keep watch. Also, if you sense anything unusual, wake me up too.'
Spamton nodded, so you went to sleep peacefully.
You slept drowsily in a dark dream world. Calling it completely quiet and peaceful isn't entirely accurate, because after passing through that darkness, you still fell into the dream. To be honest, you almost forgot this memory, but in the dream world, everything remained so clear. Now you looked with some resentment at the salesman in front of you, still dressed in a red suit and smiling, while you had no control over your own actions.
So you know it's just a lucid dream; as long as you wake up after watching the process of the dream, everything will end. But honestly, to you, it's like a nightmare, so you firmly believe you might wake up before Spamton calls you. After all, having nightmares often means it's hard to have a good sleep experience. But think about where you're asleep now...... You won't have so many resentments.
You'd rather encounter more darkness in your dreams, even if it's boundless, just a patch of pitch black that makes you uneasy, even if just a glance makes you shiver uncontrollably, even if, at this very moment, besides this narrow dream street, you stand there with the salesman across from you, and all that's left is darkness.
Alright, since you're here, you can see the other person's lips opening and closing rapidly. You want to hear clearly, to fill in your hazy memories, but no matter how hard you try, you still can't make out clearly. Even if you focus intently, you can only catch the faintest words. You only know that from your impatient tone, you must have made some kind of deal at the time, then you take out your wallet and hand all the coins to the salesperson across from that time. Then comes darkness again. You don't know what happened next—you probably returned to the world of light.
In your dream, you were still trying to recall something, trying to find the vague or lost memories from before. But before you could continue thinking or enjoy a deep, dark sleep, you felt something violently shaking your arm. The crackling sound of electric currents or the unpleasant scraping of wood echoed beside you, sounding like something was being said. So you couldn't help but pull out your pillow and give it a quick blow to the source of the sound.
Now the other person completely quieted down, and your head rested on the bed board. The bed board was a bit firm; if you landed directly on it, it would probably hurt quite a bit. Fortunately, your head wasn't far from the bed board at that moment. Now you were fully awake, quickly picked up the pillow and put it back on the bed, roughly restoring its position.
Then you hear sounds outside—the door is closed, but the sound is getting closer and closer. You believe that in the next second, that person will be gripping the doorknob. The footsteps have already stopped in front of the door. You can imagine that hand is already on the doorknob, you hear the clicking of the knob turning—you swallow hard and instinctively hug Spamton tightly. Spamton seems to want to say something more, but you cover his mouth. You know your heart is pounding fast; you can almost hear the clear thumping sounds, right beside your ear.

After all, although ...... He did avoid these guys a bit, or rather, had a certain fear, disgust, and anger, but he couldn't go on like this forever. Moreover...... Spamton knew that everything was no longer what it used to be.
You chose to respect Spamton's choice, so after ordering, you called the waiter to take the menu, and the Addisons at the table looked over at your call. When they saw Spamton, their expressions and bodies froze.
You nervously swallowed nervously, glanced at Spamton, and saw the little puppet flash a cocky grin, then flip the middle finger at the table of Addisons.
You choked up for no reason, then you saw that pink Addison seemed furious, wanting to rush over and beat Spamton or something. I wasn't sure if you were mistaken, but you felt the veins on his head bulge. The other Addisons stopped him, grabbing his arm to tell him not to act rashly. You seemed to hear some kind of persuasive voice.
You were speechless for two seconds and simply chose to cross your arms and watch the show. After all, it wasn't really your business—this was Spamton's previous lingering interpersonal relationship and dispute. Honestly, you didn't fully understand his personality.
You just saw that pink Addison also give Spamton the middle finger, and then your mouth twitched. You pulled Spamton over and simply picked him up and placed him on the inside, so he wouldn't have to flip the finger silently with the other side again. It was like some kind of arena match. Then the waiter happened to bring out all the dishes. You stuffed the grilled meat slices into Spamton's bowl, and some stuffed into his mouth, saving him from saying anything else.
Spamton glared at you, and you glared back at him, unwilling to back down. He finally chewed and swallowed the meat you had just put into his mouth, but before he could speak, you shoved another piece of meat into his mouth, so he could only keep chewing.
You hummed softly twice and whispered to Spamton, "Eat your food properly! Stop doing such childish things." "As you spoke, you gently shoved him.
Fortunately, after that, Spamton didn't make any further noises; he just stood at his seat and continued picking up the barbecue to eat. You spent the rest of the time peacefully. The Addisons finished eating earlier and deliberately passed by your table. Then the pink Addison gave Spamton the middle finger, and Spamton returned the favor.
You pat your forehead, feeling a bit tired for some reason. Fortunately, the shop quiets down afterwards, and after you finish your meal, you leave the Cyber BBQ restaurant with Spamton.
You complained casually: "Why did you just make an international friendly gesture with those guys? I know you don't like those Dark People...... But what if a fight breaks out? I'm confident I can beat those people on the other side......"
Spamton was silent for a moment. Indeed, things were just as you said, but he also knew these Addisons cared about their reputation and reputation. After all, they still had to advertise everywhere, so of course they couldn't start fighting inside the store—at most, they'd handle it privately. That's why he did it on purpose.
So Spamton simply said softly, "No, they [absolutely won't] [fight loudly]." ”
"Then it's just like you said...... You're not right, aren't these guys waiting for us up ahead!" You whispered to Spamton, cursing because you saw those Addisons blocking the alley in the knife housing district. You skillfully picked up a discarded steel pipe from the ground and placed Spamton on your shoulder.
"Alright, then I'll just give you a good beating. I can finally get your revenge." You beamed with excitement, then swung the steel pipe at Addison opposite you. You didn't care about turn-based combat in this world; what did it have to do with you? You're not a game in real life. Addison on the other side clearly hadn't expected you to play completely against the rules. After all, turn-based combat doesn't follow these rules. In the chaos, colorful magical lights flashed by, but you didn't care about any of that. You just swung the physics holy sword in your hand—well, it wasn't a crowbar, but it was about enough. Then you knocked Addison on the neck, and out of kindness, you only knocked them out.
Then you casually tossed your hair, tossed the pole to the floor, and took big strides to walk forward. But before you could take two steps, you felt someone grab your pant leg. Impatiently, you glanced down and saw it was still the pink Addison. You patiently stopped, ready to hear what last words he had left. At the same time, you felt an itch to grab the pole from earlier.
And Addison just trembled as he gave Spamton another middle finger, then collapsed again without saying a word. You looked speechlessly at Spamton on his shoulder, but he just gave you an innocent glance. You sighed, brushed the nonexistent dust off your palm, and this time you really took Spamton and strode away.
By the way, you complained to him: "I told you to provoke those guys...... Now look, you still have to put in effort to make them submit. If it were only you, what would you do? This time, it's all thanks to me." ”
Spamton's demeanor was unusually obedient, making you hesitate and turn to look at him twice, but he simply said, "It's precisely because I know of your existence that I'm willing to step into the unknown." ”
It's precisely because he knows you're here, and that you won't let things unfold, that's why he does it.
You paused for a moment, because his words made you a bit embarrassed. You cleared your throat twice, scratched your head, then turned your head away and whispered, "Oh dear...... Alright, I get what you mean. You're right. I really wouldn't just leave you alone. "Of course, you wouldn't go causing trouble on your own initiative.
As you spoke, you cleared your throat seriously: "Alright, I plan to go back to the Light World first. I think my wish has already come true...... Do you need to go check somewhere? By the way, what wish did you actually make...... "You're curious about this, but it seems Spamton really doesn't want to tell you. He shook his head mysteriously, just making a gesture to keep quiet. You sighed, just about to say something else and put him at home for now, when you heard him speak."
"But I think I can now go to the Light World with you." He said, standing at your doorstep, about to open it. Hearing this, your eyes widened as you pointed at yourself and then at Spamton.
"Are you sure...... Can you really go to the World of Light now? But isn't your presence in the World of Light just some kind of junk email...... You muttered, then turned and left the door, heading toward the entrance to the world of light and darkness you had previously traveled back and forth. It was a blurry beam of white light, impossible to see ahead. It just existed at the end of the road.
You take a deep breath, just close your eyes, then reach out to touch that pure white light. After the dazzling light flickers, you return to the world of light.
You let out a sigh of relief and instinctively glanced at your shoulder, noticing that Spamton was indeed sitting on your shoulder. Curious, you grabbed him and squeezed him, and he really did exist—after all, the texture was exactly the same. You didn't know exactly how Spamton did it, so you just asked curiously, "Is this the wish you made?" ”
But Spamton just smiled without answering your question, and you weren't that annoyed. In short, he hadn't answered your questions more than once or twice—everyone has their own little secrets, and that's normal.
You couldn't be bothered to study what had happened to Spamton. You just took out your phone to glance at it, checked your contacts and social apps, then clenched your fist and shouted 'Yes.' Of course, you didn't mind sharing your joy. Maybe Spamton had guessed a bit, but you just said excitedly, "My wish has indeed come true! I want to be completely cut off from my family, though I don't know exactly how this game system manages it...... But indeed, it worked." "You're very happy. After all, this means you're free from now on and won't be bound by your family anymore. After all, you've already hated your family from the bottom of your heart."
…… Maybe it's not for any special reason. Although they're stingy materially, it's not a bad treatment. But you've never enjoyed emotional giving, and they actually ask you to reciprocate in return—both materially and emotionally. Honestly, that's why you dislike them—after all, your relationship isn't equal, and what you get isn't equal.
Whether or not you regret it later, at least for now, this is your wish, so you will never regret it.
"Your wish should have come true too...... I'm not sure either, but as long as it's a good thing, that's enough." You whistled out an off-key whistle and put away your phone. Honestly, you have nowhere else to go in the Light World, so it's better to take Spamton back to the Dark World.
But before you could move, Spamton called out to you: "I think we should first [check the newspaper information]. ”
You blink, a beat late, remembering that Spamton was talking about what happened in the game world. After all, those game worlds should have happened in the real world of light, so you still looked up those events in the order of the game world, since you were also somewhat curious about the outcome of those events.
You first looked up information related to the first world. After a long time, you only remembered the [Forest Murder Case] and something like that, but quickly came to the conclusion: [Thanks to the efforts of all the tourists, the serial murder case at the forest tourist resort has been officially closed. The police have uncovered the truth and learned that it is related to a recent wrongful conviction. The case has now been overturned, and the culprit will be punished......]
You blink, thinking this might be a good outcome, so you start looking into the second case...... To be honest, you're not really sure what this is, just searching [Building Arson Case]: [The mysterious event inside the building has come to an end!] The legend of the mermaid really exists—it's a mermaid's curse that caused the resurgence and hallucinations inside the building. Here, I remind everyone to have a compassionate heart and not to be evil or greedy......]
You exhaled and instinctively met Spamton's gaze on your shoulder. Although your names weren't on either case, you knew these were the gifts the world left behind after you completed the side quest.
You swallowed hard. Honestly, the third case should exist in an impossible future, so you didn't know what to search for. You just looked up the name of that research institute. Fortunately, you still remembered it.
You looked at the search results in disbelief and clicked in to take a second look.
[Shocking! A research member from a certain research institute actually conducted unauthorized research on the zombie virus without approval of the report application, causing multiple deaths and mutations into monsters! ]
You look at the monster pictures you posted and they really are the ones you defeated back then in the post-apocalyptic world.
Looking further down, you were eager to know what happened next.
[Fortunately, a member of the research institute discovered the cure for the zombie virus, saving the besieged institute, and even the entire world! The involved researchers have been apprehended and are awaiting further investigation...]
You exhaled and felt somewhat relieved. Although your names did not appear and everything was erased, you had truly done something to save the world, and at this moment, you felt happy about it.
So you keep searching. This time, you just look up the [17th century witch hunts], and a bunch of information pops up that makes you dizzy. Spamton, on the other hand, swipes a few times on your phone and then clicks into a report precisely.
[It is rumored that in the 17th century, angels descended to the world and released those 'witches' who were imprisoned and hopelessly awaiting death. The subsequent witch hunts ceased, reducing casualties, but the losses that had already occurred remained. Luckily, due to the immediate halt of the witch hunts, the visibly observable crop and meat harvests that year were higher than in previous years...]
You sighed in relief. Although not everyone had been saved, it seemed that the outcome was actually quite good.
So you confidently searched for the next item. You hesitated a bit, but in the end, you typed in the name of this hotel.
You opened the most sensational news.
[Public opinion conflict and war broke out! Revealed truths about a certain hotel sparked public outrage. The police have apprehended all involved personnel inside the hotel, but the disseminator of the information has not yet been found...]
When you got to this part, you swallowed hard and tapped your forehead. 'Oh no, I forgot to switch to a different account when sending the message back then.'
Including the second-to-last event, you also used your own account.
Spamton said nothing; he simply picked up the phone and typed in the name of XX company, which was your penultimate world.
You saw the latest report stating that the girl's father has been convicted of a crime and has been taken away for processing, while the person who posted the case still hasn't been found. The same person was at the previous hotel.
You cleared your throat: "I should register a new account...... and Spamton nodded in agreement.
'I can [provide help], [your] new account will have no connection to the [information disseminator],' he added.
You nodded, naturally agreeing: 'Alright, I’ll leave it to you.' Saying that, you took the phone back, hesitated for a moment, and finally entered your parents’ names.
There was all sorts of chaotic content, but nothing related to that case, and you smiled with relief, as all this had not yet actually happened.
By now, it was almost evening, and the moon was slowly rising. You put away your phone and stretched: "Alright, since you're in the world of light, come have dinner with me, then let's go to school together...... Maybe I can get you a diploma or something, but this year's recruitment period is already over, probably next year...... You muttered as you made plans, while Spamton just listened quietly.
Suddenly, he glanced at the sky and then said to you, '[The moonlight is beautiful tonight].'
You were momentarily stunned and instinctively looked up at the night sky, then wondered aloud, 'What, there aren’t any monsters falling from the moon either, what are you talking about?'
But today's moon was indeed beautiful—big and round. Thinking this, you naturally said, "But today's moon is indeed big and round, and tonight's moonlight is truly beautiful." "You don't have much education. If your classical prose skills were a bit higher, you would have written poetry based on the moonlight."
You hear Spamton sigh, so you look at him in confusion, then at the moon. Suddenly, you somewhat understand what he means—you just remember that someone across the East once said this as a subtle confession, and it spread widely. But at first, of course, you didn't react, since unless you spoke to you directly, you wouldn't realize it.
So you stroked your chin, hesitated at Spamton, and then said, "So what you actually mean is...... Are you saying you love me? "It seems there can't be any other meaning besides that."
Spamton nodded: "Of course." He didn't dwell on it too much, since if you really didn't understand...... He actually had no choice but to wait until one day you suddenly had an epiphany.
You nod blankly: "Uh, alright, I love you too, but why are you repeating this now...... Is it because everything has settled, so you want to confirm it again? ”
You hear him sigh again, and you scratch your head, unable to figure out what you've misunderstood this time.
"No, I just want to repeat 'I love you' again, 'That's all.'" You can't see his expression clearly; you just hear his voice in the night. It seems that as the night shifts, his voice also becomes somewhat elusive—after all, the neon lights happened to flicker at that very moment.
For some reason, you suddenly feel that if he couldn't reach the world of light today, he wouldn't repeat that sentence, and might even try to do the same thing as before...... Taking a gamble seems both clever and foolish. You look down at him for a moment, then suddenly pick him up, then hold him up and meet your gaze.
"Mm-hmm...... I love you too. Although I don't know if my feelings for me at this moment will change in the future, if they do, I'll tell you. Well, maybe this is something you don't expect to happen. "You mutter, after all, you've seen his expression change—you always feel like his smile has disappeared.
So you cleared your throat twice and decided to skip the topic for now: "Alright, let's not talk about that—are you planning to return to the Dark World first, or find a place to live in the Light World?" To be honest...... The rental for the Dark World apartment is still a long time away, and I really can't bear to part with it...... You muttered to yourself, counting on your fingers, suddenly realizing that less than half a year had passed since this trip, yet you felt as if you had already lived a lifetime. Or rather, you felt that what you've experienced over these six months is far richer than anything you've ever experienced before. Of course, including this little puppet in your hand. Before this, you never imagined that you might have any story with the salesman you once met in the Dark World—it would be a romantic one.
"That [house lease] can [provide refund services]." Spamton said. Actually, he probably didn't care where he actually lived; after all, in the Dark World, there wasn't much worth holding onto...... He was still considered a Dark Citizen, only able to use his body in the Dark World to enter and exit the Light World. In fact, he didn't understand the game system, or rather, how the Heaven Wishing Machine managed it, but he didn't regret his current fate.
You nodded, glanced at Spamton again, and asked again, "So you plan to live with me in the world of light?" ”
"Maybe it will be quite helpful for your [Adult University academic questions]?" He wasn't entirely sure, so this was just a question.
But you burst out laughing: "No, I can go to school in any environment...... Oh, and I have to remind you to sign up, but how do you solve your ID issue? You're basically entering illegally now...... You started muttering this, starting to worry. Spamton was silent for a moment, then touched his own pocket. Though he said it was a pocket, only the pocket of his jacket was worth looking at, and he really did pull out a driver's license from inside.
His name was still clearly written on it: Spamton G. Spamton.
Not only that, but there were even birth dates, issuance dates, and resident numbers. You glanced at the documents, and sure enough, they weren't fake. You stroked your chin and nodded, "Alright, then there's no problem...... But it's too late today. Tomorrow we'll go check out the house and rent it. Since there's nothing to move in anyway, let's just go on a big shopping spree! ”
Besides, you still have to attend class first, so you don't have time to deal with anything else. Fortunately, the teacher just thought Spamton was a doll or something and didn't interfere. You took Spamton to class all night, and he was so frustrated pretending to be a well-behaved doll in your arms.
After class, you took Spamton back to the Dark World. You were already very tired, and after a quick wash and tidying up, you hugged Spamton and lay down on the bed. Half-awake, you heard Spamton in his arms ask you a question.
"If you didn't have the [Heaven Wishing Machine], what would you do?"
You think he's just asking what he already knows, but you still yawn and force yourself to answer: "What's there to talk about...... As for me, I was probably just struggling in society, working hard to earn some money, and then one day I couldn't help but fall out with my family. That's all there is to it." "But you probably wouldn't kill anyone...... So, it was probably just your brother framing you, but you actually don't have any hope of surviving yourself.
Or rather, for you, there was no real meaning in survival...... But now, you're willing to walk with Spamton. If one day you find such days dull, then just deal with it then. But you think Spamton probably occasionally gives you some fright, so you probably won't ever feel bored.
After saying this, you hugged Spamton and drifted into a deep sleep. Once again, you dreamed of Spamton as a salesman, dressed in a red suit, looking radiant, and he was talking to you. You knew he was talking about wanting to see your soul. Of course, you couldn't show it to him—but in the dream, you were driven by a daze, driving your soul and body apart. It was a red heart, still faintly radiating some light.
Spamton seemed somewhat captivated, then he looked up and smiled at you: "Miss, your heart-shaped object is truly [beautiful and unique]. I think I already [love] you." ”
You instinctively step back, remembering that maybe this was the conversation you first met, but after that, you tacitly put everything out of your mind—after all, everything was different from now. Your soul trembled, as if stirred by those words, since you had never experienced anything like this before. So you fled in panic, just throwing away money in hopes of washing away this inexplicable memory.
And indeed, you must hurry up, since no one has mentioned it again. But your actions back then may have been a silent prayer in your heart, hoping that one day there will be a new connection between you. Mutual debt is always a form of connection and bondage.
And now, everything is over. You don't want to worry about the truth of those words, but after waking up, you're still a bit sleepy, and then you kiss Spamton on the forehead.
He had come to his senses at this moment, probably hesitating for a moment, then tilted his head and kissed your lips.
You stretched and sat up, finally fully awake. You changed your clothes with full energy, then took Spamton out for breakfast, met with the landlord of your rental apartment, successfully moved out, and then headed to the world of light.
You looked for a place near the school, viewed several units, and finally decided to rent one of the well-decorated ones that wasn't too expensive. Although it was a one-bedroom, you and Spamton both slept together, so of course it was fine.
And for some reason, landlords and other Lightfolk only treat Spamton as a doll. Even if the doll moves and talks, there's no reaction from them. You might wonder if Lightfolk's acceptance is a bit too high.
But Spamton didn't react much. In short, you rented a new big house, but it was empty, with nothing at all, so you just slung Spamton over your shoulder and went shopping.
First up are mattresses and similar items—mattresses—in short, a whole range of bedding items you need to buy. You can boldly wash bed sheets and duvet covers and then dry them, so they're ready to use right away. Then you start adding daily necessities, like pots and pans, and regular toiletries. Once you get these, you'll have some everyday clothes and items you might use but don't use often...... And kitchen supplies.
You pick up a bucket of oil, look at the label and put it in your cart, then look at Spamton on your shoulder, and sincerely ask, "Spamton, can you cook?" ”
Spamton hesitated for a moment but still nodded: "[Yes]?" But I can't guarantee that the [dish flavors] will match [your dining taste]. ”
You scratched your head: "It's fine." I'm not very particular about taste, I eat whatever you make...... Ah, right, but is there a bit of a problem with the seasoning? Is your taste bud good? ”
"[Theoretically], I [achieve the process of self-repair of taste]." At least when dining out with you, Spamton no longer felt numb to his taste. At first, he found it hard to believe—but later on, he got used to it.
To be honest, he was somewhat grateful for the game system. After all, without it, he wouldn't have met you, nor would he have encountered the present future. Although the game system clearly didn't intend to get you to clear the final level—you had already changed, so it didn't succeed. In the end, your wishes still need to be fulfilled.
You breathed a sigh of relief and nodded, "Alright, then I'll leave the cooking to you—not that I can't cook, I just want to taste what it's like to be served occasionally." "You said this with confidence, Spamton sighed, but in the end, he was instructing you to buy the vegetables he needed and such.
Besides that, you bought some instant food in case you don't have time one day, so you'll have something to eat later.
After bringing all these things home, the small room now had a warmer atmosphere. You carried Spamton out again, this time to sweep the clothing store.
"By the way, what clothes do you want to buy?" If he has no objections, you can buy him some children's clothes for little girls, usually princess dresses or such. The sizes are actually a bit larger and definitely suit him well.
For some reason, Spamton felt a chill down his spine, so he hurriedly said, "I hope it's a [Classic Suit]." "If he heard correctly, you must have sighed in great disappointment!"
But in the end, you still secretly bought him a few children's princess dresses and didn't let him see them. Anyway, you can quietly put them on later! You just want to look, there's nothing wrong with that, you thought righteously.
After a busy schedule, you finally lay down on that big bed, holding Spamton and staring at the ceiling, the corners of your mouth involuntarily lifting.
After all, a brand new, unknown new life was about to begin.
Sunday· END

title: Horror Game Port 1 - Old House in the Forest
path: articles/en/spt/恐怖片大逃杀 end/天堂许愿机器/恐怖游戏端口1-林中古屋.html
content:
Sptx you, ooc count me
…… Poe got hooked, so the style of this series leans a bit more toward Poe's writing style. Also, since it's a horror game with a genre similar to infinite stream (? ) It's not entirely based on the original work.
This piece leans more towards the style of Edgar Allan Poe, with relatively more description and less narrative dialogue.
——
…… To be honest, you have no idea why you've come here. Just a moment ago, you were drinking beer at a barbecue restaurant, enjoying a tipsy sensation and thinking about what to do next. But the next second, you're sitting here shrouded in darkness, gloomy leaves pressing down overhead, on soft ground where only faint light filters through the gaps between the lush leaves. You casually touch the soft ground, and the first thing you feel is the slightly rough, dry surface of the leaves. Then, with an unintentional press, you hear the crunching sound of the fallen leaves piled together.
You can't just sit and wait for death, so you brush the dust off your clothes and stand up, ignoring the pain in your tailbone from suddenly sitting on the ground. Then you gradually adjust to this drowsy darkness—honestly, you really hope to find a way out so you can leave here quickly, and you don't care what exactly is happening to you, or what is happening beside you. Because you know that it could only mean bad omens, because you have uneasy signs, and you are a selfish person—so you only plan to leave alone.
Unfortunately, just as you recognized the direction of the wind in the forest and planned to follow the wind and step on the creaking leaves, you heard a sound like a pop-up window. In short, it was a bell, and it sounded like an explosion in your mind. You had to stop, almost annoyed, staring at the transparent window before you, which even glowed faintly.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest together with your companions. ]
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'killer.' ]
You looked at these two lines of text helplessly, so you looked around, then lowered your head and saw another but identical pop-up window—in the subtle dimming, you could barely recognize it as the tiny figure that had been standing nearby before, its outline almost like a puppet. To be honest, at the time you even thought it didn't really exist, after all, this was a forest, and maybe ...... Maybe it was just the incarnation of some tree.
But now, through the screen's light, you can finally see his pale face—or maybe it's his own complexion. He wears a pair of ridiculous pinkish-yellow glasses, so you can't see his mood. Of course, you're not very curious about it. You just crouch down, looking him up and down, and he seems wary, but doesn't say a word. After hesitating for a moment, the puppet finally reaches out his hand to you.
"I think we need to cooperate with [you] and I to leave this [world]." His voice sounded strange, with a crackling sound like electricity. You scratched your ear and felt a bit uncomfortable, but for you, perhaps having another companion in this darkness was actually a blessing—after all, you all saw that panel, and he had no other missions, so perhaps you could let go of your unfounded vigilance and just take this little puppet and escape this forest together.
Of course, as for that side quest, it's probably fine not to complete it...... Just as you were thinking this, you saw the text on that panel update.
[Main Quest: Escape this forest with your companions.] Reward: Survive successfully and have seven days off, immune to all lethal factors
[Side quest: Uncover the truth behind the 'Killer'.] ] Reward: 10,000 gold
You smacked your lips in annoyance. Honestly, this was like suddenly getting involved in some kind of horror game—honestly, ten thousand dark coins made you a bit envious, but you had no deductive skills. You've always believed in physics and cryptography. If you can't unlock it, just break it outright!
So you looked down at the little puppet again, raised your eyebrows, and reached out your hand to him: "Alright, since things have come to this, we can only reach a partnership. But just to be clear, since I can't handle side quests like this kind of deduction and cryptography, I'll leave it to you." You said it as if it were only natural, and without waiting for him to refuse, you continued to add more.
"As for the main quest—don't worry, I'll take you with me and leave here. I don't know how you should address me, but just call me Y/N." You shrugged, watching him reach out his hand toward you. You casually grabbed his hand and shook it, then grabbed it and lifted it up, placing him on your shoulder.
After all, you just heard an unsettling rustling sound from the leaves not far away. It wasn't the sound of wind, but clearer, more obvious human voices. Someone was walking through the woods in this direction, probably just patrolling normally. After all, you had just tried it. The light screen couldn't be broken, so maybe it wasn't because you saw it.
Before he could answer, you heard footsteps getting closer behind you. After all, the sound of stepping on withered leaves was too obvious, not to mention the sound of chainsaws starting the wheels, the sizzling sound, and a faint, terrifying smell of blood—so you just grinned: "Forget it, these things can wait a bit. For now, let's run!" "Better hold on!" ”
With that, you pushed off the ground and dashed out. Honestly, you're quite good at sports, so running a distance is easy—even fast, not difficult. Right now, you're only slightly out of breath, with lactic acid accumulating in your legs and a slight ache. You didn't mind at all, just weaving through the woods, listening to the ominous sound of a chainsaw moving farther away, while you found a more lush, densely packed spot and rushed in.
You were still running, and before Spamton could answer, he was forced to clutch your clothes. Honestly, he definitely didn't want to be thrown off in a place like this—although for the main quest, you'd probably go back to save him, but he didn't want to experience that kind of anxiety. And just as he was about to speak, he was blown into the air, so the words he wanted to say were twisted by the howling wind, spreading and spreading with eerie sounds.
"My [name] is—" Unfortunately, the voices behind him were all faded by the wind.
And you just raise your voice and ask, "You—are—saying—what—"
Spamton hated his current situation—unsettling, confusing, and precarious. He always had to come up with a plan to protect himself, always figure out a way to live a better life. Of course, he was willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, even if it was just a brief experience of being a despised rat, as long as he still had the ability to choose, as long as he had the ability to think, he would never let himself willingly remain in that situation.
And he recognizes you. He knows you are a Citizen of Light he met a few years ago. Unfortunately, he didn't get what he truly wanted from you, but was sent off by money.
But now, relying solely on his own abilities, he couldn't accomplish anything. He was confident that if you hadn't taken him away from that place, he would have been finished, declared his death, and declared it all with deep resentment and displeasure.
If it weren't for you, maybe he wouldn't have ended up in this situation—but without you, he absolutely couldn't have escaped it. If you didn't seem completely unaware, he'd almost think all of this was your deliberate design.
