Your steps were light, yet you walked quickly. Though you hesitated, you didn't change direction and just kept moving forward. But now, even though there was no one chasing you, you kept looking back as if making sure no one was following.
Spamton also notices and reminds you: "Before [appear], [keep moving forward]. ”
You frowned, but your voice carried a hint of irritation and dissatisfaction: "I know, of course I don't need your reminder...... But given the current situation, I can't confirm the time, so I can't confirm when that killer will come after me...... This is really nerve-wracking...... You muttered to yourself, but suddenly realized that without giving him time, yet telling him exactly when he'd come after you—could this be part of the killer's scheme?
"Maybe [you] need [chat], to [shake off tension and regain pleasure]?" he said.
You were silent for a moment, sighed irritably, and looked at the still-bright sky—the sunlight outside was just right, with a few rays of sunlight streaming through the gaps in the leaves, falling onto the ground. Occasionally, the honey-like color would drip onto you, as if even your clothes could melt with moisture. But in the woods, all you could feel was the coldness. More often, vast patches of shade fell on the ground. With the sound of the wind, those irregular shadows danced and rose and fell on the ground. The wind was music, accompaniment, the main theme of everything—of course, there was also the sound of chainsaws that might start at some point, steel, the smell of blood. Even just walking through the shaded ground, you felt surrounded by this scent.
You opened your mouth, but didn't make a sound at first. You knew you were still hesitating; you didn't want Spamton to ask the same question again, since they were probably just temporary partners, and you didn't need to reveal your life experiences. Even though you knew you were from two different worlds, he wouldn't want to use those things to stab you in the back when you got back.
But you hesitate for a moment, swallow a mouthful of cold wind, cough for a while, quicken your pace, and finally start running again—because you hear the sound of a chainsaw behind you in the distance. You understand: time is up, you can't afford to waste any more. Those irrelevant nonsense can be brought up later, though whether there is any chat time, you don't know.
So at this moment, you just instinctively pressed your shoulder: "...... Alright, let's chat again next time. Right now, we should be running first!" You said, raising your eyebrows happily. Honestly, you even felt relieved and delighted at the killer's pursuit at this moment. You could avoid this question, and you even regretted saying that sentence back then.
Even when you can endure it, why are you willing to say it when you know the other person is a complete stranger? Is it because strangers are more likely to fall for these feelings to you?
…… Forget it, I'll save that question for another time. Thinking about it now is too exhausting. You pat your head, and Spamton, seeing you start running, has no choice but to grab your clothes again to keep him from being thrown off. You start running quickly, stepping on the leaves. At that moment, you no longer care about noise, so you step heavily on those leaves. The broken leaves let out a mournful cry, but you keep moving forward, running forward until the scattered leaves become sparse, and you step on soft yet somewhat firm ground, leaving a gentle dent with your footsteps.
And you kept moving forward, running forward until you could no longer hear the chainsaw. The killer must have gone in another direction. Only then did you suddenly stop holding onto a tree trunk, gasping for breath, patting your slightly sore leg, and pulling Spamton back onto your shoulder.
Then you patted your shoulder that was also a bit sore from his weight and grinned: "Aha...... Looks like that guy isn't chasing after you. Let's walk slowly for a while, just like we rest...... You mutter, then remember, glaring fiercely at Spamton.
"So annoying...... I'm the only one walking around, and you're great—you don't have to do anything, I'm the only one running......" you muttered.
Spamton was about to explain when you heard you add another sentence, and you had already adjusted yourself: "Forget it...... Tsk! Anyway, it's nothing, and we agreed to let you handle the brain-solving part. I don't like to think about it. So I'll just do some physical work!" As you spoke, you got motivated again, stepping on solid ground as you walked forward.
He swallowed back what he had just wanted to say, changing the subject: "Perhaps, the timing is just right. We should [return home]." We haven't checked that [hidden room]. ”
You nodded: "What you said makes sense, but let's wait and see for ourselves...... Since we're here, I feel the wind here is stronger and more obvious. I'm really curious about what is happening here." Saying this, you parted the blocking branches and followed the light forward.
So Spamton swallowed the sentence he still wanted to say—after all, if he just stayed here for a while, it wouldn't matter. Besides, he did have more questions he wanted to ask you. He wanted to know the answers to previous questions, since learning more about partners is always beneficial, and besides, it probably wasn't just this one collaboration—he had a feeling about that. As for why things had turned out like this, it was probably because of that original transaction.
Perhaps feeling a bit guilty at that moment—maybe he was curious, or maybe he just chose to trust you. So Spamton sat on your shoulder, swaying as he watched as you walked into the light and arrived at a clearing. Directly ahead was a road, with few leaves, just clean dirt and car tracks. You could tell there were quite a few people there. There were still a few RVs parked in the clearing, but unfortunately, no one was there, and it looked like it hadn't been used for days, making it feel rather deserted.
You smacked your lips: "Alright, you roughly know how to complete the main quest. Just grab a car from here and drive away, just follow that road...... Oh no, I don't even remember how I got there...... By the end, you felt a bit guilty and lowered your voice.
At this moment, Spamton's voice rang out: "I have a clear plan." ”
So you nod cheerfully: "Oh, oh, you remember...... Then I'll leave it to you! Oh my god, I was just wondering what to do next time, maybe I should make some marks on my way back...... But if there were marks, that killer would probably find ......? "As you keep talking, you're not quite sure either.
Spamton shook his head: "[No], I'll [point the way] for you. [You] just need to [follow the guidance] and [complete the plan]. ”
"Mm, as long as you don't point the wrong way, I believe you." You nodded again.
Spamton just glanced at your profile again, probably sighing inwardly. Honestly, I really believe you made the right choice. You stumbled on the right path and found the right direction. And he really remembers your direction, your way from. After all, the landmark is so obvious—if you walk a short distance, you'll see that tree. He also remembers exactly which direction you took after leaving the cabin, so it's totally fine.
But now, you twisted your neck, not paying attention to what Spamton was thinking, only briefly calming yourself. After all, you couldn't just stay immersed in this excitement and joy: "Alright, let's go back! We still have to finish that side quest first. It's ten thousand bucks, and I can't just let it slide." You swore confidently, retreating back into the woods, then, confidently relying on your impression, walked off in one direction.
Spamton hesitated for a moment, unsure of what to say, but he didn't want to shatter your confidence at this moment. Maybe he was a bit mischievous—after all, he had always been hanging on your shoulders before, and when things were awkward, he needed to regain some respect, so he didn't remind you. Or maybe he just wanted to use this opportunity to remind you about your relationship.
So you touch the trunk, feeling that this cold shade before you feels familiar, but looking behind you, it's still a forest. You don't know where to go, so you squat down in frustration, looking at the scattered leaves scattered on the ground...... Leaves, ah.
For the first time in a while, you felt the wind in the quiet. You watched the leaves drift with the wind and then changed direction. You still remember the direction the wind had gone when it arrived, and where the leaves were stretching out. Although the wind now seems to have changed direction, because the leaves were blown off their original course, this spot happened to be where the land and leaves meet. You could still see where the leaves were heading at first, and that was where you came from. So you stood up confidently, changed direction, and continued forward. This time, you were heading in the right direction, because you had only sped up for a short distance before vaguely seeing that little wooden cabin.
…… Spamton didn't expect you to find the right direction so quickly. He's ready—if you ask about it, he'll give you the right answer. Of course, all of this comes with a price and reward. He just didn't expect you wouldn't need this deal at all. Just like back then, just like before.
He stopped his thoughts, no longer recalling the past, just silently gazed at your profile, then looked ahead. Maybe this time things would change, and everything would be different.
And you finally managed to run back to that cabin. Maybe the most dangerous place is the safest place. Of course, you don't believe that saying, after all...... You think rather than that, you might as well become that danger yourself, or just defeat it altogether. This time, you climbed through the window and ran toward the bookshelf. You skillfully fiddled with the books, arranged the 19321110, and then the shelf rumbled as it moved to the side. You opened your mouth wide and saw a door appear behind you.
"Wow...... Looks like there might be something good in this room. "You muttered instinctively, rubbing your hands together. You're quite curious about what might be in this room, and you can't help but get nervous.
"[No], or maybe [evidence of a crime]." Spamton reminded.
You didn't care about any of that, just shook your head and said, "Anyway, whatever it is...... I feel like the side quest can be completed smoothly at this point. Anyway, let's go in and take a look first." With that, you pushed open the door.
But the room was pitch black, deep and shadowy, and somehow a gust of wind started blowing from behind you. You shivered instinctively, and in the darkness, countless possibilities began to form in your mind.
In that darkness, and in the faint, flickering candlelight that had appeared at some point, you could vaguely see your own shadow. You wondered where the wind came from, why the candlelight was flickering—and where was the flame coming from? Clearly, this place should be pitch black.
You couldn't help but shiver. You clearly didn't feel the cold, but through the faint firelight, you saw yourself—a mirror not far away—or rather, a blackened window glass. On it, only a faint image could be seen. The person who had blacked it didn't want others to notice it. The wind still lingered through the window slit, gently stirring the window lattice, making a clicking sound.
This also explains why the candle flame flickers. Probably so. In short, everything seems explainable. Thinking this, you lower your head to look at the candle flame somewhere low, wondering how the candle flame actually comes from.
Then, you realize you've forgotten something—Spamton, who has followed you into this dark room. You open your mouth to call his name, but hesitate, afraid to speak in the oppressive darkness. That unknown darkness and silence envelop you, and in that silence, you can unexpectedly hear the sound of your heart.
As for why it was pitch dark—after all, when you opened the door and entered the dark room, the door behind you rumbled shut again. So now you still regret it. If you'd known last time, you wouldn't have waited for the last time. You might as well have risked your life to hide in the dark room, especially since there was a window here.
At this very moment, you shake your head, shake off those thoughts, and lower your head to look at the candlelight. After your vision adjusts to some darkness, you realize the person holding the candlestick is actually Spamton. He doesn't say a word, just quietly holding the candlestick and watching you, lost in thought, so much so that in the darkness, you inexplicably feel intimidated when looking at his glasses.
As for Spamton? He hadn't spoken at all, since he wanted to see how you would react. To be honest, he didn't do this on purpose. After noticing your silence, he looked at your face by candlelight, and at that moment found yourself panicked and timid—sometimes timid, sometimes brave and resilient. Spamton found watching your emotional changes interesting. He roughly had a guess...... Maybe in the future, he could make some kind of deal with you in the dark, as if you were afraid of the dark.
Then you cough twice: "Cough, cough...... Where do you get the anger? "That's your biggest confusion."
"I [found] a [flint] on the floor of the darkroom." Spamton pointed to the floor not far away. You follow his point, and there really is a flint there.
"Alright, it seems you have good eyesight in the dark too." You shrugged and said casually, while Spamton neither agreed nor disagreed; he was just subconsciously observing his surroundings.
You bent down and gently took the candlestick from Spamton's hand, but he didn't stop you. Then you walked not far away, looking at the candlesticks of all sizes and heights filling the room, and gently approached with the candle flame in your hand, lighting one candlestick after another. Then, in this dim yet bright room, you stared at the things on the floor and fell silent, then couldn't help but start retching. Now you knew what the faint, lingering scent of blood in the air really was.
Because—lying on the floor were several heads casually thrown there, most of which wore terrified expressions. Some were still fresh, but their faces were a bit swollen, showing an unattractive bluish-purple color. More than that, probably because they had been placed for a long time, red or yellow fluids had flowed out, and the blood mixed together was nearly dried up, the skin shriveled and gradually turned dark brownish-black. The cut surfaces also turned black, and you could see the greasy yellow dripping down before slowly drying up.
You pinched your nose. Besides that, there was a magic circle carved on the ground. These heads looked like offerings, perhaps simply for worship—who were they worshipping? Because when you looked up, you saw two tombstones directly ahead.
Spamton didn't say anything, just closed his eyes, then grabbed the clothes at your pant leg. You felt the pressure on your pant leg and looked down at him—well, you could only see the top of the little puppet's head, so you couldn't be bothered to think further. You just circled around the two tombstones and looked up, only to find that the walls were actually filled with various photos—including cropped printed text.
You get dizzy just looking at these words, and you don't want to decrypt them, so you pick up Spamton and sit on your shoulder. It's still more convenient to let Spamton look directly.
You turned your head to glance at him, pursed your lips, and said, "In that case, I'll just leave these text and photos for you to see. If you say you want to see something, just let me move a seat." "At this moment, you're just a ruthless commuting machine."
Spamton meets your gaze. Well, fine, he can only see sincerity and clear foolishness in your eyes, and it's clear you have no desire to decode—but from his guess, you actually do think anyway, just a bit slow to react. But since you want to, he still looks at the wall.
First are the photos—you saw those too, most of them solo shots, faces you don't recognize. Only two were of two people, and then you thoughtfully nodded at one of the pictures: "Ah...... These two people, I've seen before, are the people who appeared in the group photo that the killer didn't ruin—probably his parents. ”
Spamton nodded and turned to another photo, which also showed a married couple. Between the two photos were several letters, which looked handwritten, though it was unclear how the killer had found him. In short, it looked ...... letters from them pouring out their hearts, with handwriting both male and female.
So Spamton pointed to the photo: "That photo is his 'parents'' [affair partner]." ”
You nod thoughtfully: "Ahh...... I see. So what about these people? "You've given up thinking and don't want to look. Let Spamton take a look.
"Then [you] need to move to the [left]." he said.
So you move a few steps to the left to make it easier for Spamton to look. He read the text hanging on the wall. To be honest, it was all commentary—some printed, some clipped from newspapers, mostly commentary on previous reports, mocking that his parents had both cheated on another couple and died as if it were right. Some comments called for a lighter sentence, suggesting that people in this world despise cheating even more—perhaps a world that accepts couples killing one of the cheaters.
So he turned his head to you, and possibly to the light screen that appeared at some point, explaining: "After the [death report], the person who appeared on the photo wall mocked the [report's content] and [parents]. Therefore, he decided to [take revenge], and at the same time, [mourning] and [sacrifice] to his parents. And the [hunting behavior] is meant to make the [targeted] and [former perpetrator] feel [fear] and experience [the same confusion they once had]. The only question is how he [chooses the target]......"
You all saw it. With his words, the completion rate of side quests kept rising, only stopping when he reached 80%.
You rubbed your chin, wondering how to pick a target, how to get people to come here...... Then you thought about the car you saw in that clearing and casually said, "This place is a tourist destination...... It used to be the place where his parents drove over here? ”
You see the progress bar for side quests has turned to 88%
So you nod involuntarily, and Spamton quieted down. He quietly watched your profile, realizing that even if he thought he understood you, he could still notice something different the next moment.
And you didn't notice his gaze, just continued talking to yourself, or maybe guessed: "And as long as you spread some rumors and rumors that the couple who died here have become vengeful spirits or something, only by coming here to worship will they avoid being entangled. Those with hidden feelings will fall for it!" ”
But you're not just guessing. In fact, when you arrived at that clearing earlier and hurriedly glanced past the few campervans parked there, you caught sight of candles and other items left in the car, along with bouquets—clearly meant for those coming to pay respects.
So you still combine your previous findings with your speculation, and then you'll find that the side quest progress has reached 100%, with flowers and fireworks appearing on the screen—probably congratulations on completing the quest.
You cheerfully say, "Wow, this task is done—ten thousand, that's ten thousand!" You were excited, but the next second, you realized that ten thousand coins had turned into ten thousand dark coins, and you lost your smile. To be honest, although most of it was done for Spamton, at least 20% was done by you, and without you, Spamton wouldn't know what would have happened at this moment!
So you glanced at Spamton quietly; he probably felt guilty too. You sensed the little puppet's body was probably stiff, but you didn't care about it. You just grabbed his shoulder and started shaking him.
"I don't care...... You have to give me half of these ten thousand. Dark coins are fine, but I want the currency circulating in the dark world too! I can't give you everything, or what would I be! "You grumbled in annoyance, tugging Spamton, watching him make a surrender gesture, and only then did you feel a bit satisfied.
"So, quickly tell me the address...... When I get back, I'm going to the Dark World to catch you......" you said in a chilling tone, grabbing him by the back of the neck and lifting him up in front of you. You stared at him fiercely. Good, you could tell Spamton was about to tell you something—you felt satisfied.
But before you could answer, you all heard the door ringing. Listening in the darkroom sounds dull and blurry, and you instinctively tensed up. You have to know, the bookshelf hasn't been restored to its original state; the killer will definitely come to check the room, and maybe you two will die here—so you quickly run to the window to try to open it, not caring whether Spamton has answered you or not. You shake it twice and find the window is completely nailed shut, unless ...... unless you smash the window and get out.
You gazed quietly at the pitch-black window, then at Spamton holding it—you instinctively reached out and pinched the little puppet's skin. Hmm, it really did look like wood, but it still had some hardness, so smashing the window might be fine! Spamton, watching your movements and gaze, had a bad feeling, and the next second, that feeling came true.
Because you lifted him up with both hands, then really smashed a huge hole in the window—the crisp sound of glass shattering. The next second, you could hear the killer quicken his pace, the heavy footsteps approaching the dark room. There was no time to say anything else. You looked at the gap in the window you had smashed and struggled to carry Spamton out. Honestly, Spamton was actually quite useful, you thought to yourself.
As for Spamton...... Honestly, breaking glass or being scratched by broken glass is really painful, but probably because the force is too large, that long-lasting pain actually fades after a while.
But you didn't care that much. When death was near, who cared what it looked like? You just ran forward holding Spamton, then instinctively looked down at him. He silently pointed you in the right direction, so you kept running in that direction, until a light suddenly appeared ahead, until the rustling leaves beneath your feet disappeared, until you stepped onto soft ground again. You saw a vehicle parked ahead, and you found a car with its key still stuck in the car and not removed...... Well, to be honest, it seems none of the cars had their keys removed—maybe it was the killer who stuck them? After all, giving a little hope makes the hunting game more interesting, and lets you see the inherent flaws of human fighting and betrayal.
You can't think too much about it, just quickly climb onto the car, put the Spamton in the passenger seat, and then swerve off on the starting car. You can hear the chainsaw approaching your direction, and if you turn around, you can still see the killer.
The car kept shaking, and Spamton didn't have time to fasten his seatbelt, only raising his voice a bit: "[Request: Smooth journey—]"
And you raised your voice: "Ah—I never got my license, just driving recklessly. Bear with me, as long as I can get out, that's enough—" You floored the accelerator and pushed the speed to maximum. Soon, the sound of the chainsaw disappeared. The woods ahead gradually thinned, revealing an exit to the outside world. You could vaguely see a few houses and a distant highway.
“Oh, right, so where exactly are you—address—”
Before reaching the finish line, you pant and raise your voice. You turn your head and watch Spamton's mouth open and close, but unfortunately, you don't hear it. Because as you cross the finish line, a blinding white light flashes, everything around you melts in that instant, and you can't help but close your eyes. The next moment you open them, you find yourself sitting up in your cramped, dark rental apartment.
You remember Spamton's mouth movements barely audible...... Trash, does he live in a garbage heap? Are you kidding? You suspect it's your own dream, but the next second, a strange voice rings out, reminding you that none of that was a dream at all.
“Ding dong, main quest completed successfully, congratulations, player.”
Lin Secondhand House· END

content:
You calmly patted your cheek...... Forget it, not calm at all. You glanced at the time—it was still 3:30 a.m., just as you finished your part-time job and were about to go to bed, and somehow it ended up in that game—it must be Spamton's fault, how could it be your own fault? You firmly believed this, pushed aside the quilt with torn threads exposing the cotton, got out of bed, passed over the stacks of instant noodle boxes and chocolate wrappers on the floor, closed the old computer with its screen lit up, and glanced at the front door.
…… There's a bill on the door urging you to pay your water, electricity, and gas. You glance at the old calendar hanging on the wall, think for a moment, count on your fingers, and realize tomorrow is the payment deadline. Of course, since you can also move out of the lease, it doesn't really matter whether you pay or not. This is just next month's fee.
And after you got fired, you don't have money left to pay the collection and rent. You plan to pack up the last bit of things tomorrow and head to the Underworld—mainly to get your money back! Anyway, you think renting in the Underworld is fine!
…… So, let's sleep first. You closed the door. Luckily, in this weather, it was still a bit cold, but it was barely manageable. And you made it through the coldest times, so it didn't matter at all. You just skillfully curled yourself up, wrapped yourself in a quilt with a few holes, and drifted off to sleep.
The next morning, you still woke up punctually at nine, because normally you'd be going to the hospital at ten o'clock to work as a morgue porter, but yesterday you happened to be fired. You opened a box of instant noodles, boiled some water, ate a little, threw away the box, changed into decent clothes, and packed some luggage—all you could pack was just a slightly bigger backpack.
Then you thought about the location, touched your still empty belly, mustered your strength, and headed to the place where you remembered the intersection of the light and dark worlds. You passed through that entrance and entered the dark world. To be honest, you were a bit nervous. After all, last time you had entered by mistake and had no particular purpose, so it didn't matter. But today, you still had other motives, and you knew nothing about the paths of the dark world.
Forget it, since you're here, it's better to settle in. You tugged at the strap of your backpack, looked at the blue-black buildings and the neon signs hanging on the tall buildings, then at the neon lights slowly lighting up as you walked by. The shadows stretched longer and then lit up again with the next light—well, it looked like they were welcoming you. You calmly thought, what is there left to welcome someone like you?
But that thought lasts only a moment. You keep moving forward, forward—and then obviously, you're lost. According to what Spamton said earlier, you think he probably lives in some kind of garbage station-like place? It can't be that he lives in garbage...... But now, looking at the brightly lit streets and cars speeding by, you stop and look around. Good, it seems there isn't much of a person worth stopping to ask for, because all the faces you've never seen are quietly watching you. They think you haven't noticed at all, but you have noticed long ago, just pretending not to see them.
Maybe it's because you're a citizen of light. You find joy in hardship, but in fact, you're a failed citizen of light. Patting your cheek, you decide to move in a different direction and stop dwelling on these emotions. But as you take a step forward, you almost slip. Looking down, you see a foot stepping on a billboard. The bill is very old, wrinkled at the edges, and the image is no longer vibrant, but has turned a withered yellow. You've probably been drifting in this city for several days, since you've noticed several footprints on it.
You pulled your foot back and picked up a corner of the ad with a hint of disdain to take a look. Ah...... Actually, the design was pretty good, with the text and images arranged just right...... But that's not the point! You pulled your wandering attention back and glanced at the image on the ad—oh, the annoying salesman you had encountered when you accidentally entered the dark world earlier. As for the name...... Your movement froze. What had been a casual glance now fixed on that name.
SPAMTON G. SPAMTON.
…… Aha, you laughed silently twice inwardly, without any amusement. To be honest, you really did want to laugh out loud, maybe just ...... You wanted to mock yourself, maybe that's how it is? Your hand weakly loosened the flyer, watching it drift away with the wind that appeared at some unknown moment, not knowing whose foot it would land on or whose face it would hit, but you didn't care.
You were just a bit annoyed, but also a bit curious—after all, you were curious, and you never recognized him from start to finish. Now you still find it hard to believe—the gap is just too big.
But who it is and what their real identity is—it doesn't matter to them. It won't stop you from asking them to share the money that should have belonged to you! So you're just heading in the direction you chose. You know, that direction looks rather dull, and the walls are a bit old—maybe the direction of the garbage dump. You guess like this and try to lighten your mood.
Sure enough, but this place should probably be called a garbage heap too...... I really can't think of a good word to describe it. You walk around those piles of trash, then frown and pinch your nose. Honestly, you absolutely don't want to rummage through the trash! Your life isn't that down-and-out. So now you hope Spamton will be more self-conscious and step out on its own, since you haven't found any residents at the garbage station.
You walk forward, and instead of piles of trash ahead, there are trash bins of all sizes. You finally don't have to cover your nose anymore. So you let go and start looking around, then your gaze settles on one of the large trash bins. You stroke your chin.
After all, you saw the lid of the trash bin move twice, and it looked like it wasn't sealed at all. If it were just that, it would be fine, but after that, it moved several times after a while. So guess who's probably inside, and you think that's your target this time.
So you take a deep breath, get ready, suddenly open the trash bin lid, and then pull Spamton out.
He seemed a bit stunned, but upon seeing you, he quickly recovered and said, "It's [you]." ”
You nod, loosen the lid of the trash bin, and reach out to Spamton to make a hand gesture for money: "Yes, it's me, hand over the money! My five thousand, that's my five thousand!" ”
As you say this, grab Spamton and glar at him fiercely.
“…… Maybe [you] need [usage recommendations]? "I don't know why, but you felt this little puppet shivering—maybe it's a bit guilty?"
And you just snorted coldly: "No need. Now I know, you're the salesman who cheated all the money from me back then, so this time I won't trust you again! Just give me the money directly!" ”
Then you meet the gaze of the little puppet in front of you. You watch him silently for a moment, then reluctantly nod: "Then, I'll [lead], [you] will follow the action." ”
"That's more like it." You set him down on the ground with satisfaction, nodded, and watched him walk forward. You followed him slowly—to be honest, you hadn't noticed there was a hidden door just now, and it was a shortcut. You silently sighed in your heart.
Seeing that you were about to walk a bit further, you lowered your head to look at the back of the little puppet ahead, hesitated for a moment, and finally asked, "That ...... So I want to know, why did you make a deal with me back then?" ”
Actually, you thought you would forget about it, since it was mysterious back then and sounded like a scammer. You talk about getting what you most want for a tiny price, but you wonder how the other person knows what your dad's wish is, and the trivial price—you say you wouldn't care at all, but who knows what this salesman is really for?
In short, you only wanted to lose money to avoid disaster, so you painfully gave all the money you had to Spamton. Honestly, that was your paycheck! So you never wanted to come back to the underworld afterward, and felt that stumble that day was truly unlucky.

The bright lights were so bright and blinding that you wanted to turn them off, but you were still thinking about Spamton, who hadn't gone to bed yet, so you didn't move. Oh my god, you almost feel moved for yourself. After all, you're such a good person, even willing to hold on a little longer for this.
Yawning again, you finally saw him come out. After all, you could hear him climbing onto the bed with your eyes closed, and of course, you also felt the bed sink in a lump together. Although it was slow, probably because he spent some time getting into bed. You still didn't open your eyes, just clumsily getting up and feeling for the switch on the wall, then turned off the light. Your vision turned dark again, so you happily and comfortably lay back down.
But after just a short while, you felt the blanket being pulled. It took you a moment to realize something: oh, you only prepared a blanket, not something for Spamton to cover up. So you awkwardly coughed twice inwardly, then turned over and chose to throw the blanket in that direction. In the darkness, even though you opened your eyes, you still couldn't see anything, so you were just following your instincts. Fortunately, you probably caught it, since you now feel there's some air leaking there.
You were a bit speechless, choosing to close your eyes and press your blanket against yourself—well, it didn't help much. You simply reached forward and felt around, then pulled Spamton a little closer toward you. Good, now there won't be any air leaking, but you feel like if you turn around, you'll press on him.
After a moment of silence, you choose to ignore it, just close your eyes and sleep!
You slept deeply and comfortably, a peaceful night without any dreams, sleeping soundly until dawn. You groggily opened your eyes, reacted dully for a moment, and realized Spamton was now in your arms...... Uh, but this was warm, and the blanket didn't leak air. But how did things end up like this? You couldn't help but start thinking about it.
After thinking for a long time, you still can't come up with an answer, so you can only guess it might be an instinctive behavior while sleeping. After all, you still like to wrap yourself tightly in a blanket like a zongzi, and you're used to sleeping alone. So it's probably normal that you didn't recognize Spamton as a person while you were asleep.
So you let go of Spamton, scratched your head, and didn't forget to apologize to him: "Uh, sorry, I didn't notice last night...... So I still think if you go to bed on the floor, you'll sleep more freely...... Of course you won't make him another blanket, because you're lazy. So thinking about the current situation, it's actually acceptable again.
"...... [It's okay]. In the [game], [you] are in this [state] too." "He looks like he's already awake, maybe he didn't sleep well at all. You wouldn't care about that. Since he hasn't complained much, just pretend nothing happened.
So you just coughed dryly: "Haha...... Really? That's really embarrassing. "Of course, you didn't look that embarrassed, just gave a couple of awkward laughs. Indeed, you remembered, it was the same before. You were hugging Spamton and fast asleep, since you had to rest well before that killer returned.
Spamton didn't answer your question, just jumped to the next topic: "Maybe you could [consider] [breakfast time]." He really did wake up long ago. After all, being held by you isn't very comfortable. It's not unacceptable, but he always finds it a bit strange. Ultimately, maybe it's because your relationship isn't that close. So all of this feels a bit strange.
As for the specific strangeness—probably, everything seems indifferent in the game, but once you leave the game world, it feels like you have to look at it separately. You know this, and of course, he understands it too.
But whether you actually do it depends on your feelings. So now everything seems strange, since none of this is separated, yet the same pattern continues.
However, perhaps because they understood the situation, no one mentioned this abnormal condition, only maintaining it.
You let out a couple of 'oh ohs', yawned, and recalled slowly: "By the way, I forgot to buy breakfast...... There's absolutely nothing left at home, so let's go out for breakfast!" "Because it's still a bit cold outside, you don't want to crawl out of bed to change clothes. The blanket is so warm—if you weren't hungry, you'd even want to lie under the covers a little longer."
Now, you chose to change clothes under the covers. Spamton quietly turned away, probably consciously. Of course, he could still hear the voices behind him clearly. After a rustling sound, things finally quieted down, and your voice came again.
"Alright, I'm done changing...... Hurry up and finish changing your own clothes. It's not like I didn't buy you new ones, so don't wear the old one anyway...... You muttered, then took out another set of clothes and tossed them next to Spamton, then you went over to wash up first.
Spamton was silent for a moment, then finally got out of bed.
Anyway, after all this was over, you skillfully lifted him onto your shoulder, patted your cheek to sober yourself up, and then walked out the door to look for food. There were quite a few breakfast shops on the next street. At least you happily bought bread and sandwiches, dipped them in jam, and poked Spamton to signal him to pay. He split the price evenly with you, you accepted it happily, then stuffed a sandwich into his mouth.
He probably never expected you to do this, and in a flustered panic, he started eating the sandwich with both hands.
Soon, the breakfast was over. Eating bread sandwiches alone was quite choking, so you bought two steaming cups of orange juice. Even if you treated Spamton, you didn't ask him for money, but when he finally relaxed halfway through the sandwich, you thoughtfully handed him a straw. Of course, the force might be a bit strong; if he chokes, it wouldn't matter to you. You just happily thought you were so thoughtful, and you also drank the orange juice yourself.
After drinking the sweet and sour orange juice, you finally feel alive, your body warm, and you've eaten. You pat your belly, yawn, and feel a bit sleepy—you pat your cheeks to try to wake up. At that moment, you feel Spamton poking your cheek, and instinctively you raise the glass of orange juice, since he hasn't finished it yet.
But when you turn your head, you realize he actually handed you the dark coins. You glanced at them—it was exactly the price of two glasses of orange juice. You were a bit speechless and couldn't help but mutter, "I was already planning to treat you, so why did it end up being you inviting me......" Though you said that, you still accepted the dark coins without hesitation and then shoved the orange juice into his hand.
"I want to express my sincere gratitude to you." He held the glass of orange juice in both hands, but didn't drink it. Instead, his tone was filled with seriousness as he spoke.
You waved your hand: "If you were truly thanking me, you wouldn't just treat me to a meal of orange juice, right? At least treat me to a big meal...... You complained, feeling Spamton's shoulder stiffen for a moment. You were heading home, but moving slowly. Now your hand was about to touch the doorknob, so you couldn't help but glance back at Spamton.
“…… What, are you really going to treat me? Then I'm going to a fancy restaurant, I want to eat roast squab, roast lamb, and fried steak...... What else is there...... "You casually mentioned a few dish names, then couldn't continue. Forgive me, you've never been to a fancy restaurant, so of course you don't recognize those names. You only recognized some dishes when you happened to pass by before.
"No, it's just about [thinking] about [ways of expressing gratitude]." he said.
You shrugged: "Ah, if only it were the simplest way...... You just need to help me finish the side quests properly. After all, I can't be bothered to think about the answers to those questions. If it were me, at best, I could seriously complete the main quests...... "Just being able to complete the main quests seriously is already great! You're too tired, you really don't want to think about the problems anymore."
"I promise, I will diligently complete the [side quest]." Spamton said. Of course, his willingness to help you complete the side quests wasn't just to express his gratitude. What he said of thanking you was just a rough gesture...... He thought, he didn't really have to do it all at once. As for completing side quests, half was waiting for you to take him along to complete the main quests, and the other half was that he also needed the reward amounts for the side quests. Moreover, he had a feeling that these tasks might not appear for nothing.
"Mm hm hm, that's good." Only then did you nod in satisfaction. After all… you didn’t really care whether he was expressing gratitude; you just needed a companion.
After all, you're just a collaborator, that's all. Back home, you picked up Spamton and set him down on the floor. At least for now, most of what you needed to do was done, and you couldn't think of anything else for now. You simply sat on the sofa and started scrolling through the phone you had just bought in the Dark World yesterday.
Spamton also climbed onto the sofa and sat next to you. You could still hear the sound of his straw, but you didn’t bother with it. You just kept scrolling through the news and updates from the Dark World, and nothing seemed particularly noteworthy.
The game system's free week expires after a brief week of settling in the Dark World. On this day, you sit on the sofa as usual, but your vision goes blank. After a strong dizziness, you arrive somewhere else. Of course, the ground next to you is Spamton.
Monday·END

title: Horror Game Port 3 - Adding Fuel to the Fire

content:
[Main Quest: Explore the Building, Head to the Top Floor] Reward: One Month of Rest and Security Protection.
[Side Quest: Explore the Building and Learn the Cause of Its Current State] Reward: 100,000 currency + 100,000 Dark Coins
The light screen appeared before you, and seeing the reward this time, you let out a sigh of relief—if the rewards aren't separated, you'll really have to settle in the Dark World, but at least for now, you don't have that plan.
You looked around—thick fog, thick fog, endless fog, surrounding and obscuring everything else. Maybe the sunlight was just right, since the sky was clear, with only endless splashes of blue paint and no accidental graffiti of white clouds. Maybe it would be strange if there was fog right now—but you knew, it was just a forbidden place to explore. Only the building before you stood tall, as if it could pierce straight into the clouds. Through the building, you could even see the reflected sunlight, so dazzling that you couldn't help but close your eyes when you looked up—but you still noticed that through the window, you couldn't see inside the building. Of course, perhaps because the sunlight was just right, you shouldn't have seen it anyway.
But—you look at the glass door before you, unable to see what is inside, only through the glass you see pitch black. This is probably the strangest place, since there are glass windows all around. Even if there is darkness without light, it shouldn't be pitch black, but should be filled with bright light, or rather, a bright scene in between.
However, you took a deep breath and swallowed hard. No matter how strange it was, it didn't matter—it just looked strange on the outside. It didn't mean you would encounter strange things once inside, nor did it add any pressure to be paranoid. Persuading yourself like this, you lowered your head, looked at Spamton, then skillfully lifted him up and sat him on your shoulder, casually saying, "Alright, the side quest is still yours to complete. Reaching the top of the building is still a breeze, isn't it?" ”
Although you say this, you know the building looks neglected for years. Even the lock on the glass door is rusted, forming iron-red rust swirling over the lock. Of course, it probably won't damage it if you touch it—it's just that you always have to be suspicious. And that means the elevator in this building must be broken, meaning you probably have to walk up the stairs. This is probably a test of physical strength and endurance. However, you naturally aren't afraid of this kind of test; in fact, you're eager to try.
"Naturally, this is a cooperation treaty." he said.
You nodded casually and stepped forward to tentatively push open the glass door. You thought that if the main character of the game was to explore the building, they probably wouldn't block you at the door; otherwise, there would be nowhere else to look for the key. Sure enough—you only gently pushed the door, but at first it was unmoving and clumsy, stuck by the lock, so you could still see only complete darkness. But when you instinctively touched the lock and instinctively grabbed the rust, it broke apart, making a crisp clanging sound as it fell to the ground.
You stared silently at the red lock, unsure whether it was an illusion or if it was truly so, but in that instant, you saw a bright red and even orange-yellow glow like a red-hot branding iron. Beneath the lock, on the clean gray-white floor, gushing blood gushed out. It wasn't a sudden gush of blood, but rather ...... It slowly oozed out. Though it was blood, it wasn't exactly fresh; instead, it carried an unsettling black-red color, lingering in that moment with an irritating stench of rot and blood. Widening your eyes, it was as if you were under a nightmare, or perhaps you didn't want to miss such a sight. Although you didn't find it particularly noteworthy, perhaps you found it novel, since you had never seen anything supernatural before.
Until the blood spread, slowly spreading to your feet, until the black slowly rose around your calves, until—you didn't know what was about to happen, because you felt your face being poked—it was Spamton. You shivered instinctively, blinked. Indeed, everything before you was just an illusion, because now, everything before you was clean, except for the broken lock and the rust spilled onto the floor.
You patted your cheeks, glanced at Spamton, and for once, felt a bit embarrassed: "...... Thank you. ”
He didn't answer your question, but simply asked, "Just now, [you] kept [staring] [in the same direction]...... Did you [notice]? "Spamton also observed for a while and noticed you seemed almost obsessed, staring blankly in the same direction, your eyes wide open, showing no other reaction. That's when he decided to try to awaken your attention.
You scratched your cheek awkwardly, silently recalled for a moment, and then said, "Ah...... Hmm. Let's just say that's how it is, but are you really not seeing it? "It seems you're the only one who saw what just happened.
You look at Spamton, and as expected, he shakes his head. That's the answer you'd expect.
Well, it seems like only you saw it. You let out a long sigh: "Ah...... It's nothing, maybe it's a good thing you couldn't see? Could it be that my inspiration was too strong to see this scene...... You muttered to yourself, instinctively avoiding the topic. After all, you didn't know how to describe it, so you took a deep breath and pushed open the door.
Spamton wanted to say something more, but now you had entered the building. The door slammed shut with a bang. When you turned around, all you could see was unsettling black. If you didn't know that the glass door wasn't painted black, you'd believe it was black anyway. You tried to pull the doorknob, but it was tightly shut and wouldn't open again.
You exhale, but at that moment you force a smile, the corners of your mouth lifting: "Hmm...... Very good, it looks like you can't get out, so you can only explore forward—is the theme here something you can't look back at? Just like that Greek mythology...... Uh...... At this point, you get stuck, because you've only heard of it but aren't familiar with the name of that legend. Of course, you're just trying to hide that sudden chill.
And Spamton didn't answer you. He also didn't know what Greek mythology you were talking about was...... Well, maybe he actually knew.
So he hesitated for a moment and replied, "Orps and Eurydice?" ”
You turn around and clapp: "Yes, that's the name!" Hmm...... It's a choice between death and survival, a fate where once you turn back, you'll always face death. Or perhaps, it's also a symbol...... You muttered this phrase in a daze, took two steps forward, and gazed at the building. The white floor seemed as if it had never been abandoned; the floor even reflected the ceiling's reflection in its cleanliness and honesty, and as you walked on it, your reflection was reflected too. Shadows refracted between the tiles, sometimes long, sometimes short, tinged with shadowy hues, and at rare times tinged with sunlight, leaving only unknown light.
You deliberately looked around. Naturally, all the windows were closed, or rather, all the glass was intact. But now, through this glass, all you could see was the outside blue—only blue, endless blue. If that's the case, why was the scent inside the building still so fresh? Could there be another vent, or maybe it was coming down from upstairs? You couldn't help but make this association. And...... Even though the windows were tightly shut and there shouldn't be any sensation, you could still feel the wind blowing from the left side. You were certain that the window on that side was closed.
You sigh and ask, "Do you feel the wind?" ”
Spamton hesitated for a moment, then just shook his head. Actually, he didn't feel anything. When you led him into the building, all he saw was a patch of chipped floors, yellowed gray-yellow cement exposed by broken tiles, peeling paint on the walls, and ugly gray-white or yellow cracks that couldn't be removed. He didn't feel any wind, since all the windows had been nailed shut. What he saw was just a dim yellow, and at that very moment, the door behind him was nailed to the wooden boards.
…… So, he didn't even know how you managed to successfully lead him into the building. At that moment, he didn't ask any additional questions.
You were silent for a moment, then met Spamton's gaze. His gaze seemed so innocent, and you couldn't help but ask, "Speaking of which, is it that we actually feel different, or that what we see is just different?" "You just think it's possible. After all, if only you could sense it, that would be too strange. You wouldn't accept it. So you have to find some reason that convincing yourself."
"Maybe. What I saw was the scene of the Ruined Building." "He doesn't intend to hide anything from you, after all, you still need to find a way out of here. Keeping information secret is not a good thing, and this isn't some role-playing game where you have to betray your teammates."
You widened your eyes, surprised that just a casual remark would turn into a prophecy. So it really is different.
So you couldn't help but murmur twice, "It really is different...... On my side, what I see is a new building? Well, it's not like what you see. Since you're seeing an abandoned building, what I see is probably a building still in its heyday...... You murmured to yourself, curiosity piqued as you began exploring this floor. To be honest, it was empty and nothing particularly noteworthy, but you couldn't help but search for the direction the wind was coming from. Your hand involuntarily touched the pristine white wall—and then you were startled.
After all, when you first touched it, it was indeed cold, but it was a slightly slippery sensation, making you want to vomit and even get goosebumps. At least you withdrew your hand and looked at the pristine white wall, but for some reason, you could see some skin color, and even faintly see veins flowing with bluish-purple.
You swallowed twice and instinctively poked Spamton: "Uh...... Honestly, from your perspective, what does this wall look like? ”
After you said that, Spamton took a closer look at the wall. Just now, he had only paid extra attention to the signs of damage and the orange-red bricks peeking out from behind the wall, showing that the repair hadn't been done very seriously. Now, he looked at the wall again, saw the wall panel, and naturally noticed what was behind the half-peeling, crumbling wall.
"...... [Wall], with [Black] [Hair]. Beneath [Wall Skin] is [Yellow] [Fat]. "Calling it yellow isn't quite accurate; it should be brownish anymore. After all, it's not very fresh anymore, probably a long time ago. I don't know why it turned this way, maybe mixed with flesh and blood." Of course, Spamton didn't say this out loud.
"And, the 'wall shell cracks' are 'burnt marks.'" These are marks of a mix of dark brown and brownish-yellow hues, so maybe the fat had also been roasted. Although at this moment, all that remained was the stench of rot. It was precisely at this moment that he noticed that the dark brown burn marks on the wall weren't just fractures; in fact, the entire wall was more or less mixed with these marks.
You retched twice. Well, you actually can't see or feel anything, so it's just for show. After adjusting your posture, you pat your cheek and take a deep breath: "Alright, let's not linger here and keep moving forward." You said, continuing in the direction the wind was coming from.
Until you stopped in front of a wall, you realized that the wind was coming from behind it, though you didn’t know why. You hesitated for a moment, tapped twice on the wall, and heard a hollow echo. After a brief pause, you said, 'There should be a hidden door here… Can you see where the doorknob is from your perspective?'
Spamton saw a door with no markings, even completely dark, of course, it also bore burn marks, which seemed to be spread throughout the entire building. He looked down and saw the doorknob, then reached out to point a direction for you.
"[Over there]."
You followed his direction and indeed felt yourself grasp a doorknob. Every moment you pressed down, opening the door, and the first thing you saw was darkness. Strangely… there was a dim yellow oil lamp hanging on the wall.
By the dim yellow light, you saw that there was indeed a window on the wall not far away. Probably because of the backlight, the room wasn't very bright, just dim, but it was always much better than having no light at all. You hesitated as you looked at the furnishings inside the room, then noticed what was on the floor—seemingly barrels of gasoline, and the floor was sticky, clearly poured gasoline, though no one knew how much time had passed. No, no, if that were the case, this must be a memory from before it was abandoned, meaning someone had planned to burn it down back then.
You swallowed hard. Other than that, there seemed to be nothing else inside, except for a wooden table placed against the other wall. You forced yourself to step on the grease and went over to check. The table was completely empty, and the drawer was the same—ah, it was still a bit better than being empty. When you opened the drawer, you found a note that read, "They all deserve to die!! "It was written in red characters, though I wasn't sure if it was bloodstains. At least it smelled like barely noticeable blood.
You close the drawer and turn your head to look at Spamton: "Hmm...... Uh, what I want to ask is, what does the interior of this room look like from your perspective? "As you spoke, you noticed a pitch-black spot beneath the opposite wall, with no light illuminating it, making it look like some hidden hole. You could vaguely sense a faint breeze coming from inside, so you planned to take the oil lamp down from the wall to investigate carefully.
“…… Only the [scorched marks], from the [walls] to the [floor], [from inside to outside]. "That's what he said. You wanted to ask something else, so in that moment you were distracted for a second, but you were sure you had firmly grasped the oil lamp, and you were sure there was absolutely no problem. But the next second, the oil lamp fell straight to the floor, as if what you had just grabbed was just a futile illusion.
Then, the wick fell to the floor, igniting the gasoline spilled on the floor and igniting it. Instinctively, you ran toward the room, thinking that once you left, all the flames would be blocked, but the gasoline bottles were melting as if proclaiming that fate had once passed, declaring that everything could not be defied. Even if you hadn't touched the oil lamp, all of this was just a memory of the past, impossible to change. You held your breath, wanting to look toward the door, but Spamton poked your cheek again.
"The [main gate] is not an [escape route]; the [gate] has already been blocked by [wooden boards]. [You] should [go upstairs]." "He also saw the flames—not exactly that. In fact, he only saw pitch-black marks, felt the scorching heat approaching, and even smelled a foul smell of burnt steam. So he knew it was a raging fire, and instinctively felt fear.
So at the end, he quickly added, "Now, [leave immediately!! ] That's [scorching hot!] 】”
Of course, you knew you weren't burning, even though the oil lamp and flames looked like illusions—just an uncontrollable fire that had broken out long ago. But you could still feel the scorching wind, so you knew you needed to run. The front door couldn't open again, probably because your perspective was different and you hadn't noticed, so at this moment, you should run upstairs. Gritting your teeth, you turned around and ran toward the staircase. Fortunately, when you reached the stairs, the flames only scorched the entire floor, clinging to the walls, scorching the greasy skin and yellow grease. The stench of burning flesh spread out, and you covered your nose in discomfort.
Fortunately, the flames didn't catch up to the stairs, probably because no gasoline was poured down the hallway. But was that really the case? You doubted it. Because your hand instinctively pressed against the handrail, and in that moment you felt shaking and about to fall. You looked up at the handrail, only to be horrified to find it was also covered in reddish-brown rust, and the stairs beneath your feet were covered in dried black-brown blood and a foul smell. Perhaps that's why the flames didn't catch up.
"Well, at least we managed to escape...... But what are you seeing now? What I saw was a staircase covered in blood. It didn't look right. Could this be the scene after it was abandoned...... you murmured.
Spamton couldn't see the flames behind him, but he could feel the burning aura fading away, at a certain distance. Of course, before you spoke, he was already examining the stairs and had made his own judgment, so at this moment, when you asked, he simply said, "I [think] that our [perspective] has changed." "That's precisely why what he sees now is completely intact." What he saw were brand-new iron handrails and pristine white steps, and of course, the smooth, unusually white walls—after all, they looked like human skin rather than paint, including the current staircase. No...... Maybe the stairs weren't.
You scratched your head in frustration, frowning and sighing, "Hey, I guess that's true...... How can the perspective still change? If the view changed, I wouldn't be able to decrypt it...... As you spoke, you almost wanted to sigh, but you still carefully walked up the stairs toward the next floor. For some reason, when you looked down the hallway, it always felt dark ahead.
Spamton didn't say a word, nor did he answer your question. Maybe a shift in perspective would be a good thing, that's what he thought......
But when he looked up ahead, he realized it was just a bright hallway, so he began to wonder what he had seen again—maybe a pitch-black passage? Or maybe something else...... But before he could think further, this time your thought was interrupted—Spamton realized he was being pulled off his shoulders and then held in his arms.
He silently looks up at you: "[You] don't feel [tired]?" "It's precisely because you feel tired that he keeps sitting on your shoulder."
And you awkwardly laughed twice: "Uh, that's not ...... Ahem, although it's a bit tiring, physical fatigue is definitely better than mental exhaustion. "You start talking nonsense seriously. Of course, you know yourself that you're just scared, but you can't help but start talking nonsense. Maybe talking nonsense in panic actually dispels some of that fear, at least now you feel much better.
Spamton didn't expose your lie. Of course he knew you were probably panicking and scared when he said that. He didn't need to expose you; it's just that when you hold him tightly, he always feels uncomfortable, but that uncomfortable feeling is hard to put into words—probably just awkwardness. That feeling only fades when you climb the stairs and put him back on your shoulder.
Looking at the charred scene before you, you can't help but feel a slight sense of emotion. So this is exactly what Spamton had just witnessed? No wonder...... After all, these walls are almost dark brown now, and the fallen human skin still emits a foul stench of burnt beard and rot. You have no idea how these things have been preserved after a fire.
Moreover, those doors also bore burnt marks, but they were all iron doors, so they were only stained with charred black and reddish-brown rust. The decorations on them were completely ruined, leaving no trace behind—no, there were still some marks. You could still see the glue marks that had been pasted on the representative objects, as well as the paper curled up together.
Taking a deep breath, you cautiously move forward and ask, "Which room do you think is better to inspect?" After all, at this moment, from your perspective, these doors are almost identical, with no differences, and nothing particularly noteworthy.
Spamton looked around; indeed, from his perspective, it was a brand new house, so the decorations of these rooms were all different. The first door on the left was empty, too clean, which made it look rather eerie; The second door had a wreath hanging from it, and the door sign was written with some kind of text—probably indicating whose room it was; The third door was covered with missing person notices, from the same person.
He thought he should go through all the doors and take a look, but for now, the third room was probably the one he should investigate more. So he spoke: "Let's go to the third room first. Also, please [stay]—I need to [identify]." You made a couple of 'ohs' sounds, then took Spamton on your shoulder and walked toward the third door. All you can see on this door are countless burnt marks of paper and glue marks, so you guess there may have been many sheets of paper pasted here, though you don't know exactly what they are.
You linger at the door for a few seconds and hear Spamton give you the answer: "These [papers] are the same person's [missing person notice], and they are the [residents] of this room." ”
Your mouth drops open, feeling that besides the fire, this building holds many secrets, so it's no wonder the mission requirements for you are like that...... And you have a bad feeling that the main quest might be a bit difficult to complete too. After all, if your perspectives are not the same, maybe the view from the top of the building will be different, and you might not be able to leave here at all. But since you're here, you might as well settle down and choose not to dwell on this matter for now.
So you just nodded, your tone still a bit relaxed: "Oh, so this family is probably missing...... Hmm, maybe this resident's story has something to do with that note on the first floor?" "Although you're just making wild guesses, and you even think that piecing together the full story would take a long time to explore, to be honest, it's really a brain-draining task.
"Maybe, can't be [guaranteed]." He simply didn't agree.
Then you all fell silent, probably because continuing to guess would yield no result. In the end, you took a deep breath and pushed open the door. It looked like all the locks inside the building were damaged...... At least you could open it smoothly, and you even found it a bit strange—maybe it was also due to the perspective? Spamton took a special look at the lock, making sure the lock he saw was intact.
But just as you were about to say something, you felt the little puppet's hand press against your mouth, so you obediently fell silent.
"[Quiet]. I see [Vision] [Conversing]. " he said in a low voice.
And you obediently nodded, indicating you understood. Actually, what you just thought about in the room was that although it had been through a fire, the door was probably locked. Except for the shoe cabinet that was slightly burned when you first entered, everything else was still intact, except for the dust gathered from years of neglect.
Spamton, meanwhile, looked at the vision sitting at the dining table ahead—a troubled young man holding his head, murmuring something to himself in the photo on the table. The photo showed a man and a woman.

Spamton didn't answer your question; he just watched the researcher stand up, stop fiddling with the instruments, but didn't touch the safe. Instead, he went to his desk and started recording his small ecological box. It looked like an ocean ecological box.
So Spamton said, "The password should be [sea]." ”
You nodded half-understandingly, turned the wheel, and opened the safe—yes, it was the password. Although you didn't know how he got the answer, seeing the perfectly preserved documents inside, you chose to pick them up and check them first.
A thick stack of experimental materials—if you can't understand them, just look at the summaries and summaries attached on the first page.
[File One
Mermaids fear fire and prefer water sources—this has already been proven. The institute once captured a mermaid for experiments, and it turned out that the experiments yielded many conclusions. If there were flames, they wouldn't even try to cross them, or would shrink into a circle of flames, even if they were burned to death.
Once killed, their corpses become monsters completely unafraid of fire, allowing them to be killed again—completely dead. Research has also found that these corpses are extremely afraid of water sources, which is very different from the habits of mermaids during their survival. Perhaps this can be used to manipulate mermaids and their corpses into our tools.
I found this building to be a suitable experimental venue. ]
[File 2
There is something strange about this building. Of course, I don't believe in the existence of immaterial things. It's just that occasional hallucinations and singing of merfolk on the rooftop lure people down, making me suspect they are merfolk acts of revenge. I have no choice but to believe in irrational, non-material existence.
Recently, I found that as long as I eliminated those illusions, I could briefly return to reality, or return to the past. After destroying those illusions using the methods I had developed, what I saw was the scene from the former rooftop.
Here's a simple method: apply the liquid of this recipe to weapons, which can produce effects similar to flame burning and scorching heat, and can also eliminate the mermaid phantoms. ]
You dullly lift your head and find a bottle of liquid in the safe.
You picked up the bottle of crimson liquid and shook it. Although you couldn't see anything, you could still faintly smell the scent of burnt food.
So you repeated the information from earlier and added, "Now, it looks like we can leave here together...... Probably?" "You're not quite sure how you can leave this place after climbing onto the rooftop."
"[That's the fact.] Maybe we can try to stop [the corpse]. ”
You scratched your head in frustration: "I wish I could, but we don't have water here...... Rather than stopping them, I actually think it's much easier to just kill them outright. If it weren't for the way there were so many corpses just now that I couldn't see them...... You muttered to yourself, put away the bottle, and walked out the door. But once you stepped outside, your expression stiffened. You saw three or five corpses who, at some point, had arrived in the corridor, slowly wandering around, looking like they were on patrol.
As soon as they saw you, they quickly swarmed around and began to attack with their claws. At this point, Spamton couldn't see it, but he could feel the howling wind, and then he saw you start swinging your axe.
Now you were feeling happy, grateful to have seen all of this now. So even though you were surrounded by corpses, you weren't afraid. However, your movements inevitably had to be a bit more intense. So, while leaning back to dodge the incoming claws, you also used your axe to cut off another hand attacking you, and didn't forget to add, "Hold on tight first. I'll deal with these monsters first—"
Spamton didn't have time to say anything more. After all, if he didn't hold onto you firmly, you'd throw him hard to the ground. So now he simply grabbed your arm. In fact, he had already been thrown off by the moment he wasn't paying attention, so he had to hold onto your arm.
And the inexplicable weight on your arm naturally made you frown. Fortunately, it was only your left arm. Your right arm swung as usual, splitting the heads of the corpses blocking your path. Watching their bodies split in half and fall to the ground, and as flames ignited on their bodies again, you couldn't help but mutter, "That wasn't mentioned in the documents just now...... Forget it, let's go first!" You casually picked up Spamton, who had just been tightly holding your arm, and put it back onto your shoulder.
With that, you picked up your axe and headed toward the rooftop. After all, the bodies lying together were engulfed in raging flames, and you definitely didn't want to be burned.
Soon, you arrived at the rooftop, and you did hear the mermaid's singing. It was sitting at the edge of the rooftop, drawing you step by step toward the mermaid. Maybe at first you were truly bewitched, as you were really walking toward that mermaid. But at that moment, Spamton pinched your face hard. He could clearly tell something was wrong with you. After all, from his perspective, there was nothing there, and when he saw your expression, it was dazed, as if your soul had been stolen, or perhaps your mind had been stolen. In short, this state was truly dangerous. He couldn't guarantee you'd wake up. He was even a bit relieved that you and he were on different perspectives, otherwise he might not have had enough time to wake you up.
You felt the pain and instantly snapped out of that dreamlike state, subconsciously breaking out in a cold sweat. You poured the crimson liquid onto the axe, and then swung it at the mermaid's illusion.
There was a crisp sound of glass shattering, and the broken noise followed. The illusion in front of you also shattered, the scene burned and fell away as if on fire, and ultimately, what appeared before you was a gloomy sky and the illusion of the brother and sister standing on the rooftop.
You stared blankly at the scene before you, then looked at Spamton: "Did you see the same dark sky and the shadows of the siblings?" ”
Spamton confirmed that the change in the sky and the appearance of the illusion were only triggered by the sound of the glass shattering just now. He merely nodded.
You instinctively clenched the axe, and suddenly, a beep sounded. You noticed on the screen that you were congratulated for completing the main quest. The brother and sister turned their heads and mouthed one phrase toward you: Thank you for discovering the truth.
In the next second, as the game ended, a flash of white light passed, and you lost consciousness.
Adding Fuel to the Fire·END
