Spamton hesitated for a moment, holding the bottle that was still a bit large for him. In the end, he took a sip from the mouth. Honestly, as long as he ignored the feelings in his heart, it didn't really matter. But he still felt a bit awkward and uncomfortable.
But you didn't pay much attention, just finished it briefly, then sat back in the driver's seat with Spamton, then cheered, "Yay, let's go now!" ”
As you spoke, you pressed the accelerator and the clutch, and the car started. Spamton didn't have time to snap out of his thoughts and ask you anything else, so he hurriedly grabbed the steering wheel and adjusted the steering wheel to avoid the car flying off in an instant.
You followed this road forward, and fortunately, it seemed to be the right path, since you had gone a bit further...... It took about three or four hours, making you a bit drowsy, and only then did you see the buildings lining the road and another checkpoint.
This time, the checkpoint didn't have any extra obstacles; it just required a human-machine verification to open the rolling shutter door and let you through. Human-machine verification was naturally very simple for you, so you enthusiastically entered the correct answer, and then passed amid the rumbling sound of the shutter opening.
…… However, you thought there would be people ahead after this, you thought you would see the refugees coming here, but all you saw was desolation and desolation. The surrounding buildings were so silent, even filled with an oppressive atmosphere. You drove onto the street, and the nearby shops were all closed, completely deserted.
You couldn't help but wipe the goosebumps on your arm and muttered quietly, "...... To be honest, although the announcement said they were in City A for refuge, and we just checked the signs, this is indeed City A, but why is there no one here? Could it be that this place has already fallen long ago? "But with the previous checkpoint, zombies probably can't get in, unless there's already mutated within City A.
“…… We should be prepared. Perhaps after the free goods measures, we have taken a light plundering of this place." Spamton said.
You couldn't help but nod, still thoughtful: "I do admit what you said makes some sense...... But how did this happen...... "You think no one would do that under normal circumstances, even though it only took about two days to reach the destination, it's still hard for you to imagine."
"Perhaps City A is the source of the virus spread, and the reason for the zombie outbreak." Spamton's voice sounded again. The car slowed down because he had just called for you to shift the gear. Now, looking at the research institute still brightly lit not far away, and then at the buildings around that were clearly unpowered, you couldn't help but sigh softly.
"Alright, you're right. It looks like the real culprit we're looking for is just ahead...... Yes, right at that research institute. ”
"Maybe there's still a chance the [People of Light] will survive." Perhaps sensing your slight frustration, Spamton couldn't help but add.
And you only wanted the kiln road, but quickly pulled yourself together again: "It's fine, you're right! There are probably others outside City A who survived, but inside City A, that's clearly not possible...... Hmph, next it's time to settle accounts with that culprit. "As you spoke, you clenched your fists.
"Yeah, stop the car first. I'll go find some weapons or something...... I can't just use the axe to cut the blade. "At this point, you remember you don't have any other weapons besides that axe, so you hurriedly hit the brakes and went to the neighboring grocery store to rummage for a while. Soon, you came out carrying two crowbars and three steel pipes, along with a hammer and a shovel you somehow found.
You picked up the mess and placed it on the back seat, then clapped your hands contentedly: "Alright, everything is ready now. Let's go!" You sit back in the driver's seat, hug the Spamton, and then press the accelerator.
Finally, you stopped at the entrance of the institute. You took a deep breath, feeling a bit nervous, and you just picked up a crowbar and two hoses, slung a shovel on your back, and walked in holding an axe. Of course, you didn't forget to carry Spamton, placing him on your shoulder again, while Spamton watched as the weapons hanging on your back and tied to you with a strap fell into a slight silence.
You didn't mind, just walked into the empty research institute with a state of alert—though empty, it was still brightly lit, and for some reason, it exuded an eerie atmosphere. Looking ahead, you only felt the sound of your footsteps echoing through this empty space, the echo of your footsteps, and you couldn't help but swallow hard.
…… You really did get nervous all of a second. If it weren't for Spamton sitting on your shoulder, you might have fallen into panic. But now, you only felt cold sweat trickling down your palm. You gripped your axe tightly and walked forward—and then, you encountered zombies.
This zombie looked quite different from the previous ones. The gap in its abdomen was indeed blooming with flowers, but the flowers were spreading throughout the body. The zombie's body itself was twisted, twisted into an arc that humans simply couldn't achieve. For some reason, the face had been shaved away, leaving only rotten, pus-yellow fluid continuously flowing down. When you saw that rotting half face, you covered your mouth, suppressing the urge to vomit. You pulled out your axe and chopped, but the first strike failed to cut off the zombie's head. You widened your eyes in astonishment—could it be that the body had been specially mutated? At this moment, you think the zombie's body is so tough that even if you put in a bit of strength, you'll only push the axe in a little.
But now, the zombie grabbed a dagger from nowhere, trying to stab you. You hurriedly dodged, then pulled a steel pipe from behind and started attacking the creature in front of you without hesitation.
Since you don't know what it is or why, just kill it decisively—indeed, after your frenzied beating, the zombie collapses to the ground, motionless, and the flowers on its body wither.
Spamton also saw this scene and warned, "Perhaps those [blooming flowers] have [special enhancement]." ”
Although he only had to sit on your shoulder and watch you take down these monsters the whole time.
You nodded, thoughtful: "Mm...... Maybe it's better to start with the flowers on the zombies from now on. Whatever, let's go in first! "Saying that, you lift your foot and walk forward. For some reason, the door to the research institute, which originally required a card, suddenly opened right in front of you. You must be someone controlling things behind the scenes."
And when you head to the next room—you see a dense horde of zombies. When you step in, all the zombies turn around in perfect unison to stare at you, then quickly move toward you. Instinctively, you pull out a grenade, pull out the safety bolt, and throw it at you, then dash in the opposite direction. You definitely don't want to fight with so many zombies!
While you were running, Spamton couldn't help but turn his head to look back. Fortunately, under one of your grenades, most of the zombies were dead and didn't come after you anymore. He turned around, grabbed your clothes tightly, wrapped his other arm around your neck, and you just glanced at him quickly before running off to the next room. Although I don't know why the research institute door opens automatically whenever you get close, you've already reached the next room.
But you don't have a map of the research institute, so you don't know where you've arrived...... At that moment, Spamton poked your cheek, signaling you to look at the only table in the empty room. You had only planned to glance quickly and leave, but now you still walked over to see what it was.
…… Ah, you found a laptop in the office area. Although you don't know why there's another laptop left here, or why this laptop can still be opened, you try pressing the power button and find that the laptop does still have power.
But after you opened it, you got stuck on the password. So you silently stared at the password screen, then at Spamton, who just shook his head, indicating he didn't know either.
You scratched your head irritably: "Alright, then let's just remember this room first...... No, if there's no map, I wouldn't know the way either. Since that's the case, I'll leave the navigation to you! "You confidently handed this over to Spamton, patted him on the shoulder, and then you headed toward the next room.
Spamton just glanced at you speechlessly, and you didn't notice that his eyes had turned into a screen filled with garbled text at that moment. Carefully holding the iron rod, he walked into the next room.
There were no zombies crowded here, making you breathe a sigh of relief. But in contrast, ...... Instead, there was a massive zombie here. Calling it a zombie is just a general summary of its species—after all, you don't really know what it really is. You just stared solemnly at the monster in front of you, much bigger than you. Its body looked like it was pieced together from countless zombies, or perhaps it had devoured them all. The patched areas were covered with rotten pink—or flesh-colored flowers. Not only that, but mucus kept dripping down the flowers, looking like a black, foul-smelling liquid. In any case, you pinched your nose, frowned, and instinctively raised the water pipe.
—For some reason, that zombie was still holding a knife and was waving it toward you. You hurriedly backed away, swung the hose at him, but it seemed useless. The zombie shook twice, and just now, your pipe had only knocked off the petals on his body, drifting and falling to the ground with black pus, wilting at an extremely fast pace. But now, the shattered spot quickly sprouted new flowers, as if all the damage you had just caused was just an illusion, and he could still regenerate.
You swallowed heavily, wondering if you needed to consider your strategy. At that moment, Spamton spoke: "[Change weapon] to make [damage] [surpass] his [Regeneration Ability]." ”
You nodded involuntarily. You knew Spamton made some sense, so you swiftly took the axe from your back and sped up, striking the softer parts of his body and the joints of the flowers. Soon, the flowers' regeneration couldn't keep up with the speed of destruction, and the corpses attached to the zombies began to fall off. You glanced quickly and saw other headless zombies. The hollows in their abdomen had expanded, but they were empty, and the flowers growing on your body had rotted and withered, completely lifeless. It seemed unlikely to suddenly get up and attack you, so you could rest assured and focus fully on facing the enemies ahead.
Finally, thanks to your persistent efforts, the massive body finally collapsed. But unlike other zombies, it didn't leave a corpse behind—it just turned to ashes in an unusual way. You blinked, still a bit stunned. But when the monster vanished, a note fell from your body. You couldn't help but step forward and pick it up, only to find a string of unfamiliar English letters written on it.
So you cast a pleading look at Spamton.
Spamton looked a bit helpless, just poked your cheek and directed you: "Try entering this [Key Cracker] into your [laptop] and see what happens." "No matter how you look at it, this is the only possibility this key can offer."
You nodded, fully convinced by his words, and entered the key exactly as it was on the laptop's unlock screen. However, this time it prompted that the password failed to enter, and with four more chances, the laptop would automatically lock and format automatically.
You glanced at Spamton quietly, and he coughed twice. Though a bit awkward, it wasn't exactly that embarrassing: "[Question: Ballpoint pen?] ]"If this password is wrong, maybe he'll have to try another way. He just happens to remember something.
You touch yourself and find in frustration that you really don't have a single ballpoint pen. After all, given the current situation, what need is there for a ballpoint pen? Then you glance at your desk and still don't find a single ballpoint pen. So you shake your head at Spamton and shrug: "No, or let's just go out now. There's a grocery store nearby anyway, so grabbing a ballpoint pen is quick." ”
Actually, Spamton already knew the answer when he asked this question...... He just wanted to buy time. After all, he couldn't recall the full content; he wasn't someone who studied this field.
You rush out of the research institute, run to the nearby grocery store, grab a ballpoint pen, and hand it to Spamton. In reality, Spamton has been pondering how to decipher this string of keys.
Holding the ballpoint pen, Spamton makes a request: "Now, go back to that [laptop], then [place] me. I need to crack the [Key Generator]." ”
You nodded, fulfilled his request perfectly, and ran back to the research institute. The hall was now empty, with nothing else to distinguish except for the zombie you had just knocked down. Following Spamton's directions, you returned to the laptop and placed it on the table.
Then you leaned against the wall, hands on hips, watching the little puppet write something on that piece of paper. You couldn't understand it, but you were just holding the water pipe—yes, after you killed that monster earlier, you switched back to the water pipe. You just watched your surroundings warily, trying to prevent more zombies from attacking you.
Sure enough, another zombie emerged from a door. After smelling your scent, it sped up toward you. You swung the hose and fiercely beat this seemingly low-level zombie. Soon, he collapsed to the ground and couldn't get up again. But more and more zombies kept closing in on you. Although they were all the lowest-level ones, and a single pipe could knock down a large area, over time you would still feel irritable. You just did your best to clear out the zombies, wiped his sweat, and looked at Spamton, asking, "...... Not healed yet?" ”
He didn't look up at you, just gestured five fingers at you. You couldn't help but ask, "Five minutes?" And he nodded.
You took a deep breath, wiped the sweat from your forehead, and continued to beat the zombies with all your might. Fortunately, you still had plenty of strength left, so just sweeping them was enough to hold out. But with the sound of impact, more and more zombie corpses fell to the ground, blocking the doorway, and the remaining zombies couldn't get in.
You were speechless for a moment, though things were peaceful now...... But when you left, you still had to find a way to clear the way. You turned to glance at Spamton—about five minutes had passed. He ran over and entered the password on his laptop. With a click, a pleasant music sounded as the laptop was opened. You couldn't help but walk over and glance at the note, then picked up Spamton.
The note read: I am about to step into death. You twitched the corner of your mouth, glanced at the twenty-six letters written on it, along with a few crooked characters that had been blacked out. After thinking for a moment, you didn't ask Spamton how he solved it, but sincerely praised, "Amazing! You solved it all! I'm really glad you're the one who teamed up with me." Saying that, you raised the little puppet and spun it around a few times.
You see the little puppet's face blushing, and it seems smoke is rising from its head: "...... [place] me [on the flat ground]!" ”
You just recklessly held him up and spun him around twice, pretending not to hear what he said, and then you finally put him down. You seemed to hear Spamton exhale, and you—after all, couldn't contain that excitement anymore—which meant you could freely explore the secrets in the computer, which must be filled with many secrets.
So you hugged him and kissed him on the face with a loud smack, then put him back on your shoulder and started checking the contents on the computer desktop. The puppet was still smoking, as if it had been cooked, but you didn't care about that, just poked open the folder on the desktop.
The name of this folder is Research Use, probably including research materials. What disappointed you was that there were no maps inside, just countless documents. After a quick glance, you finally selected two research reports on the use of potions.
[File One
Research shows that this potion can greatly enhance human vitality, even revive corpses, activating cell activity to regrow. At this level, rapidly proliferating active cells are like cancer cells, but their production is limited, causing rapid death and regeneration, maintained within a certain limit.
However, the use of this potion does not fully restore the resurrected person's sanity; instead, it enhances their cellular activity and primal animal instincts. Through human experiments and research, we found that this potion can restore youth to the living, granting vitality beyond ordinary people's abilities. However, it gradually causes the loss of sanity and reason, turning into a beast and attacking others.
Therefore, this medicine is temporarily sealed before further research and will not be widely used. Nevertheless, if it could bring the dead back to life, or even achieve immortality, many people would flock to it, eager for the formulation of this medicine.
The chemical formulation method is as follows:
■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■
Part Two:
After adjustments, the proportion of one drug was lowered while the other was raised, improving the effectiveness of the drug and potentially enabling widespread adoption.
The authorities did not approve it, and the approval was rejected, so the study was reconsidered.
Note: Hehe...... What does it matter if you don't accept it! I want to use this potion, regardless of whether others allow it...... I hope everyone can be happy. If I can see the loved ones I have lost, I guess I will be in tears no matter what......
Comment again: Things seem different from what I imagined. Why do these resurrected beings recklessly attack the living? Could it be that the medicinal potions on their bodies...... No, no, or rather, viruses are actually active and can infect others? Now it's all over...... The others have also become those revived beings who recklessly attack others.
Another note: I know I was wrong. In fact, I have already created a potion that can restore sanity to those who have come back from the dead. But there was no time to experiment with it, nor can it be promoted further. After all, now everyone has become that kind of monster, and I too am heading toward death. Let's end here. I have destroyed this world. ]
After reading it, your feelings were complicated. You clicked on another document with a similar name. The contents were simple, just recording the recipe for the sanity-restoring potion, and you earnestly asked the person destined to discover this document to take the reagent out. He prepared a tube and sealed it in the innermost office of the research institute.
You glanced at the mission panel—the side quest had already reached 100%. Whether you followed his instructions or not didn't really matter, and you didn't intend to bother with it. Still, you glanced at Spamton, choosing to ask your companion for advice: "Do you think we should go?" ”
He hesitated for a moment but nodded. You then walked forward. Fortunately, there were hardly any zombies left blocking the way. However, outside the innermost office, there was still a huge zombie. You raised your axe and skillfully took it out, then opened the office and took the vial of medicine. You walked out the door and happened to see a low-level zombie quickly walking toward you. You stopped him and just poured the vial into his mouth, his eyes clearing. You nodded, picked up the unconscious guy, placed it in front of the laptop, and then left with Spamton.
You yawned: "Phew...... Is that enough...... "Actually, you really don't care. Maybe you don't have much empathy, and your parents didn't teach you this ability to love." Spamton just stayed silent, hugging your neck.
Everything was resolved satisfactorily. Simply surviving in this world for seven days wasn't difficult. After completing the main quest, a flash of white light appeared, and once again, you heard a congratulations message for completing the task. Then you appeared again on the bed in the Dark World.
Doomsday Game· END

title: Horror Game Port 6 - Interlude - Wednesday
path: articles/en/spt/恐怖片大逃杀 end/天堂许愿机器/恐怖游戏端口6-间章-水曜日.html
content:
You grabbed that check you got for clearing the game, sat up in a flash, grinning from ear to ear. Spamton just glanced at the large pile of dark coins and didn't look again; he just stared at you.
After you pressed that check to your cheek, you finally snapped out of that excitement. At that moment, you looked at Spamton and asked in confusion, "...... Why are you looking at me?" ”
But he just shook his head without saying a word. Or maybe he just saw you happy because of money and reminded you of how he first started. Unfortunately, everything is in the past, and it's too late to look back again.
You glanced at him in confusion again, not planning to press the issue further. Instead, you lifted Spamton up again and gave him a big smack on the face, beaming: "Thanks to you this time, otherwise we definitely wouldn't have gotten the side quest rewards!" "So you don't mind if you praise him a bit more.
Or rather, you just want to praise him a few more times right now. You're racking your brains, trying to use every word you know to compliment someone. Spamton was already a bit flustered when you lifted him, and not to mention you kissed him on the cheek. Of course, his face turned red—even puppets blush! Then you started praising him again, as if you could use any word, making his face blush even more and smoke rising from his head again.
And after you get tired of talking, you smack your lips, still a bit unsatisfied. But seeing Spamton like this, you can't help but feel puzzled: "...... What's wrong with you? Did something just happen to go wrong?" As you spoke, you started shaking him.
Spamton's voice sounded somewhat frustrated: "I have no fault that needs repairs! Now, [you] have placed me at the [ground coordinates]; I just need a [program cooling method]. ”
You made two 'oh ohs' sounds. To put it bluntly, he just needed to calm down, so you laid him down on the bed, blinked twice, and looked at him: "Alright...... I'm putting you down! Come to think of it, it's getting late...... Yawn...... After the excitement just wore off, you couldn't help but cover your mouth and yawn, tears welling up in your eyes. Honestly, you really need to rest. Even though you slept in the game world, you weren't fully rested at all!
…… And after fighting so many zombies afterwards, you must be tired. Looking at the time, it's only 3 a.m., so you lie back down and fall asleep on the bed with a clear conscience.
And naturally, I forgot to ask Spamton again.
After calming down for a while, he turned around and heard your steady breathing, falling silent. After a two-second pause, he finally crawled over to your side and fell asleep next to you. After all, in the past month, you had actually slept like this a lot. Even if you slept separately on the first day, the next day you'd still squeeze together, and I don't know for whom—maybe yours, maybe his. Sometimes you'll find you're not sleeping in your original spot, other times you notice Spamton leaning closer. Over time, you tacitly accept this situation.
Actually, at first, you noticed the two of you leaning against each other and terrifiedly insisted on sleeping separately. You even placed a pillow in the middle, but early the next morning, you found the pillow was gone, and for some reason, you leaned in and slept against Spamton. You had no choice but to panic and pretend to be calm, announcing that from now on you could sleep however you wanted.
And now, as night falls, you drift into sleep. For you, it's a dreamless night's sleep, so you open your eyes refreshed, casually grab Spamton, who is sleeping next to you, play with his arm, and lazily say, "Get up, get up—" You glance at it casually; it's eight in the morning, about time to get up.
Spamton was indeed shaken by your movement, because now he was facing away from you. You couldn't see his expression, only his somewhat flustered voice: "I'm not your toy!" As he spoke, he tried to pull his arm back from your hand, but your grip was a bit too tight for him to pull back.
And you pouted, deliberately speaking in that pretentious voice: "Hey...... I'm so pitiful, sincerely calling you to get up, but your good intentions are treated like donkeys' lungs. You don't cherish it at all...... As you say that, you pretend to wipe away your tears. Honestly, if you didn't feel so close, you wouldn't say that—after all, only acquaintances can tolerate your occasional pranks...... Thinking about it this way, you somehow started to feel close to Spamton. But maybe that's the benefit.
Spamton felt a chill at your words, his body trembling involuntarily twice before saying another word. You knew when to stop and didn't continue, just shrugged: "Alright, alright, let's go out for breakfast anyway. Then when I get back, I have to keep working on the problems. I have class tonight...... You muttered to yourself, grabbed your clothes and put them on, then tossed Spamton aside to put them on.
Soon, you both went out together. You wore the clothes you brought earlier, while Spamton wore the suit you bought him last time. Watching Spamton, you nodded in satisfaction, lifted him onto your shoulders, and then cheered, "Let's go!" ”
Breakfast was still sandwiches, but this time you bought two steaming hot bottles of milk, inserted a straw, and casually stuffed one into Spamton's hand. He started drinking milk too. When breakfast was almost over, you returned home feeling refreshed, pulled out your workbook to start writing, and casually picked up Spamton and set it aside on the table. After all, you can't let him always sit on your shoulder—you'll get tired too!
So you seriously picked up your pen, eagerly flipped open your workbook, and glanced at the person sitting cross-legged at the desk...... In short, Spamton, who looked oddly quite tall, cleared his throat: "Ahem, I'm about to start working on the problems. Do whatever you want, as long as you don't bother me, it's fine!" ”
Spamton glanced at you speechlessly; he wasn't interested in figuring out what exactly was in your workbook...... After all, he couldn't understand most of it! When solving puzzles in the game world, the things he remembered were only things he might have used before, so he remembered them. Everything else...... Why bother mastering useless ones? But now, watching you focus intently on solving the problems and then looking at those problems, he just felt drowsy. He simply stared at your face.
But being stared at all the time, of course you noticed, and you actually don't like being stared at while you're working, so you put down your pen and glared fiercely at Spamton: "Why are you always staring at me! There's nothing on my face...... If you're that free, find something to do for yourself! "Your ears are still a little red, because when you turned around, you happened to meet Spamton's gaze, which made you feel a strange sensation. So you just hurriedly waved your hand, wanting to get Spamton to leave.
Spamton glanced at you quietly. He wasn't insisting on looking at you, but after all, there wasn't much to look good about you...... Or rather, he just thought you looked better. But he still nodded: "[Okay], I have other [to-dos] items." "And after hearing that, you picked him up and set him down on the ground." Then you used your hand as a fan to fan yourself, feeling a bit embarrassed inside, and for some reason, your face still felt hot and restless—maybe it was just your imagination.
In short, after putting Spamton down, you once again immerse yourself in the sea of questions, completely lost in the world and completely unaware of what else is happening outside. Spamton tidied up his clothes briefly, then pushed open the door and walked out, heading to his shop located in the junkyard—to be honest, he didn't think his shop was anything wrong. Unfortunately, no Dark People came to visit. Today was still deserted, but Spamton wasn't discouraged by it; he was long used to all this.
…… But he felt he had to find a way to change everything, so his eyes darted around as he thought of you. After all, you're a citizen of light. As long as you spread this gimmick, lots of people will come here. When the time comes...... Maybe I can become like I once was again.
Having made up his mind, Spamton glanced at the bleak little shop, calculated that it was about time, and closed the shop before heading back.
He doesn't care much about those dark coins; it's just that you must rely on them to survive in this world, and he knows that money is a major factor attracting you. And he still needs the help of you, the people of light.
…… At first, it was just a form of use and testing, and at some point, some changes occurred. Perhaps as time mercilessly passes, everything is in a state of relentless change.
When he got home and opened the door, he found you still sitting at the desk, gritting your teeth, resting your chin on your hand with a worried face, staring at a problem in front of you.
He climbed up from another chair next to the table, then crawled to the side of the table and sat back down next to your workbook. You glanced at Spamton, but didn't ask where he had just been. You're not close enough to report your schedule, and it's not normal for him to have his own things to do. Of course, you did hear the door opening. But at that moment, you couldn't help but wonder where he might go, and for now, your attention was still focused on the workbook.
So you lowered your head again to look at the exercise book. But your thoughts were still a bit distracted from the questions. At that moment, you heard Spamton say, "[Inquiry: Course schedule]?" ”
You paused for a moment, then thought about the class schedule you had received earlier on your phone, and said, "On weekdays, classes are held in the evenings, while on days off, classes are held around the clock...... That's probably how it is." "That's why you have such a free time during the day, working through problems here.
Spamton stares at you steadily, and you belatedly notice this gaze, so you can't help but put down your pen and meet his gaze.
"Maybe you're willing to accept the job I offer?" As he spoke, he reached out his hand to you.
Your expression was a bit strange, and you shook his hand up and down twice: "It's fine...... It's just work. Are you talking about the shop you opened at the junkyard?" "You still remember that place. Of course, you wouldn't criticize his taste...... It's also possible that he chose to open a shop in such a place because he was truly poor.
Spamton nodded, "The salary issue can be resolved satisfactorily." ”
Your expression grew even stranger. You pointed at yourself, then at him: "Are you sure? Didn't all those dark coins come from me and you earning together in the game world? So you should be sharing half with me too!" So basically, it's left hand to the other—you just gave me the money I earned...... You muttered to refute his point, but in the end, you didn't refuse him.
“…… Besides, I know that if you rely on just you for that shop, you probably can't sell anything, right?" You took a deep breath and asked again. To be honest, you were a bit slow to react, but you were not bad at thinking things through...... Now that he thought about it, he suddenly invited you to work, so he must have ulterior motives.
But given the time spent together, you decided to trust Spamton.
But he just stayed silent, looking at you. You could read a strange sincerity in his expression, so you couldn't help but shiver.
"Alright, I'll go anyway! Isn't that the only employee in your shop? Am I really busy...... You scratched your head, let go of his hand, and looked back at the workbook in front of you.
Out of the corner of your eye, you notice Spamton shake his head: "[No.] [You] know that there is no [Visitor] at all." ”
You shrugged, actually a bit skeptical of his story, but in the end, you were convinced: "Alright, you talk like a beast. I hope you won't lie to me." ”
Spamton lowered his head slightly. Of course, he wasn't lying to you. After all, what he said was the truth, but he was talking about the store's previous situation, not the situation he had expected after you became a clerk.
…… As for what would happen after that, he had no idea, so naturally, this wasn't a deception.
At that moment, you stretched lazily, covered your mouth, and yawned: "Alright, then I'll go to your shop tomorrow—anyway, I really do need to find a job in the Underworld! Since you're willing to provide it, I'll accept it with a smile." Mm...... But since things have come to this, shall we have dinner first? "With that, you stand up, pick up Spamton, and head outside.
After a simple lunch, you were full and burped before going to pay. The waiter looked at you and Spamton with a strange look, but you didn't pay much attention. You picked up Spamton and placed it on your shoulder, whistling off-key: "Alright, let's go to your shop. I roughly remember where it is...... But if I go the wrong way, remember to remind me. I'm not very good at finding directions. ”
You muttered a few times and headed toward the junkyard. You did make it to the junkyard, and obviously, you got lost too. You had no idea which direction to take, so you shot Spamton a pleading look.
Spamton paused for a moment, then pointed you in the right direction: "First, [vertical movement]." ”
You make a couple of hums, work hard to avoid the trash ahead, then brake suddenly, because you hear Spamton say again: "Then turn left." So you stop mechanically, make a 90-degree turn in place, and continue walking left.
When you heard Spamton sigh, he probably felt embarrassed. And you coughed lightly, a little awkwardly: "Ahem...... There's nothing I can do. After all, I don't know the way, so I can only follow what you say! ”
Spamton thought you were treating him as a navigator again, so he kept a blank expression—or rather, he was happy to play with you for a while—so he glanced and said, "Then, at [100 meters ahead], perform the [right turn]." ”
You let out a couple of 'ohs' as if suddenly enlightened, walked about a hundred steps, then turned right and moved forward. You glanced at Spamton, who was swinging his legs on your shoulder, and thoughtfully said, "It really does look like a navigator...... Why don't you just be my navigation system full-time from now on?" "Of course, you were just saying that casually.
Spamton, however, seemed to be choked and suddenly coughed twice: "[No], I'm not doing [your] navigation service to be your specialty." "He had no desire to do this job at all...... Or rather, he didn't want this job to be the only one for the rest of his life. Of course, he was still happy to provide services for you.
"Is that so? Alright, then forget it! Actually, I don't need navigation services often, so just give me some help in those moments." You shrugged. Since he hadn't given any further instructions, you continued along this road. Finally, behind the endless pile of trash, you saw that familiar shop. Although small, it was obvious it had been carefully maintained, except now it was closed and the door was tightly locked. You went up and fiddled with the lock a couple of times before it opened.
You fell silent, then looked at Spamton, whose shoulders were a bit stiff, and raised your voice slightly: "You're just setting up the lock like this—aren't you afraid someone will come to steal things?" ”
His voice sounded straightforward and righteous: "No, my [shop] has no [value] and is not a [free product]. Even if [Dark People] enjoy [discounts], they cannot get [full discounts]." ”
You tugged at the corner of your mouth, thought for a moment, then cautiously asked, "Uh...... So your shop sells junk? Or rather, it's junk ......? "After thinking for a long time, you still can't describe those possibilities as treasures. You can't imagine it, so you simply push the door open and walk in. Well, there really aren't many items displayed on the counter.
“…… It's not the [Garbage Recycling Bin]! "He retorted, still making it so firm.
You lifted Spamton off his shoulder, placed him on the table, and then leaned down slightly to meet his gaze. Well, you did sense a hint of honesty, reliability, and innocence in his expression...... Although, based on your initial bad impression of the salesman, perhaps you shouldn't have trusted him.
But in the end, you still sighed: "Alright, since you're not selling trash, then tell me what exactly you're selling. Honestly, since you want me to work here, you have to tell me what you're selling, otherwise how am I supposed to help? Unless you tell me those are some shameful treasures." "When you mentioned shameful things, you raised your voice. To be honest, you don't think Spamton can really produce anything priceless. After all, if he could, he wouldn't be sitting here anymore.
…… But since he said he's not trash, then what exactly is it? You'd be willing to listen.
Spamton fell silent. His gaze shifted for a moment, probably looking at the items on the counter, while you crossed your arms and raised your eyebrows, wanting to see how he planned to make it up. Honestly, although you couldn't fully understand what he just said, your intuition told you. He probably...... Uh, selling some counterfeit and inferior goods.
Of course, you don't think being flashy or deceiving is all that bad...... But it's just amusing to watch the other party make up excuses knowing the truth, and I'm afraid both of you know the truth.
In the end, he seemed to have made up his mind, turned to meet your gaze, his eyes full of sincerity: "These are all [Stamina Recovery] potions, [Increased Aggression] weapons, and [Additional Defense] accessories." He said with certainty.
…… You're a bit confused about the Underworld's setting. Honestly, you probably never understood it. In fact, you're a complete materialist...... At the end of the day, you don't believe in all this nonsense, which sounds like an RPG, so you tugged at the corner of your mouth, feeling it had nothing to do with you, just gave a perfunctory "Oh, oh."
…… Well, that really has nothing to do with you. You watch as Spamton takes out a potion and a bow from the counter, along with the weapon he mentioned...... You glance at it; it's a different form, but none of them are as useful as ordinary water pipes to you.
So you just dragged out a "Oh—" and then scratched your hair, feeling a bit awkward. Even though you think these things are completely useless, no wonder Spamton would feel comfortable using an unreliable lock—no one would even come to get them. Of course, you overlooked the fact that he probably couldn't afford to replace a lock. Of course, you've been through three game worlds and earned so many Dark Coins.
"Alright, I understand. But does this little shop really need help? I feel like no one is coming...... you say hesitantly.
"I need your help. I need the presence of angels." And Spamton just persisted like that.
You glanced down at him. To be honest, you hesitated a bit...... But in the end, you nodded and reluctantly agreed with his suggestion: "Alright, I'll stay here and help. But I need to bring my homework and such...... Otherwise, just sitting here idly doing nothing isn't a big deal." "Instead of wasting that time, it's better to learn more—at least that's what you think."
"Yes, and about my salary...... How much is it per month? Of course, it's fine for me to help out out of friendship, but at the very least, you should give me some dark coins as a token, right? "You rubbed your chin.
“…… One thousand Dark Coins【one month】? "Spamton hesitated a bit too.
"Deal." You agreed to the salary regulation quite readily. To be honest, you don't really know much about prices in the Dark World...... But one thousand Dark Coins is indeed quite a lot. Although for both of you, it's like flipping hands from one hand to the other.
After a brief discussion of these issues, you watched as Spamton's shop reopened. You didn't go back to bring those textbooks over, since it was only an afternoon—a rare leisure time. Staying here was good and you could chat freely.
Anyway, looking at the secluded shop, then at Spamton, you couldn't help but ask, "...... Honestly, it feels like no customers are coming, so why do you insist on opening a shop here?" "If you changed places, the foot traffic would be much bigger. Honestly, even outside the dump—uh, but there might be ready-made places here, you always feel like this place was converted from some kind of abandoned container.
“…… There is no [legal right to operate the shop]. "He simply answered your question. For some reason, you always felt that his mood was a bit down. You stroked your chin, sized him up twice, then looked at the cramped shop, lost in thought.
"Alright, but now we have money too, right? Why not move elsewhere—uh, I get it. It's related to why you've become like this. Sorry, I won't mention it anymore, I just spoke too carelessly." You quickly covered your mouth halfway through your sentence. Although you don't know exactly what legal terms exist in the Dark World, I suppose the outside world isn't very welcoming to Spamton, which is why he opened a shop here.
To be honest, although you think outside opinions can be completely ignored, they do have some impact in certain aspects. So you just glanced at Spamton with sympathy.
He seemed unaware of your gaze, just sitting there at the counter, resting his chin on his hand and looking outside. Following his gaze, all you could see was the pile of garbage, and Spamton didn't answer your question.
You shrugged, not minded, just sat down casually in the shop, then started to zone out.
After a moment of silence, you actually hear Spamton ask you a rather peculiar question. Calling it strange isn't exactly strange, but you don't think it's something you should say under the current conditions: "...... angel, what is your [dream]?" ”
"By the way, why do you call me that? Is this some special title...... You pursed your lips but still answered his question, "As for me, ideally, after graduating from adult university, I can look for a job based on the professional skills I've learned! Then live well, and if possible, completely get rid of my parents—if only we weren't on the same household registration! Of course, I want to live freely, live the way I want to be, and then show off to them." As you spoke, your eyes lit up with excitement, and you started giggling, forgetting your original question.
“…… But as for dreams! Actually, of course, there's money I can't spend all, and then I can do whatever I like, but it's probably not possible. "You shrugged.
"[Things you like]?" He simply asked.
"Ah, things I like...... Well, speaking of which, I actually like adventure, or rather, I like to travel. I like visiting all kinds of places, I enjoy learning about unique customs...... Standing firmly on another piece of land feels completely different. Saying that, I actually quite like the underworld—after all, it's fresh enough here. "You shrugged.
At this point, you propped yourself up with both hands and sat up, staring at Spamton's back and drawing out your voice: "Speaking of all the questions you've asked, I've told you everything—then tell me, what are your dreams? What do you like? Your ideals, your expectations, and how do you want to live?" "You casually throw out the question, but of course, you probably don't necessarily need to know the answer...... After all, everyone has their own secrets and things they are unwilling to easily tell others. It's just that you think it's unfair, and only by revealing everything is it is truly unfair, so you want to ask for an answer.
Then, the narrow shop fell silent, with only shallow breathing for a moment. You waited for his answer, while he remained silent, as if deep in thought.
Then you hear his voice—as usual, a strange and inexplicable hoarseness, the sizzling sound of electric currents passing through and the hoarseness of the videotape: "...... I think, it's [Becoming a Big Shot]. ”
You rub your chin: "So this is your dream...... Your ideal? Are you living just for this goal?" "At the end, you raised your voice, feeling somewhat incredulous."
Spamton just stayed silent, not answering your question for a moment. And you shrugged, feeling a bit bored: "Is that all? That's just too boring...... Don't you want to see something else, don't want to see higher and farther places? Don't you want to know the unknown of the past? ”
This time, you hear him answer you at an extremely fast pace: "[I want to]." ”
You rubbed your chin, lost in thought, then suddenly understood: "So that's how it is...... So what you love is freedom?" "Of course, this is just a sudden inference. Your words carry hesitation; you're not sure about it."
He just stayed silent and didn't answer your question. Maybe he accepted your answer, or maybe that attitude was just a way to resist. So you know, he probably doesn't want to keep talking, maybe he doesn't want to analyze his own heart to outsiders.
You just shrugged and drew out your voice: "Alright—I know! You probably don't want to say it! But I can promise you, if possible, I'll take you to higher and farther places." ”
This time, he turned to look at you. Now he was looking at you directly, reaching out his hand: "[It's a deal]?" ”
"Of course, it's a deal." You held his hand and shook it.
Although he didn't answer your question directly—and all of this was just your guess—you thought you probably knew Spamton a bit better...... No, why would you even get to know him better! You don't need that! You shook your head in panic, meeting Spamton's gaze, and he seemed a bit puzzled.
So you straightened up, cleared your throat, and said seriously, "Uh...... It's nothing, I was just thinking about some things in the world of light. Yeah, that's it. "No matter how you hear that, it feels like you're trying to cover it up. But you can't just be honest—seriously! If you really said something about him or something, that would be way too embarrassing!
At least you can't do it. So you just cough twice and change the subject: "Alright, what's for dinner?" "Better to talk about something else."
"...... Cyber Barbecue?" He spoke in a puzzled tone, but you still felt there was a hint of certainty in that tone.
You nodded your chin, and actually, you didn't really care what you ate...... Anyway, it's all the same, just a bit different in taste. So you nodded and readily agreed: "Alright, let's have some barbecue then!" ”
Then you sit in that spot, propping your chin up in a daze. To be honest, time passes quickly, but no one from the shop has come by. You start to wonder why he opened this shop—but forget it, watching his back, you inexplicably feel he won't like this question, so in the end, you bottle your doubts back.
Dinner time came quickly. You stood up, stretched, grabbed the Spamton, and headed outside. You closed the shop door and hung the lock that seemed useless. Then you put the Spamton on your shoulder, looked at the surrounding pile of trash in silence, and sincerely said, "Uh...... "Or tell me which way we're heading?" ”
Spamton silently looked at your profile, then pointed in the direction: "First, [go straight], then [turn right]." ”
You nodded in satisfaction, glad you had a navigation, followed his instructions, and finally arrived at the Cyber BBQ Restaurant.
I don't know why he seems a bit nervous, but when you step into the barbecue restaurant, that tension eases again. You glance at him in confusion, but you don't get an answer, so in the end, you can only blame it on maybe overthinking it.
In fact, Spamton was just relieved that he hadn't run into any other Addisons.
You find an empty seat by the window and sit down. After ordering, you casually pull Spamton into your arms so he can't reach the table—well, you should still be able to reach it, as long as he's standing in the seat.
Soon, the dishes you ordered arrived. You put the meat slices on the grill, but you still know your limits—after all, Spamton definitely can't touch the grill—so you chimed in, "You have to thank me properly, I'm serving you." Uh, how do you put it? Here, it's like a light servant serving the dark people...... Well, though I don't know what's special about it. ”
You shrugged, took off the grilled meat slices, placed them on the plate in front of Spamton, and then took the meat off to give to yourself.
Then you see Spamton dipping a slice of meat in a lethal amount of seasoning, and you're a bit shocked: "...... Hey, it's not like you have to dip it in so much seasoning, right?" "You glance at it—that's a lethal amount of pepper salt, it's bound to be deadly."
But Spamton just glanced at you and then swallowed it without changing his expression. Well, maybe he just likes that flavor...... No, that's not right. Thinking about the previous meal, you finally have a belated guess about his situation.
So you clapped your hands and suddenly understood: "Oh! So it turns out you have a taste disorder...... You can't really taste these flavors, right? ”
Spamton nodded silently. He hadn't intended to hide this at all; he just hadn't expected you to take so long to react. Probably...... Your reaction really is slow.
After reaching this conclusion, you happily went off to eat barbecue. Before long, the dinner was over. You burped satisfactorily, walked to pay, picked up Spamton and set it on the floor, then squatted down and poked the little puppet's face, then sternly said, "Ah...... Just finished eating, so go for a walk! I'm not responsible for taking you along, just exercise on your own! ”
That's what he said, but actually, you walked very slowly yourself, just curiously observing the buildings around you. To be honest, you hadn't stopped to really observe the world before, since you were busy preparing for exams and didn't have time to stay at all. Now, looking at the surrounding buildings and the shining neon lights, you couldn't help but sigh.
At first, Spamton was just walking beside you, and it seemed like he could walk faster. But now that your pace was slow, he couldn't help but slow down.
Watching you curiously look left and right, he couldn't help but say, "Maybe I can introduce [must-see places] to you?" ”
You just shake your head: "Forget it, I'm not here for tourism, just casually taking a look......"
After saying this, you fell silent—probably because no one wanted to break the atmosphere. Before you knew it, you had walked back home.
The days that followed were no different, except this time you weren't sitting at home pondering textbooks and problems. Instead, you sat inside Spamton's shop and continued studying. At first, you might find it a bit novel, but over time you get used to it, since the Dark People have never visited.
Until that day...... Finally, a Dark Citizen arrived, probably the day before you were about to re-enter the game world. Aside from Spamton, you actually don't know any other Dark Citizens, and at this moment, you look at the one ahead with a completely confused expression. Coincidentally, Spamton wasn't there—to be honest, you were a bit annoyed that he suddenly ran off at that moment. Didn't he usually treasure his shop? And now he suddenly said he was going to buy goods and then left?!
In any case, you still received this Dark Citizen with a smile, gave him the goods he needed, and collected a certain amount of Dark Coins. However, the Dark Citizen looked flattered, looking very happy, and kept muttering as he left: "I was actually received by the Dark Citizens......" or something like that.
You felt something was off, and after a while, Spamton did come back. It looked like he had indeed gone to buy goods, especially since he had brought back a small cart to push quite a few things. You didn't want to question him further, hesitated to speak for a moment, but after arranging those things, he looked at your expression and was the first to ask, "...... do you have some kind of [problem]?" I'm very happy to [answer you]. ”
You hesitated for a moment before saying, "I just realized that those Dark Folk ...... Are they very welcoming to the Light Folk of Darkness?" "Or is it that those Dark Folk have never even met the Light Folk before, which is why they're so excited?"
Spamton nodded and answered your question: "Of course, all the [People of Darkness] are happy to serve the [People of Light]. All [People of Darkness] welcome the arrival of the [People of Light]. ”
You rubbed your chin and stared at Spamton. He moved slightly uncomfortably, probably not used to your gaze, since you'd been staring at him the whole time.
So he couldn't help but ask, "...... Y/N, do you have any doubts about this? ”
You couldn't help but nod, paused, and then asked, "If that's the case, then you should be very welcoming to the People of Light—that is, you should welcome me...... But I feel like you actually don't have any special fondness for the People of Light." "You still hold a grudge about the first time we met, even though now you can trust him...... But there are still things from before!
Unexpectedly, he nodded decisively, which surprised even you: "You're absolutely right. Of course, I also welcome the People of Light to visit and take a look." But ......" He hadn't finished speaking before you interrupted him.
You waved your hand and said somewhat indifferently, "But you actually put interests first...... Or rather, what you care about more is yourself? Is it whether you can benefit from it? ”
He remained silent, not exactly agreeing with your answer, but not denying it either. And you didn't mind that much, just shrugged: "Alright, I understand...... Uh, I have another question—did you deliberately keep me here just now? Maybe you already knew the People of Darkness were coming to buy goods? ”
This time, silence spread between you two once again. You weren't in a hurry; you just stared at him, waiting for him to give you an answer. Maybe he couldn't stand your stare, or maybe after weighing his options, he decided it was better. After hesitating for a moment, he nodded and admitted decisively, "Yes." ”
You nod thoughtfully, even though he admitted he did it on purpose...... But you don't know why he's doing it. Honestly, you haven't figured it out yet. Thinking about it all the time isn't a good idea. You look at Spamton again, hesitate for a moment, then ask again, "So why?" ”
Alright, you'd better just ask directly!
This time, Spamton was just speechless. Watching you smile, that smile felt a bit strange, so you crossed your arms and touched the goosebumps on your arm, frowning at him and muttering, "If you won't tell me, then so be it...... Why are you laughing like that! It's kind of scary! ”
He simply kept smiling, then slowly shook his head: 'As you said, no comment.'
Spamton didn’t want to tell you his true intentions. Honestly, maybe even if he told you, you’d still choose to stay, or perhaps you would just leave angrily… and then awkwardly participate in the game again. Either way, you’re both fixed teammates.
But he didn’t dare to take that risk. He didn’t dare to bet on the chances that you would choose the former; he didn’t know what your attitude would be once you discovered his true intentions. Well, maybe he was just scared; he admitted that he cared a little.
So he paused again and said: 'Also, I will keep an appropriate distance, to facilitate your practical work.'
You frowned and looked him up and down: 'Uh… I admit that, but this isn’t exactly the kind of work I enjoy… Anyway, you’re really not lying to me, right?' You were suspicious of this, after all, he had a record, and now, inexplicably, you were on guard.
He shook his head decisively, silencing both your mouth and your doubts. In the end, you had to relax, puff out your cheeks, and look a bit displeased: "Alright, then I hope you're telling the truth this time...... You're really not lying to me, are you? ”
Spamton just smiled: 'Of course, I have no deceptive behavior, Miss Y/N.' When he said this, he was open and honest, and you couldn’t detect any sign of lying.
And Spamton truly has a clear conscience, after all...... He only hid it from you, how can that count as lying? He didn't lie to you about this.
You nodded, still somewhat skeptical: 'Alright, then I’ll trust you… I hope you’re not talking nonsense!'
However, there wasn’t actually much time for you to verify whether this was true or false, because the next day was already the time to enter the game world again. That night, you were unusually nervous, or rather, your heart was pounding. Normally, you could rest a while before switching worlds, but now you couldn’t sleep.
So you decide to tease Spamton, who is sleeping nearby. You turn around and gently shake his shoulder. Spamton opens his eyes and looks at you—clearly, he's not asleep either.
You smiled satisfactorily and started a casual conversation: 'By the way, what do you think the next world will be like?'
'I don’t know, and why are you lowering your volume?'
You realized you had indeed been speaking softly just now and coughed twice, a bit embarrassed but still self-assured: 'I… I was trying to create an atmosphere! Anyway, I can’t sleep and you seem awake too, so let’s just chat casually!'
You feel like Spamton just gives you a speechless glare, and you don't feel embarrassed at all.
'Alright, what’s your topic of discussion?'
You blinked: 'I don’t know.'
After saying this, you both fell into an awkward silence. Honestly, you were just looking for something to talk about… The excitement faded after a few casual words, and you turned over, casually patted the little puppet’s head, and fell into a deep sleep.
When you woke up again, you were already in the game world.
Wednesday· END

content:
Sptx: I've been watching too many witch hunts: Salem 1692 lately, so this is a more documentary literature ......
20,000 words.
——
[Main Quest: Survive successfully, evade religious judgment] Reward: One month of rest and safety guarantees.
[Side Quest: Ban the Religious Judgment and Save the Remaining Ones] Reward: 100,000 cash + 100,000 Dark Coins
You landed here holding Spamton—why hold on? It's a long story, since there was no other way now, at least there was nowhere for him to stay, so he could only let you hold him.
And you hesitantly looked around—or rather, you didn't even have time to take a look, since the surroundings were full of people, or as Spamton put it, all around were people of light, a dense mass that gave you no time to observe your surroundings. Even taking a deep breath only smelled human flesh and rotting iron, and all you heard were screams, wails, and chaotic pounding.
You silently covered your ears, and after a moment of silence, you still lifted Spamton onto your shoulder and set him down. Otherwise, if you covered your ears, he would fall off. There was nowhere for him to land on the ground, especially with the crowd pushing and shoving. If this little thing landed, he might get stepped on.
Spamton also silently covered his ears.
To be honest, you don't even know where you are—after all, it's chaos now. All you can see are heads and silhouettes, and occasionally panicked expressions. You seem to be right in the center of this giant cage—the reason you know it's a cage is because when you look up, all you can see is an iron ceiling, and the crowd around you can't disperse, so you know this must be a cage.
Immediately after, you feel your body sway—not just your imagination, because the others around you also start shaking—after hesitating for two seconds, you realize you are actually behind a carriage, probably outdoors, in other words, this cart is carrying your cage of prisoners somewhere unknown.
You hear the cries of those people grow louder; they seem to be banging on the railing, mumbling something, because you can faintly hear their cries even if you cover your ears.
The carriage seemed to be accelerating, because you felt your body shaking violently again, including the people around you. Spamton, who was on your shoulder, nearly fell to the ground from the shaking. You quickly let go of the hand covering your ears and pulled him back, now holding him in your arms again.
And you finally understand what some women are really saying in their loud screams: "I'm not a witch! I didn't do any of those things. The torment those girls suffered has nothing to do with me. I admit there was an evil spirit attacking me, but I have nothing to do with those devils!" ”
And you suddenly realize, what year is it now—it's the 17th century, the worst era of witch hunts, or rather, women suffered more injustice than usual. You swallow hard, hug Spamton tightly, and suddenly feel a sense of nervousness. Honestly, if there are so many people on the other side, you're really not sure you can escape. After all, even if you claim you have nothing to do with the devil, they will still distrust you and make up some reason to bind them to witches. Some women are even framing women, exposing each other, even if it's trumped-up crimes.
Are you really not sure you can succeed, even though you actually haven't done anything—perhaps, you have to figure out how to escape? With some hope and speculation, you glanced at Spamton in your arms, saw him still covering his ears, took his hand away with one hand, then leaned down slightly and whispered in his ear, "...... Uh, how likely do you think we are to successfully escape? ”
Spamton silently turned his face to glance at you. He naturally heard those words now, but he didn't know much about history, so he couldn't fully guess what time it was now. And you know, the dark Middle Ages were filled with religious trials and abuse of punishment, as if church power was always supreme, standing tat for royal authority.
"I don't know. Maybe I need to [check the general prison rules] and find the [best buying strategy]?" He hesitated for a moment before quietly answering your question. You rubbed your chin, stepped back two paces when the carriage shook again, and stopped, hugging Spamton tightly.
"Uh, escaping from a 17th-century prison shouldn't be too difficult...... right? "You whispered, but still a bit uncertain. Maybe you should ask the game system if they're willing to give you your previous weapon. As long as you have an axe or something, you're confident you can break the cage and complete your escape."
Before you could discuss further, the carriage stopped, and before you could feel suffocated in this crowded cage, you were both driven off and out of the cage. To be honest, the air in the 17th century was indeed fresh, but you didn't have time to feel the biting cold, because what awaited you next was the trial in court.
It seemed that fifty or sixty people were held in this cage, and under the strict supervision of the priest, you lined up in a long line into the trial courtroom. To be honest, the courtroom was indeed very simple: the defendant stood behind a wooden railing, the judge sat high on the platform, several recorders were handwriting something, perhaps not fully recorded, just sitting on either side below. The witness sat on one side, while you, the witch candidates waiting for questioning and trial, stood on the other.
Of course, they're all women, with only a handful of men and Spamton in your arms. So you can't help but give him a strange look—honestly...... Although there are indeed male witches, in this era, such a thing is extremely rare. Now you can't guarantee he might actually be executed, since the residents of the Dark World seem to have some magic to some extent...... But it probably won't be a problem.
The crowd was packed tightly together, noisy and noisy. The judge knocked on the wooden rope a few times, shouting for silence, and then the simple courtroom finally quieted down completely. You swallowed twice and looked at the defendant standing behind the wooden railing. She looked like a woman in her sixties or seventies, but her hair was already graying. Even as she walked to the defendant's seat, she trembled continuously, probably unable to take a single step, but her back remained straight, probably believing she had nothing to do with the devil.
But the judge glanced at you first, then the priest standing nearby gave you a meaningful look and said, "One of you is a devil." ”
You pressed your lips together. Honestly, this situation was just too frustrating.
After another round of commotion, you see the girl in the witness stand across from you striking a twisted pose, showing a pained expression and baring her teeth as if being squeezed and squeezed hard. Such a twisted posture seems impossible for ordinary people to pull off. Anyone who sees it would say it's an evil spirit causing trouble.
So the judge knocked on the wooden rope and asked, 'Do you admit to colluding with the devil?' The old woman denied this and declared herself a devout believer. Laughter seemed to spread among the seats as the recorders recorded but were altering something.
The judge ignored his answer, frowning, probably not very happy because he hadn't gotten the answer he wanted. So he simply scolded sternly, "How did you collude with the devil!" ”
"I've already said, I'm not colluding with the devil. I'm not a witch." The old woman repeated this sentence.
