His spell was originally intended to affect matters related to you, but since you asked so much of him, he wasn't unable to act.
Moreover, he might not feel a bit of compassion for the people of light here.
So he just nodded, but then reached out a hand to you, as if asking for some reward.
You slapped his palm irritably, rolled your eyes, and whispered fiercely: "Alright, I get it—isn't this just to highlight our angel's identity as an angel descended during the second trial! You still dare to make demands of me...... Forget it, I don't know what you want. You can ask me again later! ”
Indeed, although you do feel some pity for this woman, those few pieces of clothing are the greatest charity you can give—no more than that is impossible. Or do you remember that you should be brought forward for a second trial, to firmly uphold your angel identity, which is why you called Spamton to perform his spell?
Spamton glanced at you again before starting to cast the spell. You didn't know if this spell would work, but after the spell was done, the woman's complexion did improve a lot, and she seemed a bit more spirited. After observing all this, you looked at Spamton again, thinking about thanking him or something, but Spamton just shook his head and whispered to you, "The spell is just about 'external beauty'; it doesn't fully 'heal' the 'inside.'" ”
You thought for a moment and asked, "So, does that mean it can actually improve her condition a little?" "But actually, just improving her appearance is enough, because you heard the woman opposite crying out in surprise. They probably just saw that green light orb symbolizing healing flying toward the woman with a high fever. They were probably shouting, 'You really are angels, hoping angels can save their lives.' But you're just fake angels, probably not capable of saving everyone." Even so, you still try to pull yourself together a little. Think about it, there is still a way.
Spamton nodded, indicating your guess was correct, and you breathed a sigh of relief: "Either way, it's fine to help her condition improve a bit. At least let her die in less pain." You said this in a low voice. No matter what, you already foresaw the high likelihood that she would die in agony in this prison.
In the days that followed, you continued to wait for the second trial that would arrive at any unknown time. But before that, while the guards were delivering food, you happened to overhear those two shifts complaining, saying that wars had been breaking out outside lately, yet the witches were still causing trouble, causing many people to be tortured and unable to go to the battlefield, so they had to speed up the capture of witches. But the army led by that general was unstoppable, having already captured countless towns before that.
You and Spamton exchanged a glance, knowing the opportunity was coming. But before that, you were still trembling, after all, you only had underwear left, and the guard who came to deliver the meal didn't pay much attention. The woman with a fever on the other side was indeed getting better. Although prison food couldn't provide enough nutrition for her newly recovered illness, it looked like she could at least survive for a while.
You don't know when you might be rehearsed, so you ask the guards for their opinion, but he only roughly tells you to wait for the summons.
Then you had no choice but to ask Spamton again: "Maybe we should just break out of prison. It's better than just waiting here." "And you also retrieved the coat and similar things you threw to that woman earlier...... Luckily, she's okay. Otherwise, if you delay your side quest, it would have been bad. Though probably not to that extent, her death might have been inevitable.
Spamton hesitated too. In fact, he had been certain the second trial would come soon, but about half a month had already passed...... Maybe it was delayed by the external conflict, so in the end, he just nodded: "Let's wait one more day; maybe things will turn around." If not, then proceed with the [Prison Break Plan]. "Alright, maybe escaping is still better than waiting here to wait for something unexpected to happen.
So you waited another day. The good news is, the next day the guards did come and opened your cages, escorting you to the second trial. The guards pressed your arms, telling you to behave, while another guard grabbed Spamton. You really don't know why they made such a big move—after all, there were three or four guards following behind, probably afraid you'd escape.
After being escorted onto the carriage and waiting for a while, the priest led you off the carriage and returned to the defendant's seat.
Below was still a dense crowd, but there was some commotion in the witness stands. The guard...... Probably the guard who delivers your meals every day whispered something into the judge's ear. You don't know exactly what he was saying—maybe it was something happening in prison. Then the judge knocked twice on the wooden rope and shouted for silence, and everyone in the audience fell silent.
You hold Spamton and look up at the judge on the platform, unsure what he wants to ask, while the recorder sitting nearby is still quickly writing something on paper.
The judge asked seriously, "Do you know your guilt?" "I don't know why he kept asking such questions."
And you just find it a bit amusing. Honestly, the second trial feels like they're trying to frame you again, though the way you did it was a bit different...... It might as well be a good way to escape from prison from the start.
So you just pinched Spamton's cheek. This time, with a smile, you said to the judge, "We are not guilty; we are indeed angels sent by God to save this world. We have done everything we can. We hope everyone can find happiness and health. ”
The judge frowned, probably thinking about what to do next. The recorders also stopped writing, perhaps feeling that these words were not worth recording at this moment. The girls were still striking poses of torment, swaying left and right, their faces twisted and twisted in pain. Then you watched Spamton secretly cast the spell, and the girls quieted down again, as if all the pain had vanished, though a few still struck a few twisted poses.
So...... Most of them are just disguises, and entering prison is just a setup. Those who say they're tortured by witches and refuse to go to war are probably just an excuse—it's just their fear. You find it funny.
The voices of noisy discussion rose again in the witness stands. It seemed that two-thirds of the people insisted that you were indeed angels descending to earth, but the rest insisted it was just a minor spell performed by witches. Perhaps you were the leader of the witches, and you only ended their torment of the girl.
The judge tapped the wooden rope twice more and began asking the next question: "Then how did you relieve the torment on those girls?" ”
"Of course, it's the angel's [divine power]." This time, Spamton answered. You didn't speak, just glanced at the witness stand, and the remaining girls stopped moving, seemingly returning to normal.
"Then why did you remove the spells from their bodies?" The judge asked again.
"Because we can't bear to see [Full Torment], we can't bear to see [Double Price]." Spamton says again, and you can't help but cover your forehead, then Spamton's mouth.
"He said that because we are saints, angels, we do not wish to see anyone suffer." You explained for him.
The crowd grew noisy again, even more chaotic than last time. It seemed no one wanted to deliberately accuse you of being witches; even the jury members were muttering among themselves, unable to make up their minds. The judge tapped the wooden rope twice, seemingly intending to insist that you were witches, so he said, "Now I say you deliberately broke the witch's spell to evade punishment and claim to be angels. Do you admit that?" ”
You can't help but want to cover your head—well, honestly, if the judge insists on that, there's nothing you can do. He's determined to have you declared witches, so you're racking your brains trying to make excuses.
At this moment, Spamton spoke up: "So, is there any sufficient evidence to prove it?" He retorted.
The judge fell silent, and the recorder stopped writing. Instead, they started whispering among themselves, probably not even knowing how to record such cases. Should they portray you as real angels, or witches colluding with the devil?
Naturally, the court had no evidence. After all, you had only recently arrived here, and you could even say you didn't exist in this world. They couldn't fabricate evidence to accuse you out of thin air, since everyone in the witness stands was watching the scene in court.
So this sentence became your final testimony, because without solid evidence, the court could not continue to charge you. The jury members went to another room, probably discussing something. You had been standing in the defendant's seat for who knows how long, only knowing your legs were sore, your arms holding Spamton were sore, and you simply put him on your shoulder again. You heard whispers below, probably saying Spamton might really be your witchcraft puppet, and some insisted he was nothing more than an incarnation sent by God. You couldn't be bothered to correct their words; in fact, you were just a combination of the people of light and darkness, merely counterfeiters who were so-called messengers of God.
When the jury finally came out and you heard them declare you innocent, you breathed a sigh of relief. But the judge still seemed reluctant, telling the jury members to think carefully and then asking again how to recite the statutes of faith.
This time, Spamton recited it perfectly, and you didn't remember the story at all. Actually, you've been somewhat frustrated up to this point; under such conditions, it seems you haven't accomplished anything. If it weren't for Spamton, you probably would have only thought about how to escape, but now, it seems you can walk out with integrity.
While you were distracted, the jury members seemed to be arguing with the judge, but they still insisted on a not guilty verdict. In the end, the judge had no choice but to acquit you.
As if dreaming, you truly walked out safely, accompanied by a priest. Apart from the decades of unfair treatment you endured in prison, it seems you were not harmed.
But you still can't help but feel down. You really ...... It seems you haven't contributed much to this matter. But it seems there's no time to let you stay down any longer. You see that Guangping Mountain shows that the main quest progress is 100%, while the side quests are still at 0%. Even if you do nothing, you can leave now, but now Guangping Mountain has given a countdown. There will be a whole day before you leave this world.
So, there's no time to get discouraged. Patting your own face and pulling yourself together, you still need to figure out how to complete this side quest.
Spamton turned to look at your face. In fact, he had noticed you were a bit down, but now wasn't the right time—after all, the mission was tight. So he just interrupted your thoughts: "Maybe we can find that [General] now and have him take the lead in [Occupation and Renovation]." ”
You exhaled, "You're right, and time is tight. I don't know if it's still possible now." ”
After the priest escorted you out, he returned, and now you stood in a field full of wheat, barely able to tell your direction. To be honest, you didn't know where the so-called army was; you could only rely on your sixth sense, following the faint smell of blood carried by the wind as you headed in that direction. Where there was a smell of blood, it meant there were corpses, casualties, and sacrifices—which meant war had taken place there.
But now you can only go on foot, since you don't even have a means of transportation—neither an ox cart nor a horse-drawn cart. This only makes you feel a bit hopeless. Who knows when you'll reach your destination!
But since you started walking, you gritted your teeth and decided to move forward, carefully avoiding the wheat and walking onto the winding, muddy road. Honestly, you didn't want to damage the crops, since they were all painstakingly cultivated by farmers of this era. And as you walked along the road, maybe it was just your imagination, but you actually heard the sound of hooves.
You stopped and saw that about a thousand meters ahead, the army was rushing toward you. Perhaps you didn't even need to go out specifically to report this to the army; they would come to forcefully suppress the heretical trials—or perhaps an even harsher trial was about to begin, something you cannot imagine.
So you looked at Spamton on your shoulder, and just as he was looking at you at that moment. You cleared your throat a bit awkwardly and asked, "...... Do we still need to report to that army?" ”
Spamton's voice turned serious: "No, I think [you] need a [perfect dodge]. ”
You understood what he meant, but the area around was all wheat fields, and there seemed to be nowhere for you to hide—you did spot a tree not far away, and it seemed like a forest farther away, maybe you could hide in. Now, gritting your teeth, you ran toward that tree.
The army moved quickly; before you even reached the tree, swords and knives were coming at you, probably seeing you as an enemy.
You cursed twice in your heart, but Spamton grabbed your clothes to keep them from being thrown off. Seeing that you might not be able to dodge your current position, you rolled on the spot to dodge the attack coming at you. You cursed twice more in your heart, saying these people were killing indiscriminately—a bloody, brutal army. Even if this army conquered that place, those witches might not have a good end. Your heart suddenly sank. Maybe it would be better to go back now and try to break the cage and let those women out, but of course, you didn't have time to run back.
You gritted your teeth, dodged the gun that was thrusting at you again, and ran toward the woods. No one caught up. At first, a few people tried to catch up, but they were quickly pulled back. Maybe they felt that chasing only someone like you was too lowly, and since you were a woman, not a man, you posed much of a threat to them.
…… Thinking of this makes you inexplicably angry. It is precisely because of ignorance and discrimination without any reason that countless women have ended up like that, and why there is the witch trial. But this kind of thing isn't suitable to discuss at this moment; you just ran into the woods, hoping to hide for a while.
And coincidentally, a carriage was parked by the edge of the woods. You glanced at it and asked Spamton, "Do you remember how to get to the prison?" "You think that army is unreliable; you should release them yourself."
Spamton nodded.
So you relaxed, untied the horse, shook the reins, and started galloping. To be honest, you weren't very familiar with how to ride a horse, so your posture was a bit awkward and it always felt uncomfortable, but you couldn't worry about that because you only had 22 hours.
"Then, you will guide us." You took a deep breath and said.
Spamton sits on your shoulder and grabs your neck. Although it's hard to find direction on this barren land, he at least remembers how the car moved.
So he said, "First, go straight, then after about six hours, perform the right-turn procedure, and after twelve hours, proceed with the left-turn procedure." ”
You swallowed hard. Well, time was tight, and I didn't know if I would make it in time. And if I happened to get lost, it would be even worse—so as you steered your horse forward, you said, "Alright, if it's time, just remind me and I'll turn again." ”
Spamton just nodded randomly against the wind. Then, when the time was about right, he checked the time on the screen and reminded you to turn. You worked well together, and in the end, you arrived at the prison's outskirts with less than two hours left.
The countdown had turned red, and you couldn't help but swallow nervously, getting nervous. You stopped your horse and carefully bent over, using the tall cornfield as a cover to approach the prison gate. It was just a place outside haphazardly built with stone bricks, or rather, the stone walls were all towering, but it was obvious that it hadn't been carefully maintained, since you could see the mottled and mossy on top. There were two guards, yawning at the entrance to the prison.
You recognize these two guards, or rather, you are very familiar with them, since during those days when you were imprisoned, it was these two guards who brought you meals. It is evident that they weren't really strict about guarding their posts, after all, one of the guards was almost asleep, probably thinking that the prisoners couldn't possibly escape and that the outside world couldn't do anything to help them.
Unfortunately, you arrived. You continued to follow the cover of the cornfield around to the side of the prison, but you couldn't get any closer, after all, the surroundings were all barren open land. Spamton also lay on your shoulder, trying to keep a low profile to make sure you weren't discovered.
You look at those two guards, think for a moment, then quietly negotiate with Spamton: "You should run fast. Can you run up to them first to draw attention? I'll knock them out from behind." ”
Spamton glanced at you, but because of his glasses you couldn't see his emotions clearly, so you just coughed twice.
He was silent for a long moment before softly responding, 'Okay. But I hope you can succeed.'
You patted your own chest, full of confidence: 'Of course I can, trust me!'
So Spamton jumped off your shoulder. And you took a deep breath, knowing exactly what your heartbeat was. You stared intently at the two guards, and sure enough, when Spamton appeared, they moved, as if murmuring some witch's witch puppet. You also darted out from the cornfield, running behind them at high speed, and before they turned around, you slapped each of them on the neck, closing their eyes and falling before the guards could turn their heads in shock and terror.
You took two breaths, pulled yourself out of your tense state, crouched down, and snatched a bunch of keys from one of the guards, then picked up Spamton, who was walking toward you, and placed it on your shoulder.
At this point, the countdown was less than an hour away. You didn't even know why time passed so quickly, but your nerves were so excited—maybe it was the result of a sleepless night, and now it was just dawn.
…Dawn, the moment of daybreak, is also a time of rebirth; everything should become bright and beautiful. So you hurriedly crossed the prison gate carrying the bunch of keys, opening the doors of their cells for the women under their surprised gazes. There were also unfamiliar faces, seemingly new witches who had been imprisoned just yesterday, and you unlocked their cells one by one as well.
Then, when those witches—no, ordinary, pitiful, and innocent, fragile women—come out of their cages, you wave your hands and casually say, "God is gracious and has forgiven your sins. If the court wants to judge you again, tell them that angels have forgiven your sins and cleansed the traces of dealings with the devil on you." ”
As you say this, you might inappropriately think that maybe you really have been infected by Spamton, and now you say such deceptive things.
And those women, with tears of gratitude, bowed to you, nodded, and some even knelt and kowtowed, saying thanks to God's mercy, thanks to the angel's redemption, and only then did those women run out.
You also don't know where those women will go, because you looked at the screen and saw that there were only a few minutes left, and the side quest progress was still only at 50%.
You were exhausted and gave up, simply sitting cross-legged on the ground with a bitter smile. Then, when the guards finally woke up and rushed in to grab you, you smiled and embraced Spamton, disappearing from their sight.
And then you heard the system's virtual fireworks.
Endless Abyss· END

content:
Even after returning to the Dark World and leaving the game world, you still held Spamton. When you came to your senses, you exhaled and quickly let him go.
At the end of the day, you're a bit frustrated and a bit dazed. You feel like you haven't contributed much to the main quest, which frustrates you—who always praised yourself for not having Spamton or even clearing it without you—and you haven't completed all the side quests, which makes you feel a bit guilty.
…… If possible, try to complete all future side quests, you secretly thought to yourself.
However, after quieting down for a while and calming down after leaving the game world, you didn't expect a check with a denomination of 50,000 still appearing in your hand—exactly half the reward for side quests. It seems that side quest rewards are actually settled based on task progress, but realizing this only makes you more frustrated.
Meanwhile, Spamton nearby was drowned out by the swirling of dark coins. Of course, before long, those dark coins disappeared, disappearing into some unknown account. Seeing this, you couldn't help but laugh, finally feeling a bit better. Spamton glared at you, probably because you were still in a good mood, so he didn't say much.
After receiving these rewards, you glanced at the time—it was 3 a.m. So you quickly lay down, threw yourself heavily onto the bed, took a deep breath, closed your eyes, and fumbled to pull Spamton, who was sitting beside you, to lie down next to you.
“…… Alright, it's only three in the morning. If you have anything to say, let's talk about it tomorrow. Get some good rest first." After saying that, you yawned. Spamton didn't say anything more, but when you turned over, you felt the little puppet press a little closer to your chest, its head seemingly resting against your chest, which made your expression a bit strange.
Thinking about it, it seems like this was the way you used to hold him before...... But you never cared before, after all, he was just your business partner; it didn't matter if he was male or female. Honestly, you never even really cared about Spamton's gender; maybe he was just a biological male and not female...... Well, you were joking. It's just that you never cared before, and now you're fussing about it again, which feels a bit strange and a bit awkward.
But if you try to ignore that awkward feeling and try to fall asleep, you actually start to feel a bit sleepy. But deep down, you're still mindful of that bit of frustration, and that mood is getting worse. So, although your body feels sleepy, your mind is still excited—or rather, that sense of frustration is building up, making it hard for you to move on for a while.
So you opened your eyes, looked down at Spamton, who was probably really asleep with his eyes closed, and started shaking his shoulders without hesitation, saying, "Forget it, you probably haven't fallen asleep yet. Come chat with me!" ”
Spamton was woken up by your shake, glaring at you angrily, while you glared back with righteous confidence. He thought, maybe he understood what you were thinking right now, so even though he was a bit angry when you woke him up, he still dutifully comforted you, the Citizen of Light: "I think you've already worked very hard. No matter how the game ends, you can't be absent." ”
He thought, maybe normally he'd just ignore everything, and he doesn't know how to give you that damn free psychological counseling at this point. Good baby, free psychological counseling is free, then so be it. Spamton knows you need companionship and understanding, after all, he knows that no matter what, you're essentially lonely. And no matter what, he actually needs to thank you.
Hmm...... Maybe it's for some other reason, but who knows?
You sighed and started rubbing his head hard again. Honestly, his hair wasn't very smooth, and it wasn't very comfortable to the touch, but you found it very stress-relieving. Probably watching Spamton frown and endure your pressure while swaying along with your hand was very relaxing.
"I know...... Actually, I know I've done a lot, but without you, maybe the main quest wouldn't have been so easy to complete. If it weren't for you, maybe I wouldn't have been able to complete the side quests either. So, you actually have to do it. "Oh my god, you don't even know what you're talking about. Maybe it's just nonsense. But as you spoke, you couldn't help but laugh. Alright, you have to admit, without this partner, there are many things you wouldn't have accomplished.
Spamton just looked at you, then the puppet's little hand poked your cheek: "Your existence is also essential. Without you, I can't clear any game." ”
You quietly listened to him say this and couldn't help but nod: "Actually, I know this, but I...... Even knowing this, you still can't help but feel frustrated, still blame yourself, still can't help but think, if it were someone else, would it be better, or if I were a bit smarter...... Before you could finish, Spamton interrupts you, covering your mouth with both hands.
"No, [you] is [you], and my [collaborative partner] only needs [you]. Because it's [you], we can smoothly reach the [game ending]." "For some reason, although the puppet's voice still mixed with strange electric currents and messy clips that seemed to be taken from the radio, you felt that at this moment his words were very serious, and probably meant sincerely.
So you couldn't help but nod; in the end, you agreed with what he said. Well, you are you, and it can only be you. Since he agreed, it was better to maintain the status quo!
So you reached out and grabbed Spamton's face, then tugged at him. You smiled and winked at him twice, signaling that you knew about this and that he didn't need to say anything more.
So he released the hand covering your mouth, but just before you could speak, the puppet's hand covered your eyes again. You blinked in surprise, and Spamton could feel your eyelashes brushing across his palm. Honestly, it tickled a little, and for some reason, it tickled his heart too. But before that, he spoke seriously: "Then, now [you] should [get good sleep]." ”
You pouted, wanting to say something more, but since he was woken up by you and didn't scold you, you forgave him! So you pulled his hand away, just closed your eyes, and muttered, "Alright, alright, I get it. I'm going to sleep now...... Oh, you should sleep too......" As you spoke, you randomly patted his head and then stroked his hair.
Although you were still lost in these thoughts, maybe Spamton's words put you at ease, or maybe you were still a bit sleepy. In any case, before you knew it, you had fallen asleep.
Early the next morning, you sat up proudly, and at the same time picked up the still-sleepy Spamton, tossing him off the bed: "Alright, I need to change my clothes. You step aside for a moment!" ”
Fortunately, the moment you picked him up, Spamton was already awake, though his gaze still carried a hint of grievance. He took his clothes and headed to the bathroom first, soon coming out. You had also changed, so now it was your turn to wash up.
After washing up, tidying up your clothes, you head out. You sit on your shoulder with Spamton in hand, and before opening the door, Spamton takes the key hanging on the wall. You're used to it—since you don't usually remember to bring your key, you leave it all to Spamton.
Then, breakfast was probably still sandwiches...... But today you planned to change it, so after walking a bit and then turning a corner, Spamton looked a bit puzzled. He poked your cheek, and you poked his cheek too, saying, "Eating sandwiches all the time feels a bit tiring. I'm planning to change today!" ”
…… So today's breakfast turned into a proper Western restaurant, with bacon, freshly fried sausages, fried eggs, two slices of croissants, a small box of jam, and a small plate of soybeans. Although you didn't quite understand what that pairing was, you still finished your breakfast. Wiping your mouth, you waited for Spamton, who was swinging his legs from not getting a seat, to finish breakfast—honestly, you were the one who put him there. After all, he couldn't reach it himself.
For some reason, his pace had slowed down. You remember a month ago when he ate ravenously, it felt like he hadn't eaten in ages. But now, perhaps he had adapted to and enjoyed this comfortable life, so he began to savor it slowly.
…… Actually, you didn't think much of it. Honestly, you didn't have much of a demand for food—after all, you weren't interested in these foods, or rather, you weren't interested in eating at all. But watching others eat seemed pretty fun, so you propped up your chin and tilted your head, casually watching Spamton.
Of course, he could also notice the gaze on his body and your gaze. So Spamton, who was eating bread, looked up and gave you a puzzled look, asking why you were looking at him that way. You just waved your hand to show you had nothing special.
But you really didn't know how to talk and said, "I feel like you actually enjoy eating pretty well...... Uh, it's not that I look like you're enjoying it, I mean you actually enjoy your meal. ”
Spamton didn't answer your question, just glanced at you again. You couldn't shake the feeling that his expression was as if this was only natural. Well, that was indeed quite reasonable.
After breakfast and paying the dark coins, you bought two bottles of milk and handed one to Spamton, while biting the straw and drinking slowly. Even after finishing, you couldn't help but bite the straw. You were already somewhat familiar with the road, so this time you didn't need Spamton to guide you; you could still find the location of the dump, and of course, the location of his little shop.
But when you reached the door, you were startled. You thought the shop was basically deserted, so you took Spamton to enjoy breakfast slowly, and he ate very slowly himself! Now you have to think about whether he did it on purpose. After all, it seems like there's a long line in front of the shop, with all kinds of Dark People gathered at the entrance, noisy and noisy. You didn't hear clearly, and with so many people, you inexplicably felt intimidated. You definitely didn't want to go in.
So you quietly walked a little outside, then poked Spamton on his shoulder: "Can you come over today?" I'm a bit afraid to go. "But your textbooks are still in Spamton's shop. If that's the case, you'd have to ask Spamton to bring your textbooks out." Thinking about this makes you a bit worried again.
Spamton looked at the Dark People, his eyes darting around, lost in thought. Anyway, you shivered inexplicably, feeling like he wasn't thinking anything good. Still, he nodded: "Alright, today I'll do [Marketing]. However, [You] need to do [Ground Placement]. ”
Hearing this, you quickly put him down and put him on the ground, then quietly moved a couple of steps to the side, squatted down, and said to him, "Uh, but my homework book is still in your shop. Can you help me get it later?" You saw it too—there are so many people of darkness, I feel like I can't squeeze in. "You're actually someone who knows how to yield to others, so you're embarrassed to cut in line. Even if, in some ways, you seem to be one of the shop owners?"
No, you're just a clerk.
Spamton glanced at you silently. For some reason, you noticed his lenses had turned into that garbled mosaic again, as if he wanted to say something more. But in the end, he just nodded at you: "Alright. But I suggest you perform [Azimuthal Shift]; [You] cannot [Freeze in Coordinate Stop]. ”
You nodded, knowing what he meant—basically, you can't stay here. So you rubbed your knees, stood up, and walked around a pile of garbage ahead to the back. At this moment, you're actually relieved that the trash here is almost piled up like a small mountain, which makes it easier for you to hide.
So you hide behind a pile of garbage, peeking out sneakily. Honestly, you're a bit curious about what happens to those Dark People afterwards. After all, aside from the staff you normally interact with while eating and Spamton, you haven't interacted with any other Dark Folk before. You don't know why those clerks always show that excited expression every time they see you, almost fainting. You can't be a celebrity in the Dark World, right?
Then, as you saw many of the Dark People leave, still looking very dejected, you can't help but stroke your chin.
Although you don't really know what happened...... But it seems there are still a few Dark People gathered outside Spamton's shop, sounding like they're making an indignant commotion about something. No one knows exactly what Spamton said, but in the end, those Dark People left angrily. The entrance returned to quiet, but it seems they bought something to take away when they left, leaving some Dark Coins on the counter. Since the distance was a bit far, you couldn't hear clearly. You just stroked your chin and speculated, surely Spamton's business suddenly improved...... It's not impossible, but maybe he did something else without you noticing.
Anyway, after the Dark People piled up at the shop entrance had left, you sneaked out cautiously and glanced around to see if any other Dark People had noticed you—though you didn't know why you were acting like a thief at this moment, in the end you quickened your pace and entered the cramped shop, sat skillfully on the small stool you usually sit, and then took the textbook and homework book Spamton handed you.
To ease the awkward and quiet atmosphere that somehow seemed a bit awkward, you pretended to laugh cheerfully: "Seems like business has improved, hmm?" ”
…… But for some reason, after saying this, Spamton didn't respond. Instead, he lowered his head, and the atmosphere became even more awkward. You realized belatedly, you should have said the wrong thing...... Did you say the wrong thing? Even though you couldn't figure it out, what exactly did you say wrong?
But that doesn't stop you from apologizing first. After all, sometimes you really don't know how to read the atmosphere and always say something wrong for no reason: "Uh, sorry, I think I said something wrong just now?" But honestly, I don't really understand why those people gathered at your door...... Could it be that they're just here to see something new? "You're starting to guess casually.
…… After all, you really don't know the real reason, so you just make things up, and Spamton doesn't seem like he's trying to tell you the real reason.
Only then did Spamton look up at you. Of course he knew why—because you were a rare Light Clan in the Dark World, and those Clan of Darkness had never met you before. No matter the reason, they would come to see you—maybe out of pure curiosity, maybe some good intention, or maybe just a stunt for the Clan of Light.
He deliberately kept you in his shop, partly because he genuinely hopes you can learn something...... Probably, but chances like that might not be frequent, and a large part of the reason is that he hopes to use your identity as a citizen of light to achieve some goals, even though he isn't sure if that will happen.
So, how could he possibly tell you the truth? Even though he knows the real reason, he absolutely cannot say it, so he just brushes you off, half-truthfully saying, "Maybe, he really is here to [see something new]." Spamton did not lie, nor did he tell the absolute truth, and such words are the easiest to gain trust.
And sure enough, you believed it, nodding thoughtfully: "Alright...... I don't even know what's so interesting about it, so let's just leave them alone." As you spoke, you shrugged and immersed yourself again, burying your head in your textbook.
Watching the novelty...... Of course, it's about you, the New Light Citizen to them, Spamton thought, just turning away from you and sitting at the counter in a daze. He believed more people would come later, because what he told those Dark People was that those who came to buy [goods] had a [chance] to receive [Rewards from the [Beings of Light].
As for what the reward was...... It was just that you were sent to sell things to the Dark People. Plus, you could find some work too—a win-win situation.
In the following days, the foot traffic did seem to increase a bit, and for some reason, Spamton went out more often. But when he came back, he always brought something with him. You felt like he was restocking, and it was normal for him to leave for a while—but when he left, it seemed that some Dark People would come to buy things, so you had to take Spamton's place to host and help sell things. Honestly, at first you didn't get used to wearing a smile, but over time you got used to it. You just honestly sold what they needed.
…… After all, Spamton always seems to be slick with his tongue selling other things, so when the Dark Commoners come to buy things, they leave with two or three things they didn't actually want—like some kind of discount or promotional tactic. In short, you're amazed. You're still too honest and upright; you definitely won't learn these things. Occasionally tricking people is enough to make you feel guilty for quite a while.
However, those Dark People always seem very excited when they receive the goods you hand over, which you don't quite understand...... This is just like the behavior of those shop assistants before, which you can't understand. It's just that those clerks seem used to it now, while the Dark People remain just as excited. Could it be because you are a Light Citizen?
And with more and more customers lately, you really feel like you really need to find out what's going on...... Just because you're not good at socializing doesn't mean you can't.
Anyway, when another Dark Folk came to this window to buy medicine, you handed him a reagent vial while pretending casually—well, it looks like your disguise failed, but it doesn't matter: "Speaking of which, these potions are pretty ordinary. You can buy them elsewhere, right? Why come all the way to the junkyard?" "And don't think you don't care about prices at all. You've noticed these things are actually a bit more expensive than other shops, by a few dozen Dark Coins.
…… This doesn't seem like a trivial matter anymore.
So the Dark People accepted the medicine bottle and handed over the Dark Coins, but gave you a rather strange look: "Because the shop owner said that as long as you come here to shop, there's a chance you'll encounter a shop assistant who is a Light Citizen...... So when they hear this news, almost all the Dark People come to take a look. You're the shop assistant, don't you know? ”
You were a bit stunned. You really didn't know this, and Spamton had never told you before. This time, you finally felt as if a bucket of ice water had been poured over your head. Your lips trembled twice. Although you instinctively wanted to shake your head, you knew you couldn't, so you just smiled: "Ah...... I know, I feel like I've heard of it, but I just couldn't remember right away. Sorry to bother you. ”
Lies—you've never even heard of them, and this is the first time you've heard them.
That Dark Citizen nodded, happily took the vial and left, while you stood dumbfounded behind the counter, tugging at the corner of your mouth, feeling angry at being tricked, but even more so a sense of helplessness.
…… You even think that being able to tell a lie so smoothly just now is a huge joke. Oh my, you're not exactly a completely honest and upright person anymore. True, how could a truly honest person dream of windfall from the sky?
You've already experienced what it feels like to be deceived by Spamton once, but you still chose to trust him. Honestly, it's nothing special, nothing major. You know, it's probably some kind of marketing tactic, exactly what he needs, and it really works. But for some reason, there's a deep sense of helplessness and indescribable resentment, and you feel like you shouldn't have done it.
Actually, if he had told you from the start that he had come to the store for this purpose, you probably wouldn't have thought much of it, so you might just be angry that he deceived you...... Moreover, to be honest, there is a kind of anger at being looked down upon.
Although you know he does mean well, you also know that at least for now, what kind of job suits you better is not standing behind the counter as a salesperson.
But...... Well, you can't keep your imagination, because you hear the shop door being pushed open, you see Spamton coming back.
He was just as usual, just thanking you and saying, "Thank you, Miss Y/N, for taking care of me during my [outings]." As he spoke, Spamton raised his hand, probably wanting to shake your hand, just like always.
But you just quietly watch him, then exhaustedly slump your shoulders. You don't know what kind of look you have now—maybe it's disappointment. You try to stay calm, since you don't want to argue. Arguments often hurt both sides because emotions are out of control at that time.
So you just quietly ask, "I...... In your shop, is it just a mascot role? "You know, you probably just got it serious, you're certainly not just a mascot sitting here for people to admire.
Spamton looked up at you, probably realizing you had noticed something. He just stood on tiptoe, grabbed your hand, and shook it twice as a handshake, and you found this behavior a bit amusing.
"Of course not. I'm very grateful to you for your exclusive support." He only said this, without fully confirming some things.
But you also understood what he meant. You just reacted slowly, not completely lacking thinking ability. Ultimately, you were just a person whose thinking ability was about the same as ordinary people.
“…… Alright, I understand, so you didn't truly want me to work and help at your shop; you had your own purpose mixed in." You concluded, at least that's the conclusion you can reach now. Honestly, did you feel disappointed? Maybe a little...... Although at first, it didn't seem like you should have had high expectations.
At least you understand what his purpose was before that he hadn't told you. If only he had told you everything completely at the time, but unfortunately, there are no ifs.
But he just looked at you, and you two stared at each other, staring at each other in silence for a moment. It seemed he thought it might be better to just say it outright. Spamton nodded decisively: "Yes, this is my [real purpose]. But the right [interest ties] are much stronger. ”
Hmm...... In other words, he thinks that sincerity mixed with interests might be more sincere. You don't agree or deny it, after all, you actually have no idea what sincerity really is. In other words, you have no idea what those things about love and love really mean, nor do you know what they feel. However...... Maybe what he said really is true.
Your conversation was calm, and there was no argument. But for some reason, after saying this, he lowered his head, seemingly afraid to look at you again. You couldn't be bothered to ask unnecessary questions, since you already knew the general answer.
You just stood up and said decisively, "Alright...... I know you don't see me as a mascot entirely; you have good intentions, but I don't want to accept it. Also, I don't want to be a mascot to some extent, although it's convenient and I know it. But taking shortcuts...... There's no joy more than steadily gaining something, at least that's how I feel. So, I think I'm more willing to do work that suits me honestly, and I want to prove my own strength. At the very least, I have to tell myself that I can do it. ”
You announced this, then prepared to walk out of the shop. Although you said this, you still felt a bit lost, since you didn't know what other work you had to do...... Your previous job was helping move corpses in the hospital morgue. You can't go to the hospital to carry bricks or anything like that now, which doesn't seem very suitable for you......
Just as you were lost in thought, Spamton spoke up, sounding like he wanted to persuade you to stay: "I understand. [You] don't want to accept [discounts]. [You] want to make a [full payment] operation, but I also want [you] to know that [you] can always come to my [Store: Location Location] to enjoy [free coupons]." However, I don't agree with [you]. Whether it's the [Portable Road] or the [Rough Road], as long as you can become a [big shot], I think it's worth [trying]. ”
This seems like the first time you've had such a long and serious conversation...... In the past, there were occasional moments like this, and you or him would always brush it off. Sometimes, you weren't really sure what he was thinking.
You turn around and look at him seriously, and you see Spamton does wear a serious expression—he really does seem serious.
You sigh, then take a deep breath. You know what he means is that his shop will always welcome you, that this position has always existed, or rather, it was originally created especially for you.
But after thinking it over, you actually reached out and beckoned Spamton's money: "By the way. Last month's salary, and this half month's salary, you can give me first." ”
So you and Spamton stared at each other for a long time. After all, he probably didn't expect you to make such a request—honestly, your money really isn't easy to split. You hooked your fingers again, stood on your hips with your hands on your hips, and looked at Spamton confidently. After a moment of silence, he finally counted out 1,500 Dark Coins and handed them over to you—just one and a half months' salary.
After you get the money, you count it and confirm the amount is indeed 1,500, then accept it satisfactorily. Then you look at him and think for a moment. To be honest, you hesitate for a moment, since dissecting someone's inner feelings might sound awkward, and the other person might not even listen...... But it's just a sentence.
Yes, just one sentence, so you cleared your throat: "Alright, actually, I don't particularly dislike your behavior. I just feel that at least you don't need to hide it from me...... In other words, I thought we could already be considered good friends and could say a few honest words, but you still chose to deceive me, which makes me a little sad." After saying that, for some reason, you felt much lighter. Indeed, having words bottled up in your heart might make it even more painful.
It's better to just say it now, but you don't know if Spamton is willing to talk. You feel like he's always unwilling, and even if you try to peek into his thoughts, he'll block them off, always hiding as if it's some shameful secret.
Spamton looks back at you, and once again his glasses have turned completely pixelated, making it impossible to see what his true thoughts are. After all, you can't even see his eyes anymore, and now you can't even see his expression, as he lowers his head, lost in thought.
"...... sorry, I thought this would be better for you." He just said that, without explaining anything else, but for some reason, it only made you angrier.
Yet you still took a deep breath and kept your composure: "Alright, it turns out this isn't good for me. It only shows you treat me badly, doesn't it?" You shrugged as you spoke, feeling like you were about to laugh in anger.
At this moment, Spamton finally lifted his head. He looked a bit flustered, and you were sure he was indeed nervous at the moment...... Well, you don't really know what you mean to Spamton—probably just a partner. You've realized this, so your anger eventually turned into a faint exhaustion and disappointment.
But he said, "No, Miss Y/N, I want [you] to have the [best experience], [you] and I are [friend added], I just ...... maybe that's just one of my [habits]. "Oh my god, he doesn't even know what he's talking about, why things have come to this. It's as if everything is about to fall apart the next second?" Spamton could only admit that maybe he hadn't really considered what you'd think. He was just afraid you'd reject him.
…… Still, why was he afraid? He didn't know either.
You lift your head again and look him straight in the eye: "Alright, maybe you really do think about what's best for me...... Well, anyway, I've already told you, so please don't be so good in the future, okay? Although this time I was hurt, as long as I explain it clearly, I can quickly put this matter behind me. I just hope this kind of thing never happens again. ”
You see Spamton reluctantly nod: "...... I [guarantee]. ”
You don't know how effective his promise is, but hearing that makes you satisfied. After all, if he's truly a master of deception, it doesn't matter if he deceives you from the start to the end—you'd rather know nothing. It's better than being like this now.
So you relaxed and reached out a hand to him: "Alright, then let's get to know each other again. Want to be friends?" My name is Y/N. ”
He looked at you with a complicated expression, but finally reached out and held your hand: "Hello, Miss Y/N, nice to meet you." ”
You shook hands, and you finally walked out of the shop, happily holding the 1,500 Dark Coins you just received. But just before you left, you suddenly remembered something, turned back to Spamton, and shouted, "Ah, I'll be home tonight! Remember to bring my textbooks and stuff back!" ”
Out of the corner of your eye, you catch a glimpse of Spamton nodding helplessly, so you happily walk away.
Even so, you still haven't figured out what exactly you want to do...... But since you've already made it clear, you can actually do whatever you want, even if it's just a manual laborer carrying bricks at the dock. Of course, if that's what you think, you wouldn't actually do it.
…… Or maybe work as a cashier at a grocery store or something, but isn't that still pretty much the same as working in a Spamton store? Looking at it this way, it's better to be a manual laborer...... Speaking of which, the Dark World should have hospitals too, right? After all, the Light World has them, so why wouldn't the Dark World have them?
Sure enough, you did find a hospital inside Cyber City. To be honest, it seems the Dark People inside don't really need your help, since some of them already have syringes with them. It feels like the Dark Folk entering the hospital will be discharged soon. Your feelings are a bit complicated.
Still, you managed to find a job here, and although I probably handed it over to you right away for the sake of your Lightfolk, it leaves you feeling a bit complicated. To be honest, you don't like this at all, but there's nothing you can do. After all, you don't fit in with the Dark People—no matter how you look at it, you're just a Lightfolk.
And you came to the hospital because you secretly learned a bit of nursing work while at the hospital. You think those nursing skills should be enough, since you were a bit nervous when you first arrived. Who knew the work here would be so simple? Maybe it's because you're a citizen of light, so these jobs are so simple.
Anyway, you easily finished your day's work and happily left your workday. You bought a sandwich to fill your stomach. After all, even if you go home that evening, you don't know if Spamton will be waiting for you to eat together. What if? Thinking of this, you took out your Dark World phone and sent him a message, but he didn't reply. After hesitating for a moment, you still didn't call, only casually buying a bouquet of blue irises while passing by a flower shop.
After all, the fresh taste lifts your spirits, and the flowers just look good. Just then, you've finished your sandwich, so you take out your phone and check again, only to find Spamton replied to your message, telling you he hadn't had dinner.
Very good...... If he doesn't reply, you have to call him. After all, you were just too shy to call because you had stuffed your mouth with a sandwich, so you happily replied with a message asking if he had a dinner spot he wanted to visit.
Spamton said no, so after thinking for a moment, you suggested we go eat sukiyaki today.
He said yes. Maybe he doesn't mind exactly what location you mentioned.
In short, you're just happily heading home. On the way, you remember there's no vase at home, so you buy another vase. At least it looks beautiful enough—but actually, after buying it, you realize you've only bought some useless things, and your salary just went through it. Even though it's only a little, you still stick out your tongue in embarrassment.
But keeping a good mood is also very important! So you still brought the vase and the bouquet back home, happily pushed open the door, and shouted, "I'm back!" "Anyway, you know he's definitely home, otherwise he wouldn't have come back so quickly."
You naturally heard Spamton's voice: "[Welcome home]." ”
And you, happily humming an off-key tune, place the vase on the coffee table, unfold the bouquet and put it inside, pour in some water, and make sure these beautiful flowers can live a few more days.
Think about it, you really do treat this place as your home. After all, this is the place you long to come back to, the place where someone is waiting and waiting for you to come back, and it's where you can truly feel at ease. Although there were a few minor conflicts earlier, you have to admit that this might bring your relationship even closer.
At least, that's what you think.
Spamton naturally noticed your movement, and naturally, he asked, "[Question: Motive]?" "You saw him sitting on the sofa, his feet not touching the floor, still slightly swinging his legs.
And you just stand on your hips, looking somewhat satisfied at your masterpiece—even though you've just placed a vase and water and casually inserted the flowers: "Ah, the house should have some decorations, right? That way, it feels more like home, and seeing it will lift your mood." ”
“…… Indeed. Then I'll also do the [Regular Quest: Change the Bouquet]. "He was silent for a moment, then answered you like this. Spamton had to admit, your choice was the right one. Of course, he actually liked this place too, because he felt at ease in this residence. As for whether it was because you were there...... Well, Spamton thought, and even now, he had to admit that it was precisely because of you that he liked this place.
Maybe, he thinks, he really wants to trust you more, and he really can't deceive you anymore.
…… After all, compared to other things, he probably fears seeing your disappointed expression. When we talked to you earlier today, he almost thought you would abandon him after that. But it seems that perhaps you and he share the same or similar thoughts.
You didn't think too much about it. You just walked over with practiced ease, then picked up Spamton and held it in your arms: "Hmm...... Alright, let's go have dinner first! No need, just remember to replace the flowers that were already on display when they are rotted and withered. After all, sometimes I forget to bring back new flowers. Actually, my memory isn't that great. "You stuck out your tongue as you spoke.
You took Spamton to a sukiyaki yaki restaurant, which you happened to see on your way home from work. So you easily and confidently found your way and walked there, not forgetting to say to Spamton, "See, I can find the way without navigation!" You don't know what you're doing. Basically, what you mean is that even without his help, you can live well on your own, since that's how you came before.
Spamton didn’t respond, but you felt the puppet in your arms touch your arm, which could be considered a kind of response, although you didn’t really know what he meant by it.
Sukiyaki is actually a bit like hot pot, except the main ingredient is sliced Wagyu, and the topping is a hot spring egg. You broke the onsen egg and poured it into your own small bowl, then broke the egg for Spamton as well. After all, after you sat him down, his head barely showed the table.
The pot boiled quickly. You added a thin layer of wagyu slices, then scooped them out and put them in your own bowl, not forgetting to pick up two more slices for Spamton—since he definitely couldn't reach them. Who knows, the puppet's arm might even burn itself when it touches the scalding pot.
Although your actions were voluntary, you couldn’t help but complain a little: 'Ah, look how nice I am, even serving you food.' Well, it was more like seeking praise than complaining.
Spamton silently glanced at you and nodded: 'Miss Y/N [Wise and Mighty], [Unmatched].'
'…What are you praising this time?' you couldn’t help but comment, but your mood brightened. You knew what he was referring to—your achievements in the game world. Well, you admitted you had indeed contributed a lot! In short, you enjoyed the meal, not forgetting to split everything evenly, half for you, half for him.
After finishing your meal, you went to Guang World to attend classes at Adult University, or rather, you were rushing there. After all, it was already a bit late after you finished eating the sukiyaki—you almost got late. You don't know what Spamton did at home again—probably helping with cleaning. Anyway, when you got back, you saw the room was clean and tidy.
Wash up, then lie in bed with Spamton and fall into a deep sleep, have a whole rest period, then rush to the hospital in the morning to report to work, and for the next half month, you almost repeat this routine.
Until one day, a month’s time was up, and as usual, you fell asleep, but upon waking, you found yourself in another place.
Thursday· END

title: Horror Game Port 9 - Hotel Fright Dream

content:
Apologies if there are any OOCs. This chapter may contain disturbing bloody violence, as well as references to profanity. Please read with caution.
——
[Main Quest: Survive safely and escape the hotel] Reward: One month of rest and security.
[Side Quest: Successfully find evidence, report it, and bring the criminal to justice] Reward: 100,000 gold and 100,000 Dark Coins.
You hugged Spamton, looking seriously at the screen in front of you, then rubbed your chin. You turned off the screen and first looked around at the surroundings—well, it looked like a guest room inside a hotel. To be honest, although the room was a bit cramped, it was comfortable enough. The warm yellow light illuminated the entire room. Besides that, the window seat was the bed you were sitting on, and on the other side against the wall was a small table and chair. Besides that, there were simple amenities like a kettle. On the opposite wall was a projection screen similar to a TV, and the cabinet below was a flower arrangement. The hallway next door led out to a simple small wardrobe and bathroom.
Just looking at these things probably isn't a problem; the only problem is probably—
Your expression was grave so you wouldn't seem so overwhelmed as you asked, "Why are we in the same room?" "And this room only has a king bed, which means you two still have to squeeze in and sleep together. But since Spamton is so small, you can roll around freely on the big bed."
But for some well-known reasons—anyway, you looked seriously at the condoms on the counter, feeling inexplicably a bit uncomfortable staying in this room any longer.
Spamton was a bit speechless at your question, but following your gaze, he probably understood what you were thinking, so he fell silent for a moment.
The room fell into an indescribable silence at that moment. After a while, he finally spoke: "...... Perhaps to implement the [Room Change Measure]?" ”
Of course, you think the same way. Although it's fine to sleep together, aren't those previous worlds all spent this way...... It's just that the king bed room simply makes you a bit uncomfortable.
"Go try it, but maybe you can't change rooms yet." You took a deep breath, hugged Spamton, and walked out with the room card. You looked for the elevator or stairs and found that this small inn only had stairs, but the floor wasn't very high—about three floors in total, unless there was a basement or something—you had just climbed up out of curiosity to take a look.
The second and third floors are all residents' rooms, so there are quite a few rooms. The first floor has a kitchen, dining room, and library, and even the lobby has a comfortable, soft sofa. The warm yellow lighting makes this place seem a bit like it's for high-end residents—in other words, a place for the wealthy. You suddenly feel uncertain about changing rooms, since you're not sure if you can afford it—maybe you can't afford it at all.
I have no idea how this game system arranged for you to live in a place like this.
Anyway, you should walk over to the counter, clear your throat, and the receptionist at the front desk will look up and ask if you have any questions.
"Uh...... Can I change rooms? I want to swap out the king room I'm currently staying in for a standard double suite. "As you spoke, you showed your room card.
Come to think of it, she seems to have deliberately ignored the Spamton in your hand. You don't know why he's so unnoticed, but the receptionist just said she'd help you check it for a moment before looking down at her computer.
And you quietly hold Spamton, waiting.
After a while, she looked up again: "I'm sorry, miss, but the hotel doesn't have any spare rooms. The king room you booked is the last one and can't be replaced." ”
To be fair, this was actually the outcome you expected, so you just shrugged in thanks and hugged Spamton, ready to leave. Although you wanted to survive safely, you still hadn't seen anything dangerous.
But just as you were about to climb the stairs, you heard a "clatter" from the kitchen nearby, as if the blade was pressing closely against the cutting board. The receptionist seemed unfazed and continued with her own tasks. You would have been careless at first, if only you hadn't smelled a bit of strange blood.
Anyway, you stopped in your tracks, glanced back, and your pause didn't attract the receptionist's attention, so you darted around and simply led Spamton back. You sat down on the sofa in the lobby, and for easier observation, you chose a spot almost directly opposite the kitchen. In this spot, you could still smell blood.
The clanging continues. You see the man wearing a chef's hat raising his kitchen knife high and slashing fiercely, shattering the blood-red bones in front of him. The blood hasn't been properly treated and is slowly flowing down with the chopping motion. Faintly, you can almost hear the ticking sounds—the sound of blood flowing, and as a result, you smell an even stronger stench. You don't know why the chef doesn't handle the blood, which makes the meat look extremely fishy.
So you decided to ask the lady at the front desk. You walked over again, knocked twice on the counter, but couldn't think of anything else to say, so you simply asked directly, "Who is that person in the kitchen?" I noticed he hadn't even cleaned up the blood on the raw meat, and I'm worried the food he made wouldn't taste good enough. What if he couldn't provide satisfactory service? ”
The receptionist answered your question without even looking up: "The person in the kitchen is also one of our guests, not a real chef. The meals we serve are all carefully prepared." This guest said he brings his own ingredients but enjoys working in the kitchen. He also enjoys serving his special dishes to other guests. Of course, we respect our guests and do not force others. ”
You nodded, roughly understanding what was going on, but this cold yet cozy inn inexplicably made you feel fearful. Survive safely and escape from the inn...... Then you can just leave right now, right? You looked toward the main entrance. Although it was tightly shut, it was not impossible to open. You walked over and opened the door, only to be forced by the howling cold wind to close it again, making you shiver involuntarily. To be honest, it was indeed cold outside—far too cold, but inside the inn, it was surprisingly warm. And you just noticed—outside is a world of ice and snow, and the bridge in front of the inn is broken and impassable. In other words, at least for now, you can't leave. Of course, if you want to risk crossing the natural barrier, that's not impossible.
…… So, perhaps we have to wait until the bridge is repaired, or at least until the temporary passage is completed. At this moment, you turn your head to look at the hall and listen to the sounds coming from the kitchen. You suddenly feel a chill down your spine and shiver.
At that moment, Spamton actually raised his hand and poked your cheek, so you looked at the little puppet in your arms with a curious expression.
He lowers his voice and says to you, "Now, we should go to the kitchen [visit and search]." ”
Indeed, what he said made sense—whether it's a main or side quest, you should go to the kitchen to investigate. No matter what, that person's behavior is a bit strange...... Of course, this isn't a reason you can subconsciously treat the other person as a bad person.
But you shouldn't harbor ill intentions, but you must always be wary of them. You still have to go and see for yourself. You steadied yourself and still carried the little puppet toward that direction. The closer you walked into the kitchen, the louder the noise became. You saw the bloodstains stained on the chef's robe, the white apron, and the red blood—everything was so obvious. You also saw the chef's face. To be honest, his appearance was ordinary, but at that moment he seemed a bit manic, even tinged with a subtle reddish heat, as if he had suddenly caught a fever. The closer you got, the more pronounced the smell of blood became, mixed with the smell of rust. No matter what, it was unbearable, and you involuntarily frowned and covered your nose. To be honest, you don't like this smell at all, nor do you like this behavior. And looking at his expression, you think this person is really strange.
It's just that for some reason, Spamton doesn't seem affected at all. Maybe you're in this perspective and can't see exactly what kind of expression he hasn't made. But in any case, when you look down at him in a panic, you don't notice any change in his expression. So maybe he actually can't smell ......? Or maybe he can smell it, but only a faint scent?
