In any case, you struggled with that man for a while, then finally took the opportunity to circle behind him and slashed his neck hard with the back of an axe, knocking him out. Then you wrapped the rope Spamton handed you around his wrists and ankles. To avoid trouble, you tied them tightly, tied a tight knot, and searched to make sure he hadn't left any sharp objects. As for the ...... in the room, you had no choice, so you just placed him in the farthest corner, farthest from those things, and tied his mouth to prevent him from calling for help.
After finishing all this, you clapped your hands, wiped the sweat from your forehead, and took a couple of breaths. Doing all this really exhausts you.
Only then did you have time to sincerely thank Spamton: "Just now, no matter what, thank you very much." ”
Spamton just nodded modestly—of course, you might think he's just pretending to be reserved, but you can't find any evidence.
"It's fine, after all, we're partners." He said.
For some reason, whenever you hear the word 'partner' now, it always feels a bit strange, and for some reason, your mood seems a bit down. Maybe it's just that your mood is a bit off for a while! You didn't think much of it, just whistled out in an awkward tone: "Alright. Let's hurry downstairs now and check out that library! We can't stay here any longer." ”
After all, if that man manages to escape, he'll definitely gather others to gang up on you. If you do, you can't guarantee you'll win, especially since you're with Spamton. They're the real community of shared interests, and you've already escaped from two of them. If they find out, they'll definitely hunt you down.
Spamton didn't say much; clearly, he agreed with your opinion. But if you escape, you still don't know how to get out of this place. By this point, you haven't checked whether your phone has any signal...... Those worlds before didn't use phones, and you never considered these issues at all.
You took out your phone, which belongs to the world of light, and checked it. Okay, as expected, the phone had no signal. You weren't too disappointed, just quickly walked downstairs.
The banging sounds in the kitchen downstairs faded. You glanced over—the chef had left at some point, perhaps to deal with the corpse the man had just killed—his ingredients. For some reason, you felt a bit nauseous, but the receptionist was still standing there, head down, unsure what she was dealing with.
You decided to go and ask her some questions first.
So you walked up to her and knocked on the counter. The receptionist clearly recognized you—the customer who had just visited this morning had fainted in the lobby and was taken away. Her expression was still a bit surprised, but not obviously—she was puzzled that you had come to her unharmed, though her clothes were a bit disheveled.
Originally, you wanted to straighten your attitude and speak properly, but seeing her like this, you couldn't help but speak with a hint of sarcasm: "Seeing I'm not dead, you're disappointed, aren't you?" ”
The receptionist hurriedly shook her head and bowed to you. Her movements were clearly flustered, not serious: "No, honored lady, that's not what I meant. I just felt...... A bit surprised. After all, I had never seen anyone escape from that person's grasp. ”
You shrugged, looking a bit indifferent: "Now you see it. It's okay, you can still look a few more times...... Well, anyway, I didn't just escape from that person. The man in the other room is a pedophile rapist. You should know about that too, right? I escaped from that person too. ”
The receptionist looked up at you, her expression even more surprised. Clearly, she hadn't even considered such a thing—never thought anyone would succeed. Or rather, someone would resist.
“…… No need to be so surprised. I think my resistance is just self-defense. So, you actually know everything, don't you? "Your voice was lazy as you just scratched your hair, tidying up the messy hair from the fight earlier. Then you glanced at Spamton, who nodded at you, signaling that the receptionist showed no sign or intention to lie.
So you keep listening.
“…… Yes, I actually know everything. The receptionist lowered her voice, nodded nervously, and glanced around cautiously, probably afraid others might overhear.
You don't know how many other staff there are here besides this receptionist...... Ah, the real chef is probably the same; you don't know about the others.
So you just tilt your head, a bit puzzled: "If that's the case, you know almost everyone in this hotel is criminals, then why not call the police?" This is your initial doubt and the most urgent question. If you can call the police and resolve everything here, then the side quest can be easily completed. Unfortunately, you feel that none of this is that simple.
“…… Calling the police won't help. Miss. Actually, the people in this hotel are all subjects of government higher-ups conducting experimental research, so the police won't bother with this place. Even if you call the police, they say they'll handle the case and won't send anyone over. The receptionist still lowered her voice, speaking in a hurried tone.
After a moment of silence, you realize that calling the police directly won't help...... But at the same time, you have a new question.
“…… If that's the case. Why does your hotel still face outward to recruit new guests? Do those travelers become victims and victims without knowing it, just for that damn experiment? "Your voice rose a little, and your pitch rose, but to avoid disturbing those criminals, your voice was still relatively low.
Think about it, no wonder you can still stay in such high-end hotels. I bet they use some discount as an excuse to let poor people stay, since these hotels are probably something those people could never afford to stay in their whole lives.
“…… Because they needed sacrifices. And those above demanded the same, and those who sacrificed...... It's just pitiful that they sacrificed themselves. "The receptionist just shook her head. Her face was pale, her voice trembling, and her voice grew quieter and quieter. Her index finger covered her mouth, making a gesture to silence you. At the same time, she secretly pointed toward the stairs. You glanced over there. Fortunately, the chef had come down, though the originally white chef's uniform was stained with crimson blood.
You gasped, trying hard to calm that anger inside. So those old men above don't treat the lives of the lower class as human lives...... But sometimes, when those lower classes gather together, they become a force not to be underestimated.
You looked at Spamton, who nodded and then showed you a voice recorder, indicating that he had recorded everything earlier. Your feelings toward this accomplice were somewhat complicated. It wasn't pity or hatred; in the end, you just gave her a deep look before heading toward the library.
To be honest, when you first entered the library, you were startled by the dim environment and the densely packed quaint bookshelves in front of you—oh my, the hall was so bright, but only the area at the door caught the light; the rest was just dim and gloomy. Vaguely, you seemed to see green firelight, or perhaps ...... It might be a ghost. You didn't know what it was, only seeing the faint green traces drifting, so you couldn't help but shiver and pulled Spamton down tightly in your arms.
Spamton looked up at you somewhat speechlessly, but indeed, he felt a lifeless atmosphere here, though he couldn't quite say what it was. In any case, he simply suggested, "Do we need to [find a light source]?" ”
You nodded and looked around. Unfortunately, you saw nothing, no switches. Instead, there was an oil lamp on the wall flickering with a faint glow. Yet you didn't know why there was still an oil lamp hanging in the library. All the facilities in the inn were so modern, so why was this place still a hundred years old? Surely this library couldn't be from a hundred years ago as well.
…… It was as if you were telling a joke. In any case, you couldn't laugh, just walked toward the oil lamp, stood on tiptoe slightly, took it down, and illuminated a small area around it. At least you weren't so scared. But you still glanced thoughtfully at Spamton in your arms, but unfortunately you didn't rub your chin to pretend to think: "Speaking of which...... You're a puppet, and you're wood. So, can you light it? ”
But Spamton shivered at this moment. How strange—you'd never seen him react so strongly before, and he didn't know what word had provoked him. In any case, he just hurriedly said, "No, please, don't !! ] I hate [scorching hot], [burning], [heat]. ”
…… Well, now you can probably understand a bit, maybe it's reminded you of the past, so you apologize for accidentally poking at his inner wound: "Sorry, I was just talking nonsense earlier...... I forgot, you probably hate these things. ”
Your words were sincere, but Spamton was a bit stunned. He hadn't expected to receive such a sincere apology.
“…… No, [you] don't need an [apology]; everything is just [the past]. "He murmured in a low voice, as if murmuring to himself.
And you just shrugged: "Anyway, what I just said really hurt you a bit! Is it my right to apologize...... After all, I didn't mean to make you sad or afraid. And even if everything is in the past, the fear from back then must still remain." "Of course, you were just saying it casually. You don't really understand that much; you're just speaking based on your actual feelings and experiences."
…… After all, there are still many things about your past you haven't told Spamton. You think everything is in the past and doesn't matter, but when something like this happens, you still seem to feel the panic and helplessness of that moment. So you think Spamton probably feels the same way.
Spamton was silent for a moment. To be honest, he really didn't know...... Why do you care so much about the feelings of his partner? Is it just because they're friends, or because—he feels something pulsing in his chest. He doesn't really know what his inner structure is, but he does know it's probably something called the heart. So, do you actually care about him, or rather, like him?
He wasn't sure, nor did he know why, at this moment, he felt a bit anxious and insecure. Clearly, when facing everything, as long as he completed everything with confidence, that would be enough.
…… He didn't know. Maybe after a while, as long as he went through it a bit longer, he would come to understand.
And you don't care about all that nonsense. Maybe you do care about him, but for you, caring about your friend's feelings is normal. It's not like you dislike or hate him, and you insist on making him suffer. Isn't it normal to want him to live a little happier?
You just carried the oil lamp and carefully walked forward. The rustic bookshelf was covered in dust, showing that no one had touched these books in a long time. There were two books that were still brand new, though I had no idea what they were for.
Anyway, you should take a look at it.
The first book is experimental data, which seems to describe what experiments were conducted on those people and how they were confined in this hotel for observation. You can't help but shiver, since these are all some inhumane experiments—probably something that tampered with their nerves. You don't really know.
Besides that, when you reach the end of the book, you see something extra.
[About 'Hypnos']
'Hypnos, the deity, often wears a crown of daisy, appearing like a beautiful young man. However, his true form is a terrifying existence, twisted like a nightmare.'
'He is regarded as the deity who controls sleep and dreams, belonging to the ranks of the Old Gods. He often dwells at the boundary of reality and dreams, observing those who dream.
Dreams are his domain. It is said that if you are targeted by him in a dream, you will be transformed into a form He finds interesting. Your human instincts will be cut off and separated, and you will never escape from the dream world.
If trapped in dreams, life will be spent as His toy or pastime... If this "life" truly has an end." 】
You shivered again, feeling like you'd seen something you shouldn't have, giving you goosebumps all over.
Spamton, on the other hand, appeared perfectly fine and energetic. He simply read the passage by the glow of the oil lamp, then concluded: "It seems those [prisoners] are also suffering in the [Dream World]. ”
He also helped you stroke your goosebumps. Although the puppet's little hand was a bit cold, you felt much better.
You couldn't help but nod: "Yes, I wonder how the people who experimented on them managed to do it...... Well, to be honest, after reading these experiment records, I realized that the ones who used them for experiments were actually the ones who deserved to be arrested." Your expression turned serious.
Spamton nodded as well: "However, when it comes to the 'mastermind's true culprit,' we have absolutely no clue." ”
You flipped through the experiment records again. Indeed, the experimenter was very cautious, leaving almost nothing related to themselves behind. But since this book is frequently flipped through, you guess that the experimenter might actually be nearby. So—just have someone take out this place in one go. But you think that experimenter will definitely leave you a way out.
You closed the book, stuffed it back onto the shelf, and picked up another book that looked dustless, with many signs of flipping through. You casually said, "Hmm, but these people can't escape death too. The experimenter seems to have some conscience—in fact, he was actually using death row prisoners for experiments." "But whether it improved or worsened, you can't tell just from the experimental records. You're confused, and there are so many symbols on it that you can't understand at all."
Another book seems to say that the bridge before the cliff appears when encountering demons, because that bridge exists at the boundary between yin and yang. It is neither real nor illusory, but has survived here through certain means.
You don't really know how you did it, but after flipping through it, the last page contains records related to the time of encountering demons.
['The 'Hour of Encountering Demons' is a mysterious period in Eastern legend.
Generally, it refers to the one hour before and after dusk, when yin and yang alternate, the boundary between the two realms becomes blurred, and demons and ghosts are more likely to appear. Ancient people believed that dim lighting made it easier to encounter evil spirits, hence the term 'encountering demons,' meaning encountering demons. In folk customs, going out at this time is taboo to avoid encountering 'hidden spirits' or encountering the true form of monsters.'
'If we explain it from a scientific perspective, we can understand the reason: changes in light at dusk cause the cone cells and rod cells in the eye to switch between them. When people cannot adapt to changes in light, they may develop illusions due to fear of the unknown, mistaking others for something else.' 】
…… Although you are a materialist atheist, it seems you can only trust these strange and mysterious things now; otherwise, you might never be able to leave this place, because this inn is an isolated island. That means perhaps that bridge is actually a monster, which is why it appears when encountering demons. In any case, there is indeed a way to leave. You put the book back on the shelf, just about to turn and leave, but then you realize the door behind you is gone, and the inside of the library has gone dark. You raise the oil lamp in your hand, your face turning pale. You seem to hear some sounds behind you. No matter what, the surroundings seem to become infinitely spacious, and the dusty and rustic bookshelves that had just been gathered have now vanished.
You turn around and look toward the source of the sound. You hold Spamton tightly in your arms—or rather, a bit too tight. Spamton frowns, but he says nothing more, just lets you move.
After all, he knows your nerves are tense right now, and he can't provoke your emotions any further.
You look pale-faced, only to find that in the very center of this darkness, for some reason, there is an altar—for some reason, everything around it appears so clear, with no light at all, and a mirror in the center is shining, silvery white, as if reflecting moonlight that doesn't exist.
Around it, something black worm-like creatures writhed continuously, looking like lumps rising and falling, faintly reeking of blood—like rust. You guessed that the black marks were actually stained with dark red blood. Regardless, this suspicion made you nauseous.
No, wait, if you look closely, those lumps don't seem to rise and fall—maybe they're just stationary. After all, if you get closer, you'll realize that what you initially thought were black lumps are actually people wrapped in black robes.
They were kneeling on the ground, chanting incantations as they crowded around the altar, so excited that their robes trembled all over.
You quieted down, just holding the oil lamp. Spamton actually couldn't see anything; all he could see were bookshelves one after another, and you made your way through them, carrying him with you. He also smelled a whiff of rust. No matter what, he felt it probably wasn't a good thing, but when he pinched your cheek, you showed no reaction. At this moment, he couldn't care about your possible vulnerability. He tried to shake your arm to wake you, but you didn't react at all. Or rather, you didn't even notice Spamton in his arms, just listened blankly.
"Ah! Ah! Shabu Nicholas! The Black Goat of the Forest, which breeds millions of offspring! ”
Strange syllables are pieced together into words.
"Let all things be united as one! We call for your arrival! Supreme Mother Goddess! Goddess of Dark Abundance! O Black Goat of the Forest, who bears millions of offspring! Ah! Shabu Nicholas! ”
"Please follow the thousands of children and fill us with your seeds! Let more people come to your temple to worship!" ”
"Come on, come on! Goat! Black Goat of the Forest! Collect our offering! ”
Even though they were speaking a language you couldn't understand, for some reason you could hear it clearly. You shivered instinctively, and the puppet's little hand once again touched your arm. Only then did you realize Spamton was still in your arms. You glanced down at him, then looked up again. Everything before you vanished like smoke like a phantom, and before you was a brand-new bookshelf. All the books were brand new, with no sign of being turned through them.
“…… Did you see the illusion from earlier? "You asked after a moment of silence. You hadn't even realized Spamton was there earlier, which made you shudder.
Spamton just shook his head: "Apart from the [smell of rust] and countless [bookshelf], [empty space]." ”
You pause for a moment, then deflat: "Alright, then I don't even know how I ended up seeing those hallucinations...... First, hurry up and see if there's anything else worth reading in the library, then leave here." "You definitely don't want to be chased by a mad killer who might have escaped and called in a killer."
But it's fine that only you see those hallucinations, at least you don't have to worry about covering Spamton's eyes or anything...... Alright, you're just daydreaming and talking nonsense again. Actually, none of this really matters. Maybe it's just that inspiration is a bit strong?
In short, you look up at the bookshelf in front of you. It's brand new, and for now, you can't tell what is special about it...... After all, all the spines are written in English, Greek, French, and German that you can't understand at all, though these are probably Latin...... Oh, and Spanish and Russian. You don't understand a word of it, just that these are probably some kind of magic books. Thinking about this makes you shiver involuntarily.
You simply grab a copy and flip through it to see what is written on it. You see some messy text. Although it's in English, when put together, it gives you a feeling you can't understand.
The runes written on them seemed to be for some kind of summoning.
[Summoning Baeki's Rune]
[Rune to Summon Hasta]
[Rune to Summon Igronak]
[Rune to Summon Lilith]
[Rune to Summon Nyaratotip]
[Rune to Summon Shabu Nicholas]
[Method for Refining Shogges]
[How to Make the Crucible of the Ancient]
…… After casually flipping through the catalog, you found almost all of them were of this kind. You believe Spamton must have seen them clearly. In any case, you couldn't help but shiver, then you looked up, planning to put this book you couldn't understand or use back onto the shelf. Then you saw one eye staring intently at you in that gap. Earlier, when you were reading, it was inconvenient to put Spamton back on your shoulder to help him read. Now you shivered, shook the book, and threw it to the floor.
You were so frightened that you took two steps back, instinctively pulled out a steel pipe and grabbed it. You had no idea what was going on. You raised the oil lamp and saw that the person had taken two steps back. It was a woman, wearing a necklace with an inverted cross on her chest, grinning mischievously. She looked rather thin and weak, lacking any intimidating presence, but you still didn't dare let your guard down.
The woman, on the other hand, was still grinning, probably looking very happy: "Ah, so you're also a follower of the Black Holy Mother! I saw you take this book. I've always wanted to witness the miracle the Black Holy Mother has delivered...... But I've never succeeded once, so this time I want to summon her and give it a try. Why don't you try it too?" ”
…… It looks like he's just a cultist, and you breathe a little easier. But when you glance at Spamton, he nods gently, signaling that he's already turned on the voice recorder, or at least he did it when you first met this woman.
You're not sure if killing these people directly counts as bringing them to justice. If it were really that simple, you might actually be tempted...... But it's better to just go through some trouble.
So you just shake your head: "Sorry, but I don't intend to ......"
But before he could finish, Spamton interrupted him. He covered your mouth and simply asked, "[Black Saint]?" ”
"Oh, that's the one, the Black Goat Mother! Look, I still have a mark." As she spoke, she proudly showed off the mark on her hand.
You squinted and took a look. The brand and palm print had almost perfectly blended together, resembling an eye but also like a mouth. Overall, it was quite strange. Although the fusion was quite good, seeing her proudly begging for praise left you speechless for a moment.
The shape and location of this imprint remind you of a female demon and a god in Greek mythology...... Lamia and the god Pan. In some legends, Lamia was cursed to devour her child, and her eyes grew in her hands. In some myths, the story of Pan having eyes in the palm and devouring a child is performed by Pan. Since Pan also has attributes of a herdsman, some scholars believe this is a variant of the ancient myth of the agricultural god eating her child.
…… After all, you've read some Greek mythology, and you remember that the god Pan was actually a variant of Shab Nicholas.
So your expression twisted for a moment.
She was still lost in her own pleasure, talking to herself: "Oh dear...... It's just a pity that the other travelers don't believe in shabu, calling them atheists. It's still that the life in their own hands makes them feel even more intoxicated. What do you mean? It's just pure punishment that makes a person suffer, to die, and then chops up their flesh and bones for cooking. How can that be called art—oh, wait, I'm a follower of the Black Holy Mother, not the King of Yellow." As she spoke, she hurriedly covered her mouth again.
And you feel like laughing, your mood relaxing for once. To be honest, although this girl hasn't done much, she can still be considered an accomplice to those people...... Precisely because she is also a bystander, precisely because she hasn't actually done anything.
And you probably understand Spamton's meaning now: first, keep this girl steady, then you can escape. Summoning isn't something that can be done overnight.
Although you didn't know if this was a good idea, for now, this was the only option, so you took Spamton's hand away...... In short, you nudged him twice with the hand holding the lamp, and slipped the lamp into his hand, putting the steel pipe away. Then you held him in your arms. After all, you were frightened and needed to calm yourself down a bit.
You shook your head and nodded: "Mm...... Although I'm actually an atheist myself, I think I can go with you and give it a try—maybe it works?" "To be honest, you don't really think there's a chance of success."
At this moment, she looked at you seriously twice, first feeling a bit disappointed, then bursting out laughing: "What is it...... You're also an atheist, huh? It's really boring. But looking at it this way, You're actually the kind of person who is half believed, half skeptical. People like that can't be complete atheists, but they won't be theists either, because they always doubt the existence of gods. ”
You are speechless.
To be honest, before that, you always thought you were a complete materialist atheist...... But today, you suddenly became uncertain. She was right—you really are the kind of person who is half skeptical, someone who says you don't believe in God while still wanting to test yourself.
And she merely began to chant a phrase, seriously and head-shaking: "Since you are like warm water, neither cold nor hot, I will spit you out." ”
…… You know this is a phrase from the Bible. What does she mean by saying it now? Anyway, you felt as if you had fallen into an ice cave, just staring at her in silence, unable to speak.
She didn't explain this sentence, just waved her hand impatiently: "Anyway, only devout believers can participate in the summoning ceremony. Go away, go away, you completely unfaithful." What a pity...... If they were complete atheists, if they could find a few words to convince them, they might come to believe in people. People like you are the hardest to deal with. ”
After saying this, she skipped away, feeling like a bone stuck in your throat. You silently shoved the book back on the shelf, unsure what else to do.
So you have Spamton carry the lamp, while you just stand there in a daze.
It wasn't until Spamton poked your cheek that you finally snapped out of it, lowered your head to look at him, and said, "...... What's wrong? ”
…… You don't even know what happened to you. Well, maybe everything is a mess, and now, or rather, from now on, even the once firm heart is shaken at this moment.
Spamton just looked up at you, and he lifted the lamp, illuminating your face. For a moment, the light seemed a bit glaring and you couldn't help but squint.
“…… Nothing, but Miss Y/N, you must believe in yourself." That's all he said.
You quietly lowered your head to look at him. Spamton was silent for a moment because of your gaze before continuing, "I don't think [you] have any fault. [Half-doubt] is usually the best [situation]. ”
You stared at him and suddenly couldn't help but laugh out loud. Your mood really improved a lot, to the point that you could even joke with him: "So, I guess I have a half-doubting attitude toward you too, right?" "If he had said something like that before, you would definitely have done it. After all, he's not someone you can trust forever, especially since he said it himself!"
But now, even if he says that, you still believe what he says. Although you were hurt by him not long ago, it was just a small matter; once it passes, it doesn't become a lasting wound for you. So you still choose to trust him, because now he is your business partner, or your friend, and ......
What else is there? You can't think of anything right away, so wait until you remember later.
Spamton was silent for a moment, then nodded and shook his head: "Yes, I think [you] should [must] do this, but I don't [have hope] [you] and don't [trust]." He felt conflicted and conflicted, and in the end just said this. He didn't know if this was good or bad. Maybe maintaining the status quo was also good.
…… But perhaps taking a step forward is just as good, even though the road ahead is unknown.
"Hmm...... So what should we do...... "You pretended to be troubled, stroked your chin, and then, as you wished, saw Spamton's tight lips turning a bit nervous, and his glasses were completely pixelated. "Alright, even though you said that, I'll still trust you, because we're very, very good friends...... Uh, probably best friends?" "You think about it and feel a bit uncertain.
Then you added, a bit fiercely: "I trust you so much, you can't stab me in the back, or I'll definitely hunt you down. I mean what I say!" "Although it's hard to say if you'll be able to do that by then, it doesn't stop you from making threats first."
Spamton's glasses returned to their original pinkish color. He just nodded silently, and you nodded in satisfaction. That girl had long since left, and for a while, only you two remained in the library. It looked rather eerie. You shivered and hurried back to the entrance. Now you could see that bright and warm hall again. You hung the lamp back on before walking back into the hall. There was a clock hanging above the front desk. You glanced at it—it was almost dusk.
…… If it's about Fengmo Shi, going out now should be pretty much the same. You hugged Spamton, pushed open the door with one hand, and walked straight out. After all, you'd probably gathered enough evidence. Luckily, you had muted your camera beforehand, so they didn't notice your little moves. You turned on the camera to check, confirmed that you had recorded all three ruthless men upstairs, and only then did you turn off the camera with satisfaction.
Then you look up. The sun is shining brightly today. At dusk, the shadow of the inn casts its shadow down, enveloping you, stretching and stretching until it covers the cliff and reaches the other end. Then you widen your eyes—you see, as the shadow casts, a black bridge appears between the cliff and the other end. Although it sways and has an illusion, it probably really exists. In any case, you carefully walked over, squatted down, and touched it with your finger to confirm that the bridge really existed.
But Spamton just shook his head at you, indicating he couldn't see the bridge. Perhaps, it was someone as skeptical as you who, at this moment, believed in the existence of the demon encounter and saw it.
Anyway, you take a deep breath. To prevent the bridge from suddenly disappearing, you speed up desperately to the other side. Then you bend over to catch your breath, then look back at the hotel one last time. The screen flashes to remind you that the main quest is complete and you will leave the world in 24 hours.
At this point, you don't have time to deal with anything else—luckily, you're probably in the same era, or maybe even the same world. In any case, you don't dare to think too much about it. You just log into your account at the nearest internet café, ask Spamton to help you edit a stunning copy, then upload your footage of your filming and recording, and click send.
If calling the police directly doesn't help, then they use public opinion. Under pressure from public opinion, the police will always find a way to give the public the truth. Although you may feel a bit nervous, you may not be sure if this will really work.
…… But it seems that because you sent bloody and violent content, you're now being chased by the police. Luckily, you only have 24 hours—oh, now it's 20 hours.
You and Spamton dodged, and for once, you rummaged through the trash can, since you were basically penniless now. Meanwhile, you anxiously waited for the side quest to be completed. Although you wanted to complain about the current situation, time was tight, and you had no mood to say anything more. Spamton clearly knew this and didn't say much.
…… Finally, in the final second before leaving the world, you see the side quest's progress bar hit 100%. After that, you and Spamton lose consciousness.
Inn Jingmeng · END

content:
You suddenly sat up from the bed, looking at the familiar desk shrouded in darkness before you, the faint light outside the window, and the tall building, and then you dumbly realized you had returned...... It was truly thrilling—in the last second of the countdown, the mission progress reached 100%. Anyway, you held the check for one hundred thousand and cheered, almost kissing you.
Spamton, sitting next to you, silently lifts his head to look at you.
You were excited for a while before finally remembering the little puppet who played the game with you. So you looked down at him, and saw that he was sitting obediently on the bed, looking very pure and innocent. Only you knew he was not innocent at all.

In this situation, you naturally care more about Spamton's situation.
“…… Well, alright, so can you not give up that damn heart-shaped object?" In the end, you still managed to say it with difficulty. If he really needs ...... Then just pretend you don't know he found a scapegoat!
He shook his head: "It's not a [necessity], but it's an [important guarantee]." "If only that set of armor would be enough to succeed...... Of course, things probably aren't that simple.
"Alright...... Well, but maybe I can help. Do you need my help with something? "After thinking it over, you've decided not to change Spamton's plan, but if his plan goes wrong, then everything will be ruined. You don't want that to happen yet.
“…… Perhaps, for the Queen's Mansion's Underground Abyss, can you navigate to it on foot? ”
And you blink at him, completely unfamiliar with the way, not even knowing where this so-called Queen’s mansion actually is. But after spending a long time together, you understand him a little bit, and based on his words, you can still infer a little of what he means: "Are you asking if I can go to the basement of the Queen's mansion?"
Spamton just nodded, affirming your words.
You continue to look at him blankly: "But I don’t know the way! I have no idea how to get there!"
Honestly, you really don't know the way. The roads in Cyber City are so winding and annoying, and you're terrible with directions. If it weren't for Spamton leading you all the way, you could have gone off track just by following the navigation on your own.
Spamton stared at you for a while, then sighed helplessly: "I might [at that time] be unable to [act as] [your] [navigation system], so I will first [navigate: in the direction of the Queen’s mansion], and get [you] familiar with the [route]."
You nod: "Okay… then I’ll trouble you. Will you take me there now?"
Spamton nodded too, and you lifted him onto your shoulder to sit down, then closed the shop. Honestly, you've walked so much at the dump that you're already familiar with the roads here, so you didn't need his navigation to walk out. But for some reason, the roads Spamton pointed you to next were all some remote alleys...... Your eyes were spinning. Even though you felt this road was going much faster since you were there soon, you still looked at Spamton, rubbing your temples in frustration: "Can we switch to the main road and walk on...... All the roads you're taking are alleys—I don't recognize them at all! How am I supposed to get there then! Sounds like you're the one going there yourself...... If I don't know where to go, I won't be able to help you!" "You sound quite justified, even putting your hands on your hips to boost your arrogance. You already have the feeling that you're the villains by default. Later, Spamton might have to do some bad things, and you have to be his contact.
“…… Not [Support]. "Spamton was at a loss for words. He just wanted you to witness it, and if possible, to help out or something?" Even if he didn't help, it didn't matter. He arrogantly believed everything was perfect, and as long as he acted according to the plan, everything would be perfect. He didn't need the wishes given by the game system.
You pursed your lips: "You're about to snatch someone's heart-shaped object. That's basically killing someone. If that's not a helper, then what is......"
But before you could finish, both of your faces instantly changed and turned pale. You hurriedly grabbed Spamton and held him in your arms, running deeper into the alley. Now you were glad you had come down a small alley.
A familiar white light flashed in front of you, and before losing consciousness, you only managed to say: "Weren’t we supposed to have a month off? It’s only been two days—"
It's just that the game system doesn't answer your meaning.
Friday· END

content:
[Main Quest: Unraveling the Reason for the Avenger's Revenge] Reward: One month of rest and security guarantees.
[Side Quest: From the moment you enter the game, stop those who are killed by the Avengers] Reward: 100,000 gold + 100,000 Dark Coins
You sat on the ground, still shaken with your Spamton, hugging you. Honestly, you might even be a bit confused about what was happening...... You promised a month of rest—why did you have to return to the game world the next day? And for some reason, the game screen in front of you was broken, and there was a faint, inexplicable crackling sound of electricity, giving you a sense of unease and chills, making you shiver instinctively.
Spamton murmurs in your arms, "It seems ...... the Heavenly Wishing Machine might be completely destroyed after we achieve all our objectives." "For some reason, he also felt uneasy, but what followed was more trembling and excitement. Perhaps, at least if he couldn't achieve that ultimate goal, then the game system would help him achieve it." Although it didn't seem like anything good...... Maybe.
You looked down at Spamton in surprise. Muttering, "You actually call it the Heavenly Wishing Machine...... That doesn't sound like a good name. I just call it the game system." "Although I previously communicated with you through text messages on the light screen saying that after completing all tasks, I would grant you a wish, you didn't fully believe it. Compared to so-called vague wishes, you still believed more in your own power and in your choice to move forward. Maybe you could change something, maybe it could make everything different."
But it seems Spamton believes more than half of it; otherwise, why would it call it the Heavenly Wishing Machine?
But you don't have time to study this now, because side quests already track progress at the very start of the game. This time, the side quest is the opposite—the progress bar is actually 100%. After just a few words, it has already reached 90%. You quickly looked up to take in the surroundings. You didn't realize until you looked, but when you looked, you were shocked. You two were actually in a desolate wilderness, seemingly in a small grove. After all, the environment was dim, and you could faintly hear the rustling of leaves—the rustling of leaves in the wind. Not far ahead, there was a faint light, shining straight on a tree ahead. That must be the headlight. You also saw a car parked there, with 'taxi' written on it—it was a taxi. You were about to stand up and walk straight ahead, since the taxi was parked here with its lights on, and you couldn't tell if someone was inside. But the sound that followed made you stop in your tracks.
It was the man's screams and gasps, the woman's sobs and sharp screams, and her helpless cries for help, faintly mixed with a hint of profanity. You didn't even need to walk over to know what was happening. You couldn't help but feel a bit nauseous. Then, instinctively, you covered Spamton's eyes and quickened your pace running toward him. Those small hands belonging to the puppet also covered your eyes. You wanted to sigh helplessly, but then you heard the woman's increasingly painful and weak moans. Your face grew even paler, just hoping you could run a little faster—fast enough to prevent that tragic scene from happening.
…… But the distance was too far. You couldn't change anything. When you finally reached a spot where you could see the scene clearly, the puppet's small hand instinctively lowered itself. You stared blankly at the man's hand gripping the woman's neck, his face twisted with excitement and twisted expression, making your heart tremble uncontrollably. The woman just weakly tilted her head to the side, clearly dead. Her skirt was torn to shreds, and you could vaguely see the liquid flowing from below. The man only pulled up his pants, finally showing a look of satisfaction, and spat at the woman's corpse with a look of disgust. Under the glaring white light of the car headlights, you could barely see that the man's arms were covered in scratches left by the girl's nails, some too deep, tearing the skin and still bleeding.
You feel guilty for failing to save the girl, and at the same time, you think she's done too well. Somehow, you actually see what seems to be white smoke...... Or a cyan light. In short, that pale-green, semi-transparent soul floats out from the woman. Her face is still filled with confusion, instinctive pain and hatred. As the taxi driver ahead is about to leave, she instinctively stretches out her claws, trying to attack the man. But the ghost only pierces through his body and doesn't harm him at all. Perhaps sensing the ghost's chill, the driver instinctively shivers.
You poked Spamton's cheek in your arms and whispered, "Did you see any ghosts?" ”
Spamton just shook his head, you know, he didn't see anything.
Alright, looks like only you can see this ghost...... So this side quest depends on you to complete, but you think this revenge is fair and just, and there's nothing to stop — well, but a vigilante justice can't completely make her feel pain, so it's better to stop her actions. Although you don't care whether the other person lives or dies, you still feel that the other person should fully realize their mistakes before voluntarily choosing punishment. That is true repentance and true revenge.
Just as you were lost in thought about these questions, you noticed the pale ghost floating in front of you, as if it noticed you could see her. She pleaded with her hands clasped together, making a prayerful gesture. You felt a bit troubled, but you understood what she meant—she hoped you could help her get revenge on the taxi driver.
Then, unexpectedly, the woman spoke. Her voice was cold and carried the hoarseness left after a long scream: "...... If possible, I hope I can kill him right here." ”
You were a bit stunned when you heard her voice, then started to struggle. Honestly, if it were just a simple report and the other party would accept punishment, it wouldn't matter, but...... You want to kill the other party? You don't want your hands stained with blood yet.
Spamton watched you standing there in a daze, watching as if you were reacting to something, and anxiously poked your cheek. Because the ghost you mentioned earlier was afraid you'd be trapped in some illusion and unable to escape, and besides that, he couldn't help much.
You finally snap out of it, shake your head at her, and try to say something else, but the woman seems to have lost her senses, and the anger and dissatisfaction on her face become even more obvious. She charges straight at you—then you widen your eyes because you realize your perspective is actually overhead. You can see your body casually tossing the Spamton from your arms and then picking up an iron pipe that had fallen from the ground—probably what used to be some kind of junkyard. In any case, your movements weren't very skillful as you walked toward the taxi driver, who had his back to you and didn't notice anything. After all, he was leisurely lighting a cigarette and enjoying himself, while talking on the phone.
You widened your eyes and anxiously reached out to touch that body. You wanted to reclaim your own body. Come on, you definitely didn't want to do something controlled by outsiders that wasn't your own choice. Spamton clearly realized that you had probably become a different person now. He wondered if some wandering spirit had taken over your body. He thought, all of this was probably related to the ghost you had just asked him about.
He watched as "you" held up the iron pipe, about to fall at the taxi driver. Then he quickly stepped forward and grabbed "yours"'s legs. "You" struggled to move forward for a moment, but frowned and kicked the little puppet away.
You felt heartbroken watching it, but it seemed that at that moment, "you" were distracted, so you gritted your teeth and flew down again, touching your own body. Finally, this time you felt the touch of a real object. You blinked twice and watched as the pale ghost was pushed out by you, glaring at you with a face full of hatred. You were still holding the iron pipe, about to fall and blow the driver's head apart. You quickly pulled back and changed direction, hitting the driver's neck. Then the driver collapsed limply, and the phone fell to the ground. You expressionlessly picked up his phone, hung up, then called the police, describing the scene and that you were witnesses.
Then the call ended. You hurriedly squatted down and picked up Spamton, who had just been kicked hard, dusted him off, kissed his forehead, and gently stroked the spot where he had just been kicked. Somewhat unskilled, yet cautiously asked, "...... Just now, sorry, I didn't expect someone to take over my body. Are you alright?" ”
Spamton just looked at you and shook his head: "[No], as long as [you] [come unscathed], that's enough." ”
You pressed your lips together. Honestly, your feelings were a bit complicated. You weren't quite sure what kind of feelings you had for Spamton...... After all, you weren't used to what it felt like for someone to truly care about you. In any case, a strange warmth flowed into your heart.
And that pale ghost still hovered beside you, speaking with a face full of hatred: "Why did you stop me from making a move just now?" ”
You let out a sigh of relief and looked at her seriously: "After all, I think...... Killing him directly isn't the best form of revenge, or rather, revenge. I think it's better to let the police arrest him. Then he'll have plenty of time to repent. ”
Then you hear the woman murmur to herself, "But in this area...... There is no death penalty, and rape is not sentenced to several years. ”
You were momentarily stunned, not knowing how to respond. But Spamton looked up as if he could see her, though in fact he was just looking in the same direction as you.
He was quite serious: "No, then [you] would commit the crime of murder. Under your control, my [Angel] would [fall to hell] because of it." "You actually know what Spamton means. And at this moment, calling you an angel or something...... You feel a bit embarrassed, but you cleared your throat twice to ease the awkwardness.
The woman's gaze dropped, somewhat ethereal and elusive. You only heard her sneer coldly: "Actually, you can't see me either, so why are you pretending here?" Oh, so she was just defending you...... Does he like you? "The woman lifted her head and looked at you with great interest.
You coughed twice again, feeling completely embarrassed. Even though your voice was stammering, you still quietly explained, "...... Yes, we're a couple." After saying this, you felt Spamton, who was holding you in his arms, kiss your chin, making your face blush even more.
The woman just snorted coldly: "Couples?" Men are no good. ”
You instinctively explained, "He's not a man...... No, he's not human, he's ...... Uh...... "What exactly is Spamton?" You can't explain clearly. When you look down, you see Spamton glaring at you fiercely, so you smile a little embarrassedly and scratch your head.
However...... Maybe you can still find an adjective? Anyway, you've found a reason: "Yeah, yes, he's a puppet." In a way, this doesn't seem entirely wrong.
At this moment, the woman seemed amused by you and chuckled, "No wonder, I also thought he didn't seem like a real person. So it turns out he was a puppet you made to satisfy your own love." "She seemed to misunderstand something, but you didn't want to dwell on this issue any longer, just nodded wildly with a soft 'mm-ah' sound."
Her mood actually improved considerably: "Alright, as long as you like it. But it seems like you're the only person who can see me now, so I have to follow you first, and you have to help me get my revenge." ”
You feel a pang of toothache and a headache: "Why should I help you get revenge?" "Heaven have mercy, you two just met by chance, why make things difficult for a passerby?"
She looked at you and calmly stated a fact: "I just tried, I can't take his body. Maybe I can only take the body of someone who can see me...... If you don't help, I'll take your body and kill those few people!" She finally managed to come to her senses, but now she was confused again, so you could only nod helplessly and panicked.
Only then did she cheer up again. Probably because her mind was still unclear, she drifted a bit farther away. She wondered what she was doing. You watched helplessly as that pale blue ghost drifted away, then pressed Spamton's head, your gaze wandering: "I don't even know what kind of thing you are...... So she just made something up, but it seemed she believed it. ”
Spamton simply nodded lightly: "It's okay." ”
You rubbed his head again, shaking left and right until Spamton felt a bit dizzy. Frowning, he wanted to say something to stop you, but you suddenly stopped and sighed wistfully: "Sigh, but it looks like both the main and side quests need to be completed...... Because she wants to follow us and have me help her get revenge. ”
Honestly, you're really venting your emotions...... Whether it's friendships or romantic relationships, it's okay to do this, right? You're not sure either, since you basically have no friends and have never been in a relationship. So after saying this, you nervously wait for Spamton's answer. Whatever he says, you'll accept it, even if it might put you in a bad mood...... If that's the case, then isn't everything wrong?
Before you could figure out the answer, Spamton grabbed your arm and answered your question seriously: "I think this is a [good thing] for [you], saving us the trouble of searching for [clues] on our own, and it's a [shocking price: $4.99] [a [good thing]. ”
Well, it does seem like a good thing, but you probably feel the same way, but it all feels a bit unreal.
Then Spamton added, "I hope [you] can understand that whether it's a [friendship] or a [romantic relationship], you can [share] your secret emotions with each other. [You] shouldn't [give up] to [yourself] because of me." "Clearly, he could more or less sense the hint of unease in your words. You hadn't shown any unease when you were dissatisfied with him before, but now you suddenly felt worried...... He probably understood what was going on. Of course, he was willing to explain this to you, after all, as a Addison before, he had learned a bit of everything to some extent.
You paused for a moment, then instinctively nodded, and then you smiled again. This time, your smile wasn't as cautious as before, but rather completely free of gloom: "Oh, you're right, I really shouldn't be like this...... So, does love exist to make the other person better?" You held him and followed the ghost forward, asking as you went. You were simply a bit curious.
"Maybe...... It's hoping the other person will "add the finishing touch," maybe it's just "helping each other in times of need," but "relationships between men and women" are about sharing each other, and also about "entertaining themselves." He held back for a long time before coming up with these words, but he was trying to explain it to you.
And you just nodded thoughtfully. Honestly, watching the little puppet hold back a few words after holding back for a long time was pretty funny, but you held back your laughter—you knew it was just their way of speaking...... But you couldn't help but chuckle softly.
Spamton glared at you but said nothing.
"I get what you mean. You mean love is about wanting the other person to become better, hoping they can be happy...... But you also want to find joy in it? "Although you still don't quite understand what this so-called love really is, you can feel that you truly have these pure and genuine hopes in your heart, so...... Alright, you admit it, so you probably love him—no, the answer is yes.
Spamton nodded in your arms: "Yes, so I am also your [spiritual harbor.] ”
“…… Can I rely on you when I need it? No need to repeat myself. I've actually always trusted you...... Well, you have to compensate me for the things you lied to me before. Forget it, you saved me last time, so I won't let you pay for it...... You frowned and then relaxed, feeling conflicted and muttering to yourself.
Spamton was a bit helpless, and in the end just leaned in and poked your cheek with his finger.
By now, the ghost floating ahead had already run far away. She turned to see you still walking slowly, and impatiently shouted loudly, "Can't you go faster! I've already gone far out!" ”
You loudly replied to her: "I'll be right now! Wait a little longer!" ”
Then you quickened your pace slightly. At that moment, you suddenly remembered a question and hurriedly asked Spamton, "By the way, what was it about you earlier saying you made me bear the burden of a crime? Didn't you tell me last time that this is a game world?" "Precisely because this is a game world, you don't feel guilty for failing to accomplish certain things.
Spamton was silent for a moment. He had originally thought Iveco would break down and question him, but he hadn't realized you actually needed him to explain...... But if he told you this truthfully, you would probably really be devastated. But he couldn't hide it from you because of it.
…… After all, at this moment, knowing the truth is more important.
So you waited a while, and only then did Spamton speak in a low voice: "...... [you] didn't have any [Safety Precautions]?" This world is connected to the [Light World], after all, [you] could use your [identity system] in the previous world. "Maybe it's just your own admission, but no matter what, he will always pull back this cruel veil for you.
You froze, your eyes widened, and you instinctively slowed your pace. Yes, just two days ago, in the previous world, you were still using this to post public opinion on your social media account, but now how did you forget about it?
Yes, you just don't want to admit that at that moment, you just stood by and didn't help. Yes, you just don't want to admit that at that time, you could have saved that little girl but did nothing. Even if you had acted, the consequences might have been even worse...... But compared to a living human life, what is that? And the woman before her, if she hadn't suffered this disaster, she would probably be laughing with her friends and enjoying a pleasant night, rather than quietly pondering revenge in the forest.
Your heart is filled with mixed emotions. To be honest, you don't really care much about human life...... But all the education you've received and your rationality tell you that you must care, while your emotions tell you that it's just a life unrelated to you—whether you live or die doesn't matter. That's exactly why you're so pained. Maybe you're just annoyed that you seem to care when you actually don't.
Spamton looked up, watching your expression shift between light and flicker. He sighed. In fact, he had known all along that this might be the outcome, but you always have to accept the truth. He didn't know what you were thinking, so he could only guess and said, "...... [you] don't need to worry. After all, [you] are not the [culprit], and [you] are also the [victim]. ”
And you just sighed, shook your head, feeling down, and didn't want to say more: "...... It's not because of this. ”
For no reason, you recall what that girl said in the previous world: [Since you are like warm water, neither cold nor hot, then I will spit you out.] ] You feel a chill down your spine because of this...... Perhaps what she describes is exactly your current situation—not just a simple issue of theism versus atheism, but a much heavier matter rooted in personal thought.
As for theism or atheism...... Anyway, with so many strange and bizarre things happening, you're still just someone who is half-believed.
Spamton hesitated for a moment, and he could tell you were clearly not in the mood: "I told you, I am your 'spiritual harbor.'" ”
And you just forced a smile: "Mm, I know. But let's talk about this later." ”
To be honest, your mind is in chaos right now, and you can't make sense of it at all. You don't know how to explain it to Spamton. Maybe after all that, all you want to express is just one thing, and you can't even make sense of it yourself. At that moment, you only feel fear—an inexplicable, bone-chilling fear. You don't even know what you're afraid of, just quickening your pace to follow that wisp of ghost.
She looked at you and finally caught up, nodded in satisfaction: "I know you and your couple puppet probably have a lot to talk about...... Hmm, but you can't forget about helping me get revenge!" As she spoke, she bared her fangs and claws, making a terrifying gesture at you, as if hoping you would be scared.
But you only found her posture a bit amusing, and you did laugh too. The emotions you had been suppressing earlier finally relaxed a little.
She gave you a displeased look, or rather, glared at you: "What are you doing! Believe it or not, I'll take over your body and do something bad right now!" ”
"What bad things are you going to do?" You asked casually.
“…… Ordering eighteen male models at a nightclub? Feasting at a barbecue stall and then refusing to pay? She thought for a long time and hesitantly said these things.
You just lowered your head and didn't look at her. Instead, the Spamton in your arms shook her head, probably thinking the direction of your conversation wasn't very healthy. He hoped you wouldn't continue.
But you think this girl isn't a bad person, or rather, she's just innocent and should have lived a vibrant life. Thinking this way, your mood sinks again. You just ask, "...... You know there are even more illegal things, but these are just minor matters. Why don't you do those illegal and criminal acts? ”
Honestly, when you ask this question, you feel like your nerves are twitching. You know you're just taking a risk, or maybe gambling—betting that this girl is actually easy to get along with.
She was stunned for a moment. The ghost turned its head awkwardly at first, but only quickened its drift: "Because I know those are heinous crimes...... I don't want you to have a criminal record either." Her voice grew blurred as the distance faded, and you looked up at your concerned Spamton, just shaking your head to signal that everything was fine.
After that, you followed the girl out of the dense forest. No one knew how the taxi driver managed to find such a place, but as you stood on the cliff looking down, you could vaguely hear the sound of police sirens—'woo wa wa' ('woo wa' wah).
You look at the girl, who is staring blankly at the bustling city below: "It's all over." You just say softly.
She looked up at you, nodded, then proudly pointed to the mountaintop: "My boyfriend invited me to meet at that villa. My next target for revenge is him." ”
You looked up and indeed saw a brightly lit villa at the mountaintop, and beyond your cliff was the mountain path leading straight to that place. You tugged at the corner of your mouth, roughly knowing how the driver had tricked this girl...... He was probably just talking about taking a shortcut.
However...... You still have some questions you'd like to ask her.
“…… Your boyfriend, then why didn't he come to pick you up in person? Did he really let you come here in such a remote place?" You asked a question.
She just tugged at the corner of her mouth: "...... I told you, men are no good. You'll understand once you see for yourself. ”
At that moment Spamton he poked your arm. After all, he couldn't hear the girl's voice and could only infer from what you said. So you quietly repeated it to him.
Spamton thought for a moment, then solemnly raised another question: "...... Is the time he arranged to meet [you] [set sail today]?" ”
That ghost just looked at you quietly and shook his head: "No, in fact, he never invited me here to meet." ”
You were momentarily speechless, only telling Spamton this sentence. Then the ghost ignored you and floated straight upward, leaving you to run up the mountain path.
It wasn't until you stopped outside that villa, until you heard the moans coming from inside, that your expression changed—and if you heard correctly, the sounds were from two men, since the tones were clearly different, and you didn't even need to look to know what was happening inside.
At that moment, you look at the girl with some concern. You know why she came here today.
She simply stated a fact quite calmly: "Because of him, my boyfriend, he deceived me, using me as a cover to deceive his parents, while he secretly got involved with his boyfriend. He contracted AIDS and passed it on to me. Even if I don't die today, I will die sooner or later." ”
You slowly opened your mouth wide, blinking sluggishly. If that person could at least be punished by law, but this man before you couldn't—after all, it was just a moral issue, not a legal offense. Still, if it was AIDS, perhaps the handling would be very simple......
Before you could think further, the ghost changed its tone to mockery: "So now I want to seize your body and kill the two lovers inside." ”
You widened your eyes and instinctively hugged the Spamton tightly in your arms, making Spamton somewhat uncomfortable pushing your arm twice. But seeing you staring ahead with a serious and alert expression, even though he could only see a blank space—he knew exactly what you were being wary of. And holding tightly might have been because your nervousness needed to be relieved through some action, so in the end, Spamton tacitly approved your actions.
The ghost floated in place, its pale pale translucent spirit casually touching the wall of the house, naturally piercing through. She revealed a smile—one that seemed bitter and tinged with annoyance, yet also tinged with a hint of relief, even if there was still a hint of unwillingness.
“…… Just kidding, seeing how nervous you are, if I stole your body, wouldn't you two be beaten up together? But you can't hit me. "As she spoke, she even lifted her eyelids and gave you a funny face."
And you just twitch your lips, honestly, it's not funny.
She put away that expression too, just looking at you in confusion: "Isn't this funny? I thought you were probably laughing out loud by now." ”
…… Her sense of humor is hard for you to understand—maybe some kind of cognitive bias. You chose to respect and bless her.
You just shook your head and sighed helplessly: "This isn't funny, and you shouldn't keep trying to make me laugh." ”
But the ghost just tilted its head: "But Dad said that if you see someone unhappy, you have to find a way to cheer them up. That's why I used to use this trick—Dad always smiled." ”
“…… Has he ever teased you like this to make you happy?" "You just thought about it.
She fell silent, then shook her head: "No, never before." She seemed to want to say something more, but before she could speak, she withdrew her words.
Inside the house, the moans of two men were still intertwined and tangled, while outside, you were still staring at this ghost. Spamton noticed that the force binding your arms was a bit lighter, so he poked your face again, and only then did you fully come back to your senses.
You tugged at the corner of your mouth: "Alright, if I want to help you get revenge, you could just let your boyfriend get sick at random, right? For example...... Something like a cold? "You suggested casually.
"Yes, but he's in good health and won't get sick at all." The ghost said seriously.
"We have to give it a try...... Let's go get ready now. "As you spoke, you walked around the villa and actually found a place to throw trash at the back. For some reason, no one had cleared it yet. Anyway, pinching your nose and rummaging, you found a very filthy, worn-out wooden basin.
Coincidentally, not far from this villa was a lake, so you filled it with water, then climbed onto the rooftop, squatted on the eaves, and stared intently toward the door.
"...... [Switching positions]? I think [you] need a [moment of leisure]. "Just as you were staring intently toward the door below, you heard Spamton's voice.
You belatedly realize you're actually very sleepy, so you can't help but yawn...... After all, it's already late, but the eaves are definitely not a good place to sleep—unless you plan to keep pretending to be an upside-down bat on the eaves.
That ghost also drifted around you boredly: "If you ask me, they definitely won't come out tonight anyway. Just rest well for the night before coming back to camp them." ”
Spamton can't hear what the ghost says; it just turns around in your arms, gazing at you quietly.

Yet precisely because there is Spamton in the rented room now, you begin to look forward to going home.
…… For Spamton, it's probably the same. If that's the case, you might have some idea how to interpret that phrase.
After all, you not only have a home but also a lover, and have learned something from him more or less...... Although that's not what you want to learn, you have subtly picked up some of his tricks in lying and sales pitch.
So, you are two similar beings...... You can't really call yourself human, because Spamton isn't really human either. It's because of similar cores that you get close. As the saying goes, you are both lukewarm beings, and perhaps you will eventually perish, but after meeting, everything changes. After all, it's because of fundamental differences that you write different possibilities along the path of intersecting destinies.
Although Spamton didn't answer your question, you still got your own answer—perhaps the answer you got was far more genuine than what others told you. So you finally smiled with relief: "Well, if that's the case, then you're also my soul's harbor...... Well, I know maybe it shouldn't be that word, but I don't know what better word to describe it. As for what you mean to me...... I can only say it's a completely different existence. ”
If that's the case, maybe you can say 'forever' too. After all, on your life journey, you'll never meet such a special person again, and no other memories will be more vivid than those months spent together or in the gaming world.
"Ah, so... maybe I can also promise you that we will always be there for each other." Of course, if one day he doesn’t want to anymore, you’ll have to use those life-saving money he tricked you out of the first time as a threat—whether it works or not is another matter, but in any case, your fates are tightly intertwined.
This time, it was Spamton who looked up at you in surprise. He exchanged a glance with you, but you just smiled and winked at him, then leaned in and kissed him on the forehead.
This left him a bit caught off guard, just staring blankly at you...... To be honest, he was wondering how to explain that sentence, but now you look like you've completely figured it out. He wasn't sure if you really understood.
So he anxiously nodded and buried his head again. After all, his face was bright red, and of course, smoke was coming out of the puppet’s head, which you could clearly see.
You didn't intend to expose him, just put the meat slices and vegetables into the freshly boiling pot, watched Spamton finish the ice cream bowl, and then ordered an ice cream cone for him. You don't think a puppet would ruin its stomach from eating ice...... Well, to be honest, maybe not.
Spamton was holding the ice cream cone with both hands, gnawing on it. His glasses were now coated with thick white mist from the hot pot smoke, but the temperature on his face had faded quite a bit from the cold cone. You covered your mouth and chuckled quietly, as if you heard it. You kept feeling like Spamton was glaring at you. Of course, when you turned your head, Spamton was just lowering his head to bite the cone, the mist on his glasses still thick.
In short, you skillfully hugged Spamton and served food to the little puppet. Both of you had a hearty meal, and because you ordered the ice cream bowl and cone, the cold and refreshing texture was really nice. Although he didn't taste much sweetness, the texture was great, so Spamton was in a good mood.
Now you ordered an ice cream as a dessert after your meal. The weather was getting warmer, and you wanted some ice too. You waved goodbye to the boss, who looked pained, then hummed an off-key tune as you walked out.
You took a bite of the popsicle. It was milk-flavored and soft, with a bit of frostbite to it, making you shiver, but the soft texture made it taste good.
So you casually handed Spamton the ice cream to his mouth. For some reason, he seemed silent for a moment, and you didn't understand why he hadn't taken a bite, so you urged him a bit: "You should eat it." ”
Finally, he bit the part you had just taken a bite from. You seemed to hear the chewing, and after a while, he replied, "Well… thank you, Miss Y/N, for the [Kangkai]."
You nodded in satisfaction, prepared to bite the popsicle yourself again, only to stop. You finally understood what he had been hesitating about… the popsicle was now covered with his saliva.
Well, you took a deep breath and bit it anyway; after all, this was the relationship you were in now, so no big deal.
But before you even finish eating the ice cream, you feel a blanket of white before your eyes, a familiar sense of detachment washes over you. You startle in your heart. You know the game system is causing trouble, but you don't know why this time is so sudden—the promised one-month holiday!
Unfortunately, you didn’t have time to think further, nor to finish the popsicle in your hand, before losing consciousness. Spamton did too.
Saturday· END
