You've waited too long, most of your things have been played, and there's nothing new to be new. You don't know what else you can do, so you just sit blankly on the trash can, waiting for Spamton to come back. Sometimes you even have the illusion that Spamton might never come back. But you quickly dismiss that thought. You refuse to admit it, preferring to keep trusting promises that might have been dashed.
And during those countless moments of daydreaming, you can't even count how much time passed. Just propping your chin up was so boring that you fell asleep. Until today, you were woken up by the noisy noise outside.
You quietly poke your head out to observe the commercial street, and with just one glance, your gaze falls on that little thing below. With just one look, you can tell it's Spamton—absolutely, absolutely impossible to be wrong. This is what your intuition tells you, and you've always trusted your instincts.
So you thought for a moment, then jumped down from the trash can, then stood in front of Spamton, looking at the Addisons, raising an eyebrow: "What, just because he's shrunk, you all want to mock him and then bully him?" "They're clearly the same Dark People as you, the same species, both Addisons. Why should they look down on him?" "Why mock him?" "You stood in front of Spamton, frowning as you looked at the guys in front of you.
Pink snorted coldly: "It's you again, huh? We didn't bully him. We just told the truth. Didn't he just get kicked out? And now he's turned into this ghostly state—who knows what he's been through." His voice was sarcastic.
“…… I'm quite worried, after all...... No one of the Dark Civilians knew about Spamton's situation before, but now we've seen it. "Blue let out a heavy sigh.
And you sighed, "Alright, maybe you mean nothing, but I think Spammy doesn't like hearing you talk...... So, I'll take him away first?" As you spoke, you bent down and picked up the little Spamton. You felt that the little puppet's body seemed a bit stiff and trembling, so you gently patted his head and whispered to him that it was okay, that nothing was going wrong.
But Spamton's feelings are complicated, because ...... He's been protected by you again. Clearly, he doesn't want this to happen, but ...... But, in the end, it seems everything is just a cycle.
And you don't mind that; you just turn to walk in the direction you came. At least that place is relatively quiet, and no dark people will disturb you.
But just as you were about to get up and leave, Yello stepped forward to block you, then watched helplessly as his hand passed through your body—your transparent body, his eyes widened in surprise.
The other Addisons also looked at you as if they'd seen a ghost, but you just blinked innocently and made a funny face at them, "Lue Lue Lue Lue...... If you can't touch me, don't even think about catching me and Spamton—I'm his guardian spirit! "Of course, that's just your nonsense. You and Spamton aren't that close.
Those Addisons didn't dare disturb you anymore. You smoothly took Spamton back to the alley where you lived, sat back down on the trash can, and then hugged Spamton, looking a bit worried.
You first carefully leaned down and kissed his forehead, then softly asked, "...... What on earth is going on? How did you end up like this? Didn't you already become a big shot before? ”
Spamton didn't answer the question; he simply carefully took out the poster from under his tightly wrapped suit jacket and handed it to you, now a bit wrinkled.
You were a little dazed, but still opened the poster. In this poster, you saw yourself—seemingly a bit melancholic in high school, but still smiling brightly. Your eyes flickered as you gently stroked the poster, then you furrowed your brows, your vision turned gray again, your head aching. You really didn't understand what the thoughts drifting in your mind at that moment meant—but you knew, you remembered.
So you hugged the little puppet tightly, your voice trembling a little, and you couldn't help but shed tears: "...... I'm sorry, is it because of this poster that you ended up like this? ”
Spamton said, "You don't need any [apology] meaning." ”
But you shook your head firmly: "No, I have to say that...... I don't know if you regret it, but I am...... I regret it, I ...... I don't want to see you become like this...... You start to sob uncontrollably. You even start to feel afraid, start to regret. Maybe you just didn't covet those memories at first, maybe you took away the life Spamton should have, maybe it's because of you that he ended up like this.
But the little puppet just cupped your face, gently sucking the tears that dripped from your cheeks. The tears were salty, and even Spamton felt bitter inside, even though he didn't know if the Dark People truly had hearts.
“…… This is my [personal will], my [irretrievable] [choice]. "Spamton said, his voice becoming even harsher—a bit hoarse, with some crackling electric currents. You even vaguely heard one or two sounds like sparks flickering, making you wonder if you were hearing it wrong.
"Alright...... At the very least, I should thank you. Thank you for helping me recover so many memories, thank you for being willing to stay by my side and help me...... It was also because of what you ended up like this. "As you spoke, your voice gradually faded. It was an indescribable sense of guilt. You truly felt a heavy emotion for this little one before you.
Spamton just shook his head again: "No, this has nothing to do with you. It's my responsibility to bear all consequences." ”
He insisted on saying this because it was indeed his choice that led to his own fate. Although he had felt lost and wandered, he never regretted it.
“…… Is that so? I understand. If that's what you mean. "You sighed softly. After all, you couldn't go against Spamton's opinion, but as for everything else, what exactly you think, this matter is up to you to decide."
"So...... Finally, what I want to tell you is, I love you. "You hesitated for a moment, but in the end, you hugged Spamton tightly and said those words. It seemed that you had countless similar conversations between you in the dream, even in the dark world, saying similar things. But, you think, this was definitely the most sincere one of you."
Spamton also unintentionally felt a bit blushed and a little embarrassed. He didn't dare lift his head from your embrace to look at you, so he just softly murmured in your embrace.
You pat his head, ponder for a moment, and ask, "Then...... Spammy, what are you planning to do next? ”
After a moment of silence, so long that you might start to doubt something, you finally hear Spamton's urgent reply: "I want to become a [big shot] again. The Queen's [Mansion] might have some kind of secret technique in the [Underground Abyss]......" The first thing he thought of was still that basement. He hadn't had time to look around before, and now he probably wouldn't have the chance to enter the Queen's mansion. After all, those color card butlers would kick him out as soon as they saw him—in the truest sense.
You softly hummed and continued to ask, "Then...... What else? ”
“…… I will reopen a [Custom Shop] near the [Garbage Heap], and I won't give up on [Trade]. "You heard the little puppet continue.
"Can I help you with something?" You know very well that it was because of your arrival that Spamton's shop became famous throughout the cyber world. Now, it's probably the same. As long as you show up and buy something, his shop's business will naturally improve, and he can still become that big shot again.
But Spamton just shook his head, then looked up at you firmly: "No, you don't have to do anything. You're a [Supreme Member], a [Gold User], enjoying all the benefits." "He doesn't want to use you anymore."
You paused: "Don't you need me to help you with anything else?" "It's fine...... "It's just a show, nothing to lose to you. Ah, the fact that you can't leave the commercial street does have some impact."
"Absolutely [unnecessary]." Spamton said as he jumped off you, then turned his back and walked out of the alley. Now, he could no longer establish himself on the commercial street; he could only end up in the garbage heap, a place that might never be visited again, the very place where other Addisons had once thrown him over. Maybe those color card butlers wanted to throw themselves into this place too.
You widened your eyes and instinctively jumped off the trash can, wanting to follow Spamton. You couldn't just watch the person you helped and helped have fallen to nothing, so you instinctively followed. But the ghost's footsteps were quiet, unheard and Spamton didn't notice you were quietly following him.
Even after leaving the alley, you still follow Spamton. Now it's your turn to be stunned, because in the past, you couldn't get out of the commercial street, you tried, and you couldn't even get out of this alley. But now, you can easily get out.
You hurried over, bent down, and quietly grabbed Spamton's hand, stammering, "Spammy, I...... I realized I've come out. Could I help you even more? "After saying that, your eyes sparkled as you looked at Spamton.
Spamton hesitated. To be honest, he ...... He didn't know you'd actually come out with him, and even succeeded. He had never considered this possibility before, but now, he just looked up at you, his tone a bit obscure: "Then help me [move my items] to the [garbage heap] first." As he spoke, Spamton handed you one of the packages he was holding. You tried it and picked it up easily, so you happily followed behind him and continued walking toward the junkyard.
After all, if Spamton is no longer on the commercial street, what's the point of you staying here? Before, you just couldn't leave, but now, since you can leave, you won't miss the chance either.

In the end, you just took a deep breath and gave a bitter smile: "Alright, since you trust me so much, I'll give it a try—hmm, so when are we going to make our move?" ”

He just gazes at your back with a quiet gaze, saying nothing. He's waiting for you to come back. Spamton…… He will show a genuine smile in front of you, whether it's for your efforts or for your feelings. Besides, he is happy to smile for you.

Spamton sat on a tall chair behind the counter, waiting for you, and after a while, you quietly returned, sitting back down against the wall in the back.

"Ah, I was just curious about what the junkyard is like here, so I sneaked out to take a look." You scratched your head, feeling your smile was a bit stiff, but you really couldn't come up with any good reason. You just hoped Spamton wouldn't press further...... "So, do you have any [novel discoveries]?" He did follow your question and continued asking. After all, in this situation, if he didn't ask more, wouldn't his behavior seem too fake? Actually, both of you know right now; it's just a riddle here.
